# GroupTrack 2.7c — day notes 2026-10-22 (to fold into tonight's living master v166 / handoff v72)

Running list of decisions and open items from the 10-22 attach session. Everything here goes INTO the living docs at end of day;
this file is only the holding place until then.

## OPEN DECISION — private trails default (Fred 14:03, Beryl UT)
- Seen: private community/residential roads show on the map in Beryl; they disappear when the filter is set to public only.
- Finding: NO functional change today. FILTER's "Include private land" calls the same TrailFilterState.setLand the old filter
  used; the 2.6h public/private classification (Utah's own determination + PBF access tags) was not touched. The roads
  disappearing on "public only" PROVES they are classified PRIVATE correctly.
- Cause: the default is ALL (Include private land ticked) — always has been (TrailFilterState.reset: land = "ALL").
- Decision needed: keep default ALL, or default to PUBLIC ONLY (private hidden until asked for). Claude leans PUBLIC ONLY.
  Riders with a saved setting keep theirs either way.

## Rules set today
- Standard: HELP ✕ top right everywhere (✕ = leave; the COMPLETE is the screen's own action button). Panels that stay add
  ☰ MOVE and HIDE/SHOW. One help viewer (GtHelpView) on top of every screen.
- Touch rule (12:50): when a function is touched, EVERY screen it opens is brought to the standard in the same patch.
- Nothing is hidden/removed without a named home in the same patch (11:47).
- One-option rule: a button whose module has one attached process runs it directly.
- Persistence (13:30-13:33): ONE GroupTrack map state file; purpose = between sessions, return to where you left off.
  Start-up ALWAYS restores the saved view (no exceptions); Centre on Me brings you to where you are. Save as you go.
  Restore: map, then layers, then stay-panels (positions, collapsed). Never reopen one-shot dialogs. Work in progress comes
  back through its own owner (draft resolver, recorder). Spec to be drafted with the Map mock.
- Route+ (13:48-13:58): very complex — do NOT take apart. ADD ROUTE passes manual or AI to the EXISTING planning-map Route+
  (all its start-up checks), method locked. Clear leftover routes = the old Settings cleanup, asks first.
- Filter after, not before (search): one box searches everything; result types are the filter.

- HIDE (collapsed HUD + bottom row, expand icon): HELD — decide later
- HELP on old screens: done for every screen touched so far (TOUCHSTD, CLOSEX, CHKINSTD, GTRIDES).

1. BEFORE THE 2.7c RELEASE IS BUILT -- remove the one-time launch code still running every launch:
   StartupHousekeeping.jobCategories -> OwnershipReclass.applyMissingCategories (CATEGORYALWAYS-2026-10-10).
   Rule 3 (09-08): one-time launch code is removed when the next release is cut -- it was not, and shipped in 2.7a and 2.7b.
   What it does: every launch, trails missing category / use / land get them; land keeps any existing value and only a BLANK
   becomes PUBLIC (it never changes PRIVATE). On a converted tablet it is one COUNT.
   Also: add a release-cut check -- list every "rule 3 / NO MARKER / every launch" job before tagging, and remove them.

## 09:27 PUBLIC/PRIVATE ROOT CAUSE -- PROVEN on Droid 1 (P50, serial 8624SBCEDF00001789; the EP103B 24039703201775 had no matching log)
Log, Utah import finished 09:15 (1819 s):
  OwnershipReclass: ownership: 17388 rings, 9436 cells, 11s
  HomeStateImport: OOMGUARD-2026-09-15: step 8 ran out of memory -- treating as skipped
  java.lang.OutOfMemoryError ... 256 MB heap ... at CursorWindow.getString  (reading the trails cursor)
  HomeStateImport: step 8 skipped (no ownership data)      <- WRONG message: it ran out of memory
  HomeStateImport: Home state import COMPLETED for Utah    <- reported as completed
Cause: OwnershipReclass.run reads EVERY trail's geometry (WKT strings) into ArrayLists at once, on top of 17,388 ownership rings -> OOM on the 256 MB heap.
Effect: step 8 writes nothing -- no category, no use, no land for any trail. Trail detail shows no Land. Then on the next launch
  jobCategories (CATEGORYALWAYS-2026-10-10) fills every blank: category, use, and land = PUBLIC. So NO trail is ever PRIVATE.
  Fred's first suspicion (housekeeping moves everything to public) was right in effect: the launch job papers over a step 8 that failed.
  NOT the filter (shared code, ALL vs PUBLIC works on the values it is given).
Fix (2.7c, before the jobCategories removal):
  1. step 8 streams: trails read and written in pages (e.g. 2,000 rows by rowid), rings loaded once; memory bounded.
  2. an OOM / write failure is reported as FAILED on the import panel and in the log -- not "skipped (no ownership data)", not COMPLETED.
  3. a way to re-run land classification alone (no 30-minute re-import) -- for the test and for riders whose step 8 failed.
  4. THEN remove jobCategories (rule 3), and check every converged device carries real land values.
- 09:30 History (git): OOMGUARD 4204d71f6 (09-15 heap guard + OOM backstop, "streaming the read is the fix"), STREAMRINGS 372034976 (09-17 streamed the OWNERSHIP FILE), OWNERSHIPGUARD 2cc52edae (10-10 removed the stale heap pre-check). The TRAILS read was never paged -- today's OOM.
- 09:30 STEP8PAGED-2026-10-23 patch: run() pages 500 rows by rowid (own transaction per page, both stores, uses per page); a failed step 8 = stage "failed", run COMPLETED WITH ERRORS, log "step 8 FAILED: <why>"; Settings > "Classify trails again" runs step 8 alone (N classified, P private, or FAILED). jobCategories stays until proven.
- Build (Fred 09:30): PERSISTKEY + MAPTARGET + PERSISTVIEW + MAPCHIP + STEP8PAGED together. Download Y/N after.

## 16:04 BTECH Relay (from Nathan via Fred) -- a transport candidate for 2.8+
- github.com/darksteal/BTECH-Relay: an ATAK plugin linking BTECH UV-PRO / GMRS-PRO / UV-50X radios to ATAK over Bluetooth SPP + KISS TNC, AX.25 frames, compact binary packets with fragmentation, optional AES-256; PLI, GeoChat, CoT markers / routes, contact age-out, BT auto-reconnect working; voice PTT scaffold. 2 commits. Licence MIT + Commons Clause (commercial sale reserved) -> do not copy code into a paid app without permission; KISS / AX.25 / SPP are open standards -- write our own, use theirs as a guide.
- Fit: UTV riders already carry GMRS radios. 47 CFR 95.1787: GMRS handheld digital data = location (or a request) and brief text, each burst <= 1 s, no more than once per 30 s, integral antenna, not on the 467 MHz main channels -> a GroupTrack position beacon fits; tracks / routes / markers do not. Encryption: not addressed in 95.1787; amateur rules prohibit messages encoded to obscure meaning -> check before any encrypted traffic. Packet modems typically 1200 baud. Needs real radios + distance (January).
- Next: ask Nathan which stack he ran over the UV-Pro and the throughput he saw; log under the 2.8 transport separation beside Meshtastic and the Nucleus IP mesh.

2.7c Move Sequence
GroupTrack 2.7c · drafted 2026-10-22 after the attach session · for Fred's review before the 10-23 work begins
Why this document
Fred, 15:10: "we need a sequence to work with, specifying function and the order they are moved … maps killed us. We have a lot of map options that run only in automated functions — those do not belong on a menu … import maps by corridor is only an automated process … I would identify the functions we are moving and where they were located before, to help us with grouping. Map selection and source belong together."
Bring over as it exists, then restructure. Nothing is redesigned while it is moved (Fred 14:35).
Automated is not a menu item. A function that only runs inside another process (a corridor download after an import, a source refresh) is moved WITH its process and never gets a button.
Prune, then group. Once the complex processes are pulled out of the screens, what is left that a rider actually starts is what gets grouped on the menus.
Map selection and map sources belong together (one group).
Trace before attaching (10-22 lesson): any function that crosses into another screen is traced start → work → complete → cancel → back before it is handed over.
The order
Phase 1 — Persistence in ONE MAP. ONE MAP gets its own state ("grouptrack"); every read/write uses the current map's key; every map's state is captured (view, layers + selections, map type, offline mode, stay-panels). The cold-launch delete goes. Start-up path mapped at the same time.
Phase 2 — Route+ into ONE MAP. The planner's whole route process (row R1–R8 below) hosted on ONE MAP; Add Route launches on the map it is invoked from. Add Route testing here, before anything else moves.
Phase 3 — the planner's rider-started map functions into ONE MAP (rows P1–P10), with the automated pieces they call (rows A1–A6) moving inside them.
Phase 4 — the rest of the ride map into modules (rows M1–M10), so ConvoyScreen holds nothing ONE MAP needs; ConvoyScreen and the planner screen are retired.
Phase 5 — start-up from ONE MAP's persistence. GroupTrack.kt becomes the start screen.
Phase 6 — prune and realign. Remove Map Features and anything now duplicated; regroup the menus from what is left (Map type + Sources together).
Inventory — every function being moved, where it was before
rider starts it automated only — no menu item decision needed
#FunctionWhere it is todayHow it runsMenu?Proposed group (Phase 6)Phase
R1Route+ start-up checks (compare set, leftover AI routes, unnamed draft, in-progress)Planner · Map Features +ROUTEinside Route+noAdd Route2

GroupTrack 2.7c — ONE MAP — THE TARGET (locked 2026-10-21 13:24, Fred)
v2 · 2026-10-21 19:10 (v1 13:29) · v2 = rechecked against the xref of the FROZEN 2.7b (e2f001aed, 19:03): 509 functions — the only change is Send test polyline, removed from Settings (NOTESTBUTTON); still 0 without a home. · Built from the design canvas "GroupTrack One Map — launch layer prototype" (claude.ai artifact 8SH4mp7qiLLuUuFFHQDutx, worked through with Fred 12:15–13:19) and checked against docs/navigation_xref.txt (generated 2026-10-21 19:03, branch 2.7b @ e2f001aed, the frozen 2.7b: 143 panels, 509 clickable functions). Every one of the 509 functions has a home in this target (section 6).
0. As built — 2026-10-22 (v3)
The target below is unchanged; this section records where the build now differs from it, decided on the bench on 10-22 (Fred), and the order for what is left.
Bottom bar: Map · [Add Route ⇄ View] · Rides · Search · Radio Setup (Group only). Add Route is its OWN button (Fred 11:07: "getting to it quickly is key; we do not want to hide a key function between navigation layers") — it left the Rides list. Add Route and View share one slot: Add Route before the ride; View: Group / View: My Cart once checked in or recording (11:19).
Right column centred vertically (11:12): GRP Awareness (its own green / red / grey pulsing box — the in-ride issue indicator, Fred 11:38) · Mode: Group / Android only · Status: Online / Offline · MAP KEY (key icon) · FILTER (funnel) · CENTRE ON ME (bullseye; reads FOLLOWING ME / FOLLOWING GROUP while following; re-centres on its own 15 s after the last touch while recording).
Radio Setup (Group only): Configure radio for rides · Archived radio setups. Rides: View checked-in carts / change roles (first) · Create a ride · Import a ride · My rides.
Readout = today's HUD bottom left (GPS line + MY CART / GROUP).
MAP KEY = styles only (what you are looking at); FILTER = everything on / off, the trail-type definitions live in FILTER (12:25), Hide everything restores what was on, Include private land (public always shows — 09-02).
Search = one box, everything searched, filter after (types as chips), scope In &lt;state ▾&gt; / Everywhere, places online only, opens at the top.
Map = Map type (top) · Map Features (original, to be removed) · Download queues · Map sources · Open the planning map · planner placeholders.
Standard: HELP ✕ top right everywhere; one help viewer.
Order for what is left (Fred 15:02, 15:13): 1 persistence in ONE MAP (third key "grouptrack") · 2 the planner's map functions into ONE MAP (automated pieces move inside their processes, never onto menus) · 3 the rest of the ride map into modules · 4 Route+ LAST (the most intertwined) · 5 start-up from ONE MAP's persistence · 6 prune and realign (Map Features removed; Map type + Sources together). The full move sequence (every function, where it was before, how it runs, phase) is in living master v166 / handoff v72.
1. The decision: freeze 2.7b, and One Map becomes 2.7c
2.7b is frozen in scope (Fred 13:23). It ships once three things are done:
the estimate / gap-fill rule (desk test, then patch);the cleanup patch: remove the POLYTEST test button, fix the duplicate VM listener, fix the COMMHEALTH foreground-service start while the app is in the background;2.7b release notes, manual and Quick Start.
Moved to 2.7c: polyline statistics, reconnect panel v4, and the polyline-dots question. The two-person field test waits for Utah in January (Fred decides whether 2.7b goes to internal testers before it).
Why separate releases:
2.7b changed how positions flow (the tick removed, lead track, gap polyline, trim, estimate); 2.7c changes how riders move around the app. Each needs its own testing and release notes, or a trail problem cannot be traced to one change.2.7c rewrites every lettered control in manual sections 4 and 5.

2. Principles (Fred, 10-18 to 10-21)
One map. The planning map is folded in; the Ride Planning / Back to Ride switches are retired.
A launch layer over the existing features. Each process gets ONE first screen that takes every value it needs (defaults from the ride and settings), then runs to the end with no further screen prompts. The only stop kept is the confirm before something that cannot be undone.
Two layouts. Group adds a lot of complexity and is used by some. Android only is the default; Group adds the Group button, CHECK IN, the GROUP readout, other carts and the lead track. One switch decides which.
Riders ride in landscape and pan in portrait. In landscape, panels open as a side panel so the map stays in view.
Every control shows an icon and its text on an opaque background, readable on any map. No hover, no long-press meanings.
North up only. Leaflet cannot rotate, and Hybrid labels are baked into the imagery (heading-up needs a rotating map engine: not 2.7c).
Show/hide is FILTER, how lines look is KEY: as onX and Gaia do, the filter is on every view.

GroupTrack 2.7c — S1 Screen Inventory — 2026-10-22 v1
GroupTrack 2.7c — S1, the screen inventory (2026-10-22, v1)
What this is: every panel and screen in the app today (navigation_xref.txt, frozen 2.7b @ e2f001aed, 143 panels, 509 clickable functions), grouped by the launch module it will hang from in GroupTrack.kt (Fred 10-22: one module per launch point; the scaffold only calls modules). This is the attach list for the shell. Per panel: where riders reach it today (from the click tree), how it is opened, its clickable count, the inputs it asks for, whether it scrolls, the text colours it uses, and its fate in the 2.7c target. Standards (Fred 10-22): every panel scrolls (landscape breaks panels that cannot); one colour scheme for all panels (decided panel by panel in the reviews); details panels separate facts from actions and hide technical data. NO SCROLL = a long panel (over 120 lines or more than 6 buttons) with no scrolling — it breaks in landscape. Inputs and colours are counted from the code of each panel's own function; panels that call helper panels may ask for more.

GroupTrack — Quick Start
Rel 2.7b · install and set up, practise on the two maps — and add a radio to experience full group awareness while riding: no new software, nothing to learn. Every section points you to the User Manual for the detail.
GroupTrack is complete as installed — trails and maps that work with no signal, a planner that builds routes for you, and your own track recordings.New: ★ Create a Ride. One ride holds the route, the trailhead, the date and time, the maps to download and the mesh radio configuration. Send it in one click; your friends open it in one click — and ride anywhere off grid in total confidence.
Add a radio to experience full group awareness while riding — no new software, nothing to learn: everyone on the map, with no cell service. GroupTrack is two products in one: a complete personal navigation product that lets you share rides and maps with other GroupTrack users, and a true situational awareness product for your group on the trail. (About GroupTrack)
Coming in 2.7c: One Map. The ride map and the planning map become one map, with every tool reached from the buttons around its edge. While it is being finished you can try it in Settings › Layout › One Map; these exercises still describe the two maps until 2.7c is released. (What is in 2.7c so far)
★ Before every ride: send the ride invite to every rider. Everyone on the ride needs the same ride. Send the ride invite to every GroupTrack rider joining you — and make sure each one opens it and imports it before the ride. The ride brings the route, the trailhead and the maps. Without it, a rider sees carts as dots on an empty map and has nothing to follow. It matters even with no radio: a rider who has imported the ride can follow the route on their own tablet, and stays on course far more easily. (Sending a ride)
How to use this. Each section says in a paragraph what something is, with a link to its chapter in the User Manual. The exercises under it are short practice tasks — each links to the manual section that explains it in full. Open the manual any time from Help.
1 · Install, and first start
GroupTrack keeps your trails, tracks, routes and downloaded maps in its own storage on the device. Nothing you do here puts files anywhere else, and you are not asked for access to your phone's folders.
If you are updating from an older version, the first launch moves your existing data across for you — follow the prompt and leave the screen open while it works.
Grant the app the authorities it needs — location, all the time.
Follow the prompts.
Fill in your rider profile — your callsign and email. GroupTrack asks once, before the map opens.Answer the radio question — Do you have a mesh radio to use with GroupTrack? YES: switch the radio on; GRP Awareness opens — connect it, then Select a ride and apply settings to the radio → GroupTrack default. Pairing code 123456 unless your radio shows another. NO: do it later in GRP Awareness, before your first ride. New in 2.7b: the question becomes Will you use a Meshtastic radio to see your group on the map? — YES, I HAVE A RADIO / NO, THIS TABLET ONLY (group awareness off; switch it on any time in Settings → Group awareness).
Choose your home state and let it download the trails, so they work with
no signal.
When the app loads your location, you are ready to play.
That is the whole of it. The detail below is worth reading when you have a
moment — none of it is needed to get going.
Loading the trails for your home state
On first launch GroupTrack asks for location, then asks which
state you ride in and offers the one it thinks you are in.
Pick your home state and load the trail data.
Pick your state and let it run. It takes about twenty minutes and
pulls a lot of data, so do it on wifi. It is not something to start at the
trailhead.
What it is fetching, and why it takes that long: GroupTrack does not use one
trail map. It pulls from every public source that covers your state and
merges them, so a trail one agency published and another did not still appears.
For Utah that is seven catalogues plus the OpenStreetMap extract:
Utah Trails and Pathways — the state's own trail record
US Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management,
National Park Service, USGS National Trails — the federal
agencies that manage the ground
Arizona State Parks — border coverage
OpenStreetMap — the largest single source, and the one that carries
tracks and unclassified roads the agencies do not list
Another state draws on a different set. The app picks the sources that cover
the area you asked for.
It also downloads the land ownership record for your state, which is
what lets it tell public ground from private.
When it finishes you get a summary listing every source and what came in.
It waits for you — if you put the tablet down and come back later, it is still
there. ⚠ If a line says a source failed, the rest still loaded; you can reload
the state later from the same place.
Choosing what appears on the map
GroupTrack holds around 146,000 trails for Utah. Most of what is in that
number is ground you will never ride — footpaths, residential streets, cycle
paths through town. Choosing what appears is how the map becomes readable.
Map Features › Trails › SELECT — choose which kinds of trail appear.
What you get out of the box
GroupTrack starts by showing motorized trails on public land only.
Hiking, biking and equestrian trails are hidden, and so is private ground.
⚠ If a trail you know exists is not on the map, that is why — not a
fault. It is a deliberate choice for an off-road app, and it is the first thing
worth knowing.
Changing it
Map Features › Trails › SELECT. The same button you use to choose
which tracks, waypoints or routes appear.
Include private land — one tick. Near a town this is what removes the
residential street grid, which is usually why a map is hard to read there.
The trail types, in two columns: motorized and non-motorized. Tap a
row to hide that type; tap a column heading for the whole group.
And OFF on the Trails row hides every trail in one tap, for when you
want to see the ground.
Not sure what a category is?
Press CATEGORIES EXPLAINED at the foot of the Map Keys panel. It
says what each trail type actually means — which are posted for machines,
which are open unless a sign says otherwise, and which came from your own
rides.
The colours are yours
Whatever you set is what the map draws, every time you open it. You do not need to visit the key panel again for your choices to take effect.
Solid lines are motorized. Dotted lines are not. That is the
distinction worth learning, and it is one you can read in sunlight without
picking colours apart.
Tap Map Keys to see what each line means, and tap any name in that
list to change its colour, pattern or thickness. It shows the line as it is
beside the line as it would be, so you can compare before committing. What you
choose is saved.
Your rider profile
Your profile — your callsign and your email — is who you are in GroupTrack. Your callsign is your name on every map and in every report your radio sends; your email is how rides reach you. It is private: it stays on your tablet, and goes only to the riders you ride with. GroupTrack asks for it the first time it opens; change it any time in Settings → Your Profile.
Manual: Your rider profileOpening your first ride
The first time you tap a ride someone sent you, Android asks which app should open it: choose GroupTrack, then Always. The route, trailhead and waypoints arrive, and the maps along the route start downloading. If ride files open somewhere else: Android Settings → Apps → GroupTrack → Open by default → Clear defaults, then tap the file again.
Manual: Sending a ride, and getting one
Updating from 2.6?
Three one-time steps — your rider profile, updating your radio once, and opening ride files with GroupTrack — are in the release notes: Updating from 2.6.
★ Create your first ride — new in 2.7aRiding together starts with a ride. GroupTrack's community begins with the ride package — a route, starting at its defined trailhead, on a set date and time, with the maps it needs and its radio configuration. Send it to friends and riders who want to ride with you.One click, and everyone has the same preparation: the trailhead marked on their map, the route outlined to follow, the required maps downloaded along it. At the trailhead, check-in applies the ride's radio configuration for them. The fastest way to create one is a map touch: tap a route or a track on the Ride Planning Map, then CREATE RIDE — Manual: Map touches, the fastest way to Create a Ride.No more night before the ride spent downloading an area and hoping the trail goes where you think it does. No one asks where to meet, and no one waits at the trailhead while someone else catches up. Everyone's time goes to riding.Create a ride and send itOn the Ride Planning Map, tap a route. A route the planner built opens its description — tap CREATE RIDE; a route you drew opens its details — tap ADD A RIDE. (From a track you recorded: tap it, then CREATE RIDE.)The ride form opens with the route, its trailhead and its picture. Set the date and time, fill in the rest, SAVE RIDE.Work with Rides → Rides, tap your ride, Share — the invite goes to your riding partners.Manual: ★ Create a Ride · Sending a ride, and getting one
2 · Exercises — the Ride Planning Map
What a ride is
A ride is everything a group needs to ride together, in one package: the route and its trailhead, waypoints, the maps for riding off grid, and the radio settings for the ride's network. The organizer builds it on a route — or a track they rode — and sends it as a Ride invite. Each rider — any GroupTrack user — taps it: GroupTrack creates the route, its trailhead and the ride's description on the tablet, and imports the maps needed to ride it off grid. Then they ride; with a radio, riders also check in at the trailhead.
Manual: The Ride — what are its components, and what does it mean to me?
The map you use at home, online, before you go: find the ground, build a route or let the planner build one, mark waypoints, download the maps you will need, and create and send rides. Every control is lettered on the picture in its chapter.

4 · Group awareness
Add a radio to experience full group awareness while riding — no new software, nothing to learn. Your community comes onto the trail with you. Group awareness is seeing your group on the map with no cell service — every cart where it is, with its callsign and role. It needs a Meshtastic radio for each rider; GroupTrack works with any Meshtastic radio and sets it up for you. Checking in to a ride puts your radio on the ride's network and announces your role — the check-in is part of group awareness: riding solo, you never see its screens. Riding alone? Skip this section.

Lessons:
Compare a good startup log with a bad one FIRST (Fred 20:43): we had a recording of every install and still chased radios and configs. Tonight's 20:3x install is the recorded known-good startup.
A collector started in init runs at once on the main thread — everything it touches must be declared above init (the 12:14 crash).
A crash loop during Meshtastic's connect leaves half-open Bluetooth links — a plausible cause of the afternoon's Bluetooth trouble.
Never reason past evidence: every theory today that was not checked against the log was wrong at least in part (second app = Android's own service; "recovery ran before the first connect" — it did not).
Our own red message caused damage: it told the rider to Forget while the radio had just started talking.
Read the right tablet: with two plugged in every adb command uses -s &lt;serial&gt;.

A. Connection / recovery (the END-TO-END RECOVERY DESIGN)

Lessons:
Change ONE thing at a time. Rolling back the code AND rebooting together hid which one cured it; it took a bisect to separate them.
Contaminated devices prove nothing. Once Bluetooth was stuck, every later install failed whatever its code — re-establish a clean baseline (reboot) before testing a suspect. Claude wrongly "cleared" DISCPANEL at 12:09 from a contaminated test; Fred caught it.
Android refuses a lower version code silently in deploy.sh. To test older code without uninstalling (which wipes maps, rides and settings): a test branch with git revert (version code goes UP), then git merge -s ours back so the main branch stays above it.
Git Bash rewrites /sdcard/… into a Windows path — use //sdcard/… with adb shell. git log opens a pager — use git --no-pager log (or press q).
Kotlin extension functions need an import (animateFloat) — a fully-qualified call does not reach them.
Patch anchors with escapes: the file writer turned \u00b7 into a literal ·; the patch aborted cleanly. Check written patches for escaped characters.
Self-tripping post-checks, third time (REPORTNOW's comment named the very token it forbade) — word marker comments to avoid forbidden tokens.

⭐⭐⭐ GroupTrack 2.7c — ONE MAP — THE TARGET (locked 2026-10-21 13:24, Fred)
v1 · 2026-10-21 · Built from the design canvas "GroupTrack One Map — launch layer prototype" (claude.ai artifact 8SH4mp7qiLLuUuFFHQDutx, worked through with Fred 12:15–13:19) and checked against docs/navigation_xref.txt (generated 2026-10-20 17:14, branch 2.7b @ c176d4026: 143 panels, 510 clickable functions). Every one of the 510 functions has a home in this target (section 6).
1. The decision: freeze 2.7b, and One Map becomes 2.7c
2.7b is frozen in scope (Fred 13:23). It ships once three things are done:
the estimate / gap-fill rule (desk test, then patch);the cleanup patch: remove the POLYTEST test button, fix the duplicate VM listener, fix the COMMHEALTH foreground-service start while the app is in the background;2.7b release notes, manual and Quick Start.
Moved to 2.7c: polyline statistics, reconnect panel v4, and the polyline-dots question. The two-person field test waits for Utah in January (Fred decides whether 2.7b goes to internal testers before it).
Why separate releases:
2.7b changed how positions flow (the tick removed, lead track, gap polyline, trim, estimate); 2.7c changes how riders move around the app. Each needs its own testing and release notes, or a trail problem cannot be traced to one change.2.7c rewrites every lettered control in manual sections 4 and 5.
2.7c phaseWhatEstimate (not a commitment)
S1Inventory: confirm each launch point and the chain it opens today (this document is the starting list)1 day
1 · ShellThe new layout on both maps (control placement, two layouts, panels, KEY, FILTER, INTERNET, readout, distance, queue badge, landscape). Panel items first open TODAY&#x27;S screens. Test: every row of section 6 is reachable.1–2 weeks

DocsManual sections 4 and 5 rewritten to this layout2–3 days
Total ≈ 6–9 weeks at the current pace; phase 4 is the least certain.
2. Principles (Fred, 10-18 to 10-21)
One map. The planning map is folded in; the Ride Planning / Back to Ride switches are retired.
A launch layer over the existing features. Each process gets ONE first screen that takes every value it needs (defaults from the ride and settings), then runs to the end with no further screen prompts. The only stop kept is the confirm before something that cannot be undone.
Two layouts. Group adds a lot of complexity and is used by some. Android only is the default; Group adds the Group button, CHECK IN, the GROUP readout, other carts and the lead track. One switch decides which.
Riders ride in landscape and pan in portrait. In landscape, panels open as a side panel so the map stays in view.
Every control shows an icon and its text on an opaque background, readable on any map. No hover, no long-press meanings.
North up only. Leaflet cannot rotate, and Hybrid labels are baked into the imagery (heading-up needs a rotating map engine: not 2.7c).
Show/hide is FILTER, how lines look is KEY: as onX and Gaia do, the filter is on every view.

5. Found by the cross-reference: functions the prototype did not show, and their homes
MENU › Settings › Storage &amp; data: Remove all trail data · Resync tracks · Add trails from tracks (from Settings, the track import screen and the RiderTrails dialog).
MENU › Settings › Diagnostics: Check a trail · Ride statistics · Conversion record (from Settings and the old ride-config menu).
Map › Map sources: change a source (clear or keep tiles: the migrate gate) and rebuild a source (MAP RECOVERY / recreate slot).
Map › Download for offline: show what you hold / what is coming, and remove tiles from an area.
Rides › Create a route: drafts in progress (resume, rename, roll back, delete, the unnamed-draft resolver), ROUTE DETAILS notes, CREATE TRAILHEAD at save, the planner's Review / Compare and saving the compare set.
Tap a feature: rename, change type, delete, fit, aliases, Create a ride; tracks add SHARE (the track export sheet).
Record button: the automatic-pause banner (CONTINUE), the ROLE CONFLICT banner, the lead question when no Leader is known (decide in phase 2).
Unchanged in 2.7c: Android permission prompts, the startup online/offline chooser, sign-in, terms and privacy gates, the V3 account and organizer screens, the developer menu.

A. THE ESTIMATE AND GAP-FILL RULE (Fred 10-20 17:15&ndash;17:18). It supersedes the earlier route &rarr; saved route &rarr; trails &rarr; straight line chain.
What was seen (Fred 10-20 last test): the lead was not heard. The radio marker did not move after the last-heard marker was dropped, even though the lead was on a track that ran on to a trail.
Fred's words: "there is a track and a trail. should we not move at least until&hellip; intersection junction?" and "our rule was use the route only if it is the only route on the current map. in lieu of the route it should be tracks and or trails." He confirmed the same rule applies to the gap fill.
CaseThe silent-lead ESTIMATE followsThe GAP FILL (between two heard points) follows
Exactly ONE route on the current mapThat route, in its direction (as built)That route
No route, or more than one routeThe track or trail the lead was on. It moves along it and stops at the next junction, never guessing a branchThe track or trail the lead was on, joined through a junction only when the next heard point is past it
Not on any track or trailHolds at the last-heard point (as now)A straight line (a polyline replaces it when one arrives)
Saved routes (not displayed)REMOVED from both. A saved route the lead's points happen to lie on is no longer used.
Status: agreed and not built. Method: desk test first, as with the trim. Replay the 10-20 Long Fast logs through the rule, then patch. The work is in TrackRules / LeadEstimate (the estimate route source, estRouteNow()) and in the gap-fill chain in TrackWriter. Callers are untouched.
Still Fred's call: whether polyline points show as dots when no route is displayed.
B. 10-21: WHAT WAS DONE ON THE NUCLEUS (node 46, V3-OS 0.11.0), through Droid 1 on its Wi-Fi, using only Nathan's tools
Factory config saved first, in ~/Downloads/natak46/ (factory_*.json, openapi_0.11.0.json, bridge logs). The keyed originals are private and never go on Drive or git. Scrubbed copies are on Drive GroupTrack/natak46/.
Radio put on GroupTrack through HIS API with nucleus_radio_grouptrack_2026-10-21.py. It does a preview, then --apply or --restore, via adb push and nc on Droid 1. It changed MEDIUM_FAST, channel GroupTrack, slot 0 and the key, through POST /api/v1/meshtastic/config/apply. The read-back matched, and the key fingerprint (psk_fingerprint = first 8 hex of SHA-256 of the key) was verified. --restore puts back his factory Natak link and SHORT_FAST.
Proven:
  LoRa works both ways between node 46 and a T1000-E: 46 heard ours at SNR 11, and a text from 46 reached our rider.
  Wi-Fi &rarr; LoRa works: a CoT from Droid 1 went out as a 52-byte ATAK packet ("TX &rarr; LoRa | GT-wifi-test-1").
  Port 72 is NOT bridged to Wi-Fi. cot_bridge keeps only 257, text, voice and heartbeat.
His API:
  Base address http://10.20.46.1/api/v1/&hellip;, no authentication.
  0.11.0 has no heartbeat endpoint.
  The tx_min_interval_secs rate limit was added by Nathan on 09-24.
  The full spec is at /openapi.json.

C. 10-21: WHAT WAS DECIDED AFTERWARDS. It supersedes the proposal v9 and email 1 where they differ.
TopicDecision (Fred 10-21)Why
Message standardStay on the Meshtastic V1 standard: positions and role reports as TAKPacket on port 72, as the T1000-Es and GroupTrack already send. GroupTrack does NOT move to 257. Email 1 said it would, and that is corrected in email v3.Stock ATAK/iTAK users on any Meshtastic radio, with the plugin, read V1 on 72 directly. Port 78 (V2) exists only in 2.8, which is alpha. 257 carrying TAKPacketV2 is Nathan's own choice, and only his bridge reads it. Format and port go together: 72 = V1, 78 = V2. V1 on 78 would be discarded.
Gap polylineStays V2 on port 78, uncompressed (0xFF), GroupTrack to GroupTrack only. No polyline in ATAK/iTAK ("we do not need polylines in ATAK"). The ask to Nathan for polyline &rarr; CoT is dropped.Both ends are GroupTrack, and the radios relay any port without reading it. That is why it works today on 2.6.11. Nathan's bridge ignores 78, so ATAK never sees it.
Port 257Nathan's only. It is how his Wi-Fi riders reach LoRa (CoT &rarr; 257, as built). GroupTrack only READS 257. Nothing of ours goes on 257.Fred's "256" in an earlier message meant 257. Port 256 is Nathan's voice port.
Radio firmwareNo firmware update. The fleet stays on 2.6.11 (TAK_TRACKER &rarr; port 72).2.8.x is Alpha/Revoked only; 2.7.26 is the latest Beta. The first 2.8.0 build was revoked for T1000-E LR1110 start-up failures. #11607: TAK_TRACKER position reports stop after 10&ndash;15 min on 2.8.0, fix unconfirmed. Discussion #8724: T1000-E send/receive breaks after 2.7.15. 2.8 also defaults to LongTurbo, takes node IDs from the public key (our uid basis), turns position and telemetry off by default, and changes nRF52 storage (full erase). A bench test on Billy beans waits for a 2.8 Beta.
The NucleusPaused. Starlink and the internet link are removed (off grid). Ten bare radios do everything ten Nucleus units do for GroupTrack, and for ATAK/iTAK users with a radio. The Pi adds only Wi-Fi for radio-less ATAK users near its cart, the internet link, and voice. S00104 at $430 is not justified per cart; the bare radio at ~$100 (+$50 optional power) is the ask.All cart-to-cart work is LoRa. Nucleus Wi-Fi range does not cover a spread-out group. His default SHORT_FAST is shorter range than our MEDIUM_FAST. Range comes from the radio (the 1 W module plus external antenna), not the Pi.
Wi-Fi (IP) instead of BluetoothBluetooth stays. Wi-Fi is not shown to be more reliable. ESP32-class bare radio requested only as an option.Meshtastic documentation:
"Enabling Wi-Fi will disable Bluetooth" (one or the other);
"SoftAP mode is not supported" (the radio cannot be the hotspot);
reports of ESP32 Wi-Fi drops after 1&ndash;2 h, about 20% loss (old 1.3 firmware);
TCP is the secondary transport on Android.
An Android hotspot without a SIM or internet varies by device (missing on Wi-Fi-only tablets). A local-only hotspot gets a random name and password each start, which a radio cannot store. Check: Droid 1 and Droid 2 in airplane mode with Wi-Fi on &rarr; does Hotspot switch on? If a fixed network is ever needed, a USB travel router costs far less than a Pi.
Starlink later?If an off-ride view is ever wanted, the lead's GroupTrack tablet is the gateway: the mesh by radio plus the internet by Starlink Wi-Fi, forwarding to a TAK server or AWS. No Pi.Every cart's position reaches the lead over LoRa.

E. 2.7b APPLICATION SIMPLIFICATION: remove screens, let the processes take their parts as input (Fred 10-18 direction; tasks set out 10-21 12:01)
Fred 10-21: remove screens, "letting functions take parts as input so screens are not called back to back", "moving data to the launch screen", and "running processes without further screen prompts".
Fred 10-18: the app is overwhelmingly complex, and navigation must be simplified. Take the screens out of processes and move their value forward to the processes that call them, so we are not nesting six layers deep. Each flow executes one task. Separate the prompt screen from a parameter-driven process. Simplification follows the tick removal ("we will have tamed the app"), and the tick is now gone.
The rule each flow must meet:
ONE launch screen collects everything the task needs, with defaults pre-filled from the ride or settings.
It hands those values to a process function as parameters.
The process runs to the end with no further screen prompts.
A process never opens another screen to get a value; that value is a parameter or a default.
The only allowed stop is a confirmation before something destructive or irreversible.
No screen-to-screen chains.
TaskWhatHow / output
S1 InventoryEvery function that shows a screen, panel or dialog, and who calls it. Find every chain where a screen or process opens another screen, with its depth (the "six layers").The function references (function universe / where-used, the navxref tool) &rarr; a table: flow, launch screen, chain of screens, depth, the values each intermediate screen collects. Desk work only, no code change. Comes first.
S2 Split prompt from processFor each chain, pull the work out of the screens into a process function that takes its parts (parameters) as input.Process functions callable with no UI: testable, and reusable from a check-in, a ride package or another process.
S3 Move the data forwardThe values the intermediate screens collected move to the launch screen, or to defaults from the ride or settings. The intermediate screens are removed.One launch screen per task. Fewer screens in total.
S4 Order of workThe deepest and most-used chains first. One flow per patch, bench-tested before the next (as with the tick removal).The S1 table ranked by depth &times; use.
S5 ReadabilityThe text navigation line (Search, Map Features, Map Keys, Group Help, GRP Awareness, Work with Rides) is hard to read over some maps. The colour choices on the artifact detail panels.Contrast that holds on every basemap (satellite, red rock, topo).
S6 Side menuOne button slides a panel out with the navigation options, and the panel closes once an option is chosen. It replaces the text line.Fred's idea (10-18 19:37).
S7 Compare onX and GaiaHow they keep navigation flat.A short comparison to guide S3 and S6.
Also still open at the back of 2.7b: the radio-setup timeout on a delayed reboot (Wio Tracker). It reads like the phantom connection that spoils the reconnect.
F. 2.7b NAVIGATION, VISIBILITY, LOOK AND FEEL (Fred 10-21 12:04). Ideas taken from onX and Gaia. Plain labelled controls: no complex icons, no hover-for-text. Expands E's S5&ndash;S7.
Fred 10-21: "navigation and visibility improvements in app improving navigation and look and feel. reference onX and Gaia for conceptual ideas. staying away from complex or hover over icons for text".
Why no hover: a touch screen has no hover. In a moving cart, with gloves, vibration and sun glare, an icon whose meaning needs a long press or a tooltip will not be read.
What onX and Gaia do (concepts only, nothing copied):
The map is the home screen. onX: "Most of the tools you'll use live in the bottom toolbar". There are only a few controls along the top and the right side.
One location button with two states. onX: the first tap centres the map north-up, the second tap switches to heading-up.
Layers and basemap behind one button that opens a sheet. Both apps do this. Offline maps are reached from the same place in Gaia.
One big primary-action button. Gaia uses a large green "+" at the bottom right for its most common task.
A unified icon set, refined colours, fonts and layouts. This was the core of Gaia's redesign, made to make backcountry navigation simpler.
Account, settings and help sit in a main menu, off the map.
TaskWhatRule / output
V1 Navigation barReplace the hard-to-read text navigation line (Search, Map Features, Map Keys, Group Help, GRP Awareness, Work with Rides) with a short bar of 4&ndash;5 items. Each item is an icon with its text label always shown. Everything else goes in one menu: Fred's slide-out side menu (S6), which closes once an option is chosen.No more than one level of menu. Fred decides what goes in the bar and what goes in the menu.
V2 Readable on any mapEvery control and its label sits on an opaque background (a chip or panel with an edge), never as bare text over the map.Readable on satellite, red rock and topo. This fixes S5.
V3 Big touch targetsButtons sized for a moving cart and gloves, well above the phone minimum, with space between them.Size set once and used everywhere.
V4 One lookOne colour palette (built around the bright blue #1E88FF already used for the tracks), one type scale readable in sun, one simple icon set. The colours on the artifact detail panels are brought into line.Written down once as the GroupTrack style and used on every screen.
V5 Location buttonOne button: tap = centre north-up, tap again = heading-up. Shown as an icon with a label of its state.From onX.
V6 One primary actionOne large button for the task a rider does most (for example REC / start the ride). Fred names it.From Gaia.
V7 One layers buttonMap Features, Map Keys and the basemap choice behind one button that opens one sheet.Fewer items in the bar.
V8 Mock-ups firstA picture of the main map screen (the bar, menu, buttons, colours) for Fred to review before any code. Then one screen per patch, bench-tested.Done together with E: the S1 inventory shows which screens survive.
The rules for every control:
no icon without a visible label;
no meaning that only appears on long press or hover;
no bare text over the map;
no second-level menus;
the same control looks and behaves the same on every screen.
Sources (10-21): onX support, "Interactive Tutorial and Controls"; UTV Driver, "Gaia GPS Gets a Key Redesign"; Bikepacking.com, "New Gaia GPS".
G. 2.7b ONE MAP: the launch layer, designed with Fred 10-21 12:15&ndash;13:19 as a clickable prototype. It supersedes E's S5&ndash;S7 and F's V1&ndash;V8 where they differ.
Prototype (non-functional, it only navigates): design canvas "GroupTrack One Map &mdash; launch layer prototype" (claude.ai artifact 8SH4mp7qiLLuUuFFHQDutx). Boards:
landscape tablet 1280&times;800, Android only and Group;
portrait, both layouts;
a coverage table;
a screens-removed table (both tables are from the first pass; refresh pending).
Every first screen has MANUAL, which shows the v61 manual text behind it.
Principles (Fred):
One map: the planning map is folded in, and the Ride Planning / Back to Ride switches are retired.
A launch layer over the existing features: each process gets one first screen that takes all its values, then runs without further prompts.
Most riders ride in landscape and pan in portrait.
Group adds a lot of complexity and is used by some, so two layouts: Android only (the default) and Group.

The gap polyline (POLYLINE-2026-10-20) -- the design as built
Lead side (GroupTrack): dead air = the time the LEAD hears NO other cart (one cart heard = the hops relay to the rest). After &ge; 60 s of it (Fred 14:45: "a good even number" = six broadcasts), the first report heard from another cart sends ONE polyline: 20 points at equal time steps across [last heard .. heard again] from the lead's own radio fixes (option 1), plus one repeat at the next report heard &ge; 10 s later. Fewer than 2 own fixes in the window = nothing sent (logged). The lead = checked in as Leader, or the cart locked as lead at REC. Pop-up "Gap polyline sent: m:ss of dead air".
Receive, three layers (Fred 14:27 -- keep GroupTrack's message out of the mesh layer): core/data TakShapeInbox (NEW, generic: ANY TAK drawn shape, no GroupTrack knowledge; POLYTEST's GtPolylineInbox retired -- renamed *.removed_POLYLINE-2026-10-20, uncommitted, delete at clean-up) &rarr; comm layer MeshCommMessaging recognises u-d-f + uid GT-gap- &rarr; CommEvent.PolylineReceived (NEW, additive) &rarr; GroupTrack onGapPolylineReceived: pop-up; the LEAD's polyline with REC on &rarr; TrackEntry.Poly &rarr; LeadCartProcess.onGapPolyline &rarr; TrackWriter.pin. The repeat is recognised (sender + start) and not applied twice.
Pin (Fred 14:02-14:04, 14:47): the polyline REPLACES -- never a second line. Kept: the lead track up to the LAST REAL point heard before the window; removed: everything inferred after it; the 20 points joined in order by the fill rules (displayed route &rarr; known tracks &rarr; saved routes &rarr; trails &rarr; straight); the reconnect point joined to the first real point after the window; everything after stays. A point more than 50 m off the displayed route (or off every known line near it) is a DOT, never joined ("one point off turns the path into angles").
Radio setup: rebroadcast mode = ALL is now managed at check-in (written + verified: 25 checks); NONE / CORE_PORTNUMS_ONLY would stop relaying or drop TAK.
Desk test: LF loop 10,845 m pinned vs 10,768 m real (4 dots); afternoon 10,954 vs 11,115 (2 dots).
Road test 15:30-15:47 (Droid 1 leading the loop, Droid 2 parked): Droid 2 last heard the lead 15:29:01; the lead's own dead air 15:30:19 &rarr; 15:36:18 = 359 s; sent 15:36:18 (20 points, 202 bytes), received 2.1 s later (the clock difference within that), pinned with 10 of 20 as dots; repeat 15:36:38 recognised. All 20 points lie on the road Droid 1 drove (19 within 0-2 m, 1 at 22 m between fixes). The 10 dots = where this afternoon's loop left this morning's saved tracks (7 points 66-168 m from them; no route displayed) -- the rule worked as written; proposal (Fred to decide): with NO route displayed, a polyline point joins straight (it is the lead's real position).
The trim (TRIM-2026-10-20) -- my cart replaces the lead track behind me
Fred 14:49-14:56: "rather than overlay it replaces"; "any lead cart point behind my cart ... trimmed at the next my-track write"; BY TIME, not geometry ("we had problems with these rules in twists"); all times UTC epoch ms (Arizona &rarr; Utah is a time-zone change -- local time would wreak havoc).
Each MY-CART position (the feed that moves my icon -- tablet GPS, or my radio without a chip): the first lead-track SEGMENT within 50 m of my cart, searching FORWARD ONLY from the last cut; on to the next segment only while my cart is level with the joint (twists); DRIVING ORDER -- the cut moves no further along the lead's line than my cart has driven since the last cut (+150 m; steps &ge; 5 m, jitter is not driving). The DISPLAY is cut at that segment's start, by time; the written lead track stays whole (fills, pins, other carts' off-track). Polyline pins are trimmed the same way.
Desk test (TrimSim, Droid 1's real fixes lf / est / range, follower 30 s .. 20 min behind, my-cart updates every 3 / 6 / 10 s -- 45 runs): never skipped ground; the cut at most ~60 m ahead of my cart (where the lead was parked); at most one lead segment behind (&le; 435 m on these fixes; shorter with route fill). Two failures found and fixed on the way: point matching jumped 10 km to an out-and-back's return leg (fixes ~160 m apart at speed) &rarr; segments; a parked follower was cut to the lead's return home after a 10 km loop &rarr; driving order. A chipless tablet (6 s radio fixes) trims the same (Fred's concern, 16:04).
Road: Fred 15:47 "the trim definitely worked"; the log cut repeatedly from 15:42 (36 &rarr; 33 segments and on).

What the logs and the code proved today (evidence, not theory)
The tablet GPS chip needs about 5 minutes of open sky for its first lock (Unisoc chip; no SIM, no Wi-Fi assist). Log: fixStatus=A/V, num_svs. Recording works once it has locked (13:20 run). Not a defective chip (my wrong claim this morning, withdrawn).
The second stream of my cart on other tablets was our own role report (every 30 s, it carried my cart's position = the tablet's since ONEFEED). Fred: "check the logs" -- they showed it. Fixed by ROLEPOS.
Sleep 84 s after REC (Droid 2): REC at 11:11:50 in the same app process as the 10:48 recording &rarr; the sleep clock still held the earlier time &rarr; "no movement for 25 min" at the first points (11:13:14). A recording that ended asleep also left every new point dropped. Fixed by RECSLEEP.
The z0 / white screen: every restart that restored the saved frame was followed ~2.5 s later by a zero-size view at 43.06888777, -71.71875 -- exactly my cart rounded to one pixel at ZOOM 0 -- then the whole world. Leaflet's fitBounds works the zoom out from the map's size; called before the map has a size it picks zoom 0. setView (given its zoom) never did this. Offline there are no z0 tiles = white. The saved frames themselves were good (my first theory, a 0,0,0,0 saved frame, was wrong). Only ONE place restores the ride map from the saved file (start-up, ConvoyScreen ~964 + drawPersistedState); FIT uses the database's own bounds. Fixed by FITSIZE + MAPSTARTUP.

Cart positions (other carts and my cart) are already off the tick
(board, received CoT messages; OWNTAKPOS makes my radio's own position readable). The tick's drawing of the lead track goes with the tick, and my track has never been drawn
live — so both tracks are written new, as isolated callable modules, with placeholders for the parts that come in later builds.
ModuleWhat it doesBuild 1Later
TrackPath (plain Kotlin, no Android — testable alone)previous point + new point + map context (loaded route, nearby trails) → the points to draw between them, the snapped location of the new point, and the rule used: ROUTE · TRAIL · STRAIGHT · WAIT.
Order: ROUTE (both points within 50 m of the loaded route → path along the route) → TRAIL (nearest trail within the snap distance → path along it; at a junction WAIT until the next point BEYOND the junction is received — never guess a branch) → STRAIGHT.
STRAIGHT works; ROUTE and TRAIL are placeholders that answer "not applicable" and log itbuild 3 ROUTE filled · build 4 TRAIL + junction wait — inside the module only, callers untouched
CartMotiona received message → the path from TrackPath split into N one-second steps; the cart icon (and the drawn track) advance each second so carts move steadily. Goal (Fred 07:58): the mapping progress COMPLETES BEFORE THE NEXT UPDATE arrives; after a long silence (e.g. 2 min) there will be a jump — accepted.
placeholder = the full gap in ONE step (Fred 08:06: today's behaviour)build 5 stepping
CartMotion rules (proposed 07:56, taken as agreed 07:58): the steps are display-only — not stored as track points, never sent, no last-heard or status change, not used for off-track or the 50 m passed rule (only real reports count);
catch-up from the last real point to the new one, never projected ahead (consistent with "wait for real fixes"); N = the cart's NORMAL report interval so the steps finish before the next expected report (observed radios ~20 s, configured 6 s / 30 s);
a report that arrives early continues from wherever the icon is. The stepping is a short job per received message, not a standing timer. Separate NON-software task: maximise cart broadcast distance to shrink the dead spots (preset MEDIUM_FAST vs LONG_FAST, antenna placement).
The lead track (Fred 10-17 22:27–10-18 07:44):
Built — the same on every tablet: from the LEAD CART's own positions only; when he is quiet it ends at his last known position — no stand-ins (the proxy snap stays killed). ONE lead track whoever leads: old points stay as assigned, new points come only from the current leader, a lead change CONTINUES the track (replaces "a lead change starts a new line"). Every real point kept.
Lead new position = the route/trail location of the point (TrackPath's snapped location) + the track line to it (Fred 08:06).
Signal Drop: the track WAITS for a real fix (no projected points); then the gap last-known → current is drawn over the route if loaded, else over the trail(s), else straight (TrackPath).
Shown — per tablet: the purpose is the lead's path AHEAD of me, to his last point. Lead-track points my cart has PASSED are removed from the display on my tablet (kept in the data): PASSED = my cart within 50 m of the point; that point and every earlier one hidden. My cart is always drawn over the track.
Off-track: unchanged — OFF_TRACK_MILES from Settings, measured when THAT cart's own position arrives.
T7 (after the tick): the lead cart's position = the LAST POINT of the lead's polyline; the 2-minute polyline replaces the tail broadcast.

Time (Fred 10-18 08:08 → 08:09): times are a DURATION from ride initiation (REC pressed) — elapsed time is meaningful and consistent across tablets and time zones. Underneath, every message carries its UTC epoch time; elapsed = message epoch − ride-start epoch. TrackPath / CartMotion / the board never use a tablet's local clock time (Droid 2 runs on Utah time, so its logs read 2 h behind; its epoch time is the same). Ride start = each tablet's own REC press (Fred 08:11). RECEIVED-ACTIVITY RECORD (Fred 08:14 → 08:16): each tablet writes a detail file of the activity it RECEIVES — for every received report of every cart: the cart, the time received, the elapsed time since this tablet's REC, the message's own time, the location (and speed / course when sent). It is the source for the metrics later and for CartMotion's steady segments (each cart's normal report interval). Right now it only RECORDS the data — no broadcast change, no calculations (distance, metrics) yet. Format (Fred 08:17–08:20): a separate ride detail JSON beside the track file (&lt;track&gt;_ride_detail.json), held in memory by cart, written at END and when the app goes to the background (event, not timer). It holds RECEIVED reports only — my tablet's own GPS points are already in the track file and are not doubled. Lead (Fred 08:22): the lead is identified in the JSON — each report carries lead: true when that cart was the lead at that moment, and a leadChanges list records every change (elapsed, from, to) — so a replay can draw the lead track, then my cart's track. Ride detail JSON — the target definition (v1, Fred 10-18 08:14–08:26)
What it is: each tablet's record of the messaging payload it RECEIVED during one recording (REC → END) — the full received-message data captured for later analytics
(ride metrics, replay at selectable speeds, CartMotion's per-cart report interval, weak-device and range analysis). Built AFTER the tick, as part of ride metric reporting; this definition is the target.
File: &lt;track name&gt;_ride_detail.json beside the recording's track file (separate — the track file keeps my tablet's own GPS points; they are not doubled here).
Writes: held in memory, grouped by cart; written at END and when the app goes to the background (an event, not a timer).
Time: every time is UTC epoch ms; e = elapsed seconds since THIS tablet's REC (ride start = each tablet's own REC press).

Pipeline (Fred 08:30–08:31): 1) receive — the comm side makes the CoT message; the board updates the cart's TRUTH at once (last heard, status, lead) and the ride detail JSON records the report (when built — on RECEIVE, never on process); lead-track points and off-track come from the real report here. 2) CartMotion black box → 3) map position function → one or more queue entries (cart, position, due time, real / in-between) → 4) map queue: every radio receipt goes through it; an entry is processed when due — cart icon moves, the drawn track extends through TrackPath, the 50 m trim applies. In-between steps are display-only and never recorded. One queue, one process (Fred 08:33–08:34): every received message goes into the RECEIVING QUEUE (stamped with its received time); one consumer takes them in order, updates the board truth, writes the ride JSON (placeholder until the metric reporting), and CartMotion puts N entries back on the SAME queue — N = 1 now, N = the cart's steps later; same queue, same process, only N changes. Each entry is flagged real or in-between: only the REAL one updates the truth and the JSON; in-between entries only move the display. First pass (build 1): the FULL message only — ONE entry per received message, due now; no per-second entries driven by the report frequency (later, build 5).
Lead change (Fred 08:39–08:41): the new lead is picked up from where he is; NO line is drawn for him until he passes the last known lead position — he comes within 50 m of it, and the track continues from his NEXT report (ahead) — no backwards lines. Lead silent = no lead movement until heard again; heard again = the track is laid from his last point to the new one (over route/trail) on every map, shown back to each tablet's own cart. My track trails my cart.
Queue placement (08:37): the receiving queue + its consumer run in the BACKGROUND, ONCE for the app (an app-wide owner — not one per view-model copy, item J, or every message would be processed and written twice); the map drawing runs in the FOREGROUND, only while the map shows (hidden: keep each cart's latest position, catch up on return).
Model run (tracksim_2026-10-18.py, 10-18 08:36–08:45): 15 min, reports every 20 s, lead silent 140 s, a lead change at 10:00 to a cart 200 m behind — at N = 1 and at N = steps: no lead points during the silence (status Drop) · JSON = real messages only · lead changes logged · only points ahead of my cart shown · NO backward lines. Rules the model forced (now part of the design): (1) a new real report CANCELS that cart's pending steps; (2) N = the NORMAL interval (median of the last 5 gaps), never the last gap — a 160 s gap had produced 160 overlapping steps; (3) the lead LINE grows from its own end toward the real point, not from the cart icon; (4) the JSON leaves out my tablet's own GPS points; (5) the 50 m trim uses the real lead points.
THE PROCESS — seven boxes, one queue (Fred 08:45; model process_model_2026-10-18.py): 1 Receiver (every report → the receiving queue, stamped; background, once for the app) → 2 Truth (last heard, position, lead + the CLOCK, ageing only) → 3 Recorder (ride JSON on receive; not my tablet's GPS) → 4 LeadTrack (real lead points, one track, lead-change hold, waits through silence, off-track per report) → 5 TrackPath (ROUTE / TRAIL placeholders, STRAIGHT) → 6 Segmenter (CartMotion: N entries on the same queue; N = 1 now; a new report cancels pending entries) → 7 Map (foreground: icon moves, lead line grows from its end, 50 m trim, my track behind my cart).Tests 10-18 08:50 — one message: processed, queue empty, line started, 1 JSON report. Lead track · my cart and my track · lead polyline · removing the tick — the design in full (10-15)Carried here in full (Fred 10-15 EOD: the living docs must hold it, not point to the plan). Source: Tick Replacement Plan v6, sections 0, 4c, 5, 6, 11, 12, 14, 17.
A. The lead track — what the code does today (in the tick, ConvoyViewModel ~1172–1293):
While REC is on, each NEW lead position (the lead's own report, never a substitute) adds one straight segment from the previous lead position to the new one (_routeTrailSegments).
A lead change starts a new line. _leadTrackSegments = the lead only, drawn black (or per-cart colours).
Off-track = a cart farther than OFF_TRACK_MILES (Settings → Off Track) from any segment, swept every tick.
Proxy snap (a cart within ~250 ft of the quiet lead's last position stands in for the lead) — KILLED (Fred 15:15).
Found 10-15 on the ride: the lead's OWN tablet drew no lead track — its lead position came from its own radio's record, which never moved on its own tablet (the same cause as the my-cart freeze; MYCARTMSG fixes the source).
B. The lead-track rules (Fred 10-15 13:25–13:29):
Source order: 1) the route if loaded — a lead position within 50 m is snapped onto the route and the track runs along the route (ROUTETRACK); 2) no route → the trails — snap to the nearest trail and follow it; 3) neither nearby → the raw reported positions, two points joined.
At a trail junction: place only the lead's cart pointer and WAIT for the next position before connecting the track — the next point shows the branch taken; never guess a branch.
Difficulty / build order: route = easy · two points = easy · trails = touchy (junctions, parallel trails). Build: two-point first, then route, trails last once the junction rule is proven.
Off-track (Fred 14:12): the track is a PATH each cart is measured against when that cart's own position arrives — not a sweep of every cart on a timer.
Fred 10-15 EOD — a trail behind EVERY cart; the lead's trail is one of them. Same builder for every cart, fed by that cart's new fixes on the board.
Open: snap distance to a trail; what happens when the lead leaves the trail; (a) a lead change mid-ride — new line (today) or join to the new lead's position; (b) does the trail follow the projected cart during Signal Drop or wait for real fixes; (c) keep OFF_TRACK_MILES as is.
Builds: LEADTRACK-1 / TRAILS-1 = the two-point trail rebuilt on the board on each cart's new fix (no tick) + off-track per cart message → T5.5 can then remove the tick · ROUTETRACK (route snap ≤ 50 m) · trails with the junction wait. Each its own build.
C. My cart and my track:
My cart = a CoT message from the tablet's GPS (MYCARTMSG 3583eda96, Fred 17:16–17:46): uid MESHTASTIC-!&lt;my radio&gt;, point + altitude, speed/course from the fix; sent on every CHANGED fix (~1 s moving), a keep-alive once per reporting interval parked; through onBoardMessage like every other cart. My radio's own record no longer drives my cart while the tablet has had a fix in the last 15 s. No radio known / group off → the tablet-cart path.
My recorded track (GPX) is written from the tablet's own GPS (~1/s). RADIOTRACK (751a0a230) feeds my radio's new fixes to the recorder, in METRES, only for a tablet WITHOUT GPS hardware (the tick passed display feet → 3.3× high altitudes). Not yet tried on a no-GPS tablet.
REC active: my cart icon = the head of my track (every fix) (Fred 09:49–09:55) — T5c.
No-GPS tablet: my cart's message is built at the radio's frequency from the radio's fix — open (DIAGPOS, written, not applied).
Other carts between broadcasts (4c, Fred 07:55–09:39): on the route (≤ 50 m, snapped) a cart keeps moving along the route at its last reported speed until heard again (no cut-off), then ONE correction move to the reported position; off the route it holds at the last report and moves to exactly the reported position (how the group sees someone getting lost). Move only on a NEW fix. Display only — never changes the board. Status still Signal Drop 2 min / Lost 10 min.
D. The lead polyline (T7, Phase 1) and segment display (Phase 2):
Phase 1 / T7: the lead transmits his polyline — the last 2 minutes of his track, every broadcast (6 s); receivers mine ONLY its last point as the lead's position. No sender checkbox (v2 change). First check whether the polyline message exists yet; if not, sending it is part of T7.
Phase 2 (after certification): polyline SEGMENT display with an on/off toggle on the receiver — the sender always sends the same message. Polylines (the lead's own recorded segments) follow the trails work; ROUTETRACK draws the lead path over the route in Phase 1 ("not a stretch").

Reference numbers (10-12): one Meshtastic packet ≈ 230 bytes of data ≈ 40–50 points (first point ~8 bytes, then ~4 bytes each). Simplified (Douglas–Peucker, ~5 m) riding needs ~3–10 points per minute → 1 min ≈ 20–50 bytes, 2 min ≈ 35–90 bytes, 5 min ≈ 70–210 bytes (twisty may need coarser older detail). 20 min does not fit one packet and is not needed — each tablet stitches the full lead track from the pieces.
Why the ride must reach every rider (Fred): a point on a map without a route is useless. ⚠ FALLBACK RULE (Fred 10-12 19:53) — do not confuse the two: Android device only is a MODE the rider chooses (no radio asked, group functions hidden). The fallback is different: in Meshtastic group-awareness mode, when the radio disconnects, Android data is substituted for radio data on the local node — my cart takes the tablet's GPS so its information stays current (today's LINKFIX / LINKFIX2: other carts held at their last tick position, nothing invented). When the radio returns, my cart goes back to the radio's data. The data must roll back and forth with the link, as many times as it drops, with the group functions staying visible. GRPMODE must not switch the mode when the link drops, and P5.1 must keep this substitution when the tick's source moves to members() (with the radio down, members() is stale or empty — my cart comes from the tablet). Tablet check for both: in Meshtastic mode, radio off → my cart keeps moving on the tablet's GPS, others held, GRP Awareness red; radio on → my cart back on the radio's position, same cart id; repeat twice.
⚠ MY-CART SOURCE RULE (Fred 10-12 19:55) — refines the fallback rule: with GRP Awareness on, my cart is ONE cart, keyed by my callsign. Its data comes from the radio when the radio's own report has been refreshed within the last 2 broadcast intervals; if the radio's data is more than 2 broadcast intervals old, from the tablet. A fresh radio report switches it back. Same cart, same callsign, either way. Today the switch follows link health (radio "not talking" = no own report for 45 s, LINKHB). To settle 10-13 (G5): which interval — proposed: 2 × the moving interval while the tablet's GPS shows motion (e.g. 6 s → 12 s), 2 × the stationary 30 s when stopped (60 s), so a parked cart does not flip between its 30-s reports. The intervals come from the comm side (currentReporting(), P5.2) — so P5.2 moves before P5.1b.
✅ G5 DECIDED (Fred 10-12 19:57) — "really simple": the limit is 2 broadcast intervals (moving every 6 s → 12 s). When my radio's last report is older than that, my cart takes the tablet's GPS only if the tablet has moved since the last update; if it has not moved, my cart stays where the last update put it. No motion test on the radio side, no separate stationary limit — a parked cart simply does not change. Fresh radio report → back to the radio. Same cart, same callsign.
✅ TWO POSITIONS IN MY CART'S RECORD (Fred 10-12 19:58): my node records both the radio's GPS (position + fix time, from the comm side) and the tablet's GPS (position + fix time). The display applies the G5 rule to choose which to show: radio fix ≤ 2 broadcast intervals old (12 s at 6 s) → radio; older AND the tablet has moved since the last update → tablet; otherwise the last shown position. Why: it ends the GPS jitter between cart and radio — today one position field is overwritten by whichever source wrote last, so two receivers a few feet apart make the cart hop. Both values stay in the record for logging and tests. Only my own cart has two sources; other carts are radio-only and unchanged. Lands in P5.1b (ConvoyNode gains the radio and tablet fixes for my cart; the choice is one function, logged when it switches).
✅ SCOPE SPLIT (Fred 10-12 20:01): P5 redefines and populates the node elements; the display rules wait for the tick replacement.
WhenWhat
P5 (P5.1b)ConvoyNode redefined: radio fix (lat, lon, fix time — from members()) and tablet fix (lat, lon, fix time — the tablet's GPS) as separate elements, populated every tick. My cart: both. Other carts: radio fix only. Android device only: tablet fix only, radio fix empty. The display does not change in P5 — today's LINKFIX behaviour stays; the record just carries more. P5 stays plumbing, nothing visible.
Tick replacement (later)The display rules: radio fix ≤ 2 broadcast intervals (12 s at 6 s) → radio; older and the tablet has moved since the last update → tablet; otherwise the last position. Android device only → always the tablet fix (Fred 19:59: "if no group awareness we just use the android, which is the second value").

Lessons:
A patch's own comment can trip its own post-check — twice now (P2b "scanModel", P4.4 "radioOps()"). Word marker comments so they never contain a forbidden token; the scratch test caught it before Fred saw it.
gt_build's "N UNCOMMITTED change(s)" counts tracked files only — new untracked files are in the build but not in the count; a move needs an explicit git add of the folders (git then records renames).
Long commit messages: plain ASCII only (Fred's paste picked up bad characters); give add / commit / push as three separate commands and always paste git log --oneline -1.
"Never applied" ≠ "never set up": GRP Awareness judged the radio by this tablet's records; the radio's own network is the truth (RADIONET).
A stale report: the comm side's applyReport outlives the screen — cleared at the start of every apply (found in scratch review before sending P4.2).

The rule (Fred 10-11): the current manual, release notes and Quick Start are carried in the EOD set every day, beside the handoff, living master, WHERE WE ARE and ledger. Each day's user-visible changes go into them that day — text updated, and every screen that changed labelled in the manual as it changes. That is the only way to stay on top of the changes; a catch-up later becomes a large task that misses them.
Labels in the manual (visible, with a grep-able RECAPTURE-2026-10-11 comment): 📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED (red — the picture is out of date) · 📷 IMAGE TO CHECK (amber — may have changed) · 📷 NEW SCREEN — CAPTURE TO ADD (blue — a screen not yet pictured). A label is removed only when its picture is recaptured. Labels are visible to readers until then — remove or hide them before a public refresh only if Fred decides so.
Each EOD: for every rider-visible change of the day (a release, or a build headed to one): release notes entry · manual text · Quick Start step if a step changed · a label on every affected picture. New version numbers each day something changed; never reuse a file name.
Online copy (grouptrack.org) is refreshed at release time from the current versions (standing step, WEBDOCS-2026-10-03).

Lessons 10-11:
One truth per fact. Two copies of "is it paired" drifted. A state the comm side owns is read only from the comm side, and it must be kept current by the event that changes it.
Bluetooth off is a test case for every link change — and so are FORGET → PAIR and a power-cycle.
Shadow first works when the shadow cannot disturb the live path (keep-alive: yes; a second scanner: no — Android's scan quota is shared).
versionCode follows the commit, not the build — two uncommitted builds on one commit share it. Verify a deploy by the build name deploy.sh prints, the APK sha256 and lastUpdateTime.
Deploy by exact build name, after Drive has synced — two wrong builds went on today (10:14 the old 0942; 13:50 the 1127 instead of P2b-1).
My patches' post-checks tripped on my own comments five times (connectionState, pairedMacs, forgetPairing(, LINK_SILENCE_MS, scanModel). Rule: never write a checked-for token in a comment the same patch inserts.
Don't diagnose ahead of the evidence — the forget failure was not the scan (Fred's tests).

Root cause 1 — missing trails:
Symptom: after Remove all trail data + Utah re-import, the tester (and then Droid 2, deliberately) had no trails at all — e.g. Four Mile Wash, way 1003674700. The PC trace (gt_osmtrace_2026-10-10_v2.py) said the trail is KEPT and SHOWN, hash identical, land PUBLIC — so the import was right; the device's step 9 was not.
Mechanism: step 9 (OwnershipReclass.run) applied category, use AND land in one pass, and was skipped when the ownership file was missing or refused. Skipped → carto_code NULL → the map's filter carto_code NOT IN (off list) is NULL for NULL → every unclassified trail hidden, whatever Map Keys says.
Why the file was refused: OOMGUARD (09-15) checked heap headroom against the file size before reading. The streaming reader (09-17) made it obsolete, but it stayed. Fred's own 72 MB file (09-12) was loaded before the guard existed; a fresh download is 78.7 MB and was refused every time. The step reported "0", nothing in the log said why.
Fred's rule (10-10): "our categories are meaningless unless they are applied" — "the process has to run". Missing input → a default (land PUBLIC), never a skipped step.
Proof: failure replicated on Droid 2 first (clear → Utah import → no trails), the refusal found in Droid 1's log, release k on both tablets → all trails back; the launch pass repairs a tablet without a re-import.
Root cause 2 — the check-in apply error:
Symptom: "Cannot use this target: String arg == null" right after group 1b on every CHECK IN apply that restarts the radio, any ride; the radio nevertheless ended exactly on target (Fred's compare). Applying from "Apply ride to radio" never showed it; re-applying a ride already on the radio (nothing to write, no restart) never showed it.
Values were never the issue: the configurator reads only the ride's network.mesh (region, preset, slot, hop limit, TX power, role, channel name, key), the default asset's standalone reporting group and the callsign — all required; the two rides differed only in channel name, hop limit and key.
Mechanism: group 1b restarts the radio → node id goes null and back → LaunchedEffect(nodeId) rebuilds targets → the CHECK IN auto-apply LaunchedEffect(targets) fires again while autoRideId is still set → choose() runs mid-apply against a half-reconnected radio and paints the error over a successful apply.
Fix: APPLYGUARD (above). Tablet-tested 10-10: no errors on check-in.
Lessons:
A step that depends on an input must run with a default when the input is missing — never skip silently (Fred: "the process has to run").
Remove a guard when its reason goes: OOMGUARD outlived the reader it protected and broke every fresh import for three weeks.
Replicate the failure before fixing it (Fred cleared Droid 2 and reproduced the tester's empty map first).
Compose: an automatic action inside a LaunchedEffect keyed on state that changes during a long operation will re-fire — gate it on the phase.
Compare the paths that work with the path that fails (check-in vs manual apply; restart vs nothing-to-write) — that, not the values, found the apply error.
Environment: PC Python SSL "certificate expired" → download with curl; Drive upload looping → router reboot + restart Drive; deploy installed a stale build (29321322) when Drive lagged → deploy by exact name, always; Droid 2 hides app logs → logcat on Droid 1; recommit step −1 moves .db files into the inbox → moved to D:\GroupTrack_archive\db\.
My errors (Claude), recorded: said the land default "has no impact" (land was coupled with categories in step 9 — wrong); assumed Fred's 72 MB file had passed the guard (it pre-dated the guard); did not build the network option when first asked; removed the organizer choice when Fred wanted three choices; 10-11: gave a Play "What's new" text as 488 characters when it was 538.
