DECIDED 10-08 (Fred) — the boundary rules (full text: service-layer design v17 §R7): GroupTrack owns the panels (moving GRP Awareness to the comm side rejected — "not an option"); the comm module has service-level access only, headless, returning results · requests GroupTrack → comm, events comm → GroupTrack, a sender and a matching function on each side · a request never waits for its outcome · recovery is a request, the action is performed in the comm module, reconnection is an event · errors are events with reason codes; GroupTrack owns the words ("your radio is not recovering — forget it and pair again") · native Meshtastic menus and screens stay UNCHANGED, opened by request OVER GroupTrack (how they END is open) · no new direct Meshtastic calls · one service at a time, both directions — slow and steady, using the existing where-used inventory (gen_xrefs_v2.sh) before and after each step · finish line = GroupTrack in its own module, the compiler finds zero.
Separate-app model and licensing (§R7.3; not legal advice): like ATAK + Meshtastic — a mesh app that owns the radio and gives service-level access; we can ship our own open-source (GPL) mesh app ("GroupTrack Comm") so riders need no stock Meshtastic; GroupTrack talks to it at arm's length. Today and through 2.7b everything is one APK = one GPL work (source public keeps it compliant). Confirmed: the boundary is in the right place and the handoffs are compatible with the licence terms. A comm screen opens ON TOP of GroupTrack (same task, live connection, not a new session) — it cannot be embedded inside a GroupTrack panel.

FOUND AND FIXED 10-02 — THE STRANDED IMPORTWhy imports "never finished and could not be restarted — we had to clear data": extract and import ran as WorkManager jobs enqueued with ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP; the coordinator waited on them with no time limit. A job stuck queued held it forever → isImporting stayed true → the picker silently ignored Load ("import already running — ignoring request"). Closing the app killed the coordinator but not the job (Android keeps its own job database); KEEP re-attached the next import to the dead job; only clearing data removed it. Also: the gate shows the picker only on an empty trail database, so a part-finished import opened the map with half a state. Fixed by INPROCESS + KILLEDIMPORT (ec749561c), verified on Droid 2.
REJECTED — AND WHY (10-02)KILLEDIMPORT v2 — cancel leftover jobs at startup + a 3-minute queued-job limit: managed the background jobs instead of removing them; Fred's in-process call replaced it before it ran.The queue-only legibility patch (white + 11sp on two lines, dimText to grey): Fred — "just the dark slate", then white app-wide; the search found 162 uses on 47 screens.Release-notes entries for the import and slate fixes: never seen in the field.Landscape promo panels; two separate promo sets: Fred — portrait, one cohesive weekly series.The obfuscation change in the 10-02 upload: renaming breaks by-name code only in release builds; it needs its own tested build (2.7b).
RULES LEARNED 10-02A long job with two owners strands people. One owner, visible start to finish, that dies with the app, is the safe shape for anything a rider waits on.Read the colour, not the hex: a "dim" token can be a whole app's secondary text — search every use before changing one.Context-based classification needs a human pass: the slate patch called a field label "disabled" because disabledTextColor sat two lines above — the report caught it.Play links: keep &amp;hl=en_US; the bare link can 404 depending on region.

That is how the community grows.⭐⭐ THE VOCABULARY (Fred) — never mix them: a ride is the package (a bundle of joy); a route is the path the ride requires; a track is a recording; a trail is on the ground; a waypoint is a marked place; a trailhead is where a route starts and riders meet. You go on a ride, follow its route, and record your track. 🔴 PROBLEM 1 (09-30, first) — MY RADIO'S OWN REPORTS NEVER REACH MY TABLET
Symptom (Fred, 09-29 evening): GPS panel → APPLY → the steps run (Written · Disconnecting in 3 s · Reconnecting in 20 s · Done). GRP Awareness turns RED (a real disconnect), then GREEN and flashing (reconnected, hearing the group). SELECT CART lists both carts — but MY cart's pointer is not on the map. A manual DISCONNECT then CONNECT in GRP Awareness restores it. With 10 s before the reconnect a manual reconnect was needed even to get the radio back; 20 s fixed that part.
Also observed: "no activity for 24 minutes" in the app while the Mesh Nodes screen shows the radio every 15 s; the radio broadcasts every 10 s and the OTHER tablet sees it.
Analysis: a radio's broadcasts go out over the air and are never received back by its own tablet (TAK reports included). So my own radio's record on my tablet (position, last heard) is refreshed only by the radio's own local updates. The GPS panel's reconnect is a SHORTCUT — ConvoyViewModel.radioOps(ui): disconnect() = ui.setDeviceAddress("n"), reconnect() = ui.setDeviceAddress(saved) — which appears to RESET that record; my position comes back empty and nothing refills it (the list shows the cart without a position; the map cannot draw it). GRP Awareness's DISCONNECT/CONNECT go through Meshtastic's own connection manager (scanModel.disconnect(), then connect) and keep/refill it. The stale last-heard may also make my cart count as silent/Lost (HUD).
The fix (two parts, both needed): (a) the GPS panel (and the check-in's radio setup — RadioConfigWriter uses the same ops) disconnect/reconnect exactly as GRP Awareness does — find how CONNECT is wired (Main.kt → GrpAwarenessPanel: onDisconnect = { scanModel.disconnect() }; the CONNECT row) and call the same; the check-in's 09-28 first-run blindness looked the same. (b) my cart's position and presence from the TABLET (its GPS; the check-in) — the identity rule ("my cart's startup position comes from Android's GPS"). ⚠ (b) changes how MY CART is built — design it with Fred before any code (his rule: no fundamental change to a working function without a conversation).
Test: GPS panel APPLY → without touching anything: my pointer on the map, both tablets; my cart not counted Lost; the check-in's radio setup the same.
🔴 PROBLEM 2 — THE SURVEY OWNED BY THE ROUTE (with the route's global identity)
Decision (Fred 09-29): "the survey belongs to the route" — "route is the key": ten riders on one ride follow one route; their surveys build that route's rating. Even if a survey is also tied to a ride, it must resolve to the route. No track reference needed (one track per ride is kept — the first replicated).
Today's code: END → EndOfRideForm(checkIn = viewModel.endingCheckIn) → viewModel.pendingSurvey = survey → finalizeTrack() saves the track, then ConvoyRideStore.saveSurvey(trackId, sv) — the survey is keyed to the TRACK id; the survey is asked only on a public scheduled ride. At END the ride is known (the check-in) and ConvoyRideStore.rideForEdit(rideId).routeId gives its route.
Needed: (1) check whether routes carry a GLOBAL identity (the same on every tablet — the route travels in the ride file, .convoy format 3); if not, give them one at creation; (2) the survey table keyed by the route (ride kept as context) — a DB change with a migration of existing surveys (those with a known ride linked to its route; others kept track-only); (3) saveSurvey by route. Files to read: ConvoyRideStore.kt (RideSurveyInput, saveSurvey, the survey table), the route table in the spatial DB, the ride file format.
3.0: the device structure is the target; AWS mirrors it; routes → rides → surveys are the first data mined.

⭐⭐ THE ROLE RULES (Fred 09-29) — as built
One Leader, one Middle, one Tail gunner; Rider unlimited. The Leader is the key role. No Tail gunner reporting → the tail is the last cart.
Every cart speaks only for itself — nobody claims or assigns a role for anyone else. At check-in, a special role another cart holds is REFUSED (red window: "Leader is taken … held by …"); it can only be taken once RELEASED.
Changing roles at a stop: SELECT CART → CHANGE MY ROLE · now &lt;role&gt; (or tap your own cart). Choosing Rider releases a special role (announced as HQ). One person at a time; the Leader is the last assignment.
Broadcast: the special roles report every 30 s from check-in (the first three 5 s apart) until 3 minutes after REC; a change during the ride reports for 3 minutes. Any ride, scheduled or not. END stops the reports and clears the roles.
The lead: the tick sets it from a Leader report; REC with no lead asks the rider (a local pick, never broadcast); the lead stays with that cart until a Leader report changes it. No automatic pick (the old "several carts → my cart" removed); the old distance accumulator removed.

⭐⭐⭐ RIDE ROLES — THE WORKING DESIGN (proven 09-28; completion 09-29)
Carrier: a standard TAK position report (port 72) that the tablet fills in (position, callsign, role) and hands to its radio — no ack; a report, not a message. The radios' own reports are untouched.
Mapping: Leader → TeamLead · Middle → RTO · Tail gunner → ForwardObserver · Rider → HQ (only to announce a reassignment to Rider). Receive lifts ONLY these; TeamMember (the radios' own) and every other role are ignored. Blank = Rider.
Who sends: only the three special roles. When: every 30 s from check-in until 3 minutes after REC, then silent; a reassignment broadcasts the same way. Roles are fixed until reassigned or END (clears). No expiry.
Single source: the role store → the node array (rideRole, my own role included) → the tick (lead via setLeadCart on change, tail via tailNodeId) → HUD, markers, labels, SELECT CART. REC asks for the lead only while no lead is locked.
Trailhead order: everybody checks in first thing (the check-in puts each radio on the ride network); special roles among the first; ride starts when all have checked in.
09-29 full schedule · reassignment + HQ · clear at END · blank = Rider on screen · three timestamps (sent · received · applied, absolute ms).

⭐ RIDE NETWORKS — the organizer's own private network (built, VERIFIED)
Structure (Fred): organizer → optional organization → a radio config; the config is NAMED after its owner ("Fred K", later "Club / Fred K"). Matches the 09-22 convergence design (org top/optional; leader own|inherit_org; ride inherit_leader|unique; select, never merge; every leader has an effective config).
Not a choice: every organizer gets a personal network, reused for all their rides — created when the ride form first opens (ensureMyNetworkName), recorded as users.config_id (config_mode 'own'). Rides store inherit_leader + that id.
The only choice: "Create a private network for this ride" → a new network (owner RIDE, unique), also named after the organizer. Locked once the ride is sent (lock with Edit ride).
Organizer attribute: saving a ride sets users.is_organizer = 1. 3.0 community: rides are seen through their organizer (organizers are followed) — the attribute must be set from the first ride.
Never another organizer's network for your rides; theirs reach your radio only by joining their ride. deleteUnused never deletes your own or an organization's network; another organizer's may go once no ride uses it (it returns with their next ride) — "used in the last 30 days" = rides expire 30 days after their date.
In 3.0, several networks (own + organizations') → a picker; one → used automatically (2.7: always one, no prompt). No new datastore: network_configs, users, rides, organizations (empty) already exist (schema_device_additions.sql).
⭐ PUBLIC / PRIVATE (built; email line to test)
Public is the default; Private the override (switch at the top of the form, each state explained on screen).
Public: the invitation may be forwarded ("This is an open ride. Feel free to forward this email…"); at the end each rider rates it and chooses Yes/No to share their track; from 3.0 shown to the community through the organizer.
Private: "This is a private ride for the riders invited. Please don't forward this email." At the end: no survey, no sharing, no public trails added; every track stays on its tablet.
The ride FILE now carries isPublic (it did not) — every rider's tablet needs it at the end of the ride; the heal takes it from the file (older files: private).
Fallback recorded: if track sharing ever changes, a private ride pre-selects "No".
⭐ THE PRE-RIDE CHECK-IN AND THE END OF THE RIDE (built, to test)
A new FIRST state in the recording sequence: CHECK_IN → IDLE (REC) → RECORDING ⇄ PAUSED → END → CHECK_IN. You cannot record until checked in. Button: ✔ CHK IN › REC; checking in does NOT record — REC is a second tap. The odometer stays hidden before check-in. Starts at CHECK_IN (view model).
The check-in (ConvoyCheckIn.kt): open recent rides (dated today or earlier, not expired; today's first; one today → pre-selected) + No scheduled ride; callsign and role FOR THIS RIDE (profile defaults, overridable; the ride's organizer → Leader); Set up radio. Stored as the enrollment (created_by 'login'; the table already exists; enrollments.callsign holds the per-ride callsign — a deliberate return from 09-22's "retired", as an override only).
The end-of-ride form (ConvoyEndOfRideForm.kt, replacing the frozen map's Save Track dialog): a ride → the track is named after the ride, fixed (the 3.0 server names a ride's track after the ride and keeps ONE track per ride — the first shared to arrive); public ride → rating, difficulty, recommend (required), notes (optional), share Yes/No (REQUIRED, no default); private or no ride → name only. SAVE gated; "To save: …" line.
The survey belongs to the RIDE (ride + rider), not the track hash; one per rider per ride; alternate UNIQUE index ux_ride_surveys_ride_user. The rider's own local track id is kept only as the link the table requires. Written only when the track exists.
Ownership: the organizer owns the ride (public/private); each rider owns their track and survey (the share choice).
Today's start logic (permission, lead cart) is UNCHANGED until the roles build.
⭐ THE RIDE FORM, AND ROUTES THAT CARRY THEIR TRAILHEAD (form VERIFIED; route saves to test)
Form: Private ride + Radio network at the TOP (the first decision); then route + picture, name, date, rollout time, trailhead. The organizer's name/email and the zip are recorded but not shown. The description IS the route's (headline + a converted track's own text; OSM credit only for planner routes); the Description field appears only when the route has none — then required.
Routes carry their trailhead (Fred): no route is saved without one, by any method. Track conversion: the dialog requires a trailhead (within ½ mile of the track's start, or "Add a trailhead at the track's start"); new → a 'trailhead' waypoint; either way setRouteAnchor writes it into the recipe. Route+ save (Draw included): checked BEFORE anything is saved; none → nothing saved, a prompt: ADD TRAILHEAD (at the first point, named) or SELECT ON MAP (CHANGE TYPE → Trailhead), then SAVE again.
Interim (THTEXT): an older route with no trailhead near → the ride form's "Trailhead *" box; the text goes at the front of the description ("Trailhead: …") and counts for sending. Removed once every route carries its trailhead.

Commits (all pushed, origin at 7cc97b37e): 4a0a65f1f form layout + FIT v2 · a774c3478 first-point trailhead · 005ac5e6c check-in fix v2 (⚠ also carries ORDERFIX + the red button) · 7cc97b37e Edit ride + Leader's Notes.
Decisions (Fred, evening) — the rules as built:
Every route has a trailhead = its FIRST POINT (the first recorded point of a track; the first pin in Route+). A Trailhead within 0.1 mile is reused; otherwise it is created there and the save asks only for its NAME. Tracks: settled FIRST, in a popup, before the conversion (so it is on the map before the route exists). Route+: at SAVE; the old first-pin gate ("a route starts near a trailhead") RETIRED. Reason (Fred): "what is the start of a 100-mile trail?" -- the first point is the only start GroupTrack actually knows; searching "within 1/2 mile" lists was confusing and never needed once the first point is the trailhead.
ORDERFIX (root cause of "trailhead not selected"): trackToRoute wrote the anchor BEFORE the notes; writeRouteNotes replaces every row, wiping the anchor. Now notes first, anchor after. Routes converted before the fix have no anchor.
Fitting a route = only the route and its trailhead -- through the planner's OWN FIT state (other types OFF, the route + its trailhead waypoint SELECTED, savePlanningState, bounds include the trailhead). Used by FIT and by every ride picture; the map stays that way. (A page-side overlay, v1, was dropped: it hid layers behind the map state's back.)
Ride form layout (mockup v2 approved): Ride name first · Private ride · Radio network as a CHOICE ("My organizer network" / "Create a new network for this ride") with "Network assigned:" (the network's full name, or "Private – Group…"; generated when toggled, used only when the ride is added, removed on CANCEL or if unused) · Date + Rollout on one line · Leader's Notes (when needed) · Trailhead · the route's name over its picture · SAVE / CANCEL. Everything typed comes before the picture.
Leader's Notes = the ride's own notes (label on the form); the route description belongs to the route. Still blurred in code: notes start from the route's description -- separation recorded as a polish item.
Edit ride: the form filled in from the ride. Not sent: all but route and network. Sent: the date only (the store's rule -- rescheduling for weather), then send again; a new date restarts the 30 days. The manual previously said "date, time and description" -- corrected to the code's rule.
Check-in: ride, callsign and role on ONE panel; the role is ALWAYS asked (No scheduled ride too); the list is EVERY ride not yet removed (30 days after its date; future ones too), today's first -- "never more than a handful", no search. The button is red ("CHK IN > REC", 12 sp).
The lead-cart assignment at REC STAYS (Fred: removing it would break the track functions) -- dealt with on the roles day.
Roles do not travel yet: the role is stored at check-in on the tablet only; the radio still reports Team Member. The plan (its own day, nothing else touched): check-in writes the role to the radio (TAK module config) → the tick reads it → the map shows callsign · role → the lead cart from Team Lead.
Radio callsign field: its main use is setting up SOMEONE ELSE's radio at the trailhead (hint on the screen).
Superseded patch files -- never apply: patch_endride v1/v2, patch_formorder, patch_fitroute (v1), patch_thfirst (v1), patch_checkinfix (v1).
Next (Fred's order): Group Com tomorrow first → 1–2 days test/polish + the 12 screen captures → roles/cart/tick/messaging on its own day. Small ride items: Leader's Notes separation · SET TRAILHEAD for older routes (setRouteAnchor never overwrites) · CREATE RIDE on every planner detail panel · one-screen import · forwarding · check-in Set up radio preselected · remove the interim Trailhead box.

2 · THE ROLES DAY (its own day; nothing else touched):
Every cart has a role — Leader, Middle, Tail gunner or Rider — chosen at check-in and carried in its reports with its callsign (the check-in writes the role to the radio: TAK module config). One Leader, one Middle, one Tail gunner per ride; everyone else is a Rider.
The lead and tail ASSIGNMENTS are REMOVED (the REC lead-cart popup and SET AS LEAD): the tick READS the roles from the reports, the same on every device. The map shows callsign · role for every cart.
SELECT CART (the button beside MY CART) — available to every cart: the list of all carts on the ride (callsign + role); tap one to open its display.
From that list, the Leader, Middle or Tail gunner (only they) can SWITCH ROLES with the selected cart: pick which special role it takes → the selected cart gets that role, that role's previous holder takes the selected cart's old role (a swap — never two holders). Any special-role holder can move ANY of the three — so a broken-down Leader never leaves the ride stuck. Every switch announced on every tablet; the tick follows the latest switch, not a silent radio's old role. (REMOVE FROM RIDE: restricted the same way.)
The check-in preloads the ride map ("Show this ride's route and trailhead on the ride map", ticked by default, rides only): CHECK IN clears the ride map to the ride's route and trailhead, fitted (through the ride map's own saved state); at REC the leader's track and the group's positions appear on top.
3 · Polish-days item added: SHOW ON MAP in the Rides list — the planning map fitted to the ride's route and trailhead (reuses FIT); works for received rides too.
4 · Docs (late 09-27): manual v18 — Rides chapter restructured: Creating a route (routes only) · Creating a ride from a route (new) · Creating a ride from a track (new) · The ride form (was Adding a ride; id unchanged); Quick Start v59 — the Rides chapter as seven step-by-step sections (from a route, from a track, email, open a ride, program radios, the list, check-in); GroupTrack_ScreenCapture_Plan_2026-09-27_v1 — 21 numbered captures (cap_01…cap_21), each tied to its marker in the manual and Quick Start.

⭐ RIDE CREATION — every starting point (built, device-verified 09-26)
Route narrative (ConvoyNotesPanel): button row ROUTE DETAILS · CREATE RIDE · DOWNLOAD MAPS. CREATE RIDE closes the narrative and runs the SAME path as the detail panel's ADD A RIDE: RidePreview.captureThen(webViewRef, "Route", rid) { onAddRide("Route", rid) }. One ride-creation path, several ways in.
Track → route → ride (ArtifactDetailPanel CREATE RIDE on tracks → dialog: route name (refuses a used route name), the automatic first line shown, Route description (hint: skill level, terrain, highlights, cautions) → ConvoyArtifactOps.trackToRoute(context, trackId, name, description) → insertRoute → writeRouteNotes → fit + picture → ride form (trailhead within ½ mile, as for any route)).
The conversion (simplifyByHeading): keep a point wherever the heading has turned &gt; 15° since the last kept point, plus the corner before it; otherwise one every 20 m; drop jitter &lt; 3 m; first and last kept. Desk test on six 8 m-radius switchbacks: 294 → 102 points (66% removed), every original point within 1.0 m (switchbacks 0.6 m). History: 20°/30 m cut the first corner by 8.9 m (the turn was noticed after passing it → keep the corner); 5.2 m on hairpins → 15°/20 m. Real track "Panguitch Loop" (sparse recording): 2188 → 2164 points.
The route owns its narrative (Fred): the notes are written WITH the route. Payload: {"source":"convertroute", "narrative":{"headline":"Created from track &lt;track&gt; — N miles","description":"&lt;rider&gt;"}, "summary":{"total_miles":N}}; miles measured on the RECORDED points. notesFromDraft gained narrative.description → an open ABOUT THIS ROUTE section (any route with one).
Pass 1 (review) kept for re-checks: trackToConvertDraft writes a Route+ draft with "method":"convertroute" (Fred's marker). Drafts live in …/files/GroupTrack/route_drafts/ (the /sdcard/Documents/… path in RouteDraftStore's comment is stale since the storage conversion). ⚠ The in-progress list is remember(draftListTick) — a draft written from outside Route+ must bump the tick (DRAFTTICK), or it never appears.

⭐ THE CONFIGURATOR — finished for riders (built + verified 09-26)
Subsets, proven in code: Apply ride to radio = default + ride files (+ the preselected save only, from Saved configs); Saved configs = Radio now + saves; the Rides screen = rides only.
Callsign for this radio (defaults to the profile; another rider's typed → their radio; profile untouched; save titled "… — for &lt;callsign&gt;").
The second restart (Fred's diagnosis): Nathan's groups = LoRa + channel → one restart each. Our position/GPS values restart the radio AGAIN after the tablet reconnected; Android keeps a dead link "Connected"; the app never receives its own-node record (sent only in the connect exchange). Each tablet saw the OTHER radio, not its own. Fix: after the last group, 30 s, then ALWAYS one clean disconnect/reconnect (FINALCYCLE); then wait (≤ 30 s) for ourNodeInfo — same radio as at the start — one extra cycle if absent (OWNNODE); per-group gap back to 3 s (GAP3 — the reconnect waits for Connected anyway).
Timings (26 Sep): 1b back 27 s (radio 2 restarted itself ~1 s after commit) · channel back 20–23 s (no self-restart) · final cycle back 7–14 s · own record present at once · 19/19 both radios · about 3–4 min per full apply.
TX power 0: the radio stores the resolved value (30 dBm). Rule (TXMAX, overlay + change list + verify): target 0 and radio &gt; 0 → the radio's value is the target. Bench-confirms "0 = max".
One standard: NetworkGenerator.MeshDefaults — values from the default asset via loadFrom(context) just before a ride is saved; literals = logged fallback (now MEDIUM_FAST / 0 / TAK_TRACKER).
⭐ THE CHANNEL, MEASURED — MEDIUM_FAST + 4 s (09-26)
Two radios, standing, indoorsChannel utilisation
LONG_FAST, radio 1 hand-set to 3 s (09-25)~22%
LONG_FAST, both on the configurator's values9–12% (naked or connected: no difference)
MEDIUM_FAST (settled after ~10 min)4–6%
MEDIUM_FAST + smart minimum 4 s4–5%
Range (estimates, January test settles): link budget ~153 / 148 / 143 dB (LONG / MEDIUM / SHORT_FAST). T1000 observed ~1⅓ mi on LONG_FAST → expected ¾–1 mi on MEDIUM_FAST. Rider guidance: keep within ~¾ mile.
Backbone (Fred): strong radios (1 W, external antenna, high) at the lead, the tail and the middle; the leader's matters most (its track travels strong→T1000, the long direction). Limiting link = T1000 → strong. Spacing rule to measure: strong radios no further apart than twice the T1000→strong range.
Presets must match on a ride; the preset comes from the default (not per ride file) — now true for new rides (ONEDEFAULT).
Still to measure: utilisation while MOVING (the 4 s effect) · a 1 W radio's power with TX 0 · mixed T-Beam + T1000 (firmware versions; 72 vs 78).

00-2026-09-25 — THE CONFIGURATOR PROVEN, RADIOS THAT SPEAK TAK BY THEMSELVES, AND THE ARCHITECTURE MADE CONCRETE
⭐⭐ THE ARCHITECTURE, STATED (Fred 09-25) — the concrete form of "the mesh becomes a plugin"
GroupTrack receives ONE common payload — a TAK position report — and does not care about its source. It builds its node array from
the reports it receives. The Meshtastic-specific entanglement is the raw GPS mesh broadcast (port 3, plus node info for its name):
that, and only that, needs converting. TAK itself is an open, published format (CoT; Meshtastic's TAKPacket V1 on port 72 and TAKPacketV2 on
port 78; the TAKPacket-SDK) — the radio merely carries it.
The plugin (the Meshtastic side) receives from the radio and maps to TAK: raw GPS → TAK report (while the legacy switch is ON);
Meshtastic text/telemetry → TAK chat / report refresh; TAK carried by radios (72, 78, 257 via a Nucleus) → decoded and passed on. It also
SENDS: GroupTrack's TAK goes on the air as V2 (port 78). It knows ports, node numbers, node info, the radio connection.
GroupTrack (level 1) receives only TAK, from any source (the plugin today; the Nucleus Wi-Fi, a server later). It knows riders,
callsigns, positions, rides, maps.
"Me" is resolved FIRST, by the tick, on every tick — never through the plugin. Callsign = the rider profile; position = the tablet's
GPS, or (no GPS, e.g. Droid 2) the connected radio's own position read locally from the core's own-node record (ourNodeInfo).
The radio reporting to its own tablet is not a mesh message. The solo pass (me) runs on every tick; the group pass (the others) is added on
top when there are reports. Solo is not a mode — it is the base of every tick.
"Part of a group" = other riders present in the table (heard recently on this network), NOT "a radio is connected" (Droid 2 needs its
radio alone, for its own position). Only the radio's own channel can be decrypted, so everyone in the table is on this network.
The rider table (designed, NOT built — deferred to the separation work): one row per sender, keyed by radio id (!&lt;id&gt;)
or TAK uid; every message upserts — adds the sender if new, updates ONLY the values that message carries, refreshes last-heard (GPS never
touches the name). Names ONLY from reports (TAK callsign every time; node info for GPS radios; until then the radio id from the packet) —
never from the local database, which is where stale names came from. In memory; empty at start; purged after the slider's hours of silence.
The table lives in the plugin; the tick reads one report per rider. Build order when resumed: (1) listen + log beside the node DB,
(2) the tick's input swap behind a developer switch (nodeMap built from the table, loop body unchanged), (3) flip on the bench.
Node info matters only for GPS-only radios' names — and with TAK_TRACKER as the default it is not needed at all (below).
A node-info REQUEST for an unnamed GPS radio (once, re-asked after ~10 min) is available if ever wanted.
⚖ LICENSING AND THE SEPARATION — OPTION A CHOSEN AS THE DIRECTION (Fred 09-25)
Fred's concern: the boundary is also about what code must be shared. GroupTrack's own contribution at the mesh edge is exactly two things:
the callsign in the rider profile, and packaging Meshtastic GPS broadcasts into TAK for GroupTrack's consumption; everything else there
is published standard. ⚠ (not legal advice) GroupTrack is a fork of Meshtastic-Android, believed GPL-3.0 (to confirm:
head -3 LICENSE, protobufs, TAKPacket-SDK, V3_OS); a boundary INSIDE one APK is one combined work — a program boundary is what
usually separates licensing. Take a lawyer's view before the Play release.

DECISIONS 09-25
⭐ Standalone radios default to TAK_TRACKER — every radio GroupTrack configures speaks TAK and names itself; the raw-GPS converter becomes a
LEGACY switch (for radios GroupTrack did not configure). Existing ride files written before c9b539c still say TRACKER — on Droid 2 both
were edited by hand (sed on …/files/GroupTrack/rides/*.json); Droid 1's still say TRACKER (fine as a receiver).
⭐ Reporting values (the default, verified on hardware): broadcast interval 15 s = the longest gap standing still;
smart minimum interval 3 s = the fastest while moving; smart minimum distance 20 m. (Meshtastic firmware PR 2388: the broadcast interval
"is still honored as the interval for regular broadcasting"; the smart minimum is "the minimum seconds after the last sent position".)
Android's settings screens offer only hour presets — the configurator is the only in-app way to set seconds; hand-setting caused today's 3 s rhythm.
⭐ ONE staleness rule, in ONE place, with ONE value: a node not heard within the Settings slider's hours (admissionWindowHours,
range up to 12, Fred set it to 3) never becomes a cart — decided AT THE READ ("why are we reading and passing carts to be eliminated in the next
step"); own radio always kept. ConvoyNodeFilter's "heard today" (midnight) and admission-window rules are removed (a rider heard at 23:50
vanished at midnight; "once admitted, visible all day" kept phantoms; its manual-removal rule was never wired). Known gap: a radio heard on ANOTHER
channel within the window still passes → channel since if seen.
Saved configs: Apply and Compare are two separate, distinct functions ("I do not want to have to compare to apply"). Tap a config →
Apply (the configurator opens with it chosen) or Compare with… → tap a second → Managed / Everything else (information only). No whole-image restore
anywhere — a saved config is applied like everything else, managed fields only. Saves per radio (convoy_backups/&lt;radio id&gt;/),
titled by the ride they were applied from (companion .json: exact title, ride id, applied-at, verified); the first save is As found.
Configurator callsign override (REQUIRED before configuring anyone else's radio): as built it writes the callsign of the person RUNNING it
(the tablet's profile). The preview gets "Callsign for this radio" (default = profile; type another rider's), written + verified, recorded on the save;
the profile never changes. Changing a callsign = re-apply. A lent radio carries the previous rider's name until reconfigured.
Ride import: the primary path is tap the attachment → GroupTrack → Always (no picker; Always makes every later ride file open directly),
and the email says so. The menu's Import a ride is the fallback picker (opens in Downloads). Android 11+ forbids folder access to Downloads
itself and All Files Access was rejected by Play → no in-app Downloads list is possible. Email text (Fred): You're invited: &lt;ride&gt; (&lt;day&gt;) ·
If you're a GroupTrack user, tap the attachment below, choose GroupTrack, then tap "Always". This imports the route, and downloads the maps for offline
use during this ride. · Using a GroupTrack radio? Once the ride is added, open Work with Rides → Apply ride to radio. · Enjoy the ride!
The connect panel (Batch C design): tapping the Mesh text opens it: Connect (opens the radio picker — Bluetooth scan / device list,
USB — to pair, re-pair after a factory reset, switch or reconnect; Meshtastic's own connections screen) · Close · Settings (the configurator)
· Open full Mesh menu. The full Mesh menu is HIDDEN by default (the 09-04 fold) once this is built, kept until proven unnecessary, removed
before the 2.7 cut.
TAK rider identity: for TAK senders the name is in every report; for GPS-only radios the label starts as the radio id FROM THE PACKET and becomes
the callsign when a node-info report arrives; a GPS report never overwrites a name; carts are never withheld for want of a name.

⭐⭐ THE RIDE LIFECYCLE — SETTLED 09-24 (Fred)
StateReached byCan changeActions
PlannedSave with a NAME (the only minimum) — "a plan to host a ride somewhere, some time"EverythingEdit, Delete, Add route to a planned ride
In progressHas a route, something missingEverything except the routeEdit, Delete
CompletedName + route + trailhead waypoint + FUTURE date (today or later) + descriptionEverything except the routeEdit, Delete, Send
Sent previouslySent at least onceDate, start time, description (APPEND-ONLY)Resend while the date is today or later
The route is fixed from ADD A RIDE. To use another route: delete (unsent) and ADD A RIDE from the new route. Tapping the route explains this (toast).
A route is joined to a ride ONLY on the planning map: ADD A RIDE, or Add route to a planned ride (detail panel and narrative panel).
Sending is NOT a lock — "sent previously" is information; resending is always allowed. Deleting a sent ride is not allowed; deleting never deletes the route.
Originator (JSON) = who created the ride, fixed. The ride leader is a role, defaulting to the originator, claimable at the ride (organizer sick
or broken down — markGone frees it). Middle / tail gunner are claimed by riders at ride time (enrollments.role) — NOT in the ride file.
Description starts with the route narrative's headline (it states distance and duration) + "Trail data © OpenStreetMap contributors";
built routes only. The full narrative travels inside the GPX notes (with the recipe); the JSON's separate narrative field stays empty.
Lists (Send, Apply Ride) show rides dated today or later; a checkbox adds the last 30 days. The Send list shows each ride's state.
Zip derived from the trailhead (Android geocoder), display-only. Date from a calendar (yyyy-MM-dd).
Map picture: ADD A RIDE fits the planner map to the route (page function), captures a centred square, shows it on the ride screen, keeps it with the ride.
⭐⭐ NATAK — THE CALL, THE API AND THE CODE (09-24)
Nathan's answers: no boot profiles — one master .yaml, the API rewrites it, services restart, config persists until changed ·
remote access = a GroupTrack tailnet (Tailscale app) · at a trailhead = the box's own Wi-Fi AP · two APs "maybe, no promises" · apply code = the API
guide · CoT carries the original sender id (identity from the CoT uid, not the Meshtastic from) · the bridge carries only ATAK CoT today,
"as-is"; open to more · SDK pinned to latest · speed m/s (CoT) · altitude HAE, unconverted · runs SHORT_FAST (voice over LoRa); MEDIUM_FAST 8+ miles LoS
on a 22 dBm RAK4631; radios now 30 dBm · a radio-only unit is easy (Pi Zero 2, 30 dBm, GPS, config via Wi-Fi AP or USB) · a joint saturation test.
API v0.8.0 (V3_OS/docs/API.md): node config replaced whole (PUT /config + POST /apply); radio =
POST /meshtastic/config/apply {"changes":{…}}, the eleven fields only (anything else → 400), async (op-status, 409 when busy), 30–120 s;
key as base64:…; no authentication; AP SSID derived from the node id (0009-nucleus-ap); messaging on
239.10.10.60:17020; meshtasticd native API on TCP 4403; config_join_peer copies radio config from another box on the mesh.
Code (cloned to C:\Users\kixaz\natak: V3_OS, Nucleus_OS): the bridge (cot_bridge.py) sends
compressed TAKPacketV2 on port 257 (ATAK_FORWARDER) both ways; LORA_MTU = 237 (one packet, no splitting); voice on ports 256 / 260;
it owns the radio exclusively; TX_MIN_INTERVAL = 30 s per CoT uid Wi-Fi → LoRa — arbitrary (Nathan); 3–5 s is fine; it becomes a
setting. Set it BELOW the sender's rate (2 s for a 3 s sender): a cap equal to the rate aliases (3 s → ~6 s, ~9 s with the receiver's tick).
Radio update (meshtastic_api.py): validate → group 1 (owner, short name, region, preset, lora.channel_num, hop, TX,
device.role) one CLI write → reboot → wait (USB +15 s settle, TCP +5 s) → group 2 (primary channel name + psk) → reboot → wait → re-read.
Design decisions: riders join a box's Wi-Fi the ordinary Android way — GroupTrack keeps NO box records and NO Wi-Fi credentials; finds the box via the
network gateway + /api/v1/version · a ride changes only the box's RADIO (guest model; owner's Wi-Fi/mesh untouched) · the ride JSON stays
constant (nucleus block kept) until the API has security · keys (to review with Nathan): an owner key GroupTrack receives once, then rotates and
reassigns as part of reconfigure (no lockout), plus a separate Natak support key the owner can switch on/off; never in a ride file · the reporting
strategy (ATAK-style dynamic rates) is owned by the SENDING app — GroupTrack's app-sent TAK · TAK_TRACKER for standalone radios only.
Two Nucleus boards are coming (bare boards — antenna BEFORE power, always); bench plan: discovery, ride apply via API, T1000 in TRACKER/TAK_TRACKER
through the bridge, multicast capture, relay rate, TCP 4403, per-preset timing.

⭐⭐ RULES SETTLED TODAY (Fred)
Ride states: saved IN PROGRESS and changed freely until DISTRIBUTED; after that only the date changes. State is
DERIVED from rides.distributed_at and lives on the organizer's tablet, not in the JSON. Complete = route + trailhead + network.
Channel choice at ride creation: org's · mine · unique for this ride (unique = the same club, same area, same day). No own
channel → offer to create one. Built first as the simple path: every ride its own config; org / organizer inheritance later.
Receive ≠ apply. Receiving (months ahead) creates route + waypoints and downloads maps; the radio is never touched.
Apply is two separate events — a Meshtastic radio over Bluetooth/USB, a Nucleus through Natak's API — and GroupTrack
decides when. Every apply saves first; restore points are JSON files of the values we change + the long name as found;
the first is Original device config, never overwritten.
Stragglers get the ride WiFi password read aloud, join, and pull the whole ride JSON from the leader's Nucleus — so apply is always the same path.
Nothing in the code filters nodes by channel NAME — checked in readLiveNodes, ConvoyNodeFilter and the mesh modules. The channel KEY restricts visibility at the radio.
Callsign ≤ 39 characters of A–Z a–z 0–9 space . - ' (Meshtastic long name max_size:40 is the strictest carrier; TAK callsign is 120). Written as the radio's long name at apply.

⭐⭐ THE TRAILHEAD RULE (Fred 09-23)
Every route has a trailhead, stored in its RECIPE as the anchor (anchorLat / anchorLon / anchorName) — it
travels with the route and becomes the trailhead &lt;wpt&gt; in the ride's GPX.
AI builder: already required — the rider saves the trailhead waypoint first; the recipe's anchor is it.
Route+ (manual): the FIRST point needs a trailhead waypoint within ½ mile — an EXISTENCE check; the point still snaps to the
trail. None → "turn on Draw and long-press to add a trailhead waypoint, then start your route again". At save the trailhead is
found again from the first point and written into the recipe (setRouteAnchor) — nothing stored in between, so discard has nothing new to clear.
Ride creation: trailhead in the recipe → use it. Otherwise a trailhead within ½ mile of the route's start (one = use, several = selector) is written into the recipe. None → back to the map to add one, then reselect the route.
The recipe is cleared to travel — every field is a value the rider chose. The narrative is NOT (it carries OSM feature names and classes) — the writer holds it back (INCLUDE_NARRATIVE = false) pending Fred.

⭐⭐⭐ THE NUCLEUS MODEL — settled 09-23 afternoon (Fred), sent to Nathan for Thursday
Names: network id = Meshtastic channel name = Wi-Fi SSID. Callsign = radio long name, always the LOCAL user's own GroupTrack value — never stored in a config file.
Everything lives on the Android until apply. Rides are created, emailed and stored on tablets.
Apply request = the network values + the requesting user's callsign. The unit applies Wi-Fi + radio, writes the callsign as long name, returns the result and the values it replaced (the tablet keeps them as the restore point). The tablet keeps the history; the unit keeps only the default + the last used.
TWO NETWORKS, never sorted out until today: a control network (GroupTrack, the default — to reach a unit and request configs) and a riding network (Group+6 per ride).
FOUR BOOT PROFILES, selectable: (1) GroupTrack default · (2) GroupTrack last used · (3) ATAK group · (4) Meshtastic local emergency net. "Last used" fixes the vehicle-power (lunch stop) problem; "default" is how a unit returns home.
Returning to default is the key command: the leader's end-of-ride track save ASKS (never automatic, never from a rider's save) + a Return Nucleus to GroupTrack defaults item in Work with Rides.
Tailnet = a VPN overlay (Tailscale/WireGuard) on the internet — reaches a unit from anywhere WITH internet; useless at a trailhead with no signal. It is not a second local network.
Wi-Fi password: ⭐ Fred: a real word of 8+ letters, new each ride (our proposal to Nathan). The newWifiPassword() generator changes to a word list.
Channel key = 32 random bytes = AES-256 ✅ (confirmed from the file).
owner_short not written. role: not important if the Nucleus keeps its own.
⚠ Straggler path changed: a Nucleus that keeps only default + last used cannot serve a ride file, so a latecomer gets the ride from another rider's or the leader's tablet, then applies normally.
⚠ Android: an app cannot read or silently use saved Wi-Fi; GroupTrack keeps its own list (from ride files) and asks Android to connect (system prompt). Device check still owed.

⭐⭐ THE RADIO → TICK HANDOFF, AND THE TAK PAYLOAD AGAINST IT (09-23 · UPDATED 09-28 — roles and callsign through the tick, PROVEN; see the 09-28 part below)
Radio path today (ConvoyViewModel.readLiveNodes, from Meshtastic's node DB fed by NodeInfo / Position / Telemetry): nodeId = !+hex
node number · callsign = radio long_name → short_name → !num · lat/lon = latitude_i × 1e-7, a fix timed before ride start is REJECTED
(relay rebroadcast) → last known · altitude_m = altitude × 3.28084 (⚠ FEET in a field named metres) · speed_mph COMPUTED over a
60 s window · heading = ground_track ÷ 1e5 · battery = telemetry · snr · lastSeen = lastHeard · cotType constant
a-f-G-U-C · then ConvoyNodeFilter (heard today, admission window). ⛔ BUG: a node with no fix and no last known position gets
the TABLET'S own GPS — your location on someone else's cart. The radio path CANNOT supply team, role, a device identity separate from the display name, or
the rider's callsign.
TAK payload — CONFIRMED against the fork's atak.proto: TAKPacket { is_compressed · contact
{callsign, device_callsign} · group {role: MemberRole, team: Team colour, default cyan} · status {battery} · oneof
pli {latitude_i, longitude_i ×1e-7, altitude "ATAK prefers HAE", speed, course whole degrees} | chat (GeoChat) |
detail (raw CoT) }. device_callsign IS the TAK uid (no separate uid field). No timestamp and no node number in the payload —
the node comes from the packet header; staleness must be judged by receive time + hop count.

⭐⭐⭐ TAK / GPS COEXISTENCE PLAN (Fred 09-23): map TAK into the existing fields; isolate the outliers
Principles. (1) TAK is ANOTHER SOURCE for the same map entry — not a new pipeline. (2) The old radio path is unchanged and keeps running.
(3) ONE entry per device, keyed by node number (from the packet header for TAK); each packet updates the fields it carries; the NEWEST value wins per field.
(4) TAK values are converted INTO THE EXISTING UNITS (feet, mph, degrees, percent) in ConvoyViewModel, so ConvoyScreen and
ConvoyEngine see nothing new. (5) New information is ADDED to ConvoyNode with defaults — nothing that builds a node today breaks.

O1 Device identity — contact.device_callsign (the TAK uid) has no field. → add takUid (default "") — needed by enrollment seen(takUid | nodeNum).

⭐⭐⭐ UPDATED 09-28 — ROLE AND CALLSIGN THROUGH THE TICK: PROVEN ON THE BENCH
PROVEN 09-28 Answers the 09-23 line above: "the radio path CANNOT supply team, role … or the rider's callsign".
What failed first, and why (so it is never re-tried):
The role in the radio's own TAK reports (Meshtastic TAK Identity, ModuleConfig.tak team/role by admin message): the T1000-Es on their current firmware ignore it — still role=TeamMember after the write and after a full power cycle. The Identity is documented for firmware 2.8; Fred will not move the radios to 2.8 (unpredictable). Commit 056ab376c, reverted by d6be6b3c2.
Custom tablet messages (a GroupTrack frame on PRIVATE_APP, request/reply schemes) — rejected by Fred as custom messaging between radio and device. Never applied.
Writing the role through the configurator's apply — a settings write and reboot per role change; device-dependent. Not pursued.
What works (Fred's idea): broadcast the role in a standard TAK POSITION REPORT that the TABLET fills in, and lift it from the report received. The radio only carries it; no settings, no firmware, no reboot, no custom messaging. Proven both ways (Droid 1 Team Lead / Droid 2 Forward Observer), then into lead/tail on both HUDs within a couple of seconds.
Mapping: Leader → TeamLead · Middle → RTO · Tail gunner → ForwardObserver · Rider → HQ (only for a reassignment to Rider) · TeamMember (the radios' own reports) and every other role are ignored on receipt, so a radio's own report can never erase a role. Blank role = Rider.
Only the three special roles broadcast. Schedule: every 30 s from check-in until 3 minutes after REC, then silent. Roles are fixed — changed only by a new assignment (which broadcasts the same way) — and cleared at END. No expiry.
The node array is the single source: my own role goes into the same role store as everyone else's (against my radio's number); every radio node takes its role from the store first; the tick assigns lead (via setLeadCart, only on change) and tail (tailNodeId) from the roles; the HUD, markers, map labels and SELECT CART display from the nodes. REC's lead question appears only while no lead is locked.
Callsign: the tablet-only node shows the rider's callsign (check-in, else profile) instead of the device model ("P50").
Trailhead order (operational): everybody checks in first thing (the check-in puts each radio on the ride network — until then it hears nothing); the special roles among the first; the ride starts when everyone has checked in.
Commits (09-28): 1a8d3329b callsign and ride role through the tick (display) · 43a6223cb receive side (TakRoleStore, TAKPOS lifts the role) · 48c2a81a3 role report test — proven · role-tick v2 (lead/tail from roles every tick) · 59b7ebb2e own role in the same store. Restore points: restore-2026-09-28-before-tickdata, …-before-taksend, …-before-roletick.
NEXT (09-29) the full schedule (every 30 s until 3 min after REC); reassignment incl. HQ = Rider; clear at END; blank = Rider on screen (drop "bare radio"/red); three timestamps (sent · received · applied, logged in absolute ms — Droid 2 is on another time zone) to measure each step. Watch: the TAK report the tablet fills carries no status (battery) — fine for roles, noted.

RIDEFILE-2026-09-22 — THE .convoy RIDE FILE, FORMAT 3 (the owning section)
⭐⭐⭐ A ride is a package of map, route and waypoint data with a leader and a date — and it is useful with NO network at all.
The file is self-contained: emailed, opened offline, ridden, forwarded. The network is a property the ride MAY carry so the group's radios can find each other.
Replaces ConvoyEventConfig's format 2, which was radio-first and could not express a ride without radios.
THE SECTIONS
Required: kind = "grouptrack.ride" and formatVersion = 3 (a HARD CUT — a 2.6 tablet refuses it plainly rather than half-importing) ·
ride (rideId UUID — the identity between tablets — name, date, startTime, description, zipCode, createdAt) ·
leader (name, callsign, orgName ONLY).
Optional, whole sections: network · rideData · map (bounds + maxZoom, so the receiver can fetch tiles; no tiles travel).
network = id (the GT id), baseVersion, and a block per transport — mesh (region, preset, hopLimit, txPower, channelName, key) and nucleus.
⭐ Fred 09-22: always write BOTH. No question at ride creation, no schema change — whichever hardware shows up at the trailhead finds what it needs.
That also removes the worst case: a leader who picked "mesh only" in March and arrives in June with a Nucleus.
rideData = ONE GPX document carrying the route as &lt;rte&gt; and the waypoints as &lt;wpt&gt;, plus routeGeomHash, routeName and routeNotes (JSON — GroupTrack's own, no GPX equivalent).
Recorded tracks, if they ever travel, stay &lt;trk&gt;.
THE RULES
⛔ Nothing OSM-derived travels. The leader's own drawn route and waypoints are theirs to send; the trail layer underneath is not, and the receiver has its own copy.
⭐ ONLY ROUTES TRAVEL (Fred 09-22). A track never goes in a ride file — it is converted to a route first. Distilled to a polyline: the drawn line, simplified, not the recipe and not every GPS sample.
Simplify ONCE at creation, not at send, and store the distilled route as the route — otherwise the same ride produces a different hash every time it is sent.
⭐ Identity is (type, geom_hash), NEVER the hash alone. A route converted from a track has the same hash as that track — correct and useful — so import must match on type as well, or an incoming route could match a local track and vanish.
Unknown sections are KEPT on import, so a forwarded file stays complete for the next rider.
Whole sections are optional; fields inside them are not. If network is present it is complete.
The ride id is the identity. Re-importing the same file UPDATES that ride rather than making a second one — a leader can send a correction and riders simply take it.
⭐ NO EMAIL FIELD IN THE FILE (Fred 09-22, KISS). It is always sent from someone's email, and the client already shows who from. A forward is just a forward — nobody's address is ever added.
Expiration survives — 30 days past the ride date — EXCEPT a ride-specific network, which dies with the ride. Org and leader networks never expire; only rotation replaces them.
Dropped from format 2: hardwareId as primary key (a ride is not owned by a radio) · deviceId, hardwareModel, firmwareVersion · organizerUserId, organizerPhone, first/last name · the flat LoRa fields (they move inside network.mesh).
DOC: GroupTrack_ConvoyFileFormat3_2026-09-22_v1.html
THE RECEIVING SIDE — proposed, NOT yet decided
Open (zip or plain, detected by content) → check formatVersion → validate the WHOLE file before a single write (all or nothing — no ghosts) →
show the rider what arrived and let them accept → on accept: network, ride, then GPX (route dedupes by hash+type; waypoints by position and name) →
no enrollment (that happens at network login) → map bounds become an OFFER to download, never an automatic download → unknown sections stored with the ride.
OPEN: does an arriving ride import silently, or wait at a review screen? Claude argues for the review — it is the rider's tablet, and it is where an unwanted ride is declined rather than landing as a ghost.
OPEN: zipped or plain · the simplify tolerance (a few metres is invisible on a trail map and cuts size hugely; too much loses switchbacks).
NUCLEUS-2026-09-22 — NATHAN'S ANSWER, AND THE DELIVERY PARADOX
✅ SETTLED: plain CoT XML (TAK protocol v0) is the format. Nathan, 09-22: compression is zstd but handled internally by the takpacket SDK; he uses takproto to translate. Forming v0 XML CoT is "pretty easy to format, human readable, and gets funnelled directly into the takpacket system on the Nucleus."
That removes protobuf and compression work from our side entirely.
It also validates the profile: a CoT event carries the uid, the callsign, and __group with a team colour and a role — exactly what the first-launch profile now stores.
⭐ Role mapping: our leader broadcasts as TAK's Team Lead, everyone else as Team Member; GroupTrack's four roles stay local on the enrollment.
THE PARADOX (Fred 09-22): Nathan offered Tailscale push — every Nucleus runs a tailscale instance, so configs could be pushed over the internet with no email step.
But what we deliver IS the network the group will use. If delivery depends on that network, nothing can be configured until it already exists.
And GroupTrack's groups ROTATE — different riders every ride — so any push model means maintaining a list of boxes, and the day it is wrong someone arrives configured for last month's ride.
⭐ PULL SCALES, PUSH DOES NOT: the leader publishes once, each rider's tablet fetches when they join. Nobody maintains a roster of devices.
⭐⭐ DELIVERY AND APPLY ARE TWO DIFFERENT MOMENTS.
Delivery happens well before the ride — days or weeks, over the internet (our API, or an emailed file). Nothing on the radio changes.
Apply happens AT the ride — at the trailhead, often with no signal. The tablet configures the Nucleus locally, and only then does the box join.
So Natak's API should keep them apart: one call to STORE a config on the box, another to ACTIVATE a stored one. A rider can then carry three rides and pick the right one at the trailhead with nothing but the tablet.
The tailnet's right job: at the site, reaching the STRAGGLERS who never applied — the rider who did not open the email, or joined that morning. A fallback, not the delivery mechanism.
THREE ANSWERS OWED BY NATAK: (1) which port and transport CoT arrives on, and whether it takes v0 XML directly; (2) whether a Nucleus ships already joined to a tailnet, or we need an auth key; (3) whether the config API sets the SSID and password, or they come preset — that last one decides whether GroupTrack can generate the IP half of a network itself. Reply drafted 09-22; Nathan is building radios for a few days.

THE ENTRY PATH — settled 09-22 after a long back-and-forth
⭐⭐ A ride is ALWAYS made FROM a route. There is no empty "create a ride" anywhere, because a route has to be found before there is anything to make a ride from.
The map's search already does the finding — it takes a route name, a track name, or a place, and it is always available on the map. Nothing to build.
So: search by name → the route is on the map → tap it → detail panel → ADD A RIDE → the form opens with it.
ADD vs CHANGE: Add a ride is initiated from a route or track on the map. Change a ride is initiated from my open rides on the menu. Two doors, two jobs, no conditional wording on the panel.
Tracks get the same button, with a convert step first (only routes travel): show the track's name, let the rider change it, convert, then open the form. ConvoyArtifactOps.toRoute(trackId) already exists.
⛔ The planner does NOT arm anything on arrival. Route mode is a live session activity, armed only by Route+ or Draw — arming it from a menu would bring back the stuck-arm behaviour that took a week to find.
RIDEMODEL-2026-09-22 — THE IDENTITY CHAIN, THE RIDE, AND THE ROLES (the owning section)
⭐⭐⭐ Read this before touching profile, ride, org, role or radio-apply code. Everything below was decided
09-22 and is committed in the device tables. It supersedes any earlier note that ride creation picks an organizer, that
is_organizer is set by creating a ride, or that callsigns are unique.
THE CHAIN — decided once, inherited down
Leader = organizer = a role on the profile. They are not three things. GroupTrack exists so riders can find
leaders and follow their rides, so "I lead rides" is a role a rider switches on — and switching it on is what opens up
organizations and networks.
Profile → leader → organization → ride. A rider may belong to several organizations
(org_members already allows it). Ride creation asks one thing: which of my organizations is this ride
under, or none — and the network follows from the answer.
Ride creation resolves only the leader, and the leader is always you (2.7). There is nobody else's organizer on
your tablet to select. Choosing another club's leader arrives at 3.0, when the server can supply them.
Two doors into leader setup, one room: choosing Leader as the usual role on the profile, or creating a
ride when there is no setup yet. Both run the same step in profile maintenance.
Switching the usual role back to Rider does NOT remove the leader setup. The role is a default for rides; the
setup is a standing arrangement with a network riders may already hold. Removing it is an explicit act.
NETWORKS — generated at creation, in exactly three places
A network (⭐ riders never see the words "config" or "channel") is generated when its owner is created, and never
again for that owner — only replaced by rotation:
An organization is added → the org's standing network. The adder becomes its owner in org_members.
A rider chooses "my own network" in leader setup → the leader's standing network.
A leader asks for a unique network for one ride → that ride's own.
Every generation produces the same set: the GT id (GT + 9 characters — the channel name and the
network name, checked against local configs), a 32-byte key from a secure source, the ride values (region, preset,
hop limit, role, frequency slot 0 so the frequency derives from the name), TX power at or below the licence-free limit,
and the base version it was built on.
⭐ A leader who inherits the org's network generates nothing. A plain rider needs no network of their own — they
receive one in each ride file. Configs are immutable: rotation creates a new id and key and retires the old.
⭐⭐ ONE WRITE PATH. Profile maintenance is the only module that creates a rider, an org, a leader setting or a
network. Ride creation asks the questions and hands off; it generates nothing itself except a ride's own network. That is
what enforces the TX cap, the id check and the base version once instead of in every screen.
THE DISTRIBUTED MODEL — other people are ride data, not records
⭐⭐⭐ On a rider's tablet, other people exist only inside the ride. The organizer's own tablet holds the real
entities — their profile, leader setup, org and network. Every other tablet gets what it needs inside the ride file:
the organizer's name, the org's name, the network. No organizer or org records are created on the receiving side.
So a ride is self-contained — emailed, opened offline, ridden, with nothing external required. That is what lets
the app work in a distributed model before the full structure exists at 3.0.
In the tables (37153e7d0): rides.organizer_name (required) and org_name
(optional — independent leaders have none) come from the file; organizer_id is set only when you are the
organizer. enrollments.callsign (required) and display_name likewise; user_id is
set only on your own enrollment.
⭐ Callsigns may repeat. Three riders called Steve S. can all ride — uniqueness would reject the second at the
trailhead, which is exactly when it must not fail. Riders are matched by device: the TAK uid, or the node number for
a radio-only rider (indexes on both). Telling them apart on screen is the ride's job at display time — Steve S. · 7A3F.
ROLES ON THE TRAIL — four rules
Leader, middle and tail gunner are single-holder roles, one each per ride. Rider is the default and unlimited.
Release, then claim. The holder sets themselves back to rider, leaving the role vacant; then another rider claims it.
A claim on an occupied role is refused. Nobody holds two at once.
⭐⭐ Only a person changes a role. No timeouts, no automatic demotion, no inference from missing packets —
a quiet radio means nothing (a rider behind a ridge for ten minutes is still out front doing the job).
Leaving the ride releases the role. A rider who drops out is out of the group with no role. A dead tablet is handled
by someone else marking them gone — the same deliberate act.
Enforce in code, not as a database constraint. A constraint would refuse a claim whenever a release packet went
missing, on exactly the day it matters. No schema change — enrollments.role holds all four, and the
roles are reflected from broadcast data.
The ride's owner never changes. The organizer is who created it; the lead is operational.
THE PROFILE — created at first launch
Created before the map opens, right after ConvoyAuthorityGate, because the callsign has to be in
every TAK packet from the first broadcast — it cannot wait for a ride. On an upgrade it is pre-filled from the V2
profile (ConvoyUserStore / convoy_users.json: userId, first/last, email, cellPhone, vehicleType;
ORGANIZER → is_organizer; knownDevices → radios) and the rider confirms it and adds a callsign.
Required: callsign and email. Held: usual role, vehicle, team colour — the defaults each enrollment is seeded from.
⭐⭐ PRIVACY — the sentence that is true for the whole app: nothing is sent to GroupTrack unless the rider
shares, and sharing sends only their ride and their email. The callsign and position go out over the radio to the riders
in range; a ride file goes wherever the leader sends it. On the profile screen: "This stays on your tablet. GroupTrack
uses it only to identify you to your group and to share rides you send." On the share control: "Sharing sends your
ride to the GroupTrack community, with your email address so each rider counts once. Nothing else about you is sent."
The Play Data safety form is revisited when contributions ship — check the user-initiated-transfer and
end-to-end-encrypted exemptions against the form's current wording rather than answering "no data collected" on the
strength of there being no server.
THE API TOUCHPOINTS — what the rebuilt radio code may call
One direction only: identity and rides are written first, and the radio is handed the result. Every call is
com.grouptrack.core — pure Kotlin, no Android, no database — with SQLite implementations in the app.
Identity: ensureOwnProfile() · setLeader(on) · addOrganization(...) ·
joinOrganization(id) / leave(id) · useOwnNetwork() · rotate(owner).
Rides: create(name, date, route?, trailhead?, orgId?, uniqueNetwork) · export(rideId) ·
import(file) · enrol(rideId) at network login · seen(rideId, takUid|nodeNum, callsign)
on every packet · claim(role) / release() / markGone(enrolId).
Radio — four calls replacing the cluster: snapshot() (was ConvoyRadioManager writing JSON
files → now radio_snapshots) · apply(network, identity, role) (ONE call replacing five screens:
apply list, apply radio, reconnect wait, verify, master success, plus master.cfg and ConvoyProfileBuilder) ·
verify(network, identity) · restore(snapshotId) · identity() — long name = callsign,
so the rider never types a long name again.
⭐⭐ The radio layer never reads the database and never generates anything. It is handed a
NetworkConfig row and an identity. That is what stops ConvoyMasterConfig.load(context) reappearing
in every screen.

⛔ REJECTED — AND WHY (09-21)
Staging a config on the Nucleus until the ride — rides are set months ahead; one staged slot would tie the node up.
Complete-without-saving endpoint — the dry run at the site validates.
Versioned configs for rotation — replaced by remove it and a new one is generated.
A per-ride network password — excessive for a private mesh with no internet and only GroupTrack on it (Fred).
A QR code as the way onto the network — riders log in; the channel is data; a QR only represents it.
No radio config in the ride object (v22) — reversed by belt and suspenders: it silently assumed a Nucleus was always present.
TAK first — reversed to config first: the lighter model is specified, and the heavy lifting is config and connection.
Prying the old code apart — build over instead: the hard cut removes the only reason to preserve old behaviour.
A downloadable plugin now — components designed for separation instead; two installs and an inter-app API are complexity ten users don't need.
Firmware updates — the T1000-E doesn't function on newer firmware.
A pre-built fallback port for TAK — no more variables: port 78, and T7 decides.
AI-generated ads; auto-posting to groups — see MARKETING-2026-09-21.

00-2026-09-17 — WHY EVERY NON-UTAH IMPORT WAS CRASHING
⭐ CAPTURED 09-21 (said 09-17, missing until now) — IMPORT SPEED IS THE NETWORK, NOT THE CODE. The 27–31 minute
Utah runs versus ~10 minutes were the tablet's WiFi band: 2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz (Fred). The largeHeap suspicion was wrong.
⛔ Rule: measure the link before measuring the code — steps 7–8 download ~1.2 GB.
⭐⭐⭐ THE REAL CAUSE OF THE IMPORT CRASHES — AND IT IS NOT THE ONE
GUARDED THIS MORNING.
Importing NEW HAMPSHIRE on Droid 1 (29321125) died on the LAST of its six
stages:
OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate a 360 byte allocation
with 1670512 free bytes and 1631KB until OOM,
target footprint 268435456, growth limit 268435456
  at CursorWindow.nativeGetString
  at HomeStateImportController$executeRun$2$changed$1
⛔ A DIFFERENT OOM FROM loadRings. It failed on a
360 BYTE allocation against a FULL 256 MB heap — death by accumulation,
not one giant read — and the failing frame is a DATABASE CURSOR, not
readText. ⚠ OOMGUARD's heap check never even runs on this
path.
⛔⛔ AND THE APP WAS DOING SOMETHING MEANINGLESS TO GET THERE. The
ownership data is UTAH SITLA (OWNFETCH-2026-09-02). The only
test at HomeStateImportController:560 was whether the FILE EXISTS —
not whether it is relevant. So a New Hampshire import:
DOWNLOADED 78 MB of UTAH ownership data over the network;
parsed it into rings;
built grid, which indexes a ring into EVERY cell it spans (up to
20,000 cells per ring);
walked the full trail cursor with both structures still held;
and classified New Hampshire trails against Utah polygons.
⚠ CLASSIFY4-2026-09-02 made the cursor half heavier: the query
used to read only rows with no usable carto_code — ~28,000 of
146,000 — and now reads EVERY ROW. Five times the cursor work against a
heap already carrying rings and grid.
⭐⭐⭐ SO IT WAS NEVER A LOW-MEMORY-DEVICE PROBLEM. IT WAS EVERY
RIDER OUTSIDE UTAH, on any device, with survival depending on how much heap
they happened to have. Droid 1 has 256 MB and still died.
⛔ AND IT LEFT NO TRACE. The crash is on the LAST stage, so the manifest
was never written. A rider who tried, crashed and gave up appears nowhere except
Crashlytics.
✅ WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED 09-17 — and the numbers that verified it
⛔ OWNSTATE (the state gate) WAS REVERTED. It stopped
non-Utah imports dead — the screen never left the selection panel. Replaced by:
MarkerWhatVerified
OWNSKIP-2026-09-17One condition. Non-Utah: skip the 78 MB Utah download and place an EMPTY file. run()'s existing length() &lt; 1024 check then returns -1, which the caller ALREADY treats as a COMPLETED stage with zero records. No new path, no new sentinel, loop untouched.⭐ New Hampshire clean on Droid 1
STREAMRINGS-2026-09-17THE ACTUAL FIX. loadRings streams the file instead of readText(). Three helpers — scanTo, readQuoted, parseRingsStream. ⭐ Ends at bracket depth zero rather than looking ahead for the next "owner" — which is what actually closes a coordinate array.⭐⭐ Utah, see below
LARGEHEAP REVERTEDIt was insurance against a Utah crash that has never happened, and it was the prime suspect for slower imports — the download-heavy steps 7 and 8 (1.2 GB) are exactly where a bigger heap costs GC time.⚠ Inconclusive: 27 min before, 31 after
OOMGUARD heap pre-checkREMOVED as part of STREAMRINGS. ⛔ It existed because the read could not fit; with streaming it CAN, so leaving it would SKIP files we are now able to process. ⚠ The OOM BACKSTOP at the call site stays.—
