⭐⭐⭐ THE 2.6g HANDOFF STRUCTURE — CONFIG + GPX, NO BACKEND REQUIRED. HANDOFF-2026-09-20
⭐⭐ THE DATA MODEL, PROCESS AND FLOWS — GroupTrack side. RIDECONFIG-2026-09-20 (UPDATED 2026-09-21 — the agreed model)
⭐⭐⭐ UPDATED 2026-09-21 — THE AGREED MODEL. Where it differs from the 09-20 text below, this governs.
Full detail, diagrams and the tick-list: GroupTrack_RideConfigPlanning_2026-09-21_v53.html (Agreement 1) and
GroupTrack_Nucleus_ImplementationTargets_2026-09-21_v22.html. The essentials, embedded:
THE FLOWS (Agreement 1)
A · Create — the leader builds the ride: name, date, trailhead, route (created in GroupTrack, or a track converted to one), waypoints, the radio config. Only a complete ride can be sent; saving is always possible (loose check), distributing is strict (to build — V3's SAVE AS PENDING in ConvoyCreateRideScreen.kt:81–83 is the pattern).
B · Distribute — the leader emails it (email until V3). The leader's part ends there.
B2 · The rider receives and imports it — the ride object, then the GPX (route + waypoints), the map corridor queued along the route, the login and config stored, not applied. No radio is touched.
C · At the site, the leader selects the config and applies it to their own radio; with a Nucleus, sends it with the ride name + dry run → apply (node backs up to history first, labelled by ride name).
D · Riders — already on it? ready. Belt: select the ride's config in GroupTrack, back up, apply. Suspenders: with a Nucleus, log in to its network and it applies to any radio not yet on it.
E · The ride · F · Restore — from the node's history; each radio from its own backup.
THE RULES
⛔ A radio is only ever written by an apply. Every apply begins with a backup — a snapshot of every field it will change; restore writes it back.
Two ways to start an apply (selected in GroupTrack · signing in to a Nucleus network), three implementations (Bluetooth · USB · Nucleus — for a Nucleus the node's history is the backup and the dry run is the compare).
⛔ HARD CUT to a new base config: radio config = base + ride values. Arrives with 2.7, never coexists with 2.6. The default net is renamed to the GT standard — the rename fences off every pre-2.7 radio (different name → different frequency) until it is upgraded.
Upgrade a radio to 2.7 = confirm firmware 2.6.11.60ec05e (no firmware updates — the T1000-E doesn't function on newer firmware) → settings-only factory reset → base + the default net → verify; the owner's radio name is read first and put back.
The Nucleus is an enhancement, never a dependency — a ride works over LoRa alone.
IDENTITY — ⛔ SUPERSEDES THE 09-20 "network ≠ channel" CORRECTION BELOW
One generated id — GT + nine random [A-Z0-9] = the Meshtastic channel name = the WiFi network name (Fred 09-21: the network id is not typed; it is derived, equal to the channel id). Eleven characters respects Meshtastic's limit; frequency slot 0 derives the frequency from it. Today the live generator is the ride config ("CONVOY-" + 4) and the default is the fixed "Convoy".
Networks shown as long description (in 2.7, the leader's name) + the id's last four — Fred · 9QXR.
The callsign is the rider's GroupTrack user id, carried in every TAK packet. The radio's long name belongs to its owner (Fred &amp; June) — no config writes it: remove ConvoyProfileBuilder.kt:184 and the wizard's rename prompt (history: it existed because the captured master's long name !1d5bdc79 was stamped on every radio).
The channel is data; a QR only represents it, for entering it where GroupTrack isn't.
OWNERSHIP
2.7: two configs — the shipped default net (fixed GT id, key effectively public, like LongFast; every radio's home between rides) and one event ride config named for its leader. A rider holds the event configs their leaders sent.
V3 target: an org's standing config for all its rides · a leader's assigned config · a unique ride config only on request · the default net last — resolved at apply time. Configs are never deactivated (reused); rotation = remove it and a new one is generated; restore offers only configs still in the library.
The network login is part of the owner's config, not per ride, and travels in the ride object — accepted risk (Fred): private mesh, no internet, GroupTrack only.
The ride config file is today's .convoy JSON, extended — add formatVersion, role, frequencySlot, baseVersion, gpx; drop BW/SF/CR and the leader's device details. ConvoyTransferRideScreen (today's distribution) is rewritten, not deleted.
NATAK — API 0.8.0 REVIEWED, TAK ANSWERED
API (github.com/Natak-Mesh/V3_OS/docs/API.md): nucleusd FastAPI, JSON under /api/v1, nginx 80 → 8080, node at 10.20.&lt;id&gt;.1, no authentication. Config get/put, apply?dry_run, radio config read/apply (async, op-status, 30–120 s, a restart per settings group), 11 radio fields (owner/owner_short never sent by us), channel_name 1–11, tx_power 0–30 dBm, frequency_slot 0 = from the name, channel URL, QR; meshtasticd on TCP 4403; messaging multicast 239.10.10.60:17020 (differs from the earlier 224.10.10.1:17012). Repeatable from Android — plain HTTP, and admin protobufs for radios; no CLI needed.
The radios are the bridge; each Nucleus rebroadcasts LoRa ⇄ IP (packet-level — to confirm). Natak stops broadcast storms; GroupTrack's layer 2 drops duplicates by packet id.
TAK compression, answered: ATAK Plugin V2 (firmware PR #10105, April 2026) — TAKPacketV2 on its own port (78), a flags byte (0xFF raw · 0x00–0x3F zstd dictionary id), compression by TAKPacket-SDK in the app (zstd level 19, 512 KB / 4 KB dictionaries), never larger than raw. ⛔ Dictionary versions are wire-incompatible (SDK 0.9.0) and fail silently — pin and upgrade in lockstep. The fork carries V1 atak.proto (port 72, unishox2 — overflow and expansion problems); upstream Android is on SDK 0.9.1. ⚠ Firmware 2.6.11 predates V2 → test T7.
Natak asks: N1 history on every apply (both halves) · N2 history endpoints · N3 radio fields inside the node config · N4 a label (the ride name) · N5 accept our network name + login · N6 a token on writes · N7 failed-apply behaviour. Questions: packet-level rebroadcast? · 4403 across the mesh? · which multicast group carries SA? · SDK version, V1/V2, lockstep? · network name/password limits? · is a tablet's gateway its node? · who issues tokens?
⭐⭐ CAPTURED 09-21 — PLANNING FROM THE 09-17 → 09-20 TRAVEL CONVERSATIONS (by phone, not written into this
section at the time). Kept here because this section owns them; where 09-21 changed an answer, it says so.
09-18 — how a radio connects, and who configures it
⛔ The T1000-E has NO WiFi — its nRF52840 is Bluetooth/Thread/Zigbee only. "Wi-Fi positioning" on some trackers is
access-point sniffing for location, not a network connection. ESP32 radios have WiFi (Meshtastic network config, reached over TCP).
⛔⛔ THE WiFi MODE TRAP on every WiFi-capable radio: wifi_enabled disables Bluetooth. A radio that joins a
network that isn't there is unreachable and needs a physical reset. ⭐ USB configuration is the escape hatch — the strongest
argument for USB (now one of the apply's three implementations).
Android as a hotspot to configure a radio was explored (Fred: connect droid and radio, reconfigure, reboot onto the ride
network; "we only need that hotspot for config"). Outcome that day: USB is the best solution — it sets the radio's connection
from the tablet's current network without the one-or-the-other hotspot problem.
⭐ DEVICE POLICY (Fred): GroupTrack targets no specific radio — any Meshtastic-compatible device, any connection
type; models are examples, never requirements. Preferred connection is IP, to the tablet or to a Nucleus. A radio connects to
the tablet by Bluetooth or USB and is configured when the user signs in to a WiFi network. (09-21: automatic setup is T1000-E only
on the website until T2 proves channel data on other radios.)
⛔ TX POWER (Fred): "the crime is not the radio, it is using it above a certain output level." Owning high-power hardware
is legal; transmitting above the licence-free limit is not — and since the app now writes the config, a ride config that raised
TX power would make the APP the cause. Rule: TX power at or below the licence-free limit for the region; the app never raises it.
The app controls the frequency of updates, not the radio config (Fred 09-18: TAK updates from the app) — the seed of the
09-21 "config first, built for TAK" order.
09-18 — identity and the system of record
⭐ GroupTrack is the SYSTEM OF RECORD for LoRa channel identity — the app generates it; Nathan's node stores it and
provisions itself from it. Channel name = network name, same keys (09-18), confirmed 09-21 as one generated GT id.
Superseded: keys derived from one password via a KDF — 09-21 settled that keys are random values in the config.
The ride record today holds organizer, club and ride identity together; it needs splitting into a config record owned by one of
those three (09-18) — refined 09-21 into the ownership model (2.7: two configs; V3: org / leader / unique).
09-18 "riders always assume the config of the network they log into; USB is what leaders use to set their radio" —
refined 09-21 into belt and suspenders and the apply's three implementations (Bluetooth, USB, Nucleus).
09-20 — the gate before any of it is built
⛔⛔ THESE COME FIRST (Fred 09-20): unify the event structure AND the APIs across both sides; agree the ownership and process
rules — BEFORE Nathan builds his config API, and before level-1 communication separation and the move to TAK-formatted messaging.
Hand Nathan GroupTrack's structure first, so his endpoint accepts what the app produces — no translation layer. 09-21's
Agreement 1 (flows + ownership) is this gate.
⭐ The structures are standardized so values can be explored with other LoRa/WiFi vendors (Fred 09-20) — the config and
ride-config formats are GroupTrack's, not Natak-specific.
The API definition exists so GroupTrack can update the Raspberry (Nucleus) config.
The design documents sent to Nathan
GroupTrack_CommsDesign_2026-09-15_v7.html (level-1 design, sent to Natak) · GroupTrack_NucleusIntegration_2026-09-17_v3.html
(the integration and the API definition he was asked for) · GroupTrack_RideConfigPlanning_2026-09-20_v2.html (48-field contract,
TAK classification, compression questions) → now GroupTrack_RideConfigPlanning_2026-09-21_v53.html.
⛔⛔ CORRECTED 09-20 — WE DO NOT OWN THE CHANNEL ID. HARD STOP FROM MESHTASTIC.
⛔ SUPERSEDED 09-21 (Fred): the network id is the channel id — one generated value, GT + nine characters, inside Meshtastic's 11-character limit. See the UPDATED 09-21 block above.
An earlier draft of this section asserted "network ID = channel
ID, one value". THAT IS WRONG. The channel name is Meshtastic's — its length,
format and semantics are theirs, and they can change. We cannot declare a rule
about a value we do not control.
⚠ rides.channel_name varchar(11) is a SYMPTOM of that, not a
choice — the column was sized to Meshtastic's limit.
THREE DISTINCT VALUES. Only one is ours to name.
ValueWho sees itRule
LONG DESCRIPTION⭐ Rider, on every screen and panelOURS. What a rider reads. Always a long description in GroupTrack.
CHANNEL IDNobody⭐ AUTO-GENERATED: GT as the first two characters, then a system-generated unique id. Sized to fit Meshtastic. Never typed, never displayed.
NETWORK ID + PASSWORDRider, once⭐⭐ BOOTSTRAP ONLY — see below
⭐⭐ GENERATING THE CHANNEL ID REMOVES THE TRUNCATION TRAP ENTIRELY. An
11-character limit does not matter when the value is generated to fit rather than
derived from something a human typed. And it protects us if Meshtastic changes
the limit — only the generator moves.
🔴 OPEN: what makes the unique id unique, and across what scope? Two
clubs generating GT ids independently must not collide — either
central issuance, or enough entropy that collision is negligible.
⭐⭐ THE NETWORK ID AND PASSWORD ARE BOOTSTRAP ONLY
They matter for ONE thing: getting a device onto the IP network. After
that the config comes down and does the rest.
⭐ So a rider NEVER needs the channel ID — it arrives inside the config.
And they never need the long description to connect; that is display only.
The network credentials are the only value that has to travel ahead of
time.
⚠ Which also means the network ID need not be short or memorable in the same
way a trailhead password would — it is typed once at setup, not recited
across a car park.
⚠ THE KEYS ARE DERIVED, NOT SHARED. A WPA2 passphrase and a Meshtastic
PSK have different formats and lengths — they cannot be the same value.
One password feeds a KDF; each transport gets a correctly formatted key.
⛔ The derivation must be identical on every build and VERSIONED FROM DAY
ONE — two riders on different releases deriving different PSKs from the same
password is a silent, total failure.
THE DATA MODEL — one record, three owners
⭐ A RIDE is an EVENT. A CONFIG is a NETWORK IDENTITY. A ride REFERENCES a
config. Today they are conflated — channel_name/channel_psk
live per-ride, so a club cannot hold a permanent identity reused across
rides. The owner tiers are already modelled
(organizer_id NOT NULL, org_id nullable).
OwnerTenure
Club / orgPermanent, reserved
Ride leaderPermanent, reserved — belongs to the PERSON, across clubs
One-time rideExpires. rides.expires_at already exists and is NOT NULL.
🔴 OPEN: precedence. A ride referencing a club config AND holding its
own — which wins? State the rule; do not let it be inferred.
⭐ CONFIG NAMING — and why it makes RESTORE free
Configs are saved under RIDE NAME + DATE.
⭐⭐ SO "THE PRIOR CONFIG" IS NOT A SPECIAL CASE — it is the previous entry
in the list, and RESTORE IS THE SAME OPERATION AS APPLY. No undo mechanism to
build or maintain. A rider's own home setup is just another named config
("My radio, 2026-09-20") sitting alongside "Sand Hollow, 03 Oct". Going home
is selecting it.
⚠ Requires two things: the archive must capture what the RIDER actually had
(not just what the ride set), and names must stay distinguishable — ride name
plus date handles repeats a year apart.
⭐⭐ WHY THE IMAGE MATTERS
A named config holding only the fields WE set gives a rider back a partial
radio. The IMAGE gives them the whole device.
ConvoyWriteArchiveScreen already captures
localConfig + channelSet with maxChannels,
longName and deviceProfile — the full picture.
⛔ AND THAT IS ALSO WHAT BINDS IT TO A DEVICE. The 09-17 finding: the
apply method builds from a saved T1000-E image and injects values, so applying it
elsewhere writes one device's identity onto another. The image is what gives a
real restore AND what makes it device-specific. Both at once.

⭐⭐⭐ THE LOCAL CONFIG STORE — a local version of the hosted DB
A rider may receive a config a MONTH OR TWO before the ride.
They store it; they do not apply it.
⛔ SO RECEIVE AND APPLY ARE SEPARATE OPERATIONS. Today they are one
action. Importing a config must leave it stored and inert; applying it is
a later, deliberate step.
⭐⭐ THAT STORE IS A LOCAL VERSION OF THE HOSTED DATABASE — received
configs with their names, dates, owners, expiry, and which one is active.
The backend, when it returns, DELIVERS INTO the same store rather than
replacing it. ⭐ Which is why the store should be built NOW: everything else
hangs off it, and the interim email path fills the same table the backend will.
⚠ And expiry matters more than it first appeared. A rider holding three
months of configs needs stale ones to disappear — expires_at already
models it.
⭐ INTERIM DELIVERY BY EMAIL — before the backend
GPX for tracks and waypoints goes by email and is loaded before the
ride, through the import process that already works. ⭐ Maps follow the
geometry as they already do, so nothing new is needed for them.
⚠ Email attachments land in Downloads and the SAF picker reaches them —
the same path proven with 90 tracks on 09-16.
⛔ DECIDE WHETHER THE CONFIG TRAVELS WITH THE GPX. It could — but a
config carries derived keys, and an emailed key is forwardable and sits in an
inbox. State the choice rather than letting it happen.
⭐⭐ THREE PATHS TO A CONFIGURED RADIO — and the preferred one
⭐⭐⭐ THE PREFERRED SOLUTION IS THE NUCLEUS-BASED IP ATTACH.
The others are fallbacks that must exist so nobody is stranded.
PathNeeds
⭐⭐PULL OVER THE IP NETWORK — join, config comes down, appliedPREFERRED. A Nucleus present and the rider connected. ⭐ This is why the Natak work matters.
⭐APPLY FROM MY DEVICE — config received ahead and storedThe local store, filled by email today or the backend later. Works with no Nucleus at all.
⚠APPLY FROM ANY DEVICE — attach the radio, apply, hand it back⭐ Physical access ONLY. Any Android can configure any radio.
⭐ THE THIRD PATH GUARANTEES NOBODY IS STRANDED and costs nothing — it
is a consequence of how apply already works, not something to build. A leader can
configure a whole group from one device: collect radios, apply, return them.
⚠ Ugly, and not the plan. Fred: "hopefully we use network
configs."
⭐ AND IT DOES NOT BREAK THE AUTHORITY RULE. Nothing is pushed over a
network — someone physically attaches a radio. Possession is the consent.
⚠ Two apply targets, same operation:
TargetHow

NucleusApplies to the Pi's own config and reboots. ⛔ Over USB or IP — METHOD IS NATHAN'S, they are his devices.

⭐ THE FLOWS
F1 — CREATE CONFIG (leader, Mesh Radio menu)
Build a file holding the config info: shared network/channel identity, derived
keys, region, modem preset, hop limit, and whatever position parameters survive
the TAK move. Saved under ride name + date, owned by club, leader or ride.
F2 — APPLY CONFIG (Mesh Radio menu)
List available configs → select one → archive current state first → apply
to the radio, and/or to the Raspberry through the API.
F3 — REQUEST CONFIG OVER THE NETWORK ⭐⭐ THE AUTHORITY RULE
⛔ NOBODY PUSHES. The rider REQUESTS; the leader's node RESPONDS. The
request is the consent, and no endpoint exists for a stranger to reconfigure
someone's radio.
Rider connects to the network — they already hold the name and password.
Rider requests the config from the leader's node.
Node returns it.
Rider's device applies it to itself and its radio — archiving first.
⚠ The bootstrap is unchanged: name and password must reach the rider
BEFORE they can connect. Ride definition, distributed ahead — a file today,
the backend eventually.
F4 — RESTORE
⭐ Select an earlier named config and apply it. Same flow as F2. Nothing
extra exists.
🔴 THE API DEFINITION — what is required of the Nucleus
RequirementNotes
READServe the current ride config on request⭐ THE ONE RIDERS USE. F3 depends entirely on it.
WRITEAccept a network identity; provision the node AND its attached radioLeader provisioning their OWN node only
ARCHIVE + RESTORE⭐ Same pattern as ours: save prior state, be able to reapply it⛔ METHOD IS NATHAN'S — they are his devices. He chooses which backup parameters make a full reapply.
AUTHOn write and restore⚠ He flagged that internet-facing security has not been a focus
RESULTAtomic success/failure⛔ Partial application is the dangerous state — his node holds TWO things (WiFi mesh identity AND the radio), so a half-restore is a node split across two networks
⭐⭐ STATE THE RESTORE REQUIREMENT AS AN OUTCOME, NOT A FIELD LIST:
applying an archived config must return the node to a WORKING state on its
previous network — not merely the same values. That is testable, and it
leaves the method entirely to him.
⭐ And named configs make the ask SMALLER than "build me an undo" — he
needs the same named list, because applying an older entry IS the restore.
🔴 OPEN FOR NATHAN: does the node keep ONE prior config or a HISTORY?
One is simpler; a history matches what GroupTrack already does.
Bring the V3 schema's ride/config shape into 2.6g as a FILE
FORMAT the app produces and consumes. The ride definition then stands alone —
and the backend becomes a DELIVERY MECHANISM for something that already works
without it.

⛔⛔ THE AUTHORITY RULE — THE RIDER REQUESTS, THE LEADER RESPONDS
Fred 09-20: "the leader can't — the user has to REQUEST a config
and update from the leader after network connection."
⭐⭐ NOBODY PUSHES A CONFIG ONTO SOMEONE ELSE'S DEVICE. The request IS
the consent, and there is no endpoint a stranger can use to reconfigure your
radio. Same shape as joining a wifi network: you connect, then you ask for
what you need. Nothing arrives unbidden.
THE SEQUENCE:
Rider connects to the network — they already have the name and password,
that is how they got on.
Rider REQUESTS the config from the leader's node.
Leader's node returns it.
Rider's device applies it to itself and its radio.
⭐ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE NATAK API: the leader's node is the authority for
the ride's config and serves it ON REQUEST — so the API needs a READ
endpoint as much as a write one, and the READ is the one riders use. The
write is a leader provisioning their own node.
⚠ The bootstrap is unchanged: the network name and password must still
reach a rider BEFORE they can connect. That is the ride definition distributed
ahead of time — a file today, the backend eventually.
⭐⭐ WHAT THE HANDOFF CARRIES — a config plus GPX, passed BY KEY
PartCarried as
Network identity + radio parametersThe config file itself — channel name, PSK, and the radio settings the ride depends on
Track or route⭐ Passed using its KEY — the app resolves it. kml_routes.route_id / ride_tracks.route_id, both char(36) uuid.
Waypoint (trailhead)⭐ Passed using its KEY — rides.trailhead_waypoint_id, char(36).
Maps⭐⭐ IMPORTED VIA THE EXISTING IMPORT-GPX PROCESS. Not shipped as tiles — the geometry arrives and the map download follows it.
⭐⭐⭐ PASSING BY KEY RATHER THAN BY VALUE IS THE POINT. The config stays
small, the geometry travels as GPX through a path that ALREADY WORKS, and the
map download is derived from the geometry rather than specified separately.
⚠ Which also means the corridor model comes for free — tiles follow the
route, exactly as downloadMapsForTrackHash already does for imported
tracks.
⚠ OPEN: what happens when a key resolves to nothing — a rider who does
not hold that route or waypoint. Either the handoff carries the GPX alongside
the key, or the request path fetches it. State the rule rather than
discovering it.
⚠ And rides.route_id is still AMBIGUOUS — two tables use
that primary-key name and tracks exist in both (see
V3SCHEMA-2026-09-20). The handoff format must say WHICH.
⭐ WHY THIS BELONGS IN 2.6g AND NOT 3.0
It needs no server. A leader exports a config, a rider imports it, and
the ride works. The backend, when it returns, delivers the same artifact over
the wire instead of by file — so nothing built here is thrown away, and the
V3 restart inherits a format that has already been used in the field.
✅ IMPORTLOCK — ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED 09-20. IT IS THE LATCH, NOT THE MANIFEST. → 2.6g FIX
⭐⭐⭐ THE 09-17 ENTRY BELOW NAMED TWO SUSPECTS AND COULD NOT
SEPARATE THEM. TESTED PROPERLY ON 09-20 — IT IS beginImport()'s
IN-MEMORY LATCH. The manifest was never the problem.
THE TEST, run one variable at a time as the 09-17 entry asked:
Utah import crashed by exiting the screen mid-run. Six of nine sources had
completed — 48,116 Utah trails already imported — and it died
on "Utah Open Source Maps" (the Geofabrik download, the network-heavy one).
App would not start ANY import. The stranded manifest
import_2026-09-20_utah_state.json sat in imports/.
⭐ am force-stop ALONE, manifest left in place → the import
started.
⛔⛔ SO: THE LATCH BLOCKS. THE MANIFEST DOES NOT.
HomeStatePickerScreen:133 — if (!beginImport()) return
— returns silently when the latch is still set from a run that died without
releasing it. In memory, so only a process kill clears it.
⭐ AND THE MANIFEST HANDLING IS ACTUALLY CORRECT. On the next run the
dead manifest GRADUATED to history/ as
utah-2026-09-20T19-22-15.json and a fresh one was written. Nothing
had to be deleted by hand.
⛔⛔ WHICH MAKES IT WORSE FOR A RIDER, NOT BETTER. A rider has no
force-stop and no adb. They see an app that will not start an import, with
nothing to delete, no message, and no way forward. The only remedy is
force-stopping from Android settings — which nobody will think to do.
🔴 THE SECOND HALF, STILL BROKEN: RESUME NEVER FIRES
The new run started FROM SCRATCH, re-fetching all six completed
sources. ⛔ The loop at :385 is built for resume —
if (src.getString("status") == "completed") continue — but it
reads the NEW manifest, which has every source back at
pending.
⚠ Cost is time, not data: the re-fetch dedupes against rows already present.
The Utah rerun fetched 49,125 UGRC records to insert 52. But it is ~10 minutes
a rider should not have to spend.
⭐ THE 2.6g FIX — TWO PARTS
RELEASE THE LATCH, OR DO NOT LET IT STRAND. Whatever
beginImport() sets must be cleared when a run ends — including when
it ends badly. ⚠ A guard and the thing it guards must share a lifetime
(the 08-16 rule): an in-memory latch protecting a multi-minute operation that can
die is the same shape as the app-private marker protecting public-storage data.
⭐ At minimum, a stale latch must not fail SILENTLY — say something.
RESUME, OR OFFER THE CHOICE. On finding an incomplete manifest, carry
its completed statuses into the new run. ⭐ Better still, this is
subsumed by SRCLIST — the source list with completed sources
ticked and skippable. A failed source simply arrives UNTICKED and "resume" is
pressing import again.
⚠ Neither part is large. The loop already does the skipping; what is
missing is that nothing carries the prior state forward, and nothing clears the
latch on an abnormal exit.
⚠ (superseded by the 09-20 isolation above) AN INCOMPLETE MANIFEST BRICKS THE IMPORTER. IMPORTLOCK-2026-09-17
The network dropped mid-import on Droid 2. After that, no state could be
imported at all — the screen never left the selection panel. No message, no log,
nothing.
Two manifests were left in imports/ (never graduating to
history/):
import_2026-09-17_new-hampshire_state.json   07:21
import_2026-09-17_utah_state.json           06:58
The New Hampshire one shows the shape exactly: three federal sources
completed, "New Hampshire Open Source Maps" failed
(the Geofabrik download — the network-heavy one), then rider trails and classify
both completed.
⭐ AND CLASSIFY COMPLETED — so OWNSKIP works with the streaming parser in
place. The regression check passed even on an interrupted run.
⛔⛔ THE DEFECT: RESUME IS DESIGNED AND DOES NOT HAPPEN. The loop at
:385 skips sources already completed, so a rerun SHOULD
pick up at the failed Geofabrik source. It never gets the chance — nothing
launches.
⚠ WE DO NOT KNOW WHICH OF TWO THINGS BLOCKS IT, because the manifests
were deleted AND the process force-stopped together:
the stale manifest in imports/, or
beginImport() — HomeStatePickerScreen:133 returns
without doing anything if the latch is set, and a run that died would leave it
set. ⚠ In-memory, so a force-stop clears it.
🔴 FIRST TASK: determine which, ONE AT A TIME. Delete the manifest
alone and retry; if that is not enough, force-stop alone and retry.
THE FIX, TWO PARTS:
⛔ UNBLOCK IT. Whatever refuses must not silently stop a new import.
Even doing nothing else, it should start fresh rather than sit there. A rider
has no adb and no idea a manifest exists.
⭐ THEN OFFER THE CHOICE on finding an incomplete manifest:
"An earlier import of X did not finish — [Resume where it stopped]
[Start over] [Cancel]". Resume is the loop's EXISTING skip-completed
behaviour; start over clears the manifest.
⚠ Define "incomplete" carefully — a run genuinely still going also
lives in imports/. Needs a staleness test, or the app must know its
own process restarted.
⭐⭐ THE SOURCE LIST — one screen that replaces both SRCFRESH and the resume prompt. SRCLIST-2026-09-17
Fred 09-17: list the sources for the state, tick the ones already
completed so they are bypassed, and let the rider REMOVE a tick to pull that
source back into the run.
⭐⭐⭐ THIS IS BETTER THAN AN AUTOMATIC FRESHNESS CHECK. It puts the
decision where the rider can see it, needs no lastEditDate hunting
per endpoint, and cannot become a trap — if the held data is suspect, untick
and it reimports.
⭐ AND IT USES THE MANIFEST WE ALREADY WRITE. Each source's last
successful import is in history/, so the screen can show what is held
and when it arrived.
⭐⭐ ONE SCREEN, THREE JOBS:
JobHow

Skip what is currentticked by default
RESUME what failed⭐ a failed source simply arrives UNTICKED — "resume" is pressing import again
⭐⭐ SO THIS SUBSUMES IMPORTLOCK's RESUME PROMPT ENTIRELY. No separate
"did not finish — resume or start over" dialog; the state is visible and the
rider acts on it. ⚠ The unblocking half of IMPORTLOCK is still required —
the screen has to be REACHABLE, and today nothing launches at all.
⚠ MAKE THE TICK AN ACTION, NOT A STATUS. "Already imported" is a fact;
"skip this" is a choice. ⛔ The import screen's own maps checkbox had exactly that
ambiguity and it cost us a day — a control that also reports state is read as
neither.
WHY IT MATTERS — the evidence is in today's manifest: the Utah rerun
fetched 49,125 UGRC records to insert 52. Geofabrik the same shape.
A rerun pays the full cost of an import for almost none of the benefit —
27–31 minutes. ⭐ And it is exactly what AREA DOWNLOADS need: an area download
over a state already held re-imports everything to insert nothing.
🔵 An automatic freshness check remains possible LATER as a default for
the ticks — ArcGIS exposes editingInfo.lastEditDate, Geofabrik a file
date — but the list works without it, and the list is what ships.
🔵 (superseded by SRCLIST above) SKIP SOURCES THAT HAVE NOT CHANGED. SRCFRESH-2026-09-17
Fred 09-17: test the trail DB for an existing source and, if the remote
has not changed since it was imported, skip that source entirely.
⭐⭐ THE PAYOFF IS LARGE AND THE EVIDENCE IS IN TODAY'S MANIFEST. The
Utah rerun fetched 49,125 UGRC records to insert 52. Geofabrik the same
shape. A rerun pays the full cost of an import for almost none of the
benefit — and it is 27–31 minutes.
⭐ AND IT IS EXACTLY WHAT AREA DOWNLOADS NEED (Fred): an area download
over a state already held re-imports everything to insert nothing.
⚠ MECHANISM NEEDS CARE, PER SOURCE. A creation date is not always
exposed — ArcGIS layers typically report editingInfo.lastEditDate
rather than a file timestamp, and Geofabrik exposes a file date. So: check
what each endpoint offers, store it in the manifest on success, compare next
time. Not universal — per source.
⚠ And it must be overridable. A rider who suspects bad data needs a
"force re-import" or the optimisation becomes a trap.
✅ OWNSTATE-2026-09-17 — gate on APPLICABILITY, not on memory
If the import is not Utah, the Utah ownership data cannot mean anything.
So: do not download it, do not parse it, do not classify against it. Mark the
stage completed and move on.
⭐⭐ THIS REMOVES THE WHOLE CLASS rather than guarding against it. No
streaming rewrite needed for other states, no degraded import, and no
invisible skip pattern to misread six months from now.
⛔ WHY NOT JUST LET THE OOM BACKSTOP CATCH IT? It probably would — it
wraps this call. But a caught OOM leaves an UNKNOWN DEGRADED IMPORT: a
state's trails carrying clutter, on devices we cannot see, with
processed: 0 in the manifest that is indistinguishable from a
legitimate skip. ⭐ Fred: "an unknown degraded import which will surface
issues and patterns forever." The state gate makes the skip CORRECT and
RECORDED — it writes skipped_reason so a future reader can tell
it from a missing file or a memory failure.
⚠ Implementation note: this is INLINE code inside executeRun with
no lambda to return from, so the stage is marked completed AT THE GATE and the
two existing conditions (the download and the
sDb != null &amp;&amp; eDb != null block) are guarded. No early
exit, and no need to know where step 8 ends.
⚠ Hardcoded to Utah for now. ⭐ Better in the follow-up: test whether an
ownership layer EXISTS for the imported state, so adding Colorado needs data
rather than code.
⭐⭐ UTAH DOES NOT CRASH — AND THAT CHANGES THE PRIORITY
Fred: Utah never crashes, running the SAME code against MORE
trails — 145,000 against New Hampshire's smaller set, same ownership file.
⛔ SO THE OOM IS NOT ABOUT VOLUME. If it were, Utah would fail first.
🔵 HYPOTHESIS, UNCONFIRMED: Utah polygons sit OVER Utah trails, so the
spatial grid does its job and most cells hold a manageable number of rings. New
Hampshire trails fall ENTIRELY OUTSIDE every Utah polygon, so the grid lookup
misses and the code falls back to the bbox scan — which
OwnershipReclass:137 names: "it is still tested by the bbox scan
fallback." ⭐ A fallback testing every ring against every trail would be
far more expensive, and it only triggers when the data does not overlap.
⭐⭐ CONSEQUENCE: THE STREAMING REWRITE DROPS DOWN THE LIST. It was
scoped for a problem specific to the wrong-state case, which the gate now
prevents entirely. Utah runs the path that works.
📋 2.7 — OWNERSHIP, POLYGONS AND ROUTE SCORING. POLYROUTE-2026-09-17
⚠ RELEASE ASSIGNMENT: Fred said "the follow-up 2.6g release" earlier in the
session and "2.7" at the end. Recorded here under 2.7; confirm before
planning.
THREE PIECES LAND TOGETHER:
THE POLYGON DISPLAY LAYER. Private areas in red with ghosted
diagonal stripes, behind a checkbox in the key. ⭐ More honest than
reclassifying trails — it shows a rider WHY, and lets them see a boundary they
are APPROACHING rather than discovering a trail simply is not offered.
⚠ Leaflet has no native hatch; it is an SVG pattern, needed on the frozen convoy
map and the planner. ⚠ Polygons are light in COUNT, not always in VERTICES —
simplification at import is what makes it work.
THE OHV RESTRICTION LAYER — SEPARATE MEANING, SEPARATE CHECKBOX. BLM
OHV_DSG_PUB_POLY and the USFS data with SEASONS OF USE. ⛔ One
hatch cannot serve both: public land with OHV closed says go when the rider
must not; private land with permission says stop when the trail is rideable.
OWNERSHIP BEYOND UTAH — the western 10–12 states, because that is
where the land pattern makes clutter removal necessary. ⭐ Reached twice
independently: the trail-volume-vs-layer test, and the land-pattern argument.
⭐⭐⭐ AND THE ROUTING ANSWER, WHICH IS THE ELEGANT PART
(Fred 09-17).
A trail crossing a restriction polygon takes −100 in the route
scorer.
⭐ Negative totals cannot be ridden. The sign carries the meaning — a
scorer returning a negative number has said something CATEGORICAL, not just
"worse".
⭐ Bottom of the list, never presented. Same as the existing
behaviour: only positives display. So nothing new is needed in the
presentation layer at all.
⭐⭐ IT IS NOT A NEW AVOIDANCE SYSTEM — it is another weight in the
scorer that already exists. The 2.7 work is really just feed the polygons
into the existing scorer.
⭐ And it degrades gracefully with bad data: a wrong polygon costs a
lower-ranked route, not a disappeared trail. Hard avoidance would silently remove
legitimate ground with nothing to explain why.
⚠ ONE THING TO SETTLE AT BUILD TIME: whether a high-scoring route can
ABSORB a single −100 and still come out positive. If a long route with many
points of interest scores +150, one crossing leaves it at +50 and rideable —
which would be wrong. Either the penalty scales with crossings, or −100 is
applied as a FLOOR rather than a summand.
⚠ And if fewer than six routes score positive, present fewer — a short
list is honest; backfilling from the negatives would put unrideable routes in
front of a rider who assumes everything offered is valid.
00-2026-09-16 — THE OOM CRASH, AND THE VISION THE SEPARATION IS FOR
🔵 DRIVE BACKUP AND RESTORE FOR my_tracks — TEST BEFORE BUILDING. DRIVEBAK-2026-09-16
Fred: back up the internal my_tracks database to Google
Drive, and on a crash or a reinstall bring the GPX files back.
⭐⭐ RESTORE MAY ALREADY WORK — TEST IT FIRST. The import already uses a
SAF picker (OpenMultipleDocuments,
ConvoyTrackImportScreen:198), and Google Drive appears as a
provider inside that picker. A rider taps import, navigates to Drive, selects
their GPX files, and they stage exactly as local ones do. No download step, no
second copy, no API work.
🔴 THE TEST, BEFORE ANY CODE: put a GPX in Drive, run the import, see
whether Drive shows as a source. If it does, restore is DONE and only BACKUP
needs building.
⚠ The Downloads hop is unnecessary. Fred's first sketch was
Drive → Downloads → picker → import; the picker reaches Drive directly.
⭐ AND RE-IMPORTING EVERYTHING IS SAFE, which is what makes this a viable
recovery path at all: geom_hash with INSERT OR IGNORE,
plus the two-pass load. A full restore dedupes rather than duplicating.
BACKUP is the half that needs building, and it is the simpler direction:
upload my_tracks to a Drive folder. One way, no conflict resolution,
no merge.
⭐ USE THE drive.file SCOPE — an app manages only files it
created. ⛔ No broad Drive access and NO ANNUAL VERIFICATION REVIEW, which
the full drive scope requires. ⭐ And the auth already exists: Google
Sign-In is in V3 for registration.
⛔ THREE FEATURES, NOT ONE — DO NOT CONFLATE THEM:
FeatureEffort
Backup — upload one directionSmall
Restore — pull back on a new deviceSmall, possibly ZERO (see the picker test)
Sync — keep both in step⚠ MUCH HARDER. Conflict resolution, deletions, two devices editing the same track.
⭐ Hash-named immutable tracks help enormously — but DELETION still needs
a decision, which is what makes sync a different animal. Backup and restore
for a release; sync as a later question.
⭐⭐ IT LANDS WELL AGAINST THE LOSS HISTORY. The 08-01 incident destroyed
the spatial DB; the GPX files survived only because they sat outside it. Drive
backup would have made even that recoverable.
⚠ SIZE CHECK BEFORE PROMISING IT: a rider with three years of tracks is
uploading a lot, and Drive's free tier is 15 GB shared with Gmail. ⚠ The
picker is also slower over cellular with 90 files than a local import — a
different experience, not a broken one.
⛔⛔ SIX NEW INSTALLS CRASHED ON FIRST RUN. OOMGUARD-2026-09-15.
Not a regression — a long-standing hole that our devices are too well-equipped to
hit.
OutOfMemoryError: Failed to allocate a 134250504 byte allocation
with 8388608 free bytes and 112MB until OOM, growth limit 201326592
  ... TextStreamsKt.readText -> FilesKt.readText
  ... OwnershipReclass.loadRings      (R8 mismapped it to ConvoySubMenuKt)
  ... HomeStateImportController.executeRun
OwnershipReclass.loadRings():353 did
val text = f.readText() on Land_Ownership.geojson —
78,700,909 bytes measured on Droid 2.
⭐⭐ THE ARITHMETIC IS THE PROOF. readText decodes UTF-8
into a UTF-16 String, so ~78 MB of file becomes ~157 MB of chars, and
StringBuilder doubling asks for one 128 MB block on the way there. Against
a 192 MB growth limit (≈2 GB RAM device) that cannot succeed. ⛔ It is on the
FIRST-RUN home-state import — the path every new user takes, which is why it
was six for six.
⚠ Reports came from 29321125 and 29321127, both PRE-release. 29321134
was live by then. But the defect was still in it, so nobody installing fresh was
protected.
⚠ Android 11 is correlation, not cause. A 192 MB growth limit is what
lower-RAM devices get. Every affected user is on a smaller heap than our test
hardware.
✅ WHAT SHIPPED — 29321137
A — HEAP GUARD in loadRings. Estimates peak at 3× the file
(2× decode plus a doubling step) against available heap; too big → return empty
and log loudly.
B — OutOfMemoryError BACKSTOP around the step-8 call,
converting a failure to the existing changed &lt; 0 skipped
sentinel.
C — android:largeHeap="true"
(LARGEHEAP-2026-09-16). ⚠ It had never been set. On the
crashing device that is ~384 MB instead of 192 MB. Verified in the merged
manifest AND inside the AAB.
⭐⭐ WHY A AND B ARE SAFE: THE TOLERANCE ALREADY EXISTED. Step 8's own
comments say "a missing ownership file is not a reason to call the import
failed" and "Skipping for want of an ownership file is a DEGRADED run, not
a failed one." We routed a new failure into a path built for exactly this
shape of problem.
⛔ C (STREAMING) DELIBERATELY DEFERRED. Fred: "I cannot afford to
break the app and be gone a week." ⭐ Right call — the guard either fires and
skips or does nothing, whereas a rewritten scanner could silently misparse
polygons and misclassify trails, invisible from Vermont.
⭐ THE STREAMING WORK, SCOPED: parseRings is ALREADY a
character-at-a-time scanner — text[i], bracket depth, a
StringBuilder. It converts to a stream almost unchanged.
loadRings is the harder half (built on indexOf and
substring) and needs restating as a streaming scan with two
operations: advance-to-literal, and read-next-quoted-string. ⚠ One real change:
parseRings currently stops at a boundary found by looking AHEAD for
the next "owner"; streaming cannot look ahead, so it would stop at
bracket depth zero — which is what actually ends a geometry and is arguably
more correct.
⛔⛔ DO NOT DROP THE OWNERSHIP WORK — IT IS CLUTTER REMOVAL, NOT LABELLING
⚠ I argued today that OHV designation supersedes ownership and step 8 could
go away. THAT WAS WRONG and Fred corrected it.
⭐⭐⭐ Fred: "that is used to eliminate many rural roads that
cluttered the map in order to get trails in public areas. both tertiary
roads."
Private ownership is how a driveway or ranch two-track is told from a public
forest road. Both are track_grade in OSM with no distinguishing
tag — the only thing separating them is whose land they are on. Strip the
private ones and the map is usable; leave them and the screen is a mess of rural
access roads.
⛔ SO OWNERSHIP AND OHV DESIGNATION DO DIFFERENT JOBS:
DataJob
Ownership (SITLA / state layers)CLUTTER REMOVAL. Which tertiary roads are somebody's driveway.
OHV designation (BLM OHV_DSG_PUB_POLY, USFS)ACCESS. Where riding is permitted, by CFR.
⭐⭐ AND THEY DISAGREE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Public land with OHV CLOSED
(wilderness study area, seasonal closure) — ownership says go, the rider must
not. Private land WITH permission (club easement) — ownership says stop, the
trail is legitimately rideable. ⛔ A red hatch driven by ownership would be
wrong both ways, and the first is the dangerous one.
⭐⭐ SCOPE, ARRIVED AT TWICE INDEPENDENTLY: THE WESTERN 10–12 STATES.
Fred: "the western states, with so much public land bordered by rural roads,
is unique." Vast federal holdings threaded with ranch access roads and
checkerboard sections. Eastern states are mostly private with public land in
discrete parks — the ambiguity barely exists there. ⭐ Yesterday's scope test
(trail volume vs available ownership layer) and today's land-pattern argument
reach the SAME list.
🔴 CHEAP EXPERIMENT, JANUARY: import one eastern state from OSM and
look at what you get. Clean → the argument holds. Cluttered → ownership matters
everywhere and scope is back to fifty.
⭐ FEDERAL DATA SOURCES FOUND 09-16 — national, not per-state
⭐⭐ BLM Ground Transportation Linear Features (catalog.data.gov) —
includes a Limited Public Motorized Trails subset and a separate
OHV_DSG_PUB_POLY describing where OHV use is permitted under
CFR. GeoJSON available.
⭐⭐ USDA Forest Service FSGeodata Clearinghouse — national trails layer
plus a feature class giving which motorized vehicle types are allowed AND
THEIR SEASONS OF USE. ⭐ That is motorized_allowed at national
scale — the field the 07-27 analysis found was missing everywhere except sparse
OSM tagging. Seasonal closure is something no rider can infer from a map and
nobody else is showing it. ⚠ Shapefile/geodatabase, needs conversion.
State portals: Arizona has two hubs; data.gov filtered to
res_format=GeoJSON returns 78 trail datasets.
⛔ ESRI REST ENDPOINTS CAP AT 1000 RECORDS PER REQUEST. Utah's 49,125
trails need paging, not one fetch. Our UGRC import must already handle this —
check how, the same pattern applies to every ArcGIS source added.
⭐ SEQUENCING: BLM and Forest Service FIRST. Two sources, national
coverage, and the USFS vehicle-type data is what the product most lacks.
Per-state portals are the long tail.
🔵 DISPLAY IDEA (Fred): polygons are light; show private areas in red
with ghosted diagonal stripes, behind a checkbox in the key. ⭐ More honest
than reclassifying trails — it shows a rider WHY, and lets them see a boundary
they are approaching. ⚠ Leaflet has no native hatch; it is an SVG pattern, on the
frozen convoy map and the planner. ⚠ And polygons are light in COUNT, not always
in VERTICES — simplification at import is what makes it work. ⛔ Decide
whether the hatch means PRIVATE or DO-NOT-RIDE; they are different sets.
00-2026-09-15 — THE POSITION SOURCE: MEASURED, FIXED, AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE PRODUCT
⭐⭐ THE 09-14 DIAGNOSIS WAS HALF RIGHT AND THE OTHER HALF WAS
WRONG. Right: the cart feed asks only GPS and a chipless device therefore
gets nothing. Wrong: "the legacy NETWORK_PROVIDER is dormant, Play Services
moved network-derived positioning into fused." Measured on Droid 2 this
morning and it is the reverse.
network provider: Location[network 42.801104,-71.278439 hAcc=20.031  et=+1m9s]
fused provider:   Location[fused   42.801107,-71.278428 hAcc=100.0   et=+10h16m]
NETWORK is the live one — one minute old, 20 m. FUSED is ten hours
stale at 100 m.
⛔ SO FUSED IS EXCLUDED, DELIBERATELY. A stale 100 m fix is worse than
no fix: a plausible-looking position that puts a rider a hundred metres from
where they are with nothing marking it old — the same failure pattern as the
hardcoded Esri sources, output that looks correct and is not. Fred:
"fused does nothing, it provides at best an old stale location."
⚠ Do not re-add it from the "fused is the modern API" argument without
re-measuring on the target device.
✅ NETLOC-2026-09-15 — the live cart feed asks NETWORK as well as GPS
ConvoyViewModel.startPhoneGps() subscribed to
GPS_PROVIDER and nothing else. That is the feed that drives the cart
when there is no radio: readLiveNodes:833 → node map empty →
permission check → startPhoneGps() → getPhoneLocation()
→ :844-845 default to 0.0/0.0. Hence a cart with a name and
no position, silently, and a map left at its construction default.
NOW: one listener registered against GPS and NETWORK, each
registration guarded separately — previously a single throw lost the entire
feed. The listener keeps the BETTER fix, not the latest (take it if we
hold none, if what we hold is stale &gt;15s, or if the new one is at least as
accurate), so a device with a chip cannot jitter between a 3 m GPS fix and a
20 m network one on last-write-wins.
⭐ stopPhoneGps() needed no change —
removeUpdates(listener) removes ALL of that listener's
registrations.
⚠ STILL GPS-ONLY, NOT YET TOUCHED:
ConvoyViewModel:829 — getPhoneLocation()'s last-known
fallback, which has no fallback at all. That range has not been read
verbatim and no anchor will be cut from an index.
ConvoyScreen:883 and ConvoyMapViewerScreen:1837 already
do GPS → NETWORK.
🔴 AND AN UNEXPLAINED ONE: ConvoyScreen:883 asks NETWORK,
and NETWORK has a position — so why does the map still open on the world
view? Note it sits in the else of the saved-bbox check at
:869: if a frame was saved, fitBounds runs and the
location read never happens. Check that branch before assuming the read is
at fault.
⛔ THE PRODUCT STATEMENT — A DEVICE WITH NO GPS CHIP IS NOT A TRAIL DEVICE
⭐⭐⭐ Fred 09-15: "a device with no gps will not work on the
trail without a mesh radio attached. period."
Network positioning is a driveway feature by definition — it needs
coverage, and coverage is what the trail does not have. So for a chipless device
there is exactly ONE answer, not a menu.
⛔ THE BLUETOOTH OPTION IS OUT — PARKED, NOT SHIPPED. A paired phone's
own GPS chip resolves by satellite with no network at all, which would make it a
genuine trail answer. It is not currently reaching the framework on Droid 2:
no gps provider entry with a position appears in
dumpsys location at all. Plain Bluetooth pairing does not share
location — it normally needs a publishing app on the phone and a mock-location
receiver on the tablet. ⚠ Fred has used this successfully before
("I have done this before when I test from the car"), so something
changed at the device level. Device-level problem, another day. Do not offer
it to riders until it is proven again.
📋 TWO MESSAGES, TWO CONDITIONS, TWO DISMISSAL RULES (design settled 09-15)
⭐ ALL OF THIS IS GATED ON HARDWARE CHECK + NO GPS POSITION. A normal
phone never sees any of it. ConvoyGpsService:256 already detects the
no-chip case and logs "No GPS hardware — will use radio position from
mesh".
MESSAGE A — located by network. DISMISSIBLE, permanently.
Trigger: the position came from the network fallback rather than GPS or radio.
⭐ Why dismissible (Fred): "many riders will not turn their radios on
when connecting from home." A network position at the kitchen table is
normal and expected; warning daily about a condition that is fine in that moment
is the noise that trains people to tap through everything. It is a WARNING that
they must have a solution on the trail — said once, then trusted.
MESSAGE B — no position at all. NOT DISMISSIBLE, every time.
Trigger: no source produced a position. The app cannot function — there is
nothing to acknowledge away, and silencing it leaves someone using an app
that cannot do its job with no indication why. This is exactly what Droid 2 does
TODAY: a cart with a name and 0.0/0.0, a map over Nevada, and nothing said.
WORDING (approved 09-15):
This device does not meet the minimum trail requirement.
It has no GPS chip, so it can only find your location through a
network connection - and there is no network on the trail.
A mesh radio is required for this device to work off-grid.
⭐ Why this wording: it names the requirement as UNMET rather than
describing a symptom, and it ends with the one action that resolves it.
PLACEMENT: modal popup over the initial ride panel, after the panel
has settled. ⛔ Not during composition — the 09-13 storage prompt was
rendered and dismissed before input, leaving the mode unset. Requires OK
to continue.
⚠ The suppression flag for Message A needs a home — a per-device
preference, and ⛔ nowhere near map_slots.json.
⭐⭐ THE RESOLVER — ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH, THREE CONSUMERS (Fred's design, 09-15)
⭐ Fred: "a startup function to derive gps source and completes a
global variable used in three places." Today four sites each invent their own
provider chain and none of them agree. One resolver replaces all of it.
IT ANSWERS ONE QUESTION: do we have a position, and is it GPS or
network-derived. ⭐ Fred settled the categories: "the truth is always
do we have a gps position, the method is android or network derived. the
fallbacks will pick up the bluetooth gps, it is transparent." So TWO states,
not four — the mechanism (chip, Bluetooth, radio) is plumbing detail that changes
nothing for any consumer.
THREE CONSUMERS:
Initial map load — use the position instead of leaving the map at
convoy_map.html:342's setView([36.1069,-115.1711], 4).
Android device cart assignment — the no-radio fallback that currently
yields a name and 0.0/0.0.
Track recording — ⭐⭐ must accept GPS or radio ONLY and refuse a
network position. 20 m accuracy jumping between wifi access points would
write a garbage GPX. Fred: "we will never get to gps track recording with no
gps or no radio so we may not have to address it, but it should be checked."
Build the check anyway — "unreachable" is exactly what was said about a device
with no chip.
⛔⛔ TWO CONSTRAINTS ON THE RESOLVER, BOTH LEARNED THE HARD WAY:
⚠ (1) A derived-once global must be RE-DERIVABLE. Attaching a radio
changes the answer. A value set at startup and never revisited is the same class
of bug as initialized — a stored fact that stops matching reality.
Derive on read, or recompute when radio state changes.
⛔ (2) DO NOT PUT THE RESOLVER IN Application.onCreate.
That is exactly what cost 09-14. Startup ordering is not a free parameter in this
fork.

⛔ THE FALLBACK LOOP — DIAGNOSED, PARTIALLY FIXED. INITLOOP-2026-09-14
MapSourceManager.ensureInit() tested initialized — a

00-2026-09-13 — PUBLISHED, COMPLIANT, ON ALL THREE TRACKS
⭐⭐ Rel. 2.6g — 29321121 — live on internal, closed and open
testing. Three days from the appeal rejection to a compliant build with the
migration proven on two devices.
⛔ ALL THREE TRACKS HAD TO BE UPDATED, not promoted. A non-compliant
build on ANY track keeps the violation open — promotion moves a build up but
leaves the others serving what they were. ⚠ Worth knowing before the next
compliance deadline: the usual promote-up workflow does not clear a violation.
1 · ⛔⛔ REJECTED A SECOND TIME — for the permissions nobody looked for
The build went up with MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE removed, the whole
migration built and tested, and was rejected again for "all file
permissions."
⚠ Because TWO MORE were still declared:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with tools:node="replace" —
⛔ WORSE THAN UPSTREAM'S. The replace stripped the
maxSdkVersion cap Meshtastic itself applies, so the fork declared it
for EVERY API level, unbounded.
READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE capped at 32 — more defensible, same
policy family.
⭐⭐ THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE AS THE PATH SWEEP. The
09-11 sweep missed 23 sites because it grepped ONE API when two reached the same
destination. This missed two permissions because it removed ONE NAME when three
belong to the same policy family. GREP THE CATEGORY, NOT THE INSTANCE.
⭐ node="remove", NOT DELETION. Deleting the line lets
upstream Meshtastic's own declaration merge back in — it declares both, and
the MERGED manifest is what Google reviews, not the source file.
⛔ AND CHECK THE MERGED MANIFEST BEFORE UPLOADING. That check was never
run the first time. It lives at
app/build/intermediates/merged_manifests/googleRelease/processGoogleReleaseManifest/AndroidManifest.xml
and must return nothing for storage or media.
✅ Neither permission was needed, verified on device: export writes to
Downloads with NO permission on API 29+, and reads go through SAF grants.
2 · ⛔⛔ BOTH GPX IMPORT PATHS WERE DEAD — the real release blocker
⛔ THE IN-APP DOWNLOADS SCAN RETURNED AN EMPTY LIST. Not an

⭐ THE RULE THAT SHAPED THE FIX
Confirmed on device: an app may WRITE to Downloads freely, but READING what
another app put there needs permission. Track export never broke and needed
no change. ⭐ Only import was broken, and the picker IS the permission — the
rider's selection is the grant.
What was built
Fred, 09-13: "simpler to write a picker to select and move files and
execute the existing import than change everything." Right:
OpenMultipleDocuments, GPX/KML filtered, ⚠ with a
*/* fallback because GPX is frequently reported as

original deleted — all while the URI grant is live. ⭐ Self-contained: by the time
the import runs the URIs are finished with.

parse, split multi-track files, hash, dedupe and insert. It takes a
File, so the file simply has to be somewhere the app owns.

00-2026-09-12 — THE MIGRATION IS PROVEN, WITH NO PERMISSION
⭐⭐ THE WHOLE CHAIN RAN ON DEVICE WITH
MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE OUT OF THE MANIFEST — confirmed
appops reading default, not allow. Tree
grant, recursive copy, moveDocument, a 16 GB stream,
renameDocument, delete-after-verify. The app then ran entirely from
app-private storage, offline maps included.
⭐ AND IT IS FAST. 415 MB of databases and data in UNDER A MINUTE. 16 GB
of tiles in FOUR MINUTES — about 70 MB/s. ⚠ Every estimate in the 09-11 design
assumed hours; SAF is not the bottleneck anybody feared.
1 · ⛔⛔ THE LANDMINE — ConvoyConfig.migrateTiles()
A live function that moved tiles FROM app-private storage OUT to shared
storage — the pre-MBTiles migration, from when tiles were moved out for
persistence. ⛔ Exactly backwards from where storage is now going.
⚠ AND IT WOULD HAVE FIRED. Once tileRoot()
resolves internal, its source and destination are the SAME directory: it would
walk the live tile store renaming each source onto itself, then delete the parent
if the listing came back empty. ⭐ In practice a dest.exists() guard
made every source skip — harmless BY ACCIDENT rather than by design.
⛔ Its guard was a SharedPreferences flag while the data it guarded lived in
shared storage — a guard and its subject with DIFFERENT LIFETIMES, which is
the exact shape of the 08-16 reinstall wipe. Deleted, with its call site.
⭐⭐ ONLY THE CROSS-REFERENCE FOUND IT
Fred, 09-12: "that is why we created the tools. Too many
scares."
⚠ No destination-grep would have caught it. The dangerous line reads
getExternalFilesDir — which LOOKS like the place we are moving
TOWARD, not a problem. ⭐ The function-universe index lists everything that does
filesystem work regardless of how the path is spelled, and that is what surfaced
it.
⭐ The same sweep also proved the blast radius was contained: of 42
files doing file work, most use context.filesDir (already
app-private, no permission) or derive from an accessor. The accessor pattern
paid for itself.
2 · ⛔ TWENTY-THREE MORE SITES, AND WHY THE FIRST SWEEP MISSED THEM
The thirteen found on 09-11 were greps for
Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory(). These 23 use
getExternalStoragePublicDirectory(DIRECTORY_DOCUMENTS).
TWO APIs, ONE DESTINATION.
⭐⭐ GREP FOR THE DESTINATION, NOT THE API. Search the string
literals — "GroupTrack/ and "my_tracks — because those
cannot be spelled two ways.
✅ The verification grep now returns ZERO. It returned 23 that
morning.
my_tracks — 13 sites, 5 files.
ConvoyTrackOps.tracksDir() already existed as a public accessor and
NOBODY USED IT. ⚠ Five different code shapes across the thirteen, so each needed
its own anchor. mkdirs() folded into the accessor — several sites
created the directory and several assumed it existed.
TrailImporter — 6 copies of one path, collapsed into one
private helper.
Three singles — MapSourceManager,
HomeStateImportController, track_sync.log.
⭐ ConvoyTrackOps.downloadsDir() STAYS. Downloads is the rider's
own folder, it is how files get in and out, and reading it needs no permission —
the pattern Google actually wants.
⚠ THE CONTEXT PROBLEM SOLVED ITSELF. It was called "the real work of the
next session" on 09-11 — getExternalFilesDir() needs a Context and
these are object singletons. ⭐ MapSourceManager and
HomeStateImportController both had one already and now pass it to the
accessor. No upstream edit needed.
3 · ⭐⭐ HOUSEKEEPING — ONE CONTAINER, TWO PHASES, JOBS THAT GATE THEMSELVES
⛔ THE BUG IT FIXES. run()'s first line read the
schema marker and returned — so ONE job's "nothing to do" silently skipped every
other job in the function. The manifest sweep never ran on a normal launch.
⚠ And there were TWO entry points, run() and
everyLaunch(), called in that order — with init() inside
the first. Anything added to the second that touched database FILES was already
too late.
THE RULES, now written on the container itself
ONE CONTAINER. Every startup cleanup job, one function, called once
after authority resolves and before any map loads.
SEQUENTIAL, NEVER CONCURRENT. ⭐ What makes an ordering rule meaningful
at all — with threads there would be no ordering, only races.
⛔ TWO PHASES, AND init() IS THE BOUNDARY. It OPENS the
database files. Anything that MOVES, COPIES or REPLACES them runs above; anything
touching their CONTENTS runs below. ⚠ Not a position — a consequence. A schema
ALTER needs them open; a file migration needs them closed.
⛔ EVERY JOB GATES ITSELF and returns quietly when there is nothing to
do. NO JOB'S CONDITION MAY STOP THE STREAM.
INSERTION REQUIRES IMPACT ANALYSIS. Which phase, what it touches, what
it needs open or closed. Not "wherever there is a gap."
⛔ A JOB RETURNS FROM ITSELF, NEVER FROM THE CONTAINER.
⭐⭐ AND RULE 6 IS WHY THE EXTRACTION MATTERED. Fred, 09-12:
"you could embed a job in a condition you did not see. All the code is inline
and that is a lot to read to insert a new task." ⛔ A JOB CANNOT GATE
ITSELF UNTIL IT IS A FUNCTION — with the body inline, "return when there is
nothing to do" and "return from the container" are THE SAME STATEMENT. The first
attempt moved the marker check below init() and it STILL returned
from run(): same bug, one phase lower, and it looked fixed.
⭐ NO RELEASE OR UPDATE SECTIONS. Every job is called every launch and
decides for itself. Once ever → a marker it writes. Once per release → a marker
whose NAME changes. Always → nothing. ⚠ The condition travels with the job.
4 · ⭐ THE SAF CONVERSION
One broad pick on Documents, and the app finds
GroupTrack and my_tracks itself. ⛔ It reads EXACTLY
TWO FOLDERS — the grant is broader and nothing enforces the limit; it is a
discipline in the code.
The record IS the flag. One JSON in internal storage, per-item source
and destination bytes, the exception text, the granted URI, a timestamp per step.
⚠ Detailed enough to troubleshoot, because that is the point.
Maps: parked to Documents/maps with
moveDocument so GroupTrack can be renamed away without
taking the tiles. Then copied file by file, largest first, each source deleted
only after its size matches.
⛔ WHY MAPS ARE PARKED RATHER THAN LEFT IN PLACE. Fred,
09-12: leaving GroupTrack to hold them "masks the location of
where we are retrieving other components — we could run fine until we finish
copying maps." ⭐ A stale path would read the old folder and nobody would
notice until it finally went.
⭐ THE SPACE CHECK IS AGAINST THE LARGEST SINGLE FILE, not the total —
with copy-then-delete the peak is the biggest file. ⚠ SAT.mbtiles is
16 GB in ONE FILE and no loop can split it, so that is the floor. Plus a reserve:
a device run to nearly full slows badly. Droid 1 has 86 GB free and copies;
Droid 2 has 16 GB and will refuse — that is the branch still to test.
⛔ THE RENAMES STAND WHERE THE DELETES GO. Fred: "it is just a
rename, nothing exposed." The field build swaps ONE operation. ⭐ And a rename
makes a stale path fail LOUDLY instead of quietly working.
5 · ⛔ THE PERMISSION IS OUT OF THE MANIFEST
Fred, 09-12: "I think we should rebuild for this test without all object
authority — make sure we have all the access we think we have." ⭐ Right, and

permission STILL GRANTED, and moveDocument and
renameDocument had never been tried at all.
⚠ hasRealStorageAccess() NOW RETURNS TRUE, and it is not a
fudge — app-private storage requires no permission, so there is nothing to check.

1. THE BUTTONS WERE UNREACHABLE. The conversion items went on

⛔ The conversion was never invoked: no log lines, no record, the files directory
completely empty. ⚠ Nothing was broken; it was never called.
⭐ "Convoy radio menu" was matched to a FILENAME. The menu Fred uses is the
sheet in ConvoySubMenu titled "Meshtastic Radio Setup" — a LABEL

2. LaunchedEffect(Unit) FIRES REGARDLESS OF AN EARLY
RETURN. The storage prompt rendered and flashed straight past: the effect was

⚠ The other five items use the same pattern correctly — they NAVIGATE AWAY and
never return, so disposal does not matter. One that waits for a result is

notice something it was never watching.

\u26a0 into Kotlin comments as six characters rather than the symbol,

find() returned −1 and −1 is less than any index; a fixed-width

4 · ⛔⛔ THE ALL-FILES APPEAL WAS REJECTED
Rejected 09-10 — "Access to device storage not required" — and the
appeal filed the same day came back rejected. An extension request is in, asking
for time to publish a compliant build. ⚠ That buys TIME, not the argument.
⛔ Fred: "I cannot publish with that in the manifest."
⚠ What the research established, and it matters for any future attempt
OsmAnd does NOT have this permission. Their request (issue #16059) has
been open since Dec 2022, labelled "Nice to Have", never granted. They ship
offline maps working inside their own folder tree, which they call "certainly
a crippling mechanism" — but which plainly works. ⛔ So any declaration built
on "there is no alternative" invites exactly that comparison.
⭐ THE ARGUMENT THAT MIGHT HAVE WORKED was the one Fred found last:
riders back their map store up to SD cards and USB drives and restore it to
replacement devices. App-private storage makes that impossible —
Android/data is unreachable to file managers on Android 11+. That is
user data portability, and it maps onto Google's own permitted uses far better
than performance ever did.
⚠ Arguments to avoid, tested and discarded: "the app does not download
it, the user does" (the app builds the URLs, queues, retries and writes the
files); and "it is third-party public-domain content" (the policy is about which
process wrote the file, not who owns what is inside it — and it weakens the
portability claim).
5 &#183; &#11088;&#11088; THE PLAN &#8212; A PICKER, NOT A CLEAN INSTALL
&#11088; GOOGLE'S OWN REJECTION NOTICE NAMED THE WAY OUT: the
Storage Access Framework. ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE lets the rider
pick a folder; the app gets read AND write on that tree and copies the contents
into its own storage. No permission, no declaration, no review.
&#9940; SO THE CLEAN-INSTALL PLAN IS OFF, AND SO IS THE TWO-BUILD SEQUENCE. A
migration no longer needs the permission it is trying to stop using &#8212; which
was the only reason it had to happen in a separate, earlier build. &#9888; Most of
a day was spent designing around a constraint that turned out not to exist.
WHAT THE RIDER GETS: trails, tracks, routes, waypoints, drafts and
settings all survive. Only maps re-download (~17 GB). One tap instead of
export-uninstall-delete-reinstall-reimport.
The settled shape
ONE broad pick on Documents &#8212; the app then lists it
and finds GroupTrack and my_tracks itself. &#11088; A new
install takes the identical path, finds nothing, resolves. &#9940; No "I have
nothing to import" button &#8212; an earlier design had one and it was a mistake: a
rider tapping it by reflex loses everything.
&#9940; THE APP READS EXACTLY TWO FOLDERS. The grant covers all of
Documents only because that is where both can be found &#8212; it is
NOT a licence to look at anything else. Nothing enforces that; it is a discipline
in the code, and a future change that walks the tree for any other reason is a
trust violation however well intentioned.
Inside those two, everything comes. Exclusion list, not inclusion: only
maps/ (~17 GB) and *-journal. &#9940; Do not trim the
clutter &#8212; the three .trails_cleared_* markers look like junk and
are not, they stop housekeeping re-firing.
&#9940; MAPS ARE DELETED, NOT COPIED. SAF has no move, only copy, so the
device would need 17 GB free ON TOP of the 17 GB already there. Most will not have
it.
THE RECORD IS THE FLAG. A JSON in internal storage recording each step;
all-steps-completed is the trigger not to migrate again. &#9940; A FLAG, NOT A DISK
CHECK &#8212; Documents is the rider's folder and a stray file named
GroupTrack must not re-fire the migration over live data.
Deletion is a SECOND LAUNCH, offered, gated on the first launch having
actually worked &#8212; the spatial DB opens, trails are there. &#11088; A failed
copy therefore costs disk space, not data. &#9888; The grant must be PERSISTED for
this, and released afterwards.
&#11088; STEPS 1&#8211;3 FIRE THE TRIGGER, STEP 4 DOES NOT. Once copied,
never repeat &#8212; re-running over internal data the rider has since used is far
worse than leftover clutter.
The gate stands. An unresolved migration blocks the home state picker
entirely, or a rider imports 145,000 trails for an hour and then wants their old
data back.
&#9940; The second-launch screen &#8212; order of sentences matters
An early draft opened "your data has been converted successfully" and
then asked "if your app launched and everything behaved OK". &#9888; The
first sentence asserts what the second is asking, and a rider skims the first and
taps. &#11088; State the fact, then ask the question, and offer a way out that
CLOSES THE APP &#8212; a rider with a problem must not be nudged past it.
&#9989; The problem report attaches the record JSON. No manifest work
needed &#8212; FileProvider is declared at
AndroidManifest.xml:355 and convoy_file_paths.xml already
exposes external-files-path with path=".". &#9888; The
intent still needs a FileProvider URI and
FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION &#8212; a raw file://
attaches nothing and fails SILENTLY.
&#9940; AND THE SCOPE IS AN OPEN DECISION
Fred: "for 10 users how much work do we want to do?"
Minimum (~2 days): manifest + the 23 redirects, riders start over.
Middle (~3 days): the picker and the copy, NO second-phase delete &#8212;
riders remove the old folders themselves. Full (~4&#8211;5 days):
everything above.
&#11088; The middle is probably the right size: every edge case in the delete
phase is a place to be wrong on someone's real data, and what it saves a rider is
a file-manager tap they are perfectly capable of. &#9888; Decide BEFORE building
&#8212; the scope-creep detector applies.
&#9940; The 23 redirects and the manifest are unavoidable in every option.
The choice is only about the migration.

00-2026-09-10 — SIX FIXES, AND THE THIRD COPY OF THE TRUTH
What shipped into the tree today, each applied and verified separately.
⚠ The middle of the day was spent on two changes that broke the ride map and were
rolled back; both are recorded below because the reasoning still teaches.
1 · ⛔⛔ THE MAP-SOURCE FALLBACK LOCK — ROOT CAUSE, TWO LINES
Symptom: first launch of the day, three hardcoded ESRI sources instead
of the catalogue's fifteen, Select Source empty, the rider's slots read as
defaults. Only killing the app cleared it. Droid 2 09-09 (PID 31930 — the process
that had just run a full Utah import), Droid 1 09-10.
⛔ THE WHOLE BUG IN ONE LINE. loadFallback() ended
with initialized = true. init() begins
if (initialized) return. So once the fallback fired, all
FOURTEEN init() call sites — six in
ConvoyDownloadQueue, three workers, both map screens, the corridor
delete — became no-ops. Nothing could recover the session.
⭐ And ensureInit() does not FIND fallback data, it
INSTALLS it: a reader arriving before init() calls
loadFallback() itself. That is the race, and a cold start is when it
loses — no warm process, no page cache, and workers resuming from a previous
session touch the manager before any screen renders.
FIX (FALLBACKLOCK-2026-09-10): loadFallback()
no longer sets initialized; init() clears
usedFallback on success, ⚠ before syncColumnFile
reads it. An early reader still gets the three fallback sources — there is nothing
else to give it — but the next init() does the real read and recovers
within milliseconds.
⭐⭐ THE DURABLE LESSON: A FAILURE PATH THAT RECORDS ITSELF AS A
SUCCESS BLOCKS ITS OWN RECOVERY. Fred, 09-10: "we recorded a failure so
well we didn't let it recover naturally." The fallback was carefully built —
three write guards, a stack trace, explicit refusal to persist bad state — and one
line of bookkeeping made it permanent. ⚠ Look for this shape wherever a
"we tried" flag and a "we succeeded" flag are the same variable.
⚠ STILL TO VERIFY: a cold start, first launch of the day, before
touching either device. Fifteen sources = held.
FALLBACK REQUESTED may still log — that stack trace names the early
caller and is now useful rather than fatal.

00-2026-09-09 — 2.6h RESTORED: THE IMPORT RELEASE · ➡ MOVED TO 2.7b (Fred 09-29 — section 08c)
➡ Moved to 2.7b (Fred 09-29): the state import work is not taken on in 2.7a. Its open items now live in section 08c; this section stays as the record of the 09-09 measurements.
ONE SUBJECT: the import is too slow and too Utah-only. Fred, 09-09:
"we will not rush something this big into the first public release." Early
access ships on what exists today; this is what follows it.
Measured on Droid 2, 09-09, Utah, end to end: 1,762 seconds. Roughly 20
minutes of base import plus 10 for rider trails — and the rider half only applies
to someone who has imported their own tracks, so a NEW rider sees about 20.
⚠ THAT ~20 MINUTES IS THE BIGGEST INSTALL RISK IN THE PRODUCT. It is
what the store listing and every Facebook post has to warn about, and it is why
this release exists.
1 · THE PREFILTER — measured 09-09
From d2_way_tags.db, 425,000 rows:
highwayrowscan never be rideable
service205,307188,638
residential86,97783,793
tertiary14,06813,536
unclassified14,3914,051
track/path/cycleway/bridleway
104,2560
TOTAL425,000290,019 (68.2%)
⛔ THE FALSE START, AND WHAT IT TAUGHT
EXTRACTORDER-2026-09-09 moved classifyRow above
decodeLine so geometry was decoded only for rows that survived.
Sound reasoning, no measurable gain: 792s before, 868s after.
⭐⭐ THE GEOMETRY DECODE WAS NEVER THE COST. It is 425,000 individual
SQLite lookups against osm_way_tags, one per row, and moving them
earlier does not make them fewer. ⛔ I measured what could be SKIPPED and assumed
it was what was EXPENSIVE. They are not the same thing. Profile before
patching.
🔴 DECIDE: the reorder is harmless and correct but buys nothing, and it is in
the early-access AAB. Keep or revert.
⭐ THE ACTUAL FIX
Ask the tag table ONCE which ids can never be rideable, hold them in a
HashSet, and let the extract loop skip them with a membership test.
~280,000 lookups become one indexed query.
⛔ AN EXCLUDE LIST, NOT A KEEP LIST. Anything the query does not
understand stays in and is classified properly. A keep list silently drops
whatever the rules learn to handle next.
⛔ ONLY THE ROAD-CLASS GROUP IS SAFE TO SKIP. The legally-shut rows —
access=private, motor_vehicle=no — are KEPT by the
classifier and labelled so a rider can see why a trail is not offered. Excluding
them would change what lands.
⚠ Every exclusion mirrors a rule in OsmTrailClassifier. If the
classifier changes and the query does not, ground is lost silently. The
safety checks in prefilter_check_2026-09-09.py are what prove it:
unclassified must NEVER be excluded (it is in on shape alone), and
no row rescued by ohv, atv, motor_vehicle,
motorcar or four_wd_only may be caught.
2 · PREPROCESS THE DOWNLOADS
Fred, 09-09: "the 10 minutes it takes to process the trails before step 7
will have all the data here for step 7." Fetch and tag ahead of the extract so
step 7 opens with everything in place.
⛔ AN AREA DOWNLOAD MAY SPAN SEVERAL STATES. A state download is one
PBF and one GeoPackage; an area is N of each — Bar 10 crosses into Arizona and the
Nevada corner is right there. So this is a job PER STATE, merging into one tag
table, not one job.
⚠ The merge must be idempotent. A rider who has Utah and then downloads
an area crossing into Arizona must not refetch Utah. osm_way_tags
keyed on osm_id handles it — OSM ids are globally unique — but only
if the table PERSISTS between downloads.
🔴 OPEN, AND IT GATES EVERYTHING BELOW: does
osm_way_tags survive between imports, or is it dropped and rebuilt?
If rebuilt, a second state download ALREADY pays the full tag cost again, and the
ledger is meaningless until that changes.
3 · THE PER-STATE LEDGER
Fred, 09-09: "nounce the state selection list against the preprocessing
successful state and remove them from eval." Before preprocessing, subtract
the states already recorded done; fetch and tag only what is left.
⛔ RECORDED ON SUCCESS, NEVER ON START. A state marked done after a
half-finished tag pass leaves a partial table nothing revisits. ⚠ That is the
09-07 marker problem — clearing two of three left the third standing down
silently — and it is why clearTrailsOnce writes its marker AFTER the
clear, so a crash retries.
⚠ AND IT MUST KNOW WHEN TO INVALIDATE. Geofabrik refreshes their
extracts: 425,218 → 425,267 rows between two runs a day apart, 09-08 to 09-09. A
state done six months ago is stale. ⭐ Store the DATE alongside the state so the
policy can be set later without redoing the structure.
4 · RESUME AN UNFINISHED DOWNLOAD
Fred, 09-09: "a start for a failed process at that process step ... using
the failure at step as the pickup point."
Per state the steps are fetch PBF → build tag rows → prefilter → fetch
GeoPackage → extract. The ledger records which one it died at; the restart
re-enters there.
⛔ A STEP IS DONE ONLY WHEN ITS OUTPUT IS COMPLETE AND VERIFIED. A
partly-written step RESTARTS; only a verified one is skipped.
Files are easy. A PBF or GeoPackage of the expected size is a
stat; a short one is a resume or a refetch.
⚠ The tag pass is not. It is a table, not a file, and ROW COUNT ALONE
DOES NOT PROVE IT FINISHED — it proves it got somewhere. ⭐ Simplest safe rule: an
unfinished tag pass is redone from scratch. Minutes, not the twenty.
WHERE THE RESUME CHECK RUNS. ⛔ NOT in
StartupHousekeeping.run() — it checks its marker first and returns,
so anything inside fires only on launches that clear and reload. ⭐
everyLaunch(ctx), after the authority gate resolves — the
ungated pass built 09-08, already running where shared storage is available.
⚠ ITS RULES APPLY: cheap, idempotent, non-destructive, never throws.
A resume check that finds nothing pending runs on every launch forever.
🔴 DECIDE FIRST: resume automatically or prompt? A 317 MB download
restarting silently on mobile data is a one-star. And what counts as
unfinished? A PBF at 90% is resumable; a tag pass that died mid-write is not.
⭐ This is the same problem as the existing crashed-import restart from the
manifest item, one level down. Step 8 becoming a tracked stage on 09-08 was
its prerequisite.
5 · FIFTY-STATE PUBLIC/PRIVATE OWNERSHIP SOURCES
This is what makes the app Utah-only in practice. Only Utah has the
ownership polygon layer, so land_status is null everywhere else and
the private filter cannot work. A rider in Colorado installs, waits twenty
minutes and gets trails with no ownership.
⭐ It is also the honest reason the store listing has to name which states have
good coverage.
⚠ CARRIED FORWARD, AND IT IS THE TRAP: a layer that lists PUBLIC
land POSITIVELY INVERTS THE TEST. Utah's layer answers "who owns this"; a layer
answering "this is public" means absence is not private. Getting it backwards
marks public land private across a whole state.
⭐ The sampling is already settled — allPrivate() samples every
half mile plus both ends, and ANY public segment wins (Fred, 08-31). What is
missing is only the data source per state.
🔴 Which states first? ⭐ Follow where riders actually are, once early access
shows you.
WHAT THIS CLOSES
Fred, 09-09: "that closes the door on trail accuracy or loading
issues."
Loading — the prefilter and preprocessing cut the base import, the
ledger stops a second state paying full cost, the resume stops a failed download
costing everything.
Accuracy — fifty-state ownership makes land_status real
outside Utah, which the private filter and the router both depend on.
⚠ OPEN QUESTIONS, IN ORDER
Does osm_way_tags persist between imports? Gates the
ledger and the merge.
Are both downloads needed? 160 MB PBF and 317 MB GeoPackage — 2:20 and
4:47 on 09-09, about seven of the twenty minutes. The GeoPackage supplies
geometry, the PBF supplies tags. Design question, not tuning.
Keep or revert EXTRACTORDER-2026-09-09? Harmless, correct,
buys nothing, already in the early-access build.
Resume automatically or prompt?
Which states get ownership data first?
