00-2026-09-08 — THE GPX ROUND TRIP, AND THE FOUR DEFECTS IT FOUND
THE TEST THE CHECKLIST SAID HAD NEVER BEEN RUN. Export a route from one
device, import it on the other. It found four separate defects in one chain,
and not one of them was visible to code inspection — I had checked two ends of
this chain that morning and declared it complete.
⛔ THE FOUR, IN THE ORDER THEY HID EACH OTHER
The export never wrote the payload. parseGpxRoutes has
looked for &lt;grouptrack:notes&gt; since 08-29 and prefers it over
&lt;desc&gt; — "the payload wins where present, it is ours and
complete." ⛔ Nothing ever wrote it. The parser's own comment says
"our own extensions payload carries the recipe home", written in the
present tense about a writer that did not exist.
The import never stored the notes. insertRoute(name, wkt, bbox…)
— route.description was parsed and dropped on the floor. The 08-29
work fixed the reader and left the writer.
⭐ The import wrapped the payload as a headline. MY BUG, and it only
appeared once the export started working. The wrap was correct for as long as
description only ever held plain prose. Fixing the export turned a
sound assumption into a defect in one commit.
Nothing decoded the XML entities. The payload arrived as
{&amp;quot;generated&amp;quot;:…}, failed to parse, and landed in the
narrative headline as gibberish. ⚠ A REGEX IS NOT AN XML PARSER —
&lt;desc&gt; survived only because plain sentences have nothing to
escape.
⚠ &amp;amp; IS DECODED LAST. Decoding it first turns a literal
"&amp;amp;quot;" into a quote and silently corrupts text that legitimately
contained an escaped entity. The order is the correctness.
⛔⛔ HOW A HALF-FINISHED ITEM READ AS OPEN FOR SIX WEEKS
Fred: "how do we get to this point in release planning to find things that

THE RULES THAT COME OUT OF IT (Fred, 09-08)
⭐ TRUST THE RECORD WHEN IT SAYS OPEN. "we need to trust the record
if it says open." The response to an item that looks already-fixed is to
prove it end to end and then strike it — never to reason it must have been
done.
⭐ KEEP THE CHECKLIST CURRENT AS WORK LANDS, in the session it lands,
"truly the purpose of the checklist." Amending a line when you know the
answer costs seconds; re-deriving it six weeks later cost most of a day.
⭐ A LINE MUST BE ABLE TO SAY PARTIAL. Binary open/closed forces a
wrong answer when half the work is done — which is the shape of every defect
found today. "export done, import not" is a state that had no home.
⭐ ONLY OPEN ITEMS BELONG HERE. Completed work is struck and preserved
in its recap doc — already the stated rule; the practice slipped.
⚠ SOME ITEMS CANNOT BE CERTIFIED ALONE. Export proves nothing until
something imports. An item spanning two ends stays open until both exist and the
path has been exercised, however complete either half looks.

StartupHousekeeping.run() checks its marker FIRST and returns, so

marked as done. we are responsible for removing one time launch code from the
next release." The discipline is ours, not the code's. ⚠ REMOVE IT WHEN
THE NEXT RELEASE IS CUT.
THE RULES FOR ANYTHING PUT IN IT
Cheap — it runs on every launch; a startup tax accumulates unnoticed.
Idempotent — the second run must find nothing to do.
Non-destructive — deleting and overwriting is run()'s job,
behind a marker, on purpose.
Never throws — a convergence failure is not a reason to stop the app
starting.
⚠ CALLED AFTER THE GATE RESOLVES, not before. It touches
map_keys.json in SHARED STORAGE and the authority gate exists to stop
exactly that before all-files access is confirmed. Placed early it fails silently
on an ungranted device and never retries.

00-2026-09-07 — RIDER TRAILS: BUILT, DEVICE-PROVEN, COMMITTED
PURPOSE. Recorded tracks become unnamed trails wherever a ride left the
published network. The 09-06 Python prototype is now a Kotlin feature with three
entry points. Commit 61e3b2148, 10 files, 1,066 insertions.
MEASURED. Droid 1: 1,537 trails / 2,279 miles. Droid 2:
1,872 / 2,425 miles — and that number came back identical across three
separate runs, which is the evidence the scan is deterministic.
⭐ THE 09-07 DESIGN CHANGE — connectors are part of the trail
v3 wrote connectors as separate short lines. Fred: "they are the start of
the trail and connect to rest of trail points, same thing with the last point —
we are adding one new trail including derived connector."
So a rider trail is anchor node → the ground you rode → anchor node, one
polyline. ⭐ This removes a real failure mode: a run written whose connector write
failed was an island the router could not reach — decorative, by Fred's own
framing. One row, joined at both ends, or nothing.
MAX_CONN_M still applies per end; beyond 60&nbsp;m that end is left
unjoined, because a longer connector is a guess rather than a gap.
⛔ THE FIVE THINGS THAT DECIDE CORRECTNESS — do not relax any of them
Candidates PER TRACK, by bbox — never the whole table. Utah is 145,942
trails, ~5.6M segments. The Python indexes all of it because it runs on a laptop;
the same code on a 3&nbsp;GB device is an allocation that does not come back.
AFTER the reload, NEVER at the clear. StartupHousekeeping
and clearTrailsOnce only CLEAR — they hand the reload to the import
and return needsReload = true. Scanning an emptied trails table reads
every track as fully off-network and promotes all 3,651 miles as whole-track
trails, silently, with the real trails landing on top minutes later.
BEFORE step 8, not after. Step 8 classifies BY VALUE across every row.
Rider trails written after it carry no land_status and no
use_type.
⭐ THE DEDUP IS THE DIRECTION TEST, NOT THE HASH. Two GPS traces over
the same ground never hash alike — the same reason OSM and UGRC turned out to be
independent surveys with 9 matches in 89,554. A rider trail written on pass one
lies under its own track, going the same way, within NEAR_M, so pass
two reads that ground as on-network and produces nothing. The dedup happens in
the scanner, before anything reaches the database.
Live data per track, in sequence. Two riders over the same unmapped
ground: the first track's new trail is already present when the second is
scanned. Index once up front and the same ground is written twice, with different
hashes, and nothing catches it.
⭐ TWO PASSES — measured, not assumed
Droid 1: pass one 1,537, pass two 70, pass three 0.
Fred's reading, and it is the right one: "we had breaks new trails and
existing trails for them to connect to." The second pass is the network
settling around the connectors the first one wrote — new anchor nodes
exist, so a few runs close at different points and leave short stretches either
side. One pass leaves ~5% of the edge geometry unsettled; two converge every
time. The import stage runs both and sums the counts.

⛔ NO SCANNED FLAG — the 09-06 design was dropped 09-07
The 09-06 handoff specified a field on the track extension recording that a
track had been through the process. Fred killed it: "no need to flag them as
run."
⭐ And it was worse than unnecessary — it was self-defeating. The flag
would have had to be reset whenever trails were cleared, or a reload would strand
the ground. But the job only runs when trails HAVE been cleared and reloaded, so
the flags would be reset every single time the flag was used. A cursor wiped
immediately before every use is not a cursor.
What makes it safe to drop is that the scan is already idempotent underneath
(see the direction test above). Re-running costs time, never duplicates.
⚠ DO NOT RE-PROPOSE A COLUMN ON track_properties FOR
THIS. That table is the one that cannot be cleared and reloaded, so a column
added there lives forever in whatever shape it starts with.
WHERE IT RUNS — three entry points, one function
ADD TRAILS FROM TRACKS — blue Surface directly under RESYNC TRACKS in
ConvoyTrackImportScreen, with its own dialog. Always visible: the
condition that would have gated it was the flag.
Import stage _ridertrails — two passes, after the sources
and before step 8, with its own manifest entry and count.
Trigger in resolveTrackAdd — every genuine INSERT, inline
on the caller's thread, wrapped so a scan failure can never lose a track. ⚠ Inside
the wasNew branch: a duplicate re-add is the same geometry over
ground already scanned.
⚠ COST, KNOWN NOT FIXED: the trigger opens a dedup session per call,
reloading ~145,942 hashes. Fine for one add; a 90-file bulk import does it 90
times. First place to look if imports drag — the fix is one session opened around
the bulk loop.

THE REFERENCE PROTOTYPE
ridertrails_2026-09-06_v3.py reads a pulled
grouptrack_spatial.db, writes GPX, touches nothing.
⭐ If the Kotlin and the Python ever disagree, the Python is right until proven
otherwise. RiderTrailScanner is a transliteration of it, not a
re-derivation — which is why it is PURE: no database, no Android imports, no
geometry serialisation.
⚠ It does not build WKT and must not learn how. The identity hash is
taken over the serialised geometry STRING, so a second serialiser with different
spacing or number formatting yields a different identity for identical ground and
dedup silently stops recognising its own rows.
⚠ Cell keys use TRUNCATION, not floor, to match Python's
int(). Every longitude out west is negative; floor would bucket
segments one cell off and the only symptom would be a different trail count with
no error.

⭐⭐ STEP 1 — THE LEGACY MENU RESTRUCTURE. BLOCKS EVERYTHING BELOW IT.
Fred, 08-30, verbatim: "legacy menu items are being removed and restructured. no import
functionality will exist on that menu. period."
The menu is the submenu inside the Convoy/GroupTrack menu — the GroupTrack icon in the
Meshtastic left sidebar. Manual sections convoy-A and planning-L. It is
renamed Radio Setup and holds radio configuration only.
⭐ The destination already exists. Import lives at Work with Map Features → IMPORT

⚠ The Map Features panel on the map is NOT this menu and is untouched. Route+ still tucks

⛔⛔ THE BOUNDARY — READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING EITHER SIDE OF IT. The legacy menu and
the manifest intent are different things and the decisions on them are opposite.
The menu: import comes off it. Period.
The manifest intent filters: they STAY DECLARED. The existing import is repointed
to launch the new import function. Fred 08-30: he was advised against removing them, and the
suggestion was to change the existing import to launch the new one — rather than fighting the
Meshtastic manifest entries again.
⚠ Written this way deliberately: a reader who takes "no import on that menu" and deletes the
intent filters has undone the decision, and a reader who takes "repoint the import" and puts a menu
row back has undone the other half.
⛔⛔ ONE OLD IMPORT PROCESS, TWO ENTRY POINTS (Fred 08-30). A picker job on the legacy
menu selects GPX files and runs them through the old import process — and the same old process
is triggered by tapping a GPX in Downloads (the intent path).
⭐ So neither change retires it on its own. Remove the picker and the intent still lands on
the old process. Repoint the intent and the picker still calls it. Retirement takes both, and
until both are done the old path stays live through whichever entry point nobody is looking at.
⚠ ORDER: repoint the intent FIRST, then remove the picker. That way the app works through
both entry points at every moment. The other order points a live intent at a process being
dismantled underneath it.
⛔ Do not delete the old process on the strength of the menu removal alone — the menu is
only one of its two callers.
⚠ A BEHAVIOUR TO DECIDE, NOT INHERIT: the old process DELETES the source file once
totalImported &gt; 0 (recorded in the GPX-import section of this file). Tapping a GPX in
Downloads today removes the rider's file. Whether the new import keeps that must be a decision.
TO VERIFY BEFORE SCOPING: grep both callers — the menu picker's call site and the
intent handler — and confirm which one Import Ride from Downloads (the no-caller row
recorded 08-10) actually is. Also confirm what the picker hands over: the intent path delivers a
content:// URI, and if the picker uses the system file picker it does too, in which case
the temp-file copy is needed on both paths rather than one.

00-2026-08-29 — THE PLANNER CLOSED, AND A TWO-DAY BUG FOUND
The AI route planner is complete. The recipe rebuilds a batch from a saved route in one
press, and the cached-graph defect that made a second search in the same area return worse routes
is fixed and verified against the exact sequence that produced it.
CommitWhat
956a7ae54The recipe button wired end to end; creating a trailhead
selects it; the toolbar gate; layer states on compare; the quarter-mile ring; search opens at the
trailhead step; order on the assess trace.
46798c44cThe recipe goes into every draft, not only the batch
file.
851db572dcopyOf() on every cache hit; the ring
explained; the two-character state hint.
⛔⛔ THE CACHED GRAPH WAS BEING MUTATED BY EVERY PIN
The symptom, over two days: the same four pins covered 2 of 4 on one run and 4 of 4 on
another, from identical inputs — deterministic within a session, different across one.
The cause: splitEdgeAt(g, ..) writes into whatever graph it is handed, and
a cache hit returned the cached object by reference. The first run's pin splits became the
next run's starting topology.
run 1   build -> cached ; pins split it ; the cache is now carved
run 2   same key -> "Using cached map" -> pins split the ALREADY-SPLIT graph
⭐ FRED'S OBSERVATION IS WHAT CRACKED IT: "the only difference I am aware of is one
was the first run of the day and another followed a previous run in that area." Everything
else — the corridor box, the pin coordinates, the trail data — was identical. A cold cache was
right and a warm one was not, and that is a statement about state, not about routing.
⚠ IT HAD BEEN WRITTEN DOWN ON 08-27 AND LEFT UNPROVEN: "splitEdgeAt mutates the
cached graph, which would break recipe determinism SILENTLY — NOT VERIFIED." It did. Two days
of symptoms were chased while the diagnosis sat in the notes.
⭐ THE FIX: A COPY, NOT A CACHE KEY. Adding the pin set to the key would
rebuild when pins differ — but two IDENTICAL runs would still hit, and the second would inherit
the first's splits. Fred: "needs to work 100% of the time."
All seven Graph fields, including adj's inner lists, which
splitEdgeAt appends to — copying the map alone would have left the same bug in a
harder-to-find form.
⭐ VERIFIED BY REPRODUCTION: trailhead-only search, then the same four pins, on a warm
cache. Two routes with four pins and four with three — matching a cold start.
⭐ HOW IT WAS ISOLATED — AND A PROXY THAT LIED
assess_pins_v2_2026-08-29.py answers reachability against a fresh pull of the
device's own database, because three trail counts were in play: the device had 139,688 and two
test databases held 216,616 and 160,628. Measuring the wrong world would have proved
nothing.
Result: every pin snapped 218–289 ft, and all four sat in the anchor's 1,143-trail
network. So reachability was never the problem — unreachable and
onFragment were empty because they were correct — and the corridor box, which does
not involve pins at all, was never too small.
⚠ AND ITS FIRST VERSION WAS CONFIDENTLY WRONG. v1 joined trails at their
ENDPOINTS only and reported 1,836 components across 3,854 trails — barely anything
connected to anything. That cannot be true: the app built six routes through that ground.
The engine splits edges at intersections. A trail crossing another mid-span connects
there, not only where a line ends. v1 saw two trails passing through each other as strangers.
⭐ THE RULE, and it is the third time this project has met it: a proxy that is cheap to
write will answer a different question from the one asked, precisely and plausibly. The
six-thousand-foot pin snap, the subset proxy in the engine rewrite, and now this.
⭐ THE RECIPE ONLY EVER LIVED IN THE BATCH FILE
The rebuild button never appeared on any of 27 saved routes, and the reason was structural:
recipe -> batch file -> DELETED when the batch resolves
notes  -> draft file -> route_notes -> survives
SAVE SELECTED promotes a draft by copying its notes, then deletes the batch. The
narrative survived and the recipe died with it.
⭐ Fixed by putting the recipe where the journey already runs — inside the notes block,
which travels draft → route_notes → and next, the GPX description. No new plumbing at any
step.
⚠ Routes saved before today cannot be repaired; the batch that held their parameters is
gone.
⚠ WHAT THE SCORER DOES THAT MAY SURPRISE A RIDER
Fred, 08-29: "interesting that from a points standpoint a non-user route finished
second." A route taking THREE pins ranked above ones taking four.
That is the scorer working. Pins are worth 60 with per-class decay; features earn their
way in on gain per mile. A route that trades one pin for several good features and less retrace
genuinely is a better ride.
⚠ But a rider who dropped four must-sees may not expect the second-ranked route to skip
one. The compare table shows coverage, so it is visible — the ORDERING is what might warrant a
thought later.

⬜ SPECIFIED — the startup import check
Fred, 08-29: "record failure on incompletes on app restart — open imports for any
reason. Suggest a rerun of that import to correct any issue that may have arisen."
⭐ AN IMPORT STILL OPEN ON RESTART DID NOT FINISH, and that is the whole test. No failure
logging is needed at import time: network off, app killed, crash, battery — all look the same and
all want the same answer. It cannot miss anything, because it does not depend on the failure
path being reached. A process that dies mid-import writes no error but leaves an open
record.
⭐ THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS. HomeStateImportController
tracks a per-source status and skips "completed" at :259; at :916 it
scans the state JSON files for process_state == "completed".
So this is a READ, not new tracking — the same shape as
PinFeasibility.unreachable, which had been computed and ignored for days. Find the
files whose process_state is not completed, report the source and its
date, offer the rerun.
⭐ And :259 is what makes the rerun safe: completed sources are skipped, so a rerun
fetches only what is missing and duplicates nothing. The rider risks nothing by accepting.
The dialog
RuleWhy
On launch, only when something is open⚠ A message every launch gets
ignored, and then the one that matters is ignored too.
Name the source and the date"Open Source Maps, 12 August" tells the rider
whether this is today's problem or one they have been riding with for weeks.
Two buttons per entry: REMOVE and RERUN⭐ RERUN launches the import
immediately — not a link to the import screen, not a confirmation. The rider said what they
wanted.
REMOVE takes it off the reportFor the state they do not want. ⚠ Annotated
as removed, never deleted — imports number under twenty, so the history costs nothing and
the import screen still shows every attempt and its outcome.
⚠ NO TIME WINDOW. An earlier draft had one, on the reasoning that an import abandoned in
June should stop nagging by itself. It should not. Removal is a decision a rider makes; a
window hides things nobody decided about, which is exactly what REMOVE exists to prevent.
⭐ WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING — Fred, 08-29: six sources appeared to fail in nine
seconds, and the cause was the network being switched off. Not a defect, and struck from the
backlog. But the app reported nothing. A rider who does the same has no idea their trails
are incomplete, and sparse results look exactly like sparse country.

⭐⭐ THE TRAIL-TYPE FILTER — the design this classification is for (2026-08-29)
Fred's vision, stated at the end of the classification run:
"We have types which control what is eligible to be displayed — tracks, routes, trails and
waypoints. Within trails we have a setting under the legend that controls the types of trails you
will display, and those values are saved from session to session. Then in route building we show
the current filter values and allow you to accept or reselect."
Two levels, and they are different questions
ARTIFACT TYPE     tracks · routes · trails · waypoints      what is drawn at all
  └─ TRAIL TYPE   OHV · 4wd · motorized track · hiking ·    which trails, of those
                  hiking and biking · biking · equestrian ·
                  unclassified motorized · unclassified unknown
The outer level exists today. The inner one is what trail_type makes possible.
Why this is the point of the whole OSM exercise
⭐ It resolves several open threads with one mechanism:
ProblemWhat the filter does
Hiking trails now IN the tableShown, labelled, not routed — Fred:
"it can go back in because it clearly has a category identity." A path with a correct label
is a feature; a path silently mixed in was the reason 08-24 removed it.
buildGraph reads every trailReads what the filter permits.
Tracks invisible to the plannerThe same mechanism — a TYPE, not a separate
table.
A rider on a dirt bike, not a SxSA different selection over the same
data.
⚠ AND IT RETIRES AN OLD COMPROMISE. The standing rule was "display and routing are
the same filter — cannot be both." With types they can be the same mechanism with different
selections, which is what was wanted all along and was not expressible before.
Where the settings live
SurfaceBehaviour
The legendThe trail-type toggles sit here, under Trails. Saved session
to session — a rider who never wants hiking trails on the map sets it once.
Route building⭐ Shows the CURRENT filter and asks. Accept it, or
reselect for this ride. The rider is told what the planner will use rather than inheriting a map
setting silently.
⚠ AND THAT SECOND POINT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. A display setting that
silently bounds a search is exactly the kind of invisible state that cost two days this week. The
planner should say what it is about to use — and the parameters step is where it already asks
everything else.
⚠ It also belongs in the recipe. A rebuild that used a different filter from the original
would produce different routes for a reason nothing recorded.

⭐ WHAT IT FIXED, BY NAME
DROPPED, asphalt unclassified: Main Street · Center Street · 6000 West ·
Thermo Road · Manderfield Road. The community-roads-as-trails fault, solved.
unclassified is OSM's tag for a minor public road, so a paved lane matched the old
filter exactly.
ADDED, unpaved tertiary and residential: Johnson Canyon Road ·
Strevell Road · Dove Creek Road · West Pass Road · 3300 South. The rideable-roads-missing
fault, solved — and this is the Mountain Spring Road case: highway=tertiary,
surface=dirt, on the map, ridden, and never in the trails table.
⚠ TWO DROPPED ENTRIES TO EXPLAIN BEFORE THIS SHIPS: Bonneville
Shoreline Trail and Weaver Way, both track with no surface tag. They were
dropped by an access or motor_vehicle restriction, which may be correct — but the Bonneville
Shoreline is a known route and a rule that removes it needs to be understood rather than
accepted.
⚠ Open before any of this is built
The trails table has no osm_id. source_id is null on every
row and nothing carries the OSM way id — so there is no join from the device to either
source, and no incremental update is possible until the import keeps it.
Two vocabularies already exist. carto_code holds USGS values —
"2 - Hiking and Biking Allowed", "1 - Hiking Only", "5 - Biking Only", "4 - Road-concurrent" — on
38% of rows, and is null on the other 62%. The OSM classification must map INTO that
vocabulary or the table will carry three.
Rules are a first draft. Exclusions first (private, motor_vehicle=no), then motorized
confirmation, then surface for roads, then tracks in on shape. They have not been reviewed
against ground anyone has ridden beyond the examples above.
⭐⭐ OSM DATA REFRESH — clear and reimport, by source. Quarterly (08-29), SUPERSEDED BY FIXED SEMI-ANNUAL DATES (08-30)
⭐⭐ SETTLED 2026-08-30 — FIXED DATES, NOT A PER-SOURCE TIMER. Fred: "every Jan 1 and July 1st we request a reimport of all completed json sources (areas and states) that exist in the trails download history." The 90-day rolling timer below is superseded; everything else in this section stands.THE MEASUREMENT THAT SIZED IT (08-30, first real number). The 07-27 skinny and the 08-30 classified build were compared on shared osm_ids: 88,687 of 89,349 hashes identical — 662 geometries changed in about a month, 0.74%. Six months extrapolates to ~4.5%, roughly 5,600 trails on a 126k Utah table. ⭐ Small enough that twice a year is proportionate, and a prompt people learn to dismiss is worse than a longer interval.⭐ IT ALSO CONFIRMS CLEAR-AND-RELOAD OVER INCREMENTAL. A changed geometry produces a changed hash, so an incremental path cannot tell an EDIT from a NEW WAY without carrying osm_id on the device and comparing versions — and then it still faces the deletion-versus-absence problem. The measured cost of not being incremental is ~4.5% staleness at the prompt.Piece08-30 behaviourThe triggerJan 1 and Jul 1. One date for everyone. No per-source timer to track.The listEvery completed JSON source in the trails download history — states AND areas. ⛔ Completed means the completion stamp, never the presence of a record: a record written unconditionally is what marked three FAILED runs as permanently imported on 07-27.⭐ STATES FIRST, THEN AREASFred 08-30. Run all state pulls, then the areas — omitting any area whose state was already pulled, because the state import already contains that ground. A state that completes DURING this run counts.Recently importedA source completed shortly before the date rolls to the next one rather than being reimported two weeks after its first run.Offer, never actUnchanged. Six months of drift is not a reason to clear a rider's trail data while they are getting ready to ride. Keeps appearing until done.Disk⭐ Cost does NOT stack. The pipeline deletes between steps and the skinny has a standardized name, so sources run sequentially through one slot — peak storage is one source, not the sum.⚠ Therefore never concurrentTwo imports at once write over each other in the shared slot. Sequential is a CONSTRAINT here, not a preference.⚠ Resume must know WHICH sourceA failure mid-loop leaves the slot holding whichever source was running. The two recovery points (zip present → resume at process; skinny present → resume at import) must read the source from the manifest rather than assume it.Rules move too⭐ A reload picks up CLASSIFICATION RULE changes as well as data changes. The interval is how long a rider keeps yesterday's rules — which may matter more than the 4.5%, since the rules are new and will get corrections.⚠ Fred 08-30 on the redundant-pull case: "all it costs us is time to process twice, the big cost is the repeated downloads." A state download is ~332 MB against a second processing pass measured in minutes — so skip on completed state, and accept a repeated pull where two areas share a state that was NOT pulled. "It is what it is."
⭐⭐ AND THE RULE BELONGS IN EVERY AREA DOWNLOAD, NOT ONLY IN THE REFRESH LOOP (Fred 08-30). "Check json for completed full state import before adding state to the pull." Any area import, whenever it runs, resolves its state and skips the pull if a completed FULL-STATE import already exists. The refresh loop then inherits it rather than implementing it.⭐ It fixes the everyday case too: a rider who has Utah and then draws a box near Moab should not re-download Utah for ground already on the device. Nothing stops that today.Where it goes: beside the findByBbox call the area path already makes — the state resolution happens there anyway.⛔ FULL-STATE only. A prior AREA import of the same state does not count and must not suppress the pull — an area covers a box, not a state.⚠ Tell the rider. Drawing a box and having nothing happen reads as broken. "Utah is already imported — the trails in this area are on your device."⚠ findByBbox is recorded as OVER-INCLUSIVE (it tests the drawn box against each state RECTANGLE; California reaches east to −114.13). Over-inclusive is the safe direction — an area gets skipped when its state WAS pulled rather than missed — but a box near a line can resolve to an imported neighbour and skip a pull it needed. Same bbox-precision item already on the list.
Fred's plan, and it replaces the incremental-update design below:
"Use the last import date for OSM data as the trigger to refresh. Remind the user to refresh
map data — once a quarter is enough. In the startup job: pending map update, execute now or wait.
Keeps showing up till the refresh is completed. Good for another 90 days."
⭐ WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN THE INCREMENTAL DESIGN
Clear the OSM-owned rows, reimport, done. No three-way reconcile, no version comparison,
and — the hard one — no deletion-detection problem. The 08-29 research spent most of its
length on how to tell a deleted way from one that is merely absent from a truncated extract. A
clear-and-reload never asks.
⛔ AND IT ONLY WORKS BECAUSE OF SOURCE OWNERSHIP. Clearing every trail would take the
USGS rows and anything a rider created. Clearing only what OSM owns is safe by construction —
which is what makes the ownership column load-bearing rather than tidy.
The mechanism
PieceBehaviour
The triggerThe last import date for the OSM source. No version checking,
no diffing — a date.
The interval⛔ SUPERSEDED 08-30 — fixed Jan 1 / Jul 1, see above. (prior text) 90 days. Geofabrik rebuilds daily, but the QA evidence
is roughly one change per month across 1,600 trails — quarterly is proportionate to how much
actually moves.
Where it appearsThe startup job, beside the incomplete-import check. Same
place, same shape.
What it asks"Pending map update — execute now or wait."
If they wait⭐ It keeps showing up until the refresh completes. Same
rule as the incomplete-import prompt: the only way off the list is doing the thing.
AfterGood for another 90 days.
⚠ WHAT A CLEAR-AND-RELOAD COSTS, and both are acceptable:
Extension rows attached to OSM trails go with them, if they key on geometry. ⚠ That is
the one thing worth settling first — are extension rows keyed by geom_hash or by
trail_id? If by id, and the ids are reassigned on reimport, rider notes detach. If the
answer is bad, the fix is upstream of this plan.
It is a full state download. Which is why it is twice-yearly (Jan 1 / Jul 1, 08-30) and prompted rather than automatic. ⭐ And the cost does not stack across sources — the pipeline deletes between steps and the skinny has a standardized name, so a state plus its areas run sequentially through one slot.
⭐ AND ROUTES SURVIVE REGARDLESS. Fred: "do we build a route because we have two ids?
No, we build it with ids. They are not missing." A route's vertices reference trail ids and
queryGeomByIds fetches by them, so geometry moving underneath does not break a saved
route. The hash question is about joining sources, not about routing.
⚠ THE INCREMENTAL DESIGN BELOW IS NOW A FALLBACK. It stays recorded
because the reasoning about way-splitting and id stability is still true, and because if
clear-and-reload turns out to cost too much — a rider on a metered connection, or extension rows
that cannot survive it — the three-way reconcile is the alternative that was already worked
out.
⭐ THE WAY FORWARD ON OSM — four stages, in order (2026-08-29)
Fred, closing the session: "We need to build and vet our new skinny table with new categories. Then modify the OSM import process to include picking up and extracting PBF files by
state and processing by state. Then monitor state and area for 90-day age, to clear and reimport
OSM data for that state or area."
⭐ The order matters and it is the right one — prove the data before changing the
pipeline, and change the pipeline before automating when it runs.

verifyPbf OPENS the fileReads the 4-byte big-endian BlobHeader

stated reasoning: no Content-Length to compare against, so opening the artifact is the PRIMARY

resume it.
⛔⛔ THE TRAP THIS CHANGE CAUGHT, worth keeping: the enum gained two values and
nothing broke at compile time — there is no exhaustive when over
OsmStage anywhere. The real exposure was an equality test:
OsmImportPanel:548 read stage == REDUCE || stage == IMPORT, which compiles
happily and is silently wrong the moment a rung is added — a state with both files downloaded
sits at PREPARE_TAGS, zipExists reads false, and row 1 (DOWNLOAD) reports the extract as
absent while it is on disk. ⭐ Patched in the SAME change, and written explicitly (Fred: "do
it right once") rather than as stage >= PREPARE_TAGS — ordinal comparison silently
absorbs any rung added later, and a future stage should have to be considered rather than
inherited.
⚠ METHOD, MINE, 08-30: I reissued a patch under a NAME ALREADY USED and Fred ran the
stale copy — the Windows rename mechanism, the same one that has carried the wrong manual forward
more than once. The dry run's own output (5 anchors, one file) is what exposed it. ⭐ Every version
gets a unique name, and a patch should PRINT ITS OWN IDENTITY as its first line so a stale copy is
obvious immediately rather than inferred from a count further down.

⭐⭐ OsmPbfTagReader (new)Hand-written PBF reader. No new
dependency, no build change. Wire exists in core/proto but that is Meshtastic's
module with root("meshtastic.*") pruning and publishing config, so OSM protos there
would not generate without editing upstream's build.
OsmTrailClassifier (new)The rules, with
Result(type, carto, motorized) — ⭐ the router filters on the BOOLEAN, the legend on the
TYPE. Two consumers, one classification, no way for them to disagree.
⭐⭐⭐ THE METHOD THAT MADE THE READER SAFE — PYTHON FIRST, THEN TRANSLITERATE. The PBF
parsing is ours to get right, and two things in the format fail silently: the string table is
PER BLOCK and a way's keys/vals are INDICES into it (carry a table across blocks and you get real tag
names on the wrong ways — plausible output, no error); and keys/vals are PACKED varints, one
length-delimited blob, which read as unpacked come back empty.
So it was written in Python first with no OSM library — zlib and struct only —
(pbf_handparse_validate_2026-08-30_v1.py) and run against
utah-260828.osm.pbf. It reported 701,334 ways carrying a highway tag and
87,079 taken by today's filter — matching the osmium survey and the classifier ledger
exactly. access private=34511 matched to the digit, and ohv came
back carrying no @ (&gt;48" wide);designated (48" wide or less), which a mis-indexed
string table cannot produce. ⭐ The Kotlin is a transliteration of something already correct
rather than a first attempt.
⚠ Two things that run measured and would otherwise read as faults. PBF stores ALL
NODES FIRST: 3,400 blocks walked with 0 ways, then 2,107,222 ways in the last ~80 — so the
progress line sits at zero rows for most of the parse. And two thirds of what it walks is discarded
(2.1M ways, 701k with a highway tag).
⭐⭐ SYNCHRONOUS WITH A PROGRESS METER, NOT A WORKER — Fred 08-30, correcting me. I proposed
a WorkManager worker because OsmExtractWorker already uses that pattern. Fred:
"disagree, the worker is unobservable and will cause cancellation by not knowing it is running.
synchronous with a progress meter."
⭐ Same argument this checklist already carries from 08-21 about silent startup work: a job
nobody can watch is a job that gets doubted or killed. A background worker chewing 167 MB with no
visible sign is WORSE than a slow bar — the failure mode is a rider force-quitting mid-parse and
leaving a half-written artifact. ⭐ The extract uses a worker because it is short; a 167 MB parse is
not. The progress line reports WAYS WALKED as well as rows kept, because rows stay at zero through
the node section.
⭐⭐⭐ TWEAK RULES, NOT RECORDS — Fred 08-30: "it will be easier to adjust if we are
tweaking rules rather than reselecting records in a process."
Because every row in the widened net lands in the table WITH a type, a rule change is a
reclassification pass over local data: re-read osm_way_tags.db, re-run
classify, update two columns. Seconds. No download, no re-extract.
⛔⛔ THEREFORE THE TAG TABLE IS NOT DELETED WHEN THE SKINNY IS BUILT. It is the INPUT the
rules run against. The instinct to sweep a 400k-row interim file is exactly what would turn a
seconds-long reclassification back into a 500 MB re-download. It survives until the state is
reimported.
⚠ And a reclassification must update BOTH stores once imported — the skinny, and
trails.carto_code plus trail_properties.carto_code — or the device and the
interim file disagree.
⭐ It also turns the path-versus-track default from a decision into an experiment.
An untagged highway=path currently claims hiking only while an untagged
TRACK gets the honest unclassified unknown — and path is heavily used in
the western US for exactly the two-track a side-by-side rides. Left as the prototype had it so the
device numbers stay comparable; flagged in the Kotlin; settle it with the A/B result.

⚠ THREE CAUTIONS RECORDED WITH THE GROUPING
⛔ NPS IS PROBABLY NOT RIDEABLE. Fred's general rule is that federal land is open unless
posted — but NPS is the National Park Service, and park trails are commonly closed to machines
(Arches, Canyonlands, Zion). Their 442 rows carry designated_uses = Hiker/Pedestrian,
which says so. ⭐ Fred 08-31: "generally if there is a trail in a park it is not rideable unless
posted" — the INVERSE of the BLM/USFS rule. Do not fold NPS in with the rest of federal.
⚠ USFS SNOW (253) is winter-only, not a year-round route.
⚠ PRIVATE IS NOT ONE THING (Fred 08-31). Ownership owner='Private' covers a
subdivision street, a RANCH ROAD and a gated industrial track alike, and step 8 flattens all three
into R - Residential Roads. A ranch two-track is rideable ground and is exactly the
connector between public parcels. ⭐ That is almost certainly what the 24000 North
false positive was — a section-line road on private ranch land, not a street. Distinguishing them
probably comes down to DENSITY: a private road with fifty private neighbours is a subdivision; one
alone in a section is a ranch road.
🔵 OPEN QUESTIONS FROM THIS SESSION
The 16,482 track grade1-5 rows — rideable or unknown? A graded track is
arguably MORE likely rideable than an unsurfaced road, since highway=track means an
agricultural or forestry way. Biggest single judgement left.
Does max_speed_mph carry anything? Fred 08-31: a track with a posted limit is
different ground from an unmarked two-track. The column exists (trail_properties,
excluded from the detail display at ArtifactDetailPanel:215) and the skinny carries
maxspeed from the GeoPackage — but the classifier never reads it and nobody has
checked whether it is populated. One query settles it.
USFS designated_uses is digit strings — 321, 54321, 21, 654321. If those are
packed use codes on the same 1-5 vocabulary UGRC uses, 1,745 USFS trails become classifiable.
Split OSM stated from inferred motorized — 87% of 0 - Motorized Access is
inference. Splitting is a classifier change plus a reimport.
⭐⭐ THE LEGEND / FILTER PANEL — UI AND STYLING DESIGN, 2026-08-31 EOD. LEGENDUI-0831
WHAT IT IS. The current legend becomes a Route Legend / Filter panel: a key you can
read at a glance, two slice filters, per-category toggles, and the place where line styling is
customised. ⭐ Working mockup with real counts:
legend_filter_mockup_v2_2026-08-31.html.
THE FILTERS
Two slices, three states each: LAND (both / public / private) and USE (both / motorized /
non-motorized). Independent — four cells.
Per-category toggles, ALL ON by default (Fred 08-31). A rider who never opens it sees no
change; anyone wanting a cleaner map sets it once. ⚠ They work INSIDE the slice, so a count showing
5,618 / 24,414 makes it obvious the slice did that, not the toggle.
⭐ The legend is built from what is PRESENT, not a hardcoded list. A state with no
OHV-designated trails shows no OHV row. ⛔ Drop a category ONLY when it is ZERO (Fred) —
otherwise the panel jumps around as you toggle. Steps/bridge at 5 rows stays.
⚠ This also kills the drift that bit us on 08-31: a hardcoded legend said orange was
"Hiking &amp; Biking" while the map drew motorized in it. A legend derived from the data cannot be
wrong about what the data holds.
⭐⭐ STYLING IS USER-CUSTOMISABLE, AND THE POINT IS NO COMPILE BETWEEN ATTEMPTS (Fred
08-31): "no compile between color builds. we settle our design and the json ships as an
asset."
Per row: colour, line pattern, line thickness. Adjustable for trails, TRACKS AND
ROUTES — everything the key shows, not just trail categories.
⭐ The line image IS the control. Fred: "combine color, pattern and thickness in the
display for the line image ... just click on the line image display and open that line's
details." One tap on the swatch opens that row's styling. No separate edit button per row.
Same grid structure, popup selection for each value on each line.
⭐ JSON is the single source. Ships as an ASSET for the defaults, with the rider's edits
layered over it — the same pattern as osm_layers.json and its
/sdcard/…/config/ override. ⛔ The draw functions become TABLE-DRIVEN rather than
switching on hardcoded values, which permanently kills the divergence problem: on 08-31 the field
xref found THREE copies of trailColor, and spatial_artifacts.js had already
missed a patch the other two received.
⚠ Line PATTERN earns its place beyond looks: dashed reads as "less certain" naturally — shape
only could be dashed rather than merely a fainter blue — and it survives glare and colour-blindness
where hue does not.
⚠ A reset-to-defaults is essential once people can change things, and the shipped defaults
still have to be good because most riders will never open it.
LAYOUT AND PLACEMENT (Fred 08-31)
⭐ Tighten the legend box — as small as possible when it is being used AS a legend. The
styling controls are behind the swatch tap, not on the face of it.
⭐ Float the map legend under Search, Map Features and Help.
⭐ Move the Help button LAST in that stack.
⭐⭐ STATE LIVES IN A JSON FILE, NOT IN A SCREEN (Fred 08-31): "json file, can be read at
any point in any process without having to scope data fields ... and it is available between map
panels."
Both maps read it, so convoy and planning always agree. No per-screen state, no chance of
the two diverging.
It survives the screen being destroyed and rebuilt, which the map does routinely — and a
rider's settings survive a reinstall the way their trails do.
⭐ Inspectable with adb shell cat when something looks wrong, which after
this week matters.
⭐⭐ AND THE SAME FILTER GOES INTO THE ROUTE BUILDER (Fred): "same panel everything."
⛔ If the route builder had its own filter the two could disagree, and a rider would see a map showing
ground the router would not use. The objective is focusing the trails for ROUTE BUILDING — the
map is how you verify what the router has.
⚠ The route-list SQL needs the same predicates. A route's vertices reference trail ids, so
filtering routes by trail attributes is a join through those ids to land_status and
use_type. ⚠ OPEN: does "matches the filter" mean ALL segments, MOST, or ANY? Different
lists.
⚠ OPEN: do readers POLL the file or get told it changed? A route builder that read it at launch
would not notice a mid-session toggle.
🔵 STILL OPEN ON THIS DESIGN
The exact colours and patterns — untested over satellite. Thin lines shift a lot against
terrain. ⭐ Which is precisely why the JSON approach matters: settle it by editing and reloading.
The unknown category — one row in Utah ("Big Spring Canyon", NPS, carto value
is the literal string Unknown). Other states may have more. ⚠ The legend list should not
be hardcoded to nine.
Blast radius before touching the draw functions — both the field xref AND grep, as on
08-31. The xref found a third trailColor copy that a grep of
assets/*.html alone had missed.
⛔⛔ SCHEMA CHANGE = TWO DECISIONS, AND BOTH RUN BEFORE THE APP. 2026-09-01. SCHEMAPLAN-0901
WHAT HAPPENED. I added a status column to trails and, in the same
breath, a BACKFILL that walked ~47,000 rows one at a time — inside
SpatialDbManager.init(), blocking, on the database-open path. First launch ANR'd:
"wait or close app".
⛔ AND IT WAS UNNECESSARY. This release CLEARS the trails table, so every updating rider
reimports from empty. There was nothing to backfill. I wrote a migration for a state that does not
occur — and left behind, in Fred's words, "code we will never use and a process that could pop up
and hose us at any time."
⚠ AND I DID NOT ASK. Fred, 09-01: "don't put that stuff in without a discussion. we
should have moved the data back and fixed it."
⭐⭐ THE RULE THAT CAME OUT OF IT (Fred, 09-01). A schema change is TWO decisions, not one:
DecisionWhere it runs
1The ALTER — what the column is⭐⭐ BOTH, IN ONE PLACE,
BEFORE THE APP LAUNCHES. Fred: "check the db model, if it is not correct alter and then
perform the required task post alter, then launch the app."
2THE POPULATION — what fills it. ⭐ This is the hard part. Fred:
"the issue is not the db change, it is populating and aligning the data. Alter is fine on the
change, it just needs to be in the right place."
⭐ THE SLOT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS PROVEN — the authority-gate startup job, where
clearTrailsOnce and sweepManifests run. After authority, before convoy, off
the main thread since GATEASYNC, and VISIBLE to the rider. Fred: "that is what we did with trails.
that should be our solution to everything."
⛔ THE DATABASE OPEN SHOULD DO NOTHING BUT OPEN. No probing, no ALTERing, no guessing.
⚠ WHY TONIGHT'S MISTAKE WAS EVEN POSSIBLE — and this is the part worth fixing. There is
NO VERSION NUMBER ON THE SPATIAL DATABASE. The extension db has
schema_version; the spatial one does not. What exists instead is a series of independent
probes in init() — "does this column exist, if not ALTER" — repeated for every field
anyone has ever added: v3 waypoint bbox, v3 tracks type, v4 carto_code, and now status.
⭐ So there was no structure to violate. No "we are at v4, apply the v4→v5 step" — just a
pile of guesses, and a backfill slotted in among them did not look out of place.
⭐⭐ FRED'S MODEL: a schema VERSION on the spatial database, a DEFINED PROCESS per
increment — v3→v4, v4→v5 — and a floor below which the answer is clear-and-reload rather than
a migration chain nobody has tested. "It is a db change number and you can only move so far back
with clearing and reloading."
⚠ That is a real refactor — the existing probe-and-ALTER blocks in
init() all move — and it is NOT done. But it is the correct shape, and it is the same
pattern the trail clear already proves.
⭐ WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD, and it is simpler than any of it:
The ALTER TABLE trails ADD COLUMN status TEXT STAYS. Fred: "the alter table can
stay, it will execute after the clear on an empty file."
The backfill is REMOVED (NOBACKFILL-2026-09-01), with a comment in its place recording why
so nobody re-adds it.
⚠ STILL OWED: TrailImporter must write status to BOTH stores at import, the
way carto_code already is at :464. Then a fresh import populates it correctly and no
repair pass is ever needed — which is the whole point.
⭐ AND THE BUMPED MARKER IS THE MECHANISM, not an in-place fix: the release marker changes,
everyone clears and reloads, and every rider lands in the same state regardless of what they were
running before. One path, tested. An in-place migration is a SECOND path that only handles the cases
whoever wrote it happened to think of.
⭐ THE PANEL WORK — REWRITTEN CLEAN, AND SPLIT IN TWO. 2026-09-02. PANELWORK-0902
⛔⛔ EIGHT BUILDS ON ONE PANEL, AND THE CAUSE WAS ONE MISSING PARAMETER. Fred, 09-02:
"this thing is a mess, delete it and start over — why are we chasing this ridiculous thing for 8
builds?"
THE BUG: TrailFilterState is a plain singleton, not Compose state.
Toggling a category changes nothing Compose watches, so the panel bumps a tick counter
to force recomposition. KeyColumn took it. KeyRowItem did not — and
Compose SKIPS a composable whose parameters are unchanged. The tap registered, the state changed, and
the screen did not move. Fred saw "nothing is selectable" and "4 random blue boxes scattered across
rows" — the boxes were the state frozen at first composition.
⚠ The asymmetry he reported on the FIRST test — headings work, rows do not — WAS the answer.
I chased tap targets, padding, font sizes and checkbox borders instead, and each change made the panel
worse while the real defect sat one parameter away.
⭐⭐ THE LESSON: when a small file needs a fourth fix, REPLACE IT. Rewriting whole took one
pass and beat eight rounds of patching. And the rule now sits in the file's own header — every
composable that reads TrailFilterState must take tick, which makes it structural
rather than something to remember.
⭐⭐ THEN FRED SPLIT IT, AND HIS ARGUMENT WAS BETTER THAN MINE. I argued for keeping the key
and the filter together so counts and colours stayed in one place. His answer, 09-02: "now all the
selects for all features are in one place, not sometimes here and sometimes there."
WhereWhat it does
Map Features › Trails › SELECTWHICH trails show — categories, include-private
Map Keysthe key, and HOW they look — colour, pattern, weight
⭐ AND IT REUSED A DEAD CONTROL. SELECT was greyed for trails earlier the same day because
per-trail selection was a trap: SpatialDisplayManager filters to checkedIds in the
SELECTED state, so a trail imported AFTER that list was saved silently never drew — and nobody could
build such a list from ~146,000 mostly-unnamed trails. It now opens the CATEGORY filter, which is what
the button should always have meant for an artifact type this size.
⚠ The swatch appears in BOTH — in the filter so you can see what you are hiding (Fred: "we
can leave the swatch in the filter"), but it is not a control there: "no link to change
attributes, only from legend panel."
⭐ TRAIL STYLING — THE TUNING TOOL, AND THE PALETTE IT PRODUCED
Fred, 09-02: "I am going to play with this for a while and we will issue my palette as a shared
asset default." Tap a row's NAME (not the swatch — it sits beside a checkbox in a 25dp row and the
two targets would fight), get the CURRENT line beside the PROPOSED one, pick colour, pattern and
thickness. ⭐ Apply returns to the key so the rider works one category at a time and lands back
in the list.
⭐⭐ THE SCHEME FRED SETTLED ON: PATTERN CARRIES RIDEABILITY, COLOUR IS FREE. Solid for
motorized, dotted for non-motorized. "The colors do not have to be in a family." ⚠ Stronger
than the blue-family scheme it replaced, which made hue do double duty as both "rideable" and
"confidence". Pattern also survives glare and colour-blindness where hue does not.
And the palette he tuned SHIPS AS THE ASSET — pulled off the device, copied out by the
authority gate's startup job when a rider has no file of their own. ⭐ Fred: "ship the json in a
private directory and copy over — that way we can have a reset-to-defaults function", so the asset
stays pristine in the APK and a reset cannot fail for want of a source.
⛔ THE SHIPPED DEFAULT HIDES ALL FIVE NON-MOTORIZED CATEGORIES AND ALL PRIVATE LAND. Right
for an OHV app, and it WILL read as missing data to anyone who does not know. Fred: "we will cover
in quickstart." ⚠ That coverage is load-bearing, not a nicety.
⭐ ALSO SHIPPED 09-02
Trails open the DETAIL PANEL, like tracks and routes. ⛔ They could not before because
trail_id WAS NEVER IN THE GEOJSON PROPERTIES — a trail tap had nothing to hand to Kotlin,
so a popup was the only thing it could do. ⭐ And getArtifactDetail already does
SELECT * from both tables, so the panel could always have shown everything.
Readable values — source ids become real names, and smoothness is translated:
"Severe — ATV or tractor (very_horrible)". ⚠ The raw token stays in brackets; it is what you search
for against OSM.
Search results FIT the map to the artifact. Fred: "we select the returned item from the
list and then hit fit from the popup menu. Silly." Plus a close button — the FAB that used to
dismiss it went when icons became words, and nothing replaced it.
The route builder respects the filter — "we route what you put on the map". ⛔ And the
FILTER JOINED THE CACHE KEY: two searches over the same box with different filters would have
collided, and the second would have silently got the first one's graph. ⚠ The routes would have looked
plausible.
The recipe records its predicate, so a rebuild reproduces the network it was built on.
The legend FAB removed. Fred: "there is less issues aligning text" — the same
reasoning that put words in that column instead of glyphs.
⚠ Five panels this week needed a findable close: Map Keys, Map Features, Route+, the search
bar and the compare grid. THREE of them ALREADY HAD ONE — 10sp, unboxed, the same colour as the title
beside it. ⭐ A close that is not legible AS A BUTTON is the same as no close.
⭐⭐ 2.6h IS THE TRAILS RELEASE. 2026-09-06. TRAILSRELEASE-0906
Fred, 09-06: "the release is a fundamental redesign and rewrite of
trails" — and, a moment later, "and route building through those
trails."
⭐⭐ That is the framing, and it is better than a list of leftovers.
Everything in 2.6h is one subject: better trail data, more of it, rider-contributed
where the sources are silent, and route building that makes proper use of it.
⚠ And they are not separable. Adding 80 miles of rider trails today
changed what the planner returned for the same recipe. The router is only as good
as the network under it — improving one without the other is half a job.
⛔ It also settles what 2.6g is NOT. Fred: "just want to get trails
organised and completed. Additional data besides mining unknown capture is
out." 2.6g stabilises what exists; the redesign waits.
⭐ HOW RIDER TRAILS RUN IN THE APP — Fred's design.
A field on the track extension recording that this track has been
through the add-trails process. ⚠ Without it there is no way to distinguish a
track that yielded nothing from one never examined — and re-running the analysis
over 89 tracks every time would be pointless work.
A batch process inside the import-trails flow. It belongs with the
other trail-data work rather than in a corner of its own.
⭐ A green button under SYNCH, shown only when unchecked tracks exist.
No badge, no nagging, no counter — the control appears when there is something
to do and is absent when there is not, which is the same discipline as the
Mesh word only appearing while the rail is folded.
⭐⭐ RIDER TRAILS — CLOSING THE GAPS WITH YOUR OWN RIDING. 2026-09-06. RIDERTRAILS-0906
⭐⭐ THE IDEA. Fred has 89 recorded tracks. Parts of them cross ground no
published source lists as a trail. Those parts are ground he has PROVEN rideable,
and the app cannot route across any of it.
⭐ PROVEN TODAY, IN PYTHON, AND IT WORKS. Broken Ridge and Steamboat
together produced about 80 miles of new connected ground. Fred, after rebuilding
a recipe with it in: "well it fucking worked." And: "those two trails
open up riding all through the area."
⛔ THREE WRONG TURNS, AND WHAT EACH TAUGHT.
DISTANCE ALONE GIVES NONSENSE. v1 asked "is a trail point within 20 m?"
and produced 271 fragments from ONE ride — a break every 350 feet. That is
GPS drift stepping in and out of a threshold, not 271 trails.
⚠ It also only measured to stored VERTICES, so a track running beside a trail
whose points are 50 m apart read as off-trail in every gap between them.
⭐ DIRECTION IS THE TEST, NOT DISTANCE. Fred: "if there is a trail
in the same direction as the track they are the same segment. If the track is off
all by itself it becomes a trail." A track wandering 30 m off a parallel trail
is still that trail. ⚠ Undirected — a trail ridden the other way is the same
trail. 271 became 69.
⛔ AND A RUN MUST NOT END THE FIRST TIME A TRAIL APPEARS. Fred:
"we have a segment of track that has no route under it and routes back to the
trailhead. Shouldn't that whole section be a trail?" and "the travel from
last track point to next track point, that is one trail."
⭐ Passing near something, or crossing a road, was cutting one stretch of new
ground into several. v3 requires a SUSTAINED rejoin — 120 m on the network —
before a run is closed. An out-and-back is one trail, because you rode all of it
and it is continuous.
⛔⛔ THE LEAP IS THE CONNECTION. Fred: "the last node from one trail
and the first node from the new trail is a ten ft track and we drop in trail line
connecting them."
⭐ A new trail that ends five metres short of the network is a gap the router
CANNOT CROSS, and the whole exercise is decorative. A short connector is written
from the node the track last touched to the start of the new trail, and again at
the far end. ⚠ Anything over 60 m is not written — that is a guess, not a gap.
⭐ That connector is what turns recorded riding into routable ground,
and it is why the recipe returned genuinely different routes afterwards.
⚠ GPX CANNOT CARRY A TRAIL. &lt;trk&gt; imports as a track
and &lt;rte&gt; is a route — and ConvoyTrackImportScreen
does not touch the trails table at all. Trails only come from the
catalogue import.
⭐ Which settles the implementation: this belongs in the app, not in an
import. When a track is saved, find the ground with no trail under it and
write those as unnamed trails — the app owns the database, so there is no file
format in the way.
⭐ THE RULES, AS FRED SET THEM:
Unnamed, source "rides". It says you rode it, not that it is a road.
Fred: "it doesn't have to be perfect, it has to be honest."
Lumped in with every other trail for filtering — not a separate
category.
⭐⭐ RIDER TRAILS TRAVEL WITH THE ROUTE, NOT WITH THE STATE IMPORT.
Fred: "ride trails should be downloaded with route data. We know it is not on
every setup — get a route or a ride that uses it and add it."
⚠ Which also solves survival: a state reimport clearing trails does not matter,
because they come back with the routes that need them.
⭐ A SHARED ROUTE MUST CARRY EVERYTHING IT DEPENDS ON — its waypoints
AND any rider trails it crosses. Otherwise the recipient gets a route over ground
their device does not have.
⭐ EVERY TRACK PROCESSED SHOULD BE CHECKED for new unnamed trails to
create.
⚠ THE NUMBERS, for whoever builds it. Tuned on Broken Ridge and
Steamboat; expect to revisit them.
SettingValueWhat it does
NEAR_M15–20 ma trail this close, going your way, means you are on it
BEARING_D45°...and within this many degrees is THE SAME trail
MIN_RUN_M150 mshorter than this is a wobble, not a trail
REJOIN_M120 m⭐ how long the track must STAY on the network before a run closes
MAX_CONN_M60 ma longer connector is a guess, not a gap
⚠ A 0.002-degree grid (~200 m) indexes the trail segments. Comparing every
track point against 5.6 million segments unindexed would take hours.

⭐⭐⭐ THE VISION — WHAT THE SEPARATION IS ACTUALLY FOR. SEPVISION-2026-09-16
⭐⭐⭐ STAGES 1 AND 2 ARE A PRODUCT, NOT A REFACTOR.
RIDE DEFINITION IN. AWARENESS OVERLAY OUT.
That is the whole contract. Layer 1 and layer 2 together take a ride
definition — network name, keys, radio settings, the ride's identity — and
produce a map layer of who is where: every rider's position, the lead
cart's track, all of it blended from whatever transports are present.
⛔ NOTHING ABOVE THOSE TWO LAYERS NEEDS TO KNOW ANYTHING. Not which
transport a position arrived on, not that a radio exists, not how nodes were
merged, not what a channel is.
⭐⭐ THE TESTABLE END STATE, AND IT IS BETTER THAN THE IMPORT COUNT:
layers 1 and 2 must work with NO LAYER 3 PRESENT. Feed them a ride
definition, get an overlay. If that is true they are genuinely separable. If
it is not, the boundary is in the wrong place.
⭐⭐ AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT PORTABLE. A unit with a standard input
and a standard output is consumable by anything that renders map layers.
GroupTrack's own app becomes ONE CONSUMER of the overlay, not its
owner.
⭐ Fred 09-16: "that makes the ride from version three the key
deliverable to transparent cross-app implementation."
⚠ CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER READING TODAY: the ride definition is NOT
primarily a distribution artifact for riders. It is the CONFIGURATION INPUT to
the comms stack. That it also carries a route and trailhead for layer 3 is
secondary.
⭐ Interoperability needs no permission: GPX and KML are universal, and
GroupTrack-specific fields ride in a container other apps skip — the same
trick CoT's detail element pulls.
⚠ CROSS-APP DELIVERY IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL. They read our rides; we do not
get their riders' positions. A distribution channel, not a technical
partnership.
⭐⭐ THE COMPETITIVE POSITION, SHARPENED 09-16. onX Offroad HAS group
tracking — and it is Starlink/cell based. It works where there is
coverage and stops where there is not.
⭐⭐⭐ OUR ENTIRE PRODUCT EXISTS IN THE GAP THEY CANNOT SERVE, and a rider
out of coverage is exactly the rider who needs group awareness most.
⭐ The cost argument is sharper than the feature argument: their model
needs a Starlink or a data plan per group; ours needs a $50 radio per rider and
nothing monthly.
⭐ AND THEY HAVE VALIDATED THE CATEGORY FOR US. Riders already
understand "see your group on the map" — we only have to explain the difference,
not the concept.
⛔ WHICH ARGUES AGAINST THE PLUGIN IDEA, not for it. If onX already has
group tracking they do not need our LAYER — they would need our TRANSPORT, which
is the part they chose not to build. A harder sell and a worse partnership
position than standing alone.
⭐ Website line that falls out of it: "Group tracking that works
where there is no signal. No Starlink, no data plan, no monthly fee."
⭐⭐ WHY THIS IS THE FOCUS AND V3 IS NOT (Fred 09-16): "the scope of
this solution is very big. We need to focus on mesh separation and the IP
integration. Refactoring that convoy mess into three manageable separate
layers."
⭐ AND THERE IS A REASON BEYOND THE VENDOR CONVERSATION: the convoy code is
where every hard week has come from. The frozen map, the fallback loop, the
position feed, the zoom caps, the OOM — all in one tangled surface where a change
anywhere can break anything. Three clean layers is what makes the next year
cheaper, INCLUDING V3.
⛔⛔ THE DISCIPLINE, GIVEN THIS WEEK: IT IS A REFACTOR, NOT A REWRITE.
Nothing should change behaviour. The layer boundaries move; the code inside
them does not — which means every step is verifiable against CURRENT
BEHAVIOUR rather than against a spec.
⭐ PARKED WITH DOCS FILED, NOT COMPETING FOR ATTENTION: V3, the website,
the fifty-state trail work, the OHV restriction layer. None of it decays.
⭐⭐ V3 RE-UNDERSTOOD 09-16 — THE BACKEND WAS WAITING FOR SOMETHING TO HAND OFF TO. V3RIDE-2026-09-16
⭐⭐⭐ Fred: "we stopped building the back end because we
needed an off-road navigation product that functions for the back end to hand off
to. So we need map downloads, we need trails, we need routes. We build our
toolkit from a rider's point of view. Now we have backend services that hand off
to a functional product."
⛔ SO THE APRIL V3 DOCUMENTS ARE HISTORY, NOT A PLAN. They scope V3
against a 2.4-era app and their sequencing is INVERTED relative to where the code
now is. (The pickup guide even opens "The build is FAILING" — April's
state.) The components they would have had to build now exist; the
INTEGRATION is the work.
⭐⭐ WHAT A RIDE ACTUALLY IS NOW: not coordination — the delivery
mechanism for everything the app does. Enroll and you get the route, the
trails, the map tiles and the radio config. Fred: "no heavy lifting,
all built, all components exist."
⭐⭐⭐ AND THAT CLOSES THE COMMS-LAYER LOOP. Yesterday's open question was
"how does a rider get the channel name and PSK?" Answer: the same way they get
the maps. It is not a separate joining mechanism at all — it is a field in
the ride definition.
⭐⭐ IT ALSO RESOLVES THE LEADER/AUTHORITY CONFLICT. Natak: no
privileged node, none required. Ours: the ride needs a lead. Both are true —
the NETWORK has no leader, the RIDE does, and the ride is created before anyone
leaves home.
THE FLOW: publish → follow → notify → enroll → ride. ⭐ Every step has
a reason for the person doing it. A rider registers because enrolling is how
they get their maps, route and radio configured — not because the app asked.
A club publishes because that is how they distribute all of it to eight riders at
once.
⭐ FOLLOWING REMOVES THE JOB ORGANISERS HATE — maintaining an email
list, posting to Facebook, chasing people who missed it, answering "what channel
are we on" eight times. Publish once; everyone following is notified; the ride
definition carries the config so nobody asks. ⭐ Fred: following is ALREADY
BUILT.
⭐⭐ THE COLD-START PROBLEM IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS. Most of V3 is
SINGLE-CLUB, not community: Track Library, creating a ride, invite links to
people you already ride with — all work with one club and zero network
effect. Only Explore/public rides and cross-club sharing need scale.
The clearinghouse is a CONSEQUENCE, not a precondition.
⭐ Seed distribution already exists: 8–10 Utah UTV groups on Facebook.
⚠ isSubscribed() is hardcoded TRUE and the $3/month screen
is fully built — go-live is "a single function edit." ⛔ But every current
user is on a free tier never tested as paid. Flipping it with real riders
attached is a moment to plan, not to discover.

⭐⭐⭐ THE WIRE FORMAT IS ALREADY IN THE REPO — TAKPacket. TAKPKT-2026-09-15
⭐⭐⭐ THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THE WEEK. The mesh
plugin's payload is NOT ours to design. It exists, it is standard Meshtastic, and
the generated Kotlin is already in this build.
core/proto/src/main/proto/meshtastic/atak.proto →
core/proto/build/generated/source/wire/org/meshtastic/proto/TAKPacket.kt.
Carried on portnum 72 (ATAK_FORWARDER). ⭐ Every Meshtastic
node relays it. Every TAK-aware app reads it. No custom port, no repurposed
field, no radio reconfiguration, no vendor dependency.

heading_degPLI.course

anything elsedetail (field 7) — generic CoT detail XML, sender may compress/truncate; is_compressed flags it

Fourteen colours, and GroupTrack already colours node trails by
markerColor. Group identity AND map colour in one field, already
agreed across the whole ecosystem.
⚠ The MemberRole enum is tactical —
Sniper, Medic, K9,
ForwardObserver, RTO, HQ. Use
TeamLead and TeamMember; ignore the rest.
⭐ detail is the escape hatch WITH A DEFINED SHAPE — CoT
detail XML rather than a private format. So an extension stays interoperable
instead of forking the protocol.
⛔⛔ CORRECTIONS TO WHAT I ASSERTED EARLIER TODAY — recorded so the wrong
version is not carried forward.
⛔ "A stock radio can only carry a Position packet, so supplemented data
cannot reach a bare-radio rider." WRONG. The radio is
transport-agnostic — it carries whatever port a connected app pushes through
IMeshService. The constraint is on the APP, not the radio.
A T1000-E rider with a TAK-aware app sends TAKPacket like anyone
else.
⛔ "Lead must be a local selection because role cannot travel." The
CONCLUSION may still be right for product reasons, but the REASON was wrong
— Group.role travels natively. ⚠ Local selection remains the
better default (no configuration, no election, no conflict when two riders
claim it, and it works before any role is received) — but role on the wire is
now available as ENRICHMENT rather than being impossible.
⛔ "The CoT bridge is Natak's and we would need them to extend it." The
Nucleus bridge is theirs, but the Meshtastic ATAK path is upstream and
already in our fork.
⚠ UNVERIFIED, DO NOT BUILD ON IT: that Meshtastic Android 2.8.0+ ships
a BUILT-IN LOCAL TAK SERVER, making the ATAK plugin unnecessary. If true, and if
our fork is recent enough, we may already hold the merge component.
⛔ Check what we forked from before assuming anything — this is exactly the class
of inference that cost two days this week.
⭐⭐ WHAT THIS DOES TO THE PLAN.
The layer 1 / layer 2 contract is SETTLED and it is not ours:
TAKPacket in, TAKPacket out. Layer 2 receives it and
cannot tell whether it arrived over LoRa, WiFi multicast or an internet bridge —
which is the parity rule Fred set ("mesh has to look and function like the IP
plugin") expressed as a published format instead of an interface we would
have had to invent, document and defend.
⛔ BUT THE INTERNAL MODEL MUST NOT BECOME TAKPacket. Parse at the
boundary into ConvoyNode; emit at the boundary. Otherwise a tactical vocabulary
leaks upward and every future change has to be expressible in a military schema.
Same discipline as layer 2 never branching on transport.
⭐ AND MOST OF "CONVOY" NEVER GOES ON THE WIRE ANYWAY. Gap ahead, gap
behind, distance to lead, distance to tail, off-track — ConvoyEngine
computes all of them locally from node positions. They were never transmitted and
they do not need to be. The payload question was only ever position, identity
and role.
🔴 OPEN: what a LoRa-only rider receives when the group is large and
airtime is short — everyone at a reduced rate, nearest N, or lead and tail only.
⭐ That rider is the one who is separated, which is the case the product exists
for. A layer-2 decision, and the interesting part of the contract.

⭐⭐⭐ FRED'S ARCHITECTURE, 2026-09-14 — stated as background for the
separation work, and it is the target shape.
LAYER 1 — THE COMMUNICATIONS LAYER. "The point of contact is the mesh
messages being forwarded to a receiver in GroupTrack. This communication layer
should support mesh radios AND a standard IP network stack, both of which can
contribute nodes to the same group layer."
LAYER 2 — THE GROUP VISIBILITY LAYER. "Identifies all network traffic
from IP or mesh sources, assigns unique node IDs to each device, blends IP and
mesh devices, tracks GPS locations, and creates a map layer that plots the lead
cart's track as well as all other nodes' locations. Presented as a map
overlay."
LAYER 3 — THE STANDALONE ANDROID APP. The device's own location
tracking as the standard map layer. Trails, maps, recording, routing — all of it
works with no radio present.
⭐ THE GOAL: "separate the Meshtastic app from GroupTrack so it is a
checkbox plugin during the install."
⭐⭐ THE DEPENDENCY POINTS THE WRONG WAY TODAY — THIS IS AN INVERSION, NOT AN
EXTRACTION. GroupTrack is currently a guest inside Meshtastic's app: its
screens live in Meshtastic's activity, on its DI graph. Fred's design has
GroupTrack as the HOST and mesh as one contributor among several. So the work is
not "extract mesh from GroupTrack" — it is extract GroupTrack from the
fork. GroupTrack core becomes its own app containing none of Meshtastic's
code; the fork becomes the isolated mesh component.
⭐⭐ THE LAYER 1 / LAYER 2 CONTRACT IS THE WHOLE DELIVERABLE. Layer 2 must
never be able to tell where a node came from — it takes
node id · position · timestamp · provenance and blends.
THE TEST IS MECHANICAL: if any code in layer 2 branches on "is this mesh
or IP", the separation has failed and it will be written twice when cellular
arrives.
⭐ AND THERE IS ALREADY A SEED IN THE CODE:
ConvoyViewModel:158 reads
_myCartId.value = if (myNum != null) "!%08x".format(myNum) else "!phone"
— the identity scheme ALREADY has a branch for a device with no radio, written
for a different reason.
⛔ LAYER 3 MUST STAND COMPLETELY ALONE. Nothing in it may reference
layer 1 or 2 at all, not even to ask whether they exist. That is the
checkbox-off case and it is most of the product.
🔴 OPEN — DOES IP SHIP WITH THE SPLIT? Building the abstraction with one
implementation is how you get an abstraction shaped like that implementation.
⭐ Fred: "I believe IP is the future of the app and want to build that support
in." An argument for IP being the FIRST layer-1 implementation — it is Fred's
own code, no inheritance, and it proves the interface before mesh is fitted to
it.
⭐⭐⭐ THE COUPLING WAS MEASURED 09-14 AND IT IS FAR SMALLER THAN THE HISTORY
SUGGESTS. Every non-Android import inside convoy/*.kt reaching
outside the convoy package: FIFTEEN, and ELEVEN are single-use. Strip JSON
and OkHttp (neither is Meshtastic) and the real surface is:
Reaching forSites
UIViewModel7 — the only one needing a read rather than a count
DeviceProfile (proto)5
ConnectionState2
MyNodeInfo · NodeRepository · RadioConfigRepository1 each
Import/Export/InstallProfileUseCase1 each
Res · vectorResource1 each — icons
⭐⭐ ALMOST ALL OF IT LANDS IN ConvoyViewModel, AND ALMOST ALL OF
IT IS LAYER 1 BY FRED'S OWN DESIGN — node info, radio config, connection
state, device profiles. It is not tangled through the app; it is concentrated in
one file doing one job. GroupTrack's ~60 convoy files barely know Meshtastic
exists.
⚠ TWO CAVEATS ON THAT NUMBER. (1) It counts IMPORTS, not same-package
references — anything GroupTrack touches that also lives in
com.geeksville.mesh needs no import and does not appear.
(2) It does not count THE HOST: the activity, navigation graph, DI graph and
manifest. So fifteen is the FLOOR on the code side, and the hosting is a
separate question.
⭐⭐⭐ NATAK MESH / NUCLEUS — VENDOR ANSWERS, 2026-09-15.
NATAK-0915. Nathan Boyette responded to all 24 questions same-day. Product:
Raspberry Pi 4 node, 802.11s WiFi mesh, 5.8 GHz AP for clients, onboard RAK4631
Meshtastic radio. $150–200 per node, no recurring cost. Repo:
Natak-Mesh/Nucleus_OS.
QuestionAnswer
Licence⭐⭐ MIT. No obligations, no publication requirement. The cleanest possible answer given we are removing a GPL entanglement.
Arbitrary multicast?WiFi mesh: YES — add the group to their SMCroute config and "it'll just work". LoRa bridge: CoT only today, but "we can grab whatever we want and package it up".
Multicast across the mesh?⭐ YES. L3 routing, entire mesh open, all nodes see all if any path exists. The broadcast model holds.
LoRa airtimeMax packet ~0.25 s; a standard ATAK PLI ~0.07 s.
Node saturation⭐ ~25 nodes at 5 s updates, ~80 at 15 s. Ten riders is comfortably inside. The "radios are being pushed" assumption does NOT hold for this hardware.
WiFi ceiling~30 nodes (32 direct peers per node). ~30 Mbps first hop, halving per hop (half duplex).
RejoinAutomatic, seconds, once nodes see each other.
Android side⭐ Plain AP, plain DHCP, normal sockets, NO vendor SDK. SSID is XX-nucleus, serial printed on the case.
Internet uplinkHandled — ethernet takes DHCP, Babel distributes the bridge across the mesh. One Starlink at base camp serves the whole club.
Security⚠ UFW only. "Security facing the internet has not been a huge point of focus." Designed off-grid. Needs review before a club runs an uplink.
Power~0.65 A at 5 V. ⚠ No 12 V input today — he is open to building one.
Vibration⚠ No shock provisions. Suggests potting. A UTV is rougher than anything they have tested.
LoRa range (V3, 1 W)10+ miles with elevation and clean LoS; will not punch through dirt — mesh relaying is what saves it.
⛔⛔ THE V3 HAS NO BLUETOOTH. "No more bluetooth, all interaction
with the Nucleus is handled through that 5.8 GHz Wi-Fi AP or through the ethernet
port... everything is pushed through Meshtasticd software on the radio itself.
You just connect to the Wi-Fi AP and you have Wi-Fi mesh and Meshtastic."
⭐⭐ SO ON A NUCLEUS, EVEN MESH IS REACHED OVER IP. GroupTrack talks to
Meshtastic over BLE today and that path does not exist on this hardware —
it would be Meshtastic's TCP interface to meshtasticd.
Layer 1 becomes uniformly IP: mesh over TCP, group state over multicast,
internet over the same bridge. ⚠ Two connection paths to support — BLE for a
bare radio, TCP for a Nucleus — and neither visible above the line.
🔴 OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE CALL (he is slammed for a day or two):

— the node, or the app? If the node, we inherit the mixed-network bridge and
never touch LoRa. If the app, the relay lands in our code. Most consequential
remaining question.
Exact multicast group and port the bridge reads/writes (he will look it up).
How does role survive compression into a Meshtastic-sized packet, and what

⭐ PARTNERSHIP — HE IS IN. Wants past ATAK/iTAK into a simpler SxS
implementation; open to tailoring hardware and software; will ship a Nucleus
preconfigured for a GroupTrack-affiliated club ("as easy as a config setting");
interested in bundling to SxS manufacturers and software vendors (onX, Gaia).
"I appreciate you. Excited to see what we can put together."
⭐⭐ THE PRODUCT SHAPE THIS IMPLIES.
WiFi mesh for a group riding together; LoRa for the rider who is
separated. 5.8 GHz is badly blocked by terrain and vegetation, so what matters
is not reaching the lead from the tail — it is whether CONSECUTIVE riders stay
within a few hundred metres. ⭐ A convoy is a chain and each rider relays.
A gap — one rider stopped, a split at a junction — breaks the chain, and that
is exactly when you most want to see where everyone is. LoRa is not a
fallback; it is the primary safety function.
⚠ COST DECIDES THE MIX. At $150–200, every rider carrying a Nucleus is a
big ask. A $50 T1000-E in most pockets with one or two Nucleus nodes in the
group is the realistic configuration — which is why the mixed network matters
and why LoRa stays.
⭐⭐ THE STARLINK CASE IS A BUSINESS MODEL, NOT A FEATURE. One uplink at
base camp bridged into the mesh and the whole club is reachable — chase vehicles,
families at home, an event organiser on a laptop. Cost per rider stays zero and
the capability is shared. ⭐ That is where the parked V3 backend earns its
place, and it is the shape of the paid service: the app free, the club pays for
what the club uses.
⚠ DESIGN THE UPLINK AS INTERMITTENT FROM THE START. Base camp has it,
the trail does not, and the group crosses back and forth. Internet reachability
is just another transport that comes and goes — not a mode the app switches
into.
⚠ AND THE VENDOR'S OWN TEST DATA IS 2–3 NODES. Everything about 8–10
riders over ten miles is extrapolation until someone measures it.
⭐⭐ THE LICENCE POSITION — WHY THE SPLIT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS.
⚠ Not legal advice; none of this should be built on without a lawyer.
THE APP IS FREE, NOT PAID (corrected by Fred 09-14 — an earlier note in
this master said otherwise). ⭐ The goal: "I am trying to untangle the
dependency so I can add a fee for services backend without violating the open
source agreement. More of an I-TAK approach."
⭐ GPL-3 HAS NO SERVICE CLAUSE — THAT IS AGPL-3. Running modified GPL-3
software as a network service does not trigger source obligations for the
server, and the GPL explicitly permits charging for services. So a paid
backend was never the exposed part. Obligations attach to DISTRIBUTION,
which means the exposed part is the APP.
⛔ THE REAL QUESTION IS WHETHER GROUPTRACK IS A DERIVATIVE WORK of
Meshtastic-Android. Today it plainly is — the code lives in
com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/, inside the fork, in Meshtastic's
activity, on its DI graph. Free-of-charge changes nothing either way.
⭐⭐ AND THIS DECIDES THE PACKAGING MECHANISM, so it is a design constraint
rather than a preference. The FSF's position is that separate programs
communicating at ARM'S LENGTH — sockets, IPC, a bound service across process
boundaries — are generally separate works, while code sharing an ADDRESS SPACE
generally is not. ⚠ An Android dynamic-feature module runs in the same
process, so it is the WEAK end of that spectrum. If the licence position is
a goal and not a side effect, the boundary has to be real IPC between
separately-distributed programs.
⭐ IP-FIRST SUPPORTS ALL OF IT: if layer 1's IP implementation lives in
GroupTrack core — Fred's code, no inheritance — then the checkbox-OFF case is a
complete product with no GPL component shipped at all.
⭐⭐ THE FIRST CUT ALONG THE 2.7 LINE — SEPARATING MESHTASTIC. 2026-09-04. MESHSEP-0904

was local to Main.kt, so the map screens hosting the Mesh button could not see
