⛔ NOT a plain field. That is the eight-build lesson from 09-02:
TrailFilterState is a plain singleton, so every composable reading it
must take a tick parameter or Compose skips the recomposition and
the screen never moves while the state changes underneath. ⭐ mutableStateOf means
Compose observes it directly and no counter is needed anywhere.

⭐⭐ PUBLIC/PRIVATE TRAIL COMPLIANCE — THE 2.6h DEFINITION (09-14). Land-ownership research 2026-09-03. OWNSTATES-0903, UPDATED 2026-09-14 · ➡ MOVED TO 2.7b as RESTRICTED-AREA POLYLINES (Fred 09-29 — section 08c)
⭐⭐⭐ 2.6h REDEFINED 09-14 (Fred): 50-STATE PUBLIC/PRIVATE TRAIL COMPLIANCE.
2.6g is CLOSED — published on all three tracks, and the zoom-cap work was the
final piece for that update.
⭐⭐ THE DEFAULT INVERTS: ALL TRAILS ARE PUBLIC UNLESS A SOURCE SAYS
OTHERWISE. The release's job is to identify the PRIVATE ones.
⛔ This supersedes the 09-09 piece-5 framing ("only Utah has the
ownership polygon layer, so land_status is null everywhere else and
the private filter cannot work"). Null now means PUBLIC. ⭐ The consequence is
the whole point: the app works in every state on day one, and ownership
data becomes an IMPROVEMENT rather than a PREREQUISITE. A Colorado rider is no
longer waiting on forty-nine lookups before the product is usable there.
⚠ AND THE LIABILITY DIRECTION FLIPS WITH IT. The failure mode is now
ROUTING A RIDER ACROSS PRIVATE LAND, not hiding a legal trail. That is the
direction with real-world consequence, so the rider-facing wording matters:
say ownership not verified in this state rather than saying nothing.
⭐⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT INPUTS. THEY STACK; NEITHER IS REQUIRED.
InputAnswersAvailability
PBF access tags (Geofabrik)
    is this WAY shut
    every state, uniform URL, already fetched by the pipeline
Ownership polygons (state portals)
    who owns the GROUND (BLM / USFS / state trust / tribal / private)
    where a state publishes them
⭐ WHY BOTH, AND WHY THE WEST NEEDS THE SECOND (Fred 09-14):
"western lands have significant public ownership." Tags cannot see an
UNTAGGED way crossing private ground, and they cannot tell a rider they are ON
public land — which in the west is most of the map and most of the value.
⭐ THE TAG SOURCE IS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY MEASURED.
access=private is the single best-populated tag in the
extract — better covered than surface, tracktype or
anything else, and well covered where Fred rides. 34,511 Utah ways carry it. The
classifier already KEEPS those rows and labels them so a rider can see why a
trail is not offered. Files and links for the fifty states are already
identified; ⛔ no ArcGIS portal hunt is required for the base case.
⛔⛔ DO NOT REVERSE THIS FROM THE 08-30 FINDING. READ THE DIRECTION.
08-30 measured that seeding MOTORIZED from tags failed decisively —
9,019 tag-confirmed motorized ways statewide and ZERO in Broken Ridge 2
and 3, the ground Fred actually rides. The conclusion recorded was "OSM access
tagging is too sparse in western Utah to seed anything from."
⭐ That was the POSITIVE direction — prove a trail IS something. The
default-public rule only needs the NEGATIVE direction — a trail is public unless
a tag says shut — and access=private is the well-populated tag,
unlike ohv/atv/motor_vehicle. Sparse
tagging breaks inference, not exclusion. Without this distinction written
down, someone reads "the access tags are too sparse" and reverses a correct
design.
🔴 OPEN — PRECEDENCE WHEN THE TWO INPUTS DISAGREE. A way tagged
access=private sitting on BLM ground; an untagged way crossing
private. ⭐ Proposed: the more restrictive wins for routing, and the rider is
shown WHICH SOURCE said so — because "why won't it route me down this
road" is the next question. Not yet decided.
🔴 OPEN — SCOPE. THE WESTERN 10–12 STATES TEST (Fred 09-14): review may
conclude that only the western states need public/private, and that elsewhere
trail volume and data availability negate the benefit. ⭐ Answerable with
data rather than opinion: trail count per state against whether a usable
ownership layer exists. Candidates carrying both the riding volume and the
public-land patchwork: UT · AZ · NV · CO · ID · MT · WY · NM · OR · WA · CA.
🔴 CARRIED, STILL GATING (09-09): does osm_way_tags PERSIST
between imports, or is it dropped and rebuilt? If rebuilt, a second state pays
the full tag cost again.
⚠ THE POLARITY TRAP BELOW APPLIES TO THE POLYGON HALF ONLY — the
per-state entry must record WHICH KIND of layer it is, not just a URL. The
09-03 research that follows is unchanged and still correct.
⭐ LAND OWNERSHIP FOR FIFTY STATES — WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR. 2026-09-03. OWNSTATES-0903
⭐⭐ PROVEN 09-03: THE FETCH WORKS UNATTENDED. Droid 2, with no ownership
file and no markers, pulled the 78 MB layer itself and classified 145,942 trails.
Fred: "the land use file picked up perfectly." The remaining question is
the other forty-nine.
Utah, working:
https://hub.arcgis.com/api/v3/datasets/2f59731608274691922d2d16bde2404f_0/downloads/data?format=geojson&amp;spatialRefId=4326&amp;where=1%3D1
⭐ ONLY THE ITEM ID CHANGES. Everything else in that URL is the generic
ArcGIS Hub API. ⚠ spatialRefId=4326 is load-bearing — the layer is
named "WM" (web mercator) and arrives projected without it, which the polygon
test would silently mis-handle.
⭐ MOST STATE CATALOGUES ARE ArcGIS OPEN DATA (Fred, 09-03), so the same
download endpoint works and this is a LOOKUP EXERCISE rather than an integration
problem — one id per state, found once, stored in the catalogue.
StatePortalLayer to search
Utahopendata.gis.utah.gov (UGRC)Land Ownership WM ✅ working
CaliforniaWIFIRE / FRAP catalogPublic Lands Ownership / FRAP
North CarolinaNC OneMap GeoPortalManaged Areas / Federal &amp; State Lands
FloridaFlorida Geographic Data LibraryState Lands and Conservation
OthersUCLA Library GIS U.S. Data Guide"Public Land", "Conservation"
⚠ NOT ALL OF THEM ARE HUB-SHAPED. Nevada's Surface Management Agency
layer is hosted on a BLM hub rather than a state portal; Colorado's BLM office
publishes SMA as shapefile, KMZ and web service; Arizona's state trust land sits
behind a parcel viewer with no obvious download. ⭐ Three shapes, and the third
needs a person rather than a URL.
⛔⛔ THE REAL DESIGN WORK IS NOT THE URL — IT IS WHAT THE POLYGONS MEAN.
Utah's layer carries owner, agency,
admin, and our test asks: does this segment fall inside a private
polygon? ⚠ That question only works because Utah's layer maps ownership
CONTINUOUSLY across the state.
⛔ A layer that lists PUBLIC land positively inverts the test. "Not in
this layer" would then mean private or unmapped, and those are not the
same thing — one is a fact and the other is an absence. ⭐ Getting that backwards
would mark every unmapped trail private and hide it under the default filter,
which is exactly the failure mode that looks like missing data.
So the catalogue entry needs three things per state, not one:
the item id
which field carries ownership
whether the layer is continuous (absence means unmapped) or
positive (absence means the other thing)
⚠ And a state's own words are worth reading: Nevada's service says its SMA
data is a reference tool, not an authoritative source, and has not been
checked for accuracy in all areas. ⭐ That matches how the app already frames it —
this tells a rider who owns the ground, not who is welcome on it.
⭐ PUBLIC MEANS STATE AND FEDERAL (Fred, 09-03), and that is why a single
national federal layer will not do. BLM's Surface Management Agency covers federal
land across the west in one dataset — but it would miss state trust land, state
parks and state forests, which is exactly the ground riders use. Utah's SITLA
layer IS state trust land; a federal-only source would have none of it.
⚠ Consequence: per-state, from each state's own portal, even where a
national layer would be less work.

⛔⛔ THE IMPORT HAS NO OWNER — 09-03 DIAGNOSIS. IMPORTLIFE-0903
⛔ WHAT THE 09-03 LOG SHOWS, and none of it was guessed:
05:37:50  gate evaluates -- 145,942 trails -> Granted
05:38:03  Database init failed: database is locked
05:38:34  Database init failed: database is locked
05:38:45  opens -- 0 trails

⭐⭐ FOUR DEFECTS, ONE SHAPE: NOTHING OWNS THE WORK.
THE GATE ANSWERED 68 SECONDS BEFORE ITS OWN HOUSEKEEPING RAN. It said
Granted at 05:37:50 while the clear did not happen until 05:38:58 —
blocked behind two database is locked failures at 30-second
timeouts. ⛔ The rider was let into a map with no trails and no prompt, while a
delete was still running. Fred: "we are lucky this did not ANR."
CANCEL DOES NOT CANCEL. Fred cancelled New Hampshire; it downloaded a
67 MB PBF for eight more minutes and only stopped when its own download failed.
⭐ Cancel dismisses the PANEL. It has no effect on the work.
NOTHING PREVENTS A SECOND IMPORT. Utah started 37 seconds after New
Hampshire, on its own thread, over the same database. That is where the lock
contention came from.
⛔ STEP 8 DIES WITH THE COMPOSITION.
rememberCoroutineScope left the composition — the classification ran
in a scope belonging to a panel that had been dismissed. ⚠ The worst possible
outcome: the import looks finished, the trails are all there, and NOTHING is
classified. Fred saw it as every trail drawing one colour.
⭐⭐ THE COMMON CAUSE: work that matters is tied to something incidental —
a composable's lifetime, a database-open path, a Python script on one device.
Each placement looked reasonable where it sat. Fred, 09-03: "we had a very
specific design ... all in a single thread. What we got looked nothing like it.
We cannot just ignore the design and implement what you want and think it will
work out just fine."
⭐ AND THE MANIFEST LIES ABOUT IT. Step 8 has no entry of its own — both
its stages borrow sources.optJSONObject(sources.length() - 1), the
LAST SOURCE'S record. So a failed classification writes into some other source's
progress and the manifest reads as a complete import. ⛔ That is exactly why
09-03 looked successful: seven sources green, trails loaded, nothing classified,
and no record saying so.
⭐ THE FIXES, AS SPECIFIED (not yet built):
ONE HOUSEKEEPING JOB, BLOCKING. Release check → clear → ALTER →
reload, in that order, one thread, and the gate does not answer until it
returns. A red banner while it runs: Fred, 09-03, "system housekeeping is
being performed, do not interrupt." ⭐ Answering the 08-16 rule that a
one-shot destructive operation should be the loudest thing the app does.
⛔ THE ALTER ONLY EVER RUNS ON AN EMPTY TABLE. Fred: "altering a
table with no data being populated — no. It needs to be cleared and reloaded if
the table is incorrect." A column added beside populated rows is the
half-migrated state that cost 09-02. ⚠ Consequence:
SpatialDbManager.init() stops carrying migration logic entirely.
THE IMPORT MOVES OFF THE COMPOSITION SCOPE, cancel actually cancels,
and a guard refuses a second import while one is in flight.
STEP 8 BECOMES A TRACKED MANIFEST STAGE with its own entry and counts,
so a failed classification cannot read as a finished import.
⭐ PROVEN 09-03, so it does not need rediscovering: the land-ownership
URL is a plain GET returning the data directly — no token, no expiry, no queued
export, no job polling. curl -sIL gives 200 and
application/json; the body opens
{"type": "FeatureCollection", "name": "Land_Ownership_WM" in CRS84.
⚠ spatialRefId=4326 is load-bearing: the layer is named "WM" and
would otherwise arrive in web mercator.
⭐ And it CLASSIFIES CORRECTLY once it runs — Droid 1, 09-02:
145,942 classified, 43,880 private, 129 seconds.
⛔⛔ THE PROTOTYPE THAT NEVER SHIPPED — AND THE LIST THAT LOST IT. 2026-09-02. CLASSIFY4-0902
⛔⛔ DROID 1 CRASHED ON ITS FIRST VIEWPORT QUERY:
no such column: land_status. The filter builds
AND land_status='PUBLIC' AND carto_code NOT IN (...) and every query threw.
THE REASON IS WORSE THAN THE CRASH. land_status, use_type and
carto_code_source — the four-field classification, the week's central work — existed on
ONE DEVICE. A Python script put them on Droid 2 on 08-31. They were in no schema, no
migration, and nothing in the app wrote them. A grep of the whole convoy package returned
nothing.
⭐ The columns not being in any schema should have been the tell. Nothing writes a field no
schema declares. I ran the Python against Fred's device, saw four populated fields, and never asked
where they would come from on anyone else's.
⛔⛔ THE ACTUAL FAILURE WAS THE LIST (Fred, 09-02): "never made the discussion list of
open items. That was the failure." And: "I ask for updates to the handoff and the living doc
every day. Make sure we have enough detail for a new conversation handoff to be efficient. We didn't
even have a new conversation — we lost it between yesterday and today."
What happened: classify4_2026-08-31_v1.py called itself "THE SPECIFICATION for
Kotlin" in its own header. The two-level split — CAPTURE then DERIVE — was designed deliberately
because the derivation touches every record. ⛔ On 09-01 the CAPTURE half shipped and the DERIVE half
did not, and "port classify4 into the import" was in the 08-31 living master but dropped out of
the 09-01 handoff. The list I worked from the next day did not have it.
⭐⭐ THE RULE: the open list is CARRIED FORWARD, never re-derived from what is fresh in
mind. An item leaves it only when something closes it. ⚠ A handoff that is not sufficient for a cold
start is not sufficient for continuity either — this one failed inside a single unbroken thread.
⭐ THE FIX, AND IT WAS SMALL BECAUSE THE MACHINERY EXISTED. Fred, 09-02: "that should be
quick, that is why we broke it into two separate processes." OwnershipReclass already
read the SITLA polygons, built the 0.05° grid and ran point-in-polygon. It answered the right
question and wrote it into the wrong shape.
New TrailClassifier.kt — the mapping ported verbatim: nine categories, OSM's
designated_uses tested first (finer than carto_code), UGRC's numbered vocabulary second,
agency free text last. Plus USE_OF, ⭐ the only place category and use_type are
related.
Step 8 now reads EVERY ROW, not the ~28,000 with no carto_code. ⚠ The 08-31 measurement of
the old behaviour: it missed 17,283 private motorized and 20,013 private non-motorized.
It writes all four fields to trails, and carto_code to
trail_properties — both stores, because SpatialDbManager:1689 arbitrates and leaving one
behind makes a trail disagree with itself.
⛔ R - Residential Roads IS GONE. Fred, 08-31: "ownership is a SEPARATE FIELD,
not folded into the category." Folding it in is what destroyed identity on 201 rows. A private road
KEEPS its category and answers PRIVATE on land_status.
The three columns ALTERed beside the status one, each probed separately so a
device that got some and not others converges.
⭐ AND THE PREDICATE IS NULL-TOLERANT. Adding the columns alone leaves them null, and
land_status='PUBLIC' matches nothing against null — so a rider on the shipped default
would have got AN EMPTY MAP instead of a crash. ⚠ That is worse, not better: it looks like the
data is gone. Null now passes.
Clear marker bumped twice — 2026-08-24L → 09-02A → 09-02B — so every device reloads with
the classification in place.
⚠ METHOD, SIX TIMES IN ONE WEEK: anchors built from sed output failed on
invisible blank lines — three times in this patch alone. ⭐ cat -A shows them in one
command and the rule is already in the locked file. The guards refused to write every time,
which is the only reason it cost minutes rather than a build.
⛔⛔ THE ARTIFACT DISPLAY PATH — SIDE ALLEYS FOUND 09-01, AND ONE TRAIL STILL MISSING. DISPLAYPATH-0901
⭐⭐ FRED'S VERDICT, AND IT IS THE HEADLINE: "I have spent four days adding trails and
expanding our net to find why these trails are not displaying, and the whole time we had a hole in
the net." ⚠ The data was never the problem. Four days of widening coverage were spent chasing
trails that were present in the database the entire time.
⛔ AND: "I thought I knew how this code worked and I could not be more wrong. I think we
need to check changes made during spatial implementation — we do not even know what process is
called any more."
THE CASE: "Spanish George Road" — OSM, forestry/access road, PUBLIC,
MOTORIZED. Five miles east-west at 37.998 N. ⚠ Its bbox is 0.0003° tall — about 120 feet,
about as close to degenerate as a real trail gets.
What is MEASURED, not assumed:
✅ In trails with valid geometry — 794 chars of LINESTRING, clean ASCII name
(hex-checked), min_lat populated.
✅ queryTrailsByViewport returns it — the device's own trace:
raw=1 items=1 json=true, state=1 checked=-1 limit=5000.
✅ queryArtifactList's SQL, run BY HAND over the device's database with a generous
box, returns 69 rows including it.
⛔ The app's row list showed 34 and did NOT include it.
⛔ Every NEIGHBOURING trail draws and lists correctly.
⛔ It never appeared at any zoom level.
⭐ SO THE FAILURE IS PAST KOTLIN. ⚠ And to be precise about what the trace proves: the name
is present in the GeoJSON STRING handed to evaluateJavascript. It does NOT prove the
call succeeded, that 538KB parsed, or that Leaflet added the feature. ⛔ I claimed "it reaches
Leaflet"; Fred challenged it and was right to.
⭐⭐ THE SIDE ALLEYS — THREE REAL DEFECTS IN THE DISPLAY PATH, ALL FROM THE SPATIAL ERA, NONE
KNOWN THIS MORNING. Every one was found by reading, and every one could silently drop trails:
⛔ "NOT NAMED" IS A NAME (Fred). queryTrailsByViewport ordered
CASE WHEN name IS NULL OR name = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END — meant as "named trails first".
But ~69% of rows carry the LITERAL STRING "Not Named", which is neither NULL nor empty, so tens of
thousands of placeholders sorted as NAMED and competed for the cap. A 200-foot connector outranked a
ten-mile track. ⭐ FIXED: order by extent alone. Fred: "real unnamed trails can be long — I would
rather load by trail length so meaningful artifacts are loaded first."
⛔ A SECOND QUERY NOBODY WAS LOOKING AT. The row list is
SpatialDbManager.queryArtifactList, NOT queryTrailsByViewport — different
SQL, different ordering, different cap: ORDER BY name LIMIT 200. ⭐⭐ Fred said "rows
start at 200" for hours and I kept answering that I could not find a 200. It was there, at
SpatialDbManager:1987. Alphabetical, so numbered roads (10400 West, 13600 West…) fill the list and
anything starting with S never gets near it. ⚠ It cannot explain a list of 34 — but it is a real
defect and would bite the moment a viewport holds 200+ trails.
⛔ PER-TRAIL SELECTION WAS A TRAP. SpatialDisplayManager filters to
checkedIds when the state is SELECTED, so a trail imported AFTER that list was saved
silently never drew. And it never made sense for trails: Fred, "I cannot think of a reason why a
trail would be selected since we have so many unnamed." ⭐ FIXED: SELECT greyed for Trails, only
OFF and ALL, and a saved SELECTED reads as ALL so a stuck device recovers itself.
⚠ AND A FOURTH, UNRESOLVED: the row list and the draw come from DIFFERENT queries. If the
list is meant to document what was drawn, they have DRIFTED and that is a defect in itself. If it is
an independent view, then its disagreement proves less than it appears to. ⭐ Worth settling
which it is.
🔵 WHERE IT STANDS, AND WHAT IS NEXT

⭐⭐⭐ THE FILTER MODEL — TWO AXES, FOUR CELLS. SETTLED 2026-08-31. MATRIX-0831
⭐⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT TOGGLES, NOT A CATEGORY LIST (Fred 08-31):
MOTORIZED / NON-MOTORIZED on one axis, PUBLIC / PRIVATE on the other.
"two throttles that we can mix and match — a cut of public or private over motorized and
non-motorized, and both cuts will show unspecified."
⭐ AND FOUR CELLS IS THE FLOOR AND THE CEILING. Fred: "just so complex … will we cut any
deeper than that or just confuse?" — no. Going deeper (OHV vs forestry vs track) is back to nine
toggles, and the numbers say it would not earn its place: motorized-public is 53,172 rows and 64% of
it is ONE subcategory. If a rider is riding, they want all of it.
⭐⭐ COLOUR CARRIES THE DETAIL, TOGGLES CARRY THE DECISION (Fred): "we may identify them
with colors on the map but for searching and toggling that should be enough." Shades of blue show
whether something is a designated OHV route or an inferred farm track — information with no
interaction cost.

⭐⭐ THE ANSWER TO "DOES A PRIVATE BUCKET PAY?" (Fred asked before the run): YES, and
non-motorized is where it pays most — 70% private. `paved shared use` alone is 13,493 private
against 247 public. Those are sidewalks and park paths.
⛔ TOTAL PRIVATE: 41,666 rows — 29% of the table — against the 13,628 step 8 caught.
Three times as many.
⭐ THE TOGGLES ARE PER-SITUATION, NOT A POLICY (Fred 08-31): "riding near town, public
and private motorized. turn off roads etc based on what you want to see."
Near a town you want BOTH ownerships on motorized, because the private roads are how you get
through. Out in the backcountry you turn private off to clean the map. ⭐ So the default matters
less than it seems — whatever ships, the rider adjusts in one tap. And it is the argument for
never deleting: keep everything in the table and let the rider decide what is useful where they
are.
⚠ DATA CONSEQUENCE, and it is the change underneath the toggles: the two axes must
be stored INDEPENDENTLY. Both currently live in carto_code, so a row can say only
one thing — "motorized AND private" cannot be expressed. That is why step 8 overwrote the identity
rather than adding to it.
🔵 WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAYS TO CHANGE
⭐ WIDEN STEP 8 to test EVERY row, not only those with no carto code. It currently misses
17,283 private motorized and 20,013 private non-motorized. ⚠ And it must preserve the original
code so the toggle can restore it — today it overwrites and the identity is gone (1,123 of its
flips could not even be re-checked in this run for that reason).
⛔ 24,158 non-rideable rows draw CYAN today — `2 Hiking and Biking`, `3 Paved Shared Use`
and `9 Link` have NO colour case at all, so they read as possibly rideable. The biggest visual lie
on the map, and it predates everything built this week.
⚠ Unspecified (30,085) has to land somewhere on the motorized axis by default. It splits
cleanly on ownership but not on use. Today the router treats it as motorized.
⚠ OPEN, from the seglen probe (written, not yet run): are the 13,361 wholly-private
"forestry/access/farm roads" real, or is OSM splitting one long road into segments that are judged
independently? Fred: "I have a hard time believing we have forestry or access roads that do not
touch public land." ⭐ Half-mile sampling is NOT the suspect — on a twenty-mile road that is
forty points and any ONE public point keeps the segment. Segmentation is, and the fix would be
grouping by name before deciding. Same defect as `24000 North` this morning.

⭐⭐⭐ THE TOWN-GRID SOLUTION — THE RIDER DRAWS THE BOX. SETTLED 2026-08-31. RIDERBOX-0831 · B · C
Fred, 08-31: "the rider identifies the cluster and manually updates that cluster."
"this is the solution."
⭐⭐ WHY IT WORKS WHERE EVERYTHING ELSE FAILED. Every approach in CLUTTER-0830 tried to
SYNTHESISE a settlement boundary from data that does not contain one — landuse residential is absent
at Beryl Junction, buildings number 7 in the whole grid box, places_a has 11 settlements statewide,
and the streets themselves arrive as highway=unclassified, the same tag a backcountry
road carries. ⛔ There is no identifier distinguishing Avenue A from Fisher Wash Road.
⭐ So stop looking for one: the rider IS the classifier, and local knowledge is exactly what
OSM lacks out there.
⚠ AND IT IS A GESTURE THEY ALREADY KNOW — they draw boxes to download maps.
THE MECHANISM
#Step
1⭐ A FINGER-DRAWN POLYLINE, NOT A BBOX (Fred 08-31, refined). Settlements
are not rectangles — a box around Beryl Junction would take the farm roads on its edges. A closed
polyline is a polygon, and most of the machinery exists: Route+ already draws polylines by tapping,
and the artifact model already stores WKT. The only new piece is a point-in-polygon ray-cast, about
fifteen lines. ⭐ Keep the polygon's BBOX alongside it as a cheap prefilter — reject on four
comparisons, ray-cast only what survives. Same pattern the corridor work uses.
⚠ DRAWN AT z12 (Fred 08-31): the zoom where a settlement reads as a SHAPE rather than
as individual streets, and where its extent is visible at all. At z16 you are inside the grid; at z10
the town is a smudge. ⭐ ENABLED AT z11, z12 AND z13 (Fred 08-31), disabled outside with a line saying
why — otherwise someone draws a boundary at z8 that swallows a county. ⭐⭐ z13 IS THE AREA-SEARCH
LANDING ZOOM, so the rider is ALREADY THERE when they see the problem and the tool is available
without them thinking about zoom at all. ⚠ That makes z13 the common case, not the edge — the
out-of-range hint must fire only OUTSIDE z11–z13, never at the level they normally sit
at.
2⛔⛔ ONLY THE PROBLEM CLASS FLIPS — BE VERY PARTICULAR (Fred 08-31):
"we need to be very particular about what these roads current class is so we don't touch more."
Only unclassified unknown is reclassified — motorized true, nothing else known.
That is the shape fallback, and it is what Avenue A and 1st Street arrive as. ⭐ EVERYTHING ELSE
INSIDE THE POLYGON IS UNTOUCHED: a track in a town is still a track,
OHV designated stays, hiking / biking / private / paved are left alone.
That containment is what makes it safe to draw roughly with a finger — a stray edge over a
real trail does nothing.
Rows that do flip get a new carto category. The count in step 3 of the day's plan
decides whether an existing code can be repurposed or a new one is minted. ⚠ A NEGATIVE NUMBER
WILL NOT SURVIVE charAt(0) — trailColor switches on the first
character, so -1 gives -. Workable with a case for it, but check first
whether any of 1–9 is genuinely unused: from the 08-30 count, 7 Steps had 82 rows and 6 Equestrian
Primary had 72.
3⭐⭐ THE RECLASS IS THE FIRST THING THE RECIPE DOES (Fred 08-31). Everything
downstream then sees the corrected network — what is DISPLAYED and what is SELECTED, from one
step. That is the two-consumers principle holding: the exclusion is applied once to the data, not
separately to the map and the router, so they cannot disagree.
4⭐⭐ IT TRAVELS IN THE RECIPE. Fred: "we can build that table and reclass
into the recipe so sharing route clean up data." One rider marks Beryl Junction and everyone who
builds from that recipe gets the clean network. The correction spreads by use rather than by
everyone repeating the work.
⭐ It also makes a recipe rebuild genuinely reproducible for the first time: same anchor, same
mileage, same pins, and now the same network, because the exclusions arrive with it. The
recipe already fixes the other inputs precisely so a rebuild means something.
⚠ OPEN, FOR WHEN IT IS BUILT
⭐⭐ THE PROMPT, AND THE FILTERED DRAW (Fred 08-31). RIDERBOX-0831C. When the rider is
positioning for a TRAILHEAD at z11–z13, the app asks whether they see a cluster of neighbourhood
roads and uncategorized trails, and offers to draw a boundary around it.
⭐ AND WHILE THEY DRAW, THE FILTER SWITCHES TO SHOW ONLY unclassified unknown
— so the rider sees EXACTLY what they are about to affect and nothing else. That makes the
containment rule VISIBLE rather than something they have to trust: only the highlighted roads can
change, so a boundary straying over a track is obviously harmless.
⚠ TELL THEM IT IS TEMPORARY. Displayed in isolation the grid looks sparse and it reads as
data loss. One line: the other trails are still there, hidden for the moment.
⚠ MAKE THE PROMPT SPECIFIC, NOT A QUESTION. The app KNOWS how many
unclassified unknown rows are in the viewport — "47 uncategorized roads here — mark
them as neighbourhood?" is a fact it has, rather than a judgement outsourced to the rider.
⚠ AND IT MUST NOT BLOCK. The planner was rebuilt precisely because a checklist of
everything at once was too dense — one thing at a time, prompt at the bottom, map clear. Make it
conditional on a count worth acting on and dismissible without a decision, so the rider on Broken
Ridge never sees it.
PLACEMENT: in the AI route build, at the position on the map before a waypoint is
dropped. ⚠ CAUTION: the route build is FROZEN and the planner's tap handling is
the piece with the most history — the two-nested-test handler, the both-modes-off reset, the
proximity bugs. Overloading the waypoint gesture is exactly where it has broken before. Consider
an explicit "mark neighbourhood" mode reached from the same panel: one more tap, but it cannot
collide with the pin logic.
WHERE THE TABLE LIVES. It is the RIDER'S data, not source data, so it must survive a
reimport rather than being wiped with the OSM rows. ⚠ And since it travels in the recipe it is not
purely device-local either.
⭐ REVERSIBLE. Record the original class on every flipped row, so a rider who
over-draws can undo rather than reimport. ⚠ And since the reclass TRAVELS IN THE RECIPE, whoever
receives it must be able to undo it too.
⭐ THE COUNT IS THE CHECK. Report "47 roads reclassified" the moment the polygon closes.
Silent success is how a rider finds out three rides later that the boundary did not do what they
meant.
NOT RELEASED, WILL BE REVISITED (Fred 08-31). Nothing here has shipped.
⛔⛔ THE TOWN-GRID PROBLEM — EIGHT APPROACHES ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-30. CLUTTER-0830

areas (towns)."
⚠⚠ AND THE HONEST FRAMING, which took the afternoon to reach: the grid was arriving
BEFORE today's work too. Yesterday's filter was track + unclassified,
and unclassified is what Beryl's streets come in as — Avenue A–G, 1st–7th Street.
Widening the net added service, residential, path and tertiary, and the rules then rejected 329,941
of them. ⭐ So falling back to yesterday's definition does NOT fix the grid — it only removes
Mountain Spring Road again. Fred: "virtually the same map." That is correct, and it is the

WHAT WAS TRIED AND KILLED. Every one by a measurement, not an argument.

🔵 WHAT IS LEFT TO EXPLORE — two candidates, both measurable against LOCAL files, no device.
(A) unclassified with NO surface tag. That is the shape-fallback branch in
OsmTrailClassifier — it returns unclassified unknown, motorized=true, in on
shape alone. It is what admits the town grid.
⚠⚠ AND FRED'S OBJECTION TO IT IS UNANSWERED, and it is a good one: "it sounds to me that
would be the most remote areas that have not been mapped properly." ⭐ He is right that ABSENCE of
a surface tag is more likely where nobody has detailed the road — which is the backcountry. ⛔ And the
counts do NOT separate cleanly: Broken Ridge 3 has 16 unclassified against 91 tracks, Beryl grid has
8 against 45. Similar ratios. ⚠ Note also that highway=unclassified does NOT mean
"unknown" in OSM — it is a specific tag for a minor public road below tertiary. MEASURE IT BEFORE
BUILDING IT: unclassified with and without surface, per area, WITH NAMES. If backcountry loses
Fisher Wash Road, it joins the list above.
(B) access=private density (Fred 08-30). ⭐ 34,511 Utah ways carry it — the
single best-populated tag in the extract, better covered than surface, tracktype or anything
else, and well covered where Fred rides. Private ways are already excluded by the rules, so they are
not the clutter — but a CLUSTER of them marks a ranch or a development, which is what residential
landuse would have marked if it existed out there. ⚠ Second angle worth checking in the same query:
are Tierra / Sundown / Palomar Drive themselves tagged private? If so they are already excluded and
something else is drawing them.
⚠ METHOD NOTE, MINE, 08-30. I quoted 125,831 as the expected row count all afternoon
— in commit messages, patch headers and every prediction — after we had already agreed to write every
row rather than only the included ones. Those two things are incompatible: under "keep everything" the
answer was ~423,000. When the first device run showed 667,546 I diagnosed a filter mismatch, which was
real (footway did not belong), but treated it as the whole explanation when it was part of it.
⭐ And the scale of the storage decision was misrepresented by me. Fred took it understanding

⭐⭐ IDENTITY, OWNERSHIP AND NAMING — SETTLED 2026-08-30. IDENTITY-2026-08-30
Fred 08-30. Multiple source imports run in sequence, OSM last. These rules govern who
may write a trail row, what makes two arrivals the same trail, and what happens to names. ⚠ The
UPDATE rules themselves are written when the add process is written — not now.
#RuleNote
I1The creating process owns the trail row. Only that process adds or updates
it.Source is identified and recorded at CREATION. ⛔ A row written without provenance can
never gain it — the 139,688 rows on the device today have source_id null and there is no
way to work out where any came from.
I2geom_hash is the identity. One hash, one trail.A
second trail carrying an existing hash is not processed as a new row.
I3Hash exists + arrival is NAMED → the name is added as an
ALIAS.The trail is not duplicated; the other survey's name attaches to the one
row.
I4⭐ Hash exists + arrival is UNNAMED → nothing is written. No alias
write.Fred: an unnamed arrival has nothing to contribute. Keeps "unnamed" out of the
alias list entirely.
I5No trail is stored as "unnamed" — neither a new trail nor an existing
one.
I6⭐⭐ ORDERING: named sources run BEFORE OSM.The reason, Fred
08-30: a high percentage of OSM trails are unnamed — measured, 87% of tracks carry no
name. Running the named sources first gives them the chance to create the hash record, so
OSM's unnamed arrival lands on an existing hash and is dropped by I4 rather than creating an unnamed
row. ⛔ It is NOT an ownership-ordering rule.
⭐⭐ CATEGORISATION IS OURS, AND IT IS NOT A FOREIGN WRITE (Fred 08-30). "Most specific
categorization is applied. May update another source's category — that is the purpose of this
process. If we have a trail from BLM with no trail type and OSM categorizes it we need to update the
trail type. That is our data in an extension file by hash id."
⭐ This resolves the apparent conflict with I1. OSM contributing a type to a BLM-created
trail is not one source writing another's row — the classification is OUR data, held in the
extension file and keyed by hash id. The trail row stays with its creator.
⚠⚠ KEY BY HASH, NOT BY trail_id. trail_properties joins on
trail_id, a UUID minted at insert, while geom_hash is the identity.
That distinction is what caused the orphan incident — the trails clear removed 86,969 trails and
303,585 trail_properties rows joined to nothing, because the extension DB was not
cleared with them. The hash survives a reimport; the UUID does not.
⚠ OPEN, for when the add process is written: "most specific wins" needs a ranked
specificity order for the vocabulary, or every collision is a judgement call.
OHV designated over unclassified motorized is obvious;
track grade3 against unclassified motorized is not — one is specific about
surface quality, the other about permission.
⛔⛔ THE OPEN CONDITION UNDER I2/I3/I4/I6 — MEASURED, NOT SUSPECTED. Cross-source hashes
do not collide. Utah measured 9 hash matches out of 89,554 rows between OSM and UGRC, and
zero across Arizona and Nevada. Independent surveys of the same ground produce different
vertices and therefore a different hash. Name-matching found 2,021 Utah duplicates in the same
data, pruned by hand.
⚠ The consequence for I6 as written: OSM does not recognise the named row a prior source
created — it creates its own unnamed row beside it, and running last changes nothing. The mechanism
works perfectly within a source across re-imports (89,436 dropped on the Utah re-import), where
the geometry is identical by construction. Cross-source identity needs something that survives two
surveys of one trail; exact geometry hash is not it.
Recorded as the condition on these rules, not as an objection to them. Settle it when
the add process is written.
⚠ ONE RECORDED DEFECT SITS IN THE PATH I3 NEEDS. resolveTrackAdd's
DROP_NAME / DROP_ALIAS / ALIAS branches — the ones taken when
the hash already exists — do not update the name: they delete the source file and return. The
recorded symptom is a re-added item keeping the old row's name. Check that branch before I3 is
relied on.
⭐ Consistent with the 3.0 naming rule already recorded 08-22 — unnamed is no name,
so the first name replaces unnamed and becomes the single source of truth — with the caveat that
3.0 moves names to the server and back down, so whatever fills the field today must be
replaceable.

The join, and why it works
GPKG to PBF on osm_id. Both sides are OSM. The GeoPackage stores it as
text and the PBF gives an integer, so one cast joins them. Measured on Utah:
424,951 of 699,537 GPKG rows matched within the widened net.
⚠ The GPKG table is gis_osm_roads_free — no _1 suffix despite
the shapefile spec documenting one. Columns:
fid, geom, osm_id, code, fclass, name, ref, oneway, maxspeed, layer, bridge, tunnel
— and no access field of any kind, which is the whole reason the PBF is needed.
The rules, as measured
EXCLUSIONS FIRST -- the confident part
  access in (private, no)            -&gt; OUT     34,511 Utah ways carry access=private
  motor_vehicle = no  or vehicle=no  -&gt; IN, but NON-MOTORIZED, refined by
                                        foot / bicycle:
                                          both designated -&gt; hiking and biking
                                          bicycle         -&gt; biking only
                                          foot            -&gt; hiking only
                                          neither named   -&gt; non-motorized
MOTORIZED, CONFIRMED
  ohv or atv in (yes, designated)    -&gt; OHV designated
  4wd_only = yes                     -&gt; 4wd only
  motor_vehicle / motorcar yes|desig -&gt; motorized track &lt;tracktype&gt;
                                        or "unclassified motorized"
SURFACE DECIDES THE ROADS -- tertiary, residential, service, unclassified, road
  surface rideable                   -&gt; unclassified motorized
  surface paved                      -&gt; OUT          the subdivision problem
  highway = unclassified, no surface -&gt; unclassified unknown   (in, on shape)
  otherwise                          -&gt; OUT
TRACKS -- in on shape, as today
  tracktype present                  -&gt; track &lt;grade&gt;
  surface rideable                   -&gt; unclassified motorized
  otherwise                          -&gt; unclassified unknown
PATHS, CYCLEWAYS, BRIDLEWAYS -- non-motorized unless a tag says otherwise
  bicycle + foot designated          -&gt; hiking and biking
  cycleway or bicycle designated     -&gt; biking only
  bridleway                          -&gt; equestrian
  otherwise                          -&gt; hiking only
RIDEABLE = dirt ground gravel unpaved compacted fine_gravel sand earth
           grass rock mud pebblestone woodchips
PAVED    = asphalt concrete paved concrete:plates paving_stones sett cobblestone
STAGE ONE, WIDENED = track unclassified residential service path tertiary
                     cycleway bridleway byway road
STAGE ONE, TODAY   = track unclassified      (osm_layers.json filter_values)
⚠ WHY tertiary IS IN THE WIDENED NET: Mountain Spring Road, way
10113390 — highway=tertiary, surface=dirt, name_1=Pine Valley
Road. On the map, ridden, and never in the trails table. 80% of Utah tertiaries carry a
surface tag — the best coverage in the survey — so the tag sorts the dirt ones from the
asphalt.
osm_survey_2026-08-29.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
OSM-SURVEY-2026-08-29 -- what the GeoPackage throws away.
    python osm_survey_2026-08-29.py D:/Utah_OSM/utah-260828.osm.pbf
WHY: osm_layers.json selects trails from the Geofabrik GPKG on `fclass` alone,
and its own comment says why that is a problem:
    &quot;the access tags that would answer this properly (ohv, motor_vehicle,
     access) are NOT in Geofabrik&#x27;s GeoPackage at all -- the roads layer has no
     access field of any kind -- so fclass answers by SHAPE, not by permission.&quot;
Which produces both of the faults Fred sees on the ground:
  - community roads arriving AS trails -- `unclassified` is OSM&#x27;s tag for a
    minor public road, so a paved lane in a subdivision matches exactly
  - rideable roads NOT arriving -- tagged residential, service or path, none
    of which are in filter_values
THE PBF CARRIES WHAT SEPARATES THEM: surface, tracktype, smoothness, access,
motor_vehicle, 4wd_only, ohv. This counts them, on BOTH populations -- what the
current filter takes and what it rejects -- because the rules can only be built
from the difference.
Nothing is written. It reads and counts.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import osmium
PBF = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) &gt; 1 else &quot;D:/Utah_OSM/utah-260828.osm.pbf&quot;
# what osm_layers.json takes today. NOTE: the GPKG&#x27;s fclass for a track is
# &quot;track&quot; or &quot;track_gradeN&quot;; in raw OSM that is highway=track plus a separate
# tracktype tag, so the grades are counted from tracktype below.
CURRENT = {&quot;track&quot;, &quot;unclassified&quot;}
# the broadened net -- stage one of the two-stage filter. Everything a
# side-by-side could plausibly be on, to be narrowed by tags afterwards.
CANDIDATE = {
    &quot;track&quot;, &quot;unclassified&quot;, &quot;residential&quot;, &quot;service&quot;, &quot;path&quot;, &quot;footway&quot;,
    &quot;bridleway&quot;, &quot;cycleway&quot;, &quot;byway&quot;, &quot;road&quot;, &quot;living_street&quot;, &quot;tertiary&quot;,
}
# the tags Geofabrik drops, which are the whole point of this exercise
TELLING = [&quot;surface&quot;, &quot;tracktype&quot;, &quot;smoothness&quot;, &quot;access&quot;, &quot;motor_vehicle&quot;,
           &quot;4wd_only&quot;, &quot;ohv&quot;, &quot;motorcar&quot;, &quot;atv&quot;, &quot;vehicle&quot;, &quot;seasonal&quot;,
           &quot;sac_scale&quot;, &quot;trail_visibility&quot;, &quot;width&quot;, &quot;est_width&quot;]
class Survey(osmium.SimpleHandler):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.highway = Counter()
        self.taken = 0
        self.rejected = 0
        # per highway value, how many carry each telling tag
        self.tagpresence = defaultdict(Counter)
        # the values themselves, for the ones that will drive rules
        self.values = defaultdict(Counter)
        self.named = Counter()
    def way(self, w):
        hw = w.tags.get(&quot;highway&quot;)
        if hw is None:
            return
        self.highway[hw] += 1
        if hw not in CANDIDATE:
            return
        if hw in CURRENT:
            self.taken += 1
        else:
            self.rejected += 1
        if w.tags.get(&quot;name&quot;):
            self.named[hw] += 1
        for t in TELLING:
            v = w.tags.get(t)
            if v is not None:
                self.tagpresence[hw][t] += 1
                self.values[t][v] += 1
def bar(n, total, width=28):
    if not total:
        return &quot;&quot;
    return &quot;#&quot; * max(0, int(width * n / total))
def main():
    print(&quot;reading %s ...&quot; % PBF)
    s = Survey()
    s.apply_file(PBF)
    print()
    total_hw = sum(s.highway.values())
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;HIGHWAY VALUES IN UTAH  (%d ways carry a highway tag)&quot; % total_hw)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;%-16s %9s  %6s  %-9s %s&quot; % (&quot;highway&quot;, &quot;ways&quot;, &quot;%&quot;, &quot;in filter?&quot;, &quot;&quot;))
    for hw, n in s.highway.most_common(24):
        mark = &quot;TAKEN&quot; if hw in CURRENT else (&quot;candidate&quot; if hw in CANDIDATE else &quot;&quot;)
        print(&quot;%-16s %9d  %5.1f%%  %-9s %s&quot;
              % (hw, n, 100.0 * n / total_hw, mark, bar(n, s.highway.most_common(1)[0][1])))
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;THE TWO POPULATIONS&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;  taken by the current filter (track, unclassified) : %8d&quot; % s.taken)
    print(&quot;  rejected but plausibly rideable                   : %8d&quot; % s.rejected)
    print(&quot;  ratio rejected : taken                            : %8.2f&quot;
          % (s.rejected / max(1, s.taken)))
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;TAGS GEOFABRIK DROPS -- how many ways carry them, by highway value&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    cols = [t for t in TELLING if sum(s.tagpresence[h][t] for h in CANDIDATE) &gt; 0]
    head = &quot;%-14s&quot; % &quot;highway&quot;
    for t in cols[:7]:
        head += &quot;%12s&quot; % t[:11]
    print(head)
    for hw in sorted(CANDIDATE, key=lambda h: -s.highway.get(h, 0)):
        if not s.highway.get(hw):
            continue
        row = &quot;%-14s&quot; % hw[:14]
        for t in cols[:7]:
            c = s.tagpresence[hw][t]
            row += &quot;%11s%%&quot; % (&quot;%.0f&quot; % (100.0 * c / s.highway[hw]))
        print(row)
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;THE VALUES THAT WILL DRIVE THE RULES&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    for t in (&quot;surface&quot;, &quot;tracktype&quot;, &quot;access&quot;, &quot;motor_vehicle&quot;, &quot;smoothness&quot;,
              &quot;4wd_only&quot;, &quot;ohv&quot;):
        vals = s.values.get(t)
        if not vals:
            print(&quot;%-14s -- absent from this extract&quot; % t)
            continue
        top = &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s=%d&quot; % (v, n) for v, n in vals.most_common(8))
        print(&quot;%-14s %s&quot; % (t, top))
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    print(&quot;NAMED, by highway value -- an unnamed way is harder to describe to a rider&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
    for hw in sorted(CANDIDATE, key=lambda h: -s.highway.get(h, 0)):
        if not s.highway.get(hw):
            continue
        print(&quot;%-14s %6d of %7d  (%.0f%%)&quot;
              % (hw, s.named[hw], s.highway[hw],
                 100.0 * s.named[hw] / s.highway[hw]))
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    main()
osm_classify_2026-08-29.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
OSM-CLASSIFY-2026-08-29 -- widen the net, narrow by tags, count the difference.
    python osm_classify_2026-08-29.py D:/Utah_OSM/utah.gpkg D:/Utah_OSM/utah-260828.osm.pbf
THE EXERCISE, in Fred&#x27;s words: &quot;first stage filtered value with a broadened
net, second stage apply rules to map to USGS trail types.&quot;
The join is GPKG to PBF on osm_id -- both are OSM, both carry it, and the GPKG
stores it as text while the PBF gives an integer. Nothing here touches the
device: this measures what the rules WOULD do before any of it is built.
=== WHY THE GPKG CANNOT DO THIS ALONE ===
osm_layers.json says it plainly: &quot;the access tags that would answer this
properly (ohv, motor_vehicle, access) are NOT in Geofabrik&#x27;s GeoPackage at all
-- the roads layer has no access field of any kind -- so fclass answers by
SHAPE, not by permission.&quot;
Which produces both faults on the ground: community roads arriving as trails
(unclassified is OSM&#x27;s tag for a minor public road), and rideable dirt roads
not arriving (tagged residential or tertiary, which the filter excludes).
=== THE FIVE NUMBERS ===
    KEPT          in today&#x27;s filter, and the rules agree
    ADDED         rejected today, rideable under the rules
    DROPPED       in today&#x27;s filter, excluded by the rules
    CLASSIFIED    a type assigned from real tags
    UNCLASSIFIED  in, but on shape alone -- nothing said what it is
The baseline for CLASSIFIED is ZERO: trail_type is empty everywhere except
Utah today, so anything at all is new information.
=== THE VOCABULARY ===
Fred, 08-29, refining it live:
  - motor_vehicle=no is not &quot;unclassified&quot;, it is NON-MOTORIZED -- hiking,
    biking or the combination, from foot/bicycle/horse
  - &quot;unclassified motorized&quot;  motorized confirmed, kind unknown
  - &quot;unclassified unknown&quot;    nothing said anything
⭐ The last two matter because 87% of tracks are unnamed. A rider reading
&quot;37 of 77 miles is unnamed track&quot; cannot tell a maintained forest road from a
hiking path someone tagged loosely. Motorized-but-unnamed is ground they can
trust; unknown is the number worth looking at before committing.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import sqlite3
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import osmium
GPKG = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) &gt; 1 else &quot;D:/Utah_OSM/utah.gpkg&quot;
PBF = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) &gt; 2 else &quot;D:/Utah_OSM/utah-260828.osm.pbf&quot;
# stage one, today: what osm_layers.json takes
CURRENT = {&quot;track&quot;, &quot;unclassified&quot;}
# stage one, widened: everything a side-by-side could plausibly be on.
# ⚠ tertiary is in because of Mountain Spring Road -- highway=tertiary,
# surface=dirt, genuinely ridden, and excluded today. 80% of tertiaries carry
# a surface tag, the best coverage in the survey, so the tag can sort them.
WIDE = {&quot;track&quot;, &quot;unclassified&quot;, &quot;residential&quot;, &quot;service&quot;, &quot;path&quot;,
        &quot;tertiary&quot;, &quot;cycleway&quot;, &quot;bridleway&quot;, &quot;byway&quot;, &quot;road&quot;}
RIDEABLE_SURFACE = {&quot;dirt&quot;, &quot;ground&quot;, &quot;gravel&quot;, &quot;unpaved&quot;, &quot;compacted&quot;,
                    &quot;fine_gravel&quot;, &quot;sand&quot;, &quot;earth&quot;, &quot;grass&quot;, &quot;rock&quot;, &quot;mud&quot;,
                    &quot;pebblestone&quot;, &quot;woodchips&quot;}
PAVED_SURFACE = {&quot;asphalt&quot;, &quot;concrete&quot;, &quot;paved&quot;, &quot;concrete:plates&quot;,
                 &quot;paving_stones&quot;, &quot;sett&quot;, &quot;cobblestone&quot;}
class Tags(osmium.SimpleHandler):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Every way we might care about, by osm_id.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.t = {}
    def way(self, w):
        hw = w.tags.get(&quot;highway&quot;)
        if hw is None or hw not in WIDE:
            return
        keep = {}
        for k in (&quot;highway&quot;, &quot;surface&quot;, &quot;tracktype&quot;, &quot;smoothness&quot;, &quot;access&quot;,
                  &quot;motor_vehicle&quot;, &quot;4wd_only&quot;, &quot;ohv&quot;, &quot;atv&quot;, &quot;motorcar&quot;,
                  &quot;vehicle&quot;, &quot;foot&quot;, &quot;bicycle&quot;, &quot;horse&quot;, &quot;name&quot;):
            v = w.tags.get(k)
            if v is not None:
                keep[k] = v
        self.t[w.id] = keep
def classify(tg):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;(included, type). type of None means excluded.&quot;&quot;&quot;
    hw = tg.get(&quot;highway&quot;)
    access = tg.get(&quot;access&quot;)
    mv = tg.get(&quot;motor_vehicle&quot;)
    veh = tg.get(&quot;vehicle&quot;)
    surface = tg.get(&quot;surface&quot;)
    # ── EXCLUSIONS FIRST, and they are the confident part ──────────────
    # ⛔ legally shut. access=private is on 34,511 Utah ways and it is the
    # single best-populated signal in the extract.
    if access in (&quot;private&quot;, &quot;no&quot;) or mv == &quot;no&quot; or veh == &quot;no&quot;:
        # ⭐ NOT &quot;unclassified&quot; -- non-motorized is a CLASSIFICATION, and it
        # is the one that stops the planner routing a side-by-side down a
        # hiking trail.
        foot = tg.get(&quot;foot&quot;)
        bike = tg.get(&quot;bicycle&quot;)
        if mv == &quot;no&quot; or veh == &quot;no&quot;:
            if bike in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;) and foot in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
                return True, &quot;hiking and biking&quot;
            if bike in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
                return True, &quot;biking only&quot;
            if foot in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
                return True, &quot;hiking only&quot;
            return True, &quot;non-motorized&quot;
        return False, None          # private: not ours to ride
    # ── MOTORIZED, CONFIRMED ───────────────────────────────────────────
    if tg.get(&quot;ohv&quot;) in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;) or tg.get(&quot;atv&quot;) in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
        return True, &quot;OHV designated&quot;
    if tg.get(&quot;4wd_only&quot;) == &quot;yes&quot;:
        return True, &quot;4wd only&quot;
    if mv in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;) or tg.get(&quot;motorcar&quot;) in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
        if tg.get(&quot;tracktype&quot;):
            return True, &quot;motorized track %s&quot; % tg[&quot;tracktype&quot;]
        return True, &quot;unclassified motorized&quot;
    # ── SURFACE DECIDES THE ROADS ──────────────────────────────────────
    # ⭐ this is Mountain Spring Road: tertiary + dirt is rideable, tertiary +
    # asphalt is a highway. The tag exists on 80% of tertiaries.
    if hw in (&quot;tertiary&quot;, &quot;residential&quot;, &quot;service&quot;, &quot;unclassified&quot;, &quot;road&quot;):
        if surface in RIDEABLE_SURFACE:
            return True, &quot;unclassified motorized&quot;
        if surface in PAVED_SURFACE:
            return False, None      # ⛔ the subdivision problem, solved
        if hw == &quot;unclassified&quot;:
            return True, &quot;unclassified unknown&quot;   # as today, on shape
        return False, None          # a residential street with no surface tag
    # ── TRACKS: in on shape, as today, graded where OSM says so ────────
    if hw == &quot;track&quot;:
        if tg.get(&quot;tracktype&quot;):
            return True, &quot;track %s&quot; % tg[&quot;tracktype&quot;]
        if surface in RIDEABLE_SURFACE:
            return True, &quot;unclassified motorized&quot;
        return True, &quot;unclassified unknown&quot;
    # ── PATHS AND CYCLEWAYS: non-motorized unless something says otherwise
    if hw in (&quot;path&quot;, &quot;cycleway&quot;, &quot;bridleway&quot;):
        bike = tg.get(&quot;bicycle&quot;)
        foot = tg.get(&quot;foot&quot;)
        if bike in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;) and foot in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
            return True, &quot;hiking and biking&quot;
        if hw == &quot;cycleway&quot; or bike in (&quot;yes&quot;, &quot;designated&quot;):
            return True, &quot;biking only&quot;
        if hw == &quot;bridleway&quot;:
            return True, &quot;equestrian&quot;
        return True, &quot;hiking only&quot;
    return False, None
def main():
    print(&quot;reading tags from %s ...&quot; % PBF)
    h = Tags()
    h.apply_file(PBF)
    print(&quot;  %d ways in the widened net\n&quot; % len(h.t))
    db = sqlite3.connect(GPKG)
    rows = db.execute(
        &quot;SELECT osm_id, fclass, name FROM gis_osm_roads_free&quot;).fetchall()
    print(&quot;GPKG rows: %d&quot; % len(rows))
    kept = added = dropped = 0
    matched = 0
    types = Counter()
    dropped_by = Counter()
    added_by = Counter()
    dropped_names = []
    added_names = []
    for oid, fclass, name in rows:
        try:
            wid = int(oid)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        tg = h.t.get(wid)
        today = fclass in CURRENT or (fclass or &quot;&quot;).startswith(&quot;track&quot;)
        if tg is None:
            # not in the widened net at all -- only interesting if today took it
            if today:
                dropped += 1
                dropped_by[fclass] += 1
                if name and len(dropped_names) &lt; 15:
                    dropped_names.append(&quot;%s (%s)&quot; % (name, fclass))
            continue
        matched += 1
        inc, typ = classify(tg)
        if inc:
            types[typ] += 1
            if today:
                kept += 1
            else:
                added += 1
                added_by[fclass] += 1
                if name and len(added_names) &lt; 15:
                    added_names.append(&quot;%s (%s, %s)&quot;
                                       % (name, fclass, tg.get(&quot;surface&quot;, &quot;no surface&quot;)))
        elif today:
            dropped += 1
            dropped_by[fclass] += 1
            if name and len(dropped_names) &lt; 15:
                dropped_names.append(&quot;%s (%s, %s)&quot;
                                     % (name, fclass, tg.get(&quot;surface&quot;, &quot;no surface&quot;)))
    total_in = kept + added
    unclass = types[&quot;unclassified unknown&quot;]
    classified = total_in - unclass
    print(&quot;joined on osm_id: %d of %d GPKG rows had PBF tags\n&quot; % (matched, len(rows)))
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(&quot;THE FIVE NUMBERS&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(&quot;  KEPT          %7d   in today&#x27;s filter, rules agree&quot; % kept)
    print(&quot;  ADDED         %7d   rejected today, rideable under the rules&quot; % added)
    print(&quot;  DROPPED       %7d   in today&#x27;s filter, excluded now&quot; % dropped)
    print(&quot;  &quot; + &quot;-&quot; * 60)
    print(&quot;  TOTAL IN      %7d   (today: %d)&quot; % (total_in, kept + dropped))
    print(&quot;  CLASSIFIED    %7d   %.0f%% -- a type from real tags (today: 0)&quot;
          % (classified, 100.0 * classified / max(1, total_in)))
    print(&quot;  UNCLASSIFIED  %7d   %.0f%% -- in on shape, nothing said what it is&quot;
          % (unclass, 100.0 * unclass / max(1, total_in)))
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(&quot;TYPES ASSIGNED&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    for t, n in types.most_common():
        print(&quot;  %-28s %7d   %5.1f%%&quot; % (t, n, 100.0 * n / max(1, total_in)))
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(&quot;DROPPED -- was taken today, excluded by the rules&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    for f, n in dropped_by.most_common(8):
        print(&quot;  %-20s %7d&quot; % (f, n))
    print(&quot;  examples:&quot;)
    for n in dropped_names[:10]:
        print(&quot;     %s&quot; % n)
    print()
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(&quot;ADDED -- rejected today, rideable under the rules&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    for f, n in added_by.most_common(8):
        print(&quot;  %-20s %7d&quot; % (f, n))
    print(&quot;  examples:&quot;)
    for n in added_names[:10]:
        print(&quot;     %s&quot; % n)
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    main()
⭐⭐ THE APPROACH — build alongside, then clear and reimport Utah (2026-08-29)
Fred, closing: "My gut says write the new import process alongside the existing. Clear
the trails DB and reimport Utah when we have finished the new import process. That gives time to
inspect results, develop the filter etc. The launch process will basically duplicate what we have
done — clear the trails and reimport home state."
Why alongside, and not in place
Reason
The existing import keeps working⭐ A rider on the current build is
unaffected while the new path is written. Nothing is half-migrated at any point — the failure mode
that cost most of 08-28.
The switch is one reimport, not a migrationClear the trails, run the new
path, done. No reconciling two vocabularies across 139,688 rows, most of which have no
provenance to reconcile ON.
Utah is the test AND the controlThe only state whose
carto_code is populated, and the state the classification was measured against.
⭐ TIME TO INSPECT BEFORE COMMITTINGThe reimport produces a table that can
be looked at, counted and argued with before the filter is built on top of it. The filter is
stage 3 precisely because it should be designed against real classified data, not against
projections.
⭐ AND THE LAUNCH PROCESS IS THE SAME ACT. Fred: "the launch process will basically
duplicate what we have done — clear the trails and reimport home state."
Which means the Utah reimport is not a throwaway rehearsal. It IS the launch process, run
once by hand first. Whatever is written to reimport Utah becomes what ships — so it is worth
writing as the real thing rather than as a test harness.
⭐ DOES THIS IMPROVE THE DATA? — the aggregate answer
Fred: "I don't care about individual trails, I care about aggregate shapes. What
shape is the data now and what shape is the data when we are finished? Missing cats are a smaller
problem if we omitted identified trails by having a better universe."
TodayAfter
Ways in the trails table87,079125,831 &nbsp;(+44%)
Carrying a type0 &nbsp;(0%)83,916 &nbsp;(67%)
Unknown87,079 &nbsp;(100%)41,915 &nbsp;(33%)
Paved roads wrongly included~4,485 asphalt
unclassified0 — dropped by surface
Rideable ground wrongly excluded48,4910 — added
⭐ AND THE ANSWER TURNS ON FRED'S POINT, not on the classification rate.
33% unknown in a universe 44% larger and no longer full of Main Street is plainly better than
100% unknown in a smaller polluted one.
An unclassified trail is a LABELLING gap — the ground is there, the router can use it,
the rider can ride it, and a later import can fill the label in. A missing trail is a COVERAGE
gap, and nothing downstream can work around it: the planner cannot route on ground it has
never heard of, which is exactly what Mountain Spring Road demonstrated.
⭐ The composition changes character too. 28,090 ways become "unclassified motorized" —
ground a rider can trust, which today is indistinguishable from everything else in a single
undifferentiated bucket.
⭐⭐ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FOR STAGE 2 — two devices, one recipe (2026-08-29)
Fred: "I can put Droid 1 and 2 side by side, auto-build trails in areas and reconcile
the difference in ground and routes suggested. And I can use the recipe over saved routes on both
devices — identical tests with only the trails changed."
⭐ THIS IS WHY THE RECIPE MATTERED. It was built as a rider feature and a debugging tool;
it turns out to be the acceptance test for the entire OSM effort. Identical parameters, one
press each, and the only variable is the trail data underneath.
The setup
DeviceRole
Droid 1 8624SBCEDF00001789⛔ THE CONTROL. Do not clear
it. 89K trails on the old import. It holds the BEFORE, and once cleared the comparison is gone
— there is no way back to the old classification without rebuilding the old import.
Droid 2 24039703201775The new import. Cleared and reloaded
through the new path.
Why this is a real experiment and not a demo
⭐ ONE VARIABLE. The recipe fixes the anchor, the mileage band, the pace, the pins and
the loop answer. Both devices run the same build from the same saved route. Everything except
the trail data is held constant by construction.
⭐ AND THE CACHE FIX IS WHAT MAKES IT TRUSTWORTHY. Before GRAPHCOPY, a
second run in the same area returned different routes because the previous run's pin splits were
still in the cached graph. Any difference measured across devices would have been
uninterpretable — the experiment would have been measuring the cache. That is fixed and
verified.
What each outcome means
ObservationReading
Droid 2 finds routes Droid 1 cannot⭐ The widened net working — ground that
was invisible is now routable. The dirt-tertiary case: Mountain Spring Road and its
kind.
Droid 1 routes down ground Droid 2 refuses⭐ The surface exclusion working
— asphalt unclassified, the subdivision problem.
The shared backbone is identicalThe rules did not disturb the middle. ⚠
Expect this for most mileage; the changes are at the edges.
⛔ Droid 1 finds a route Droid 2 does NOTTHE IMPORTANT CASE. A rule
is dropping ground it should not. This is the one to chase — Bonneville Shoreline Trail and Weaver
Way are already on the list of candidates.
⚠ RUN THE RECIPE TWICE ON EACH DEVICE FIRST. Same device, same recipe,
no restart. If a device does not reproduce its own result, it cannot be compared with the other
one — and that check costs two presses.
⛔⛔ THE SHIP BOUNDARY — stages 1 to 3 go together, or nothing does (2026-08-29)
Fred: "Understand that we cannot test without the filters on both screen panels and
route building. Has to be a complete implementation except for refresh to ship."
⛔ THE STAGES ARE AN ORDER OF WORK, NOT AN ORDER OF RELEASE. Stage 2
alone puts hiking trails, cycleways and footpaths into the trails table — 21,845 paths and
9,595 cycleways in Utah alone — with nothing to keep them off the map or out of the routing
graph. That is strictly worse than today.
What "complete" means here
Must ship togetherWhy
Stage 1 — vetted rules and the classificationNothing downstream works
without a type on the row.
Stage 2 — the new import, ownership at creationProduces the classified
table.
Stage 3 — the filter, on BOTH map panels and in route building⛔ The
thing that makes the widened universe safe. Without it the rider sees hiking trails they did
not ask for and the planner routes a side-by-side down them.
Stage 4 — the refresh cycle. ⛔ Fixed Jan 1 / Jul 1 as of 08-30, was "90-day"; see the 08-30 card in §OSM DATA REFRESH.⭐ The only one that can follow later, and the runway is LONGER under the fixed dates. Fred: "we have 90 days to complete, based on clear and
reimport." The clear-and-reimport at stage 2 starts the clock — the data it produces is
current for 90 days by the very rule stage 4 will enforce, so the refresh cycle cannot be needed
before then. That is not a guess about priority; it is the interval itself.
It changes WHEN data is renewed, not what the data means. A rider on stale-but-correct data is
fine; a rider on unfiltered data is not.
⚠ BOTH PANELS, not one. ConvoyScreen and
ConvoyMapViewerScreen both render convoy_map.html and both draw trails.
A filter on one is a rider seeing different ground depending on which map they opened — and this
project has already been bitten by two implementations of the same idea drifting apart.
⭐ ONE FILTER, THREE CONSUMERS: the two map panels and buildGraph. Per the
standing rule — shared modules, not parallel implementations.
⭐ AND IT IS ALSO WHY THE TEST CANNOT RUN EARLY. The two-device comparison measures
routes suggested. If Droid 2 has no filter, its planner routes over hiking trails and every
difference from Droid 1 is noise. The filter is not the thing being tested — it is a
precondition for the test to mean anything.
⭐ RELEASE STRATEGY — ship route creation, hold the trail work (2026-08-29)
Fred: "We should be anticipating what needs to change in these docs based on what is
currently completed and what needs to change based on route creation. We will need to make a
decision on releasing route creation and holding trail data scrubbing and segmenting to the next
release. The last should be the 90-day update cycle. In the interim we will have users beating on
the route creation."
ReleaseContainsWhy here

table, the recipe rebuild, the narrative in the GPX, the cached-graph fix.
⭐ It is finished and device-proven, and it is the feature testers can exercise
immediately. Holding it back to travel with the trail work would waste the weeks the OSM
stages will take.
the next 2.6Trail data: scrubbing and segmenting. OSM stages 1–3 — the
classification, the new import with ownership at creation, and the filter on both map panels and
in route building.
⛔ These three ship together or not at all — see the ship boundary above. Stage 2 alone
puts hiking trails in the routing graph with nothing to keep them out.
the LAST 2.6The OSM refresh cycle — ⛔ fixed Jan 1 / Jul 1 as of 08-30, not a 90-day rolling timer. Stage 4, and the last thing in 2.6 — after it, 2.7 is the convoy rewrite.
⭐ The runway is LONGER under the fixed dates, not shorter. The clear-and-reimport at stage 2 makes the data current, and the next prompt is the next fixed date rather than 90 days after ship — so the refresh cycle cannot be needed before then. Same argument, more room.
⭐ AND THE INTERIM IS THE POINT, not a gap. Fred: "in the interim we will have users
beating on the route creation." Around 40 beta testers exercising the planner on real ground,
in real areas, while the trail work is built — which surfaces the route-creation faults that a
developer with two devices in one state will never find.
⚠ It also front-loads the feedback that matters for the trail work. A tester reporting
"the planner would not use a road I ride every week" is exactly the Mountain Spring Road case, and
each one is a rule to check before the classification ships.
⚠ ONE THING THE INTERIM CHANGES: testers will build routes on the OLD
trail data, and the trail release will change the ground underneath. Saved routes survive —
they are stored as geometry and referenced by id — but a recipe rebuilt after the trail release
may return different alternatives than it did before. That is correct behaviour and it will
look like a regression unless the release notes say so plainly.
⭐ IN-APP DOCUMENTS — 2.6g requirement (2026-08-29)
Fred: "This next release should incorporate the QuickStart document into assets and
launch QuickStart on any user's new install. Release notes should autolaunch on any update —
bullets referencing the manual, not bible-length instructions."
DocumentBundledShown
QuickStartIn assets/, beside the manual and release
notes⭐ On a NEW INSTALL, automatically. A first-run rider has no idea what the app
expects of them — the QuickStart is the shortest path from installed to riding.
Release notesIn assets/⭐ On any UPDATE,
automatically. Not on every launch — on the launch after a version change.

⚠ The tone rule, and it is a real constraint
Fred: "bullets referencing the manual, not bible-length instructions."
⚠ AN AUTOLAUNCHED DOCUMENT IS AN INTERRUPTION. The rider opened the app
to do something else, and every line they will not read makes the lines they would read less
likely to land. The release notes exist to say what changed and where to read more — the
manual carries the detail, and it is one tap away.
⭐ Which also means the release notes must be WRITTEN as bullets, not as prose that gets
truncated. The 2026-08-29 notes as drafted are close but still run long for an autolaunch — they
want cutting to bullets with manual references before they ship.
⚠ Mechanics to settle
How is "new install" told from "update"? A stored version marker: absent means new
install, different means update, same means neither. One value, and it drives both.
Dismissal. Both should be dismissible and both should stay reachable afterwards —
autolaunch once, available always.
⚠ Do not fire both. A new install is not also an update; showing release notes to
someone who has never used the app describes changes to something they have never seen.
⭐⭐ TOMORROW — the sequence, and why it is this order (2026-08-29 EOD)
Fred's plan for the day: "Take imports to a clean walkaway point with a POC that works
from a data standpoint. Then a blast analysis on what steps must be refreshed or created to
implement our manually proved process. A solid walkaway point where the process has shape and
identity, that we have to code and implement to a design. Then peel away and address manuals and
their roles in the new release, and get route planning shipped."
⭐ POC FIRST, THEN BLAST, THEN DESIGN. Everything useful today came from scripts that ran
in seconds against two files on D:. None needed a build — and one of them was confidently
wrong in a way that would have cost days had it been written in Kotlin first.

00-2026-08-28-OSM — PBF MINING, DESIGN NOTES
The next major piece. Mine the OSM PBF for trail usage values, so the trails table
carries what a way is FOR rather than only its geometry and name.
⛔ IT IS A MIGRATION, NOT A FEATURE. Changing what import produces means every user's
trails must be cleared and rebuilt. It rides on the install/upgrade job — not something a rider
chooses, and not something that can half-apply.
Why it matters
⛔ THIS IS THE FIX FOR THE PRODUCT RISK. Fred, 08-26: "it is a better
tool in the deep wilds than near towns — and most people will test near towns." At
37.8963,−113.659 the engine found sixteen candidate starts and every one was a residential street.
The trails table contains roads and cannot tell them apart.
Usage values are what separates them. Until then the planner is strongest exactly where fewest
riders will try it.
⭐ INCREMENTAL UPDATE, NOT CLEAR-AND-RELOAD — researched 2026-08-29
Fred, 08-29: "I noticed the files were updated 6 hours ago. When engineering the
update process we should ensure it updates existing data and adds new data, so we do not need to
clear and reload to address data issues."
⚠ Geofabrik rebuilds daily. An import that can only clear-and-reload leaves every rider
permanently one full reimport away from current data — and a full reimport is exactly the thing
that cannot be run casually.
What the OSM data model actually guarantees
FactWhat it means here
Every object has a unique 64-bit id and a version that increments on every
edit.⭐ source_unique_id already holds osm_id. The join key
exists.
Deletion is a new version with visible=false, not a removal.
Old versions are never destroyed; a deleted way is detectable rather than merely
absent.
Ids only change if the object TYPE changes — node to way, way to relation.
⭐ For trails, type changes are rare. The id is a reliable key.
Objects also carry timestamp, changeset and user.⚠ Worth checking whether
the Geofabrik PBF carries this metadata — if it does, change detection is a version compare rather
than a geometry hash.
⭐ AND INSTABILITY IS RARE IN PRACTICE. A maintainer running QA across
1,600+ trail relations in the UK and Ireland reports roughly one change per month.
The community view is blunt: "the majority of nodes do not get deleted and replaced."
So an id-keyed incremental update is sound. The exotic cases are worth handling, not
worth designing around.
⛔ THE ONE CASE THAT BITES LINEAR FEATURES: WAY SPLITTING
From the same QA report: "occasionally a cycle route will be split into a few pieces when it
gets unwieldy."
A trail split in three keeps ONE id and gains TWO new ones. The import sees one trail
shrink and two unrelated trails appear — and the rider's notes stay attached to the shrunken
remnant while two thirds of their trail becomes anonymous.
⚠ Detectable: an existing id whose geometry got materially shorter, plus new ids whose
endpoints meet its new ends. Worth flagging rather than silently accepting.
⛔⛔ THE RECOMMENDATION: RE-KEY THE EXTENSION DB TO osm_id
The extension DB is keyed by geom_hash. Geometry changes on every trivial
edit — a mapper straightening one bend rewrites the hash, and every rider note, property and
alias attached to that trail is orphaned. Silently.
⭐ osm_id survives edits BY DESIGN. That is what the version field is for:
the id says WHICH trail, the version says WHICH REVISION. Keying rider data to the geometry means
keying it to something OSM guarantees will change.
⚠ This is the decision the whole OSM effort turns on, and it is bigger than the PBF
mining that raised it. It also answers the open question below: if the extension DB is keyed by
id, mining that alters geometry no longer orphans anything.
⚠ Trails imported from sources with no osm_id still need geom_hash,
so both keys likely coexist — id where there is one, hash where there is not.
The three-way reconcile
for each way in the new PBF, keyed on osm_id:
  not in our table          -> INSERT
  in our table, version up  -> UPDATE geometry and tags in place
                               ⭐ extension rows follow by id, untouched
  in our table, same version-> skip entirely (the common case)
then, for rows we hold that the new PBF does not contain:
  ⚠ DO NOT DELETE ON ABSENCE. A way missing from one extract may be
  outside the new boundary, or the extract may be truncated. Mark it
  absent with a date, and only remove after it has been missing from
  several consecutive imports.
⚠ THE DELETION CASE IS THE HARD ONE and it is worth being conservative
about. Six sources already fail in nine seconds and nobody notices — an import that deletes on
absence would turn a partial download into silent data loss, and it would look exactly like
sparse country.
⚠ To check against the Utah data
QuestionWhy
Does the Geofabrik PBF carry version and timestamp?Decides whether change
detection is a cheap version compare or a geometry hash of every way.
How many of our trails have an osm_id at all?Rows without one
cannot participate in an id-keyed update and still need the hash.
How much actually changes between two daily extracts?⭐ Two PBFs a day
apart answers it directly, and sets the expectation for how often an update is worth
running.
Which of our trails are roads?Fred, 08-28: "why do roads in the trail
network not show as trails — some roads next to them do?" The import IS discriminating
somehow. Two neighbouring roads, one imported and one not, and the difference is the rule the
import actually applies — as opposed to the one we think it does.
⭐ THE TEST DATA EXISTS: D:\Utah_OSM — PBF and GeoPackage, downloaded
08-29. And Utah is the only state whose trail_type is already populated, so it is
both the sample and the control: run the mapping rules against it and compare to what is
already there.
Settled
PointNote
The rebuild mechanism existsClear and reimport is already built and
proven.
The clear covers both databases⭐ Fred, 08-28: the SQL clear runs over
trails AND the trail extension DB. Confirmed, and it matters — see below.
It runs off the install jobUpgrade-time, not rider-initiated.
⚠ Open, for the planning conversation
QuestionWhy it matters
Which values, and are any derivable from what is already imported?A value
that can be computed from existing rows needs no reimport at all.
⛔ Does the geometry change?The extension DB is keyed by
geom_hash. If mining alters what a trail's geometry looks like, every hash
changes and every extension row stops matching anything — rider notes and properties silently
orphaned. Either they are cleared with the trails or they are gone.
What protects a rider mid-trip?An upgrade that clears the trails table
while someone is parked at a trailhead is the worst possible timing.
How long does it take?⚠ Six sources currently fail in nine seconds and
nobody notices. A reimport that fails halfway leaves a partial table that looks like sparse
country.
Does it subsume the tracks work?⭐ buildGraph reads
FROM trails only. If mining fixes what is IN trails, the tracks-fill prototype may be
unnecessary — or may still be needed for ground OSM does not have.

⭐⭐ THE DESIGN GOT SIMPLER EVERY TIME FRED PUSHED ON IT
The morning's design had two screens, a compare tick, a COMPARE button, hide/unhide,
expand/shrink and a sheet. None of it survives. What killed it was Fred's own observation:
"If rows are the universe and columns are ticks, dashes or mileage numbers, three columns
are 90dp and there is nothing to expand."
The width problem that justified all the machinery did not exist. What shipped is one
panel where the column header does three things: its colour ties it to the line, tapping it
shows or hides that line, and the tick beside it marks the route to save.
⛔ And tapping hides the LINE, never the column — Fred: "if we remove it we cannot
put it back." A tap target has to survive its own action.
⭐⭐ THE SORTED ROWS ARE THE BEST IDEA IN THE TABLE. Fred: "total the mileage by
route and list the rows in descending sequence of the totals across all tracks — the most used
trail will appear first... we can spot similar backbones very quickly."
The trails at the top are what these routes are MADE OF; the ones at the bottom are what
DISTINGUISHES them. It does visually what dedupe pass 3 does numerically — the 75%
edge-overlap rule catches duplicates the search PRODUCED; this shows the rider the same thing
about the ones it KEPT.
