⚠ AND ONE FRED WAS RIGHT ABOUT BEFORE I WAS
SAVE SELECTED fetched trail geometry by viewport. Fred, in the morning: "cannot rely on
viewport." I argued it was necessary — buildWktAndBbox does need trail shapes or
routes save as chords between vertices instead of following the switchbacks.
The premise was right and the conclusion was wrong. queryGeomByIds already
existed, and the resume path used it with this comment: "fetch the snap-referenced geometry by
the lineIds the vertices carry (NOT by viewport) so reload draws the snapped shape regardless of
where the map is looking. Fixes resume chords."
⚠ Same bug, already fixed once, in this file. It worked only because zoom 11 happened to
show the whole route.
The lock
Route+ tapped
  → batch exists?  →  the table, FORCED. No way past.
  → otherwise      →  everything as today
⭐ Only batches are forced. A batch is six routes the app made unasked, so it is the
app's mess to clear and a second would be twelve. A hand-drawn draft is one route the rider chose
to start. The lock redirects rather than refuses — the rider is put in front of the thing
in the way, with the tools to clear it.
Resolved = the batch file is DELETED. No history: the saved routes are the record.
SAVE SELECTED — the order is load-bearing
per route:  load → buildWkt → insertRoute → writeRouteNotes → delete draft
then:       delete the unticked drafts
LAST:       delete the batch file
⛔ The batch file goes last because its absence IS "resolved". If it went first and a
promotion then failed, the lock would be clear and the drafts stranded.
⚠ It does not call saveCompleted: that reads routeName from Compose
state and is fire-and-forget, so five would race on RouteManager and the second load would clear
the route the first was saving. Same calls, same order, one sequential coroutine, names as
locals.
⚠ Naming: the rider types an area once and every kept route becomes
Panguitch Mi. 79 Pts. 7. Ticking nothing is legitimate but deletes everything, so it warns
— "If you proceed you must start over" — which is literal, because the recipe lives in the
batch file.

▶▶ 00-STARTHERE — 2026-08-26. READ THIS FIRST. STARTHERE-2026-08-26
⭐⭐⭐ THE ROUTE ENGINE IS REBUILT, DEVICE-PROVEN AND FAST. Measured at
Birch Spring / Pass Creek: 12 trails → 1 network, tested ceiling 4, enrichment to 7 features,
six routes between 79.0 and 80.0 miles against an 80-mile ceiling, in four seconds.
Yesterday the same ground gave one route to Brian Head from an origin 613 ft away down a
single spoke.
Fred, 08-26: "six routes are all different enough to warrant judgement." That
was the target and it is met.
⭐⭐ THE TURNING POINT, AND IT WAS NOT TECHNICAL
Fred, 08-26: "trying to rationalise the old engine with components that were not
built for the problem we were solving was the turning point. Natural resistance to replacing
the familiar with the unknown. But the familiar was a round peg in a square hole."
The greedy was built for "find me a ride somewhere near here." Once the question
became "reach these places, from where I am standing, and show me options", it was the
wrong tool — and no amount of tuning fixes a wrong tool. A whole afternoon went on
adjusting weights on a mechanism that could not answer the question.
⚠ THE RESISTANCE WAS MINE. Fred proposed replacing it early; I kept
proposing patches. Every wrong theory was an attempt to make the familiar thing correct.
⭐ RULE EARNED — it will recur in the convoy rewrite: when the question
changes, check whether the mechanism was built for it BEFORE tuning.
⭐⭐ PROTOTYPE-FIRST — 35 ENGINE REVISIONS IN A DAY
Ten seconds a run instead of thirty minutes a build. And it was not only speed — it was
the freedom to be WRONG. The subset proxy looked obviously correct and was not; the detour
screen measured from the wrong points twice; removing the cap ran forever. Each a ten-second
lesson rather than a wasted evening.
⚠ And the things they caught would otherwise have shipped silently: ride 6 at 79.7 mi
that stopping early discarded, and the 80% edge overlap between rides 4 and 6.
⭐ Carry it forward. The approval panel reads a JSON file — testable against a
hand-written batch with no engine run at all.
THE ALGORITHM, SETTLED
corridor (ceiling/3) → graph → candidate starts within 600 yds, EDGE-SPLIT
  → collapse to one origin per component (alternatives kept)
  → features via spatial grid, on ANY origin's component
  → rider pins as high-value features, split onto their trail
  → distance matrix → out-and-back filter → pairwise table + TESTED ceiling
  → working array: features earn their way in
  → ENRICH the top 20 (rides x features, not combinations)
  → dedupe: same origin+features · any origin · 75% shared trails → six
Every rule and its measurement:
GroupTrack_algorithm_annotated_2026-08-26.html.
⭐ FRED'S IDEAS DID ~94% OF THE PERFORMANCE WORK. The pairwise
table (98% of combinations killed without a tour solve), collapsing origins per
component (13 car parks onto one network were solved 13 times), the spatial grid
(5.8s → 0.1s), and enrich rather than enumerate (best ride 6 → 8 features, every ride
within 5.4 mi of the ceiling). 67.8s → 3.8s with identical results.
⛔ DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED — all measured
The origin was 613 ft away with ONE spoke. Every one of 2,500 restarts began down
it; other directions were structurally excluded. Now 24 ft, 2 spokes, 12 candidate
starts.
Pins snapped up to 6,001 ft, ten collapsing onto four nodes. Now 16–150 ft onto
named trails.
Settlements were scoring. locality 3,271, hamlet 1,220,
suburb 47, farm 21 — 4,559 of 16,992. A locality sits on roads, so
routes followed roads to reach one. Fred: "my route created in towns and
developments."
DONE was hidden when feasibility was unknown — it removed the only way out of the
step. Fred: "if i drop 4 pins i don't want to drop six more to exit."
Split edges drew the parent's whole polyline — both halves carried
e.pts, so a route crossing one emitted it twice and the line ran out and back.
Those were the straight segments near the pins.
⭐ THE THREE PROCESSES — see GroupTrack_process_spec_2026-08-26.html
ProcessOwnsState
1 RequirementsThe guided banner flow: welcome, name and band, staging
point, pins, finish⚠ Old checklist ships. Banner designed and mocked (v11), not

2 GenerationRequest → six ridesBUILT AND
DEVICE-PROVEN.
3 ApprovalSix drawn, legend, narrative, keep/clear⛔ Not

⭐ PROCESS 3 IS STANDALONE. It reads open_batch.json and the
drafts it names and does not care how they were produced — so it opens from Route+
whenever a batch is open, after a crash or days later, and is testable against a hand-written
file.
⭐ THE PANEL IS A LEGEND (Fred). Not a results list — each row is the route name
in the same colour as its line. Tap the name for the narrative; hide/unhide is the
comparison tool ("look at two, look at three"), free and reversible; multi-select
because a rider may keep more than one.
⭐ ONE BATCH AT A TIME, and the lock REDIRECTS rather than refuses. Route+ with an
open batch opens process 3 on that batch. No route activity of any kind — not the planner, not
drawing by hand — until it resolves. Resolved = the file is DELETED; the saved routes
are the record. ⚠ Unlike the import manifests, which are kept because an import can fail
silently; a batch cannot, the rider is standing in front of it.
⭐ PINS ARE SAVED WITH THE FEATURE DATA, marked mine: true, with
moved_ft and onto. The field that decides whether a route is worth
keeping is yours_reached / yours_asked — pins are high-value
features, not a membership rule, and a device run took two of three.

▶▶ 00-STARTHERE — 2026-08-25. READ THIS FIRST. STARTHERE-2026-08-25
Where it stands. Seven commits. The pin plumbing is complete and verified end to

⛔⛔ THE FINDING: RIDER-PLACED POINTS NEVER BECOME GRAPH NODES
A waypoint tapped on a trail is used to centre the corridor box and then discarded.
The ride's origin is whatever pre-existing junction node happens to be nearest —
measured at 600 feet from Fred's trailhead, with no trail in between. The route
visibly starts somewhere the rider did not choose.
Pins behave identically. Ten pins collapsed onto four nodes; one moved
6,001 feet. Three pins sharing a node is why assess() reported
floor=0.0 mi with marginal=0.0 — they are one node.
⭐ FRED'S FRAMING, AND IT IS THE CORRECT ONE. A trailhead sits on a road
with spurs radiating from it like the hub of a spoked wheel. Picking one arbitrary node picks
one spoke — and every one of the 2,500 restarts then starts down that spoke. The other
directions are not under-explored, they are structurally excluded.
This is not a pin-feature bug. It is the correctness of the whole engine.
"Find me a ride in this area" has always meant "find me a ride from one arbitrarily chosen
spoke."
⚠⚠ IT WAS OBSERVED WEEKS AGO AND EXPLAINED AWAY
Fred raised that rides radiated in one direction. The answer given was that POI
distribution dictated it. That explanation was plausible, unfalsifiable without
instrumentation, and wrong — and it stopped the investigation. The measurement that
found the real cause took twenty minutes.
THE RULE THIS EARNS: when the person who uses the app says something looks wrong,
the answer is a measurement, not an explanation.
🔴 TOMORROW — the fix, in order
Prototype the edge split in Python against D:\nav_test\spatial_after.db
at Panguitch. No Kotlin until proven. Find the nearest EDGE, not the nearest node;
project the point onto it; split A→B into A→P and P→B with miles divided at the projection;
insert P with the rider's coordinates; rewire adjacency; add P to
mainComponent if A or B is in it.
Apply it to the trailhead first. The origin matters more than the pins. With the
waypoint as a real node, all spokes are adjacent to the origin.
Then the pins. Ten pins become ten destinations where they were dropped.
Cap E's insertion. assess() enforces SNAP_POINT_MI = 0.5;
E has no cap at all and silently accepts a 6,001 ft pin. Two snap policies for the same
pin; they must agree.
⭐ THE SUCCESS TEST, in Fred's words: "i would be happy to see some
radiation of direction. more than one spoke ridden." Four routes fanning out from the hub
instead of stacking down one spoke — visible on the map in one run, no instrumentation
needed.
⚠ Watch once the origin is fixed: PENALTY = 2.2 is applied to route 1's
edges before route 2 is built. If the hub's own road is on route 1, penalising it pushes route
2 away from the hub rather than down a different spoke.

⭐⭐ RELEASE-NOTE FRAMING — the standard, Fred 08-25
Every feature entry has three parts, in this order:
Here is the feature — plainly, in a sentence.
What this feature means to you — why a rider should care.
How I used this feature — the steps, linking into the manual.
⭐ PART 2 IS THE FILTER, and it is the part that was missing. If you cannot
write what a change means to a rider, it does not belong in the release notes — it is
internal work. Half of what was drafted on 08-25 failed this test: the GPX entry said the fix
happened but never said "files other riders send you now work when you tap them", and the
trail-clear entry described a marker in a folder, which is our problem and not theirs.
⚠ Part 3 has a prerequisite: the manual needs id= anchors on its sections
before "how I used it" has anywhere to point. That is a documentation pass with no app
dependency and it unblocks every link from every document. Entries currently carry a visible
link pending anchors marker so the debt is seen rather than silently absent.
⭐ THE MANUAL PROBLEM IS ACCESS, NOT CONTENT (Fred 08-25)
"The best manual solution is to make it more accessible." Three doors, all
document-to-document links between files already bundled in the APK — no Kotlin, no help
stack:
From the QuickStart — a new rider finishing setup is exactly who needs the walkthrough
next
From the release notes — "here is what is new" links straight to "here is how to use
it"
Consistently — one anchor scheme, so a link means the same thing wherever it
appears
⚠ "Cookbook instructions relevant to the task" is the harder half. The manual is
organised by screen; a cookbook is organised by what you are trying to do. Those are
different cuts. Likely a section of task recipes that link into the screen documentation, rather
than a reorganisation of it.
⭐ DOC DELIVERY — 2.6h scope, decided 08-25
Documents ship inside the APK, so a rider always holds the set matching their build.
"This release" is whatever they are running; no online version, no mismatch possible.
QuickStart = a new rider on a first install. A summary of how things work
right now — installing, permissions, radio, getting trails on the map. Not
additive: every item is either true today or removed. Launches by itself on a new
install.
Release notes = riders who already have GroupTrack. What is new in this
release and how to use it. Opens after an update. Structure: current release open at
the top with Known Issues dated to this release, then Release history as a closed
twistie, one nested twistie per release showing number and date.
Manual = the walkthrough. Notes point at manual pages for anything needing more than
a paragraph.
⚠ Known Issues are frozen at build time because the doc ships with the APK — so each
release's list must be correct when it is built, not refreshed later.
⚠ Document revisions are labelled — RELNOTES-2.6h-r1,
QUICKSTART-2.6h-r1 — so a revision within a release is identifiable.
⛔ CONTEXTUAL HELP IS 2.7, NOT 2.6h. Linking every panel to its manual page
lands with the convoy rewrite / Meshtastic plugin work, where the panel structure is
being reorganised anyway. Design recorded in
GroupTrack_design_contextual_help_2026-08-25.html: a help stack (push on
open, pop by id — never removeLast(), panels do not close in the order they
opened), DisposableEffect so a panel cannot leak an id, dotted ids named for the
function not the label, anchor-jump into the bundled manual, and a build-time guard
that fails the build when a push has no anchor. ⭐ Adding id= anchors to the
manual is worth doing early — no app dependency.
⚠ STAGING FILTER — build it now, leave it open (Fred, 08-25)
A routable flag (column or view) deciding which trails the graph is built
from. Today it selects everything. When classification lands it is populated from the
carto value and the filter starts meaning something; buildGraph reads the same
thing either way and never changes again.
⭐ It must start permissive. A filter in place and unused is safe; a filter in place
and guessing is TRAILFILTER-K again — trails silently dropped on a value nobody audited.
Open: column on trails vs side table keyed on geom_hash, and whether
routable differs from visible.

⛔ WHY THE TAP DID NOT REACH KOTLIN — three wrong theories, recorded
"The marker consumes the click." NO. There is no stopPropagation on
that path — the tap falls through to map.on('click') and places a route vertex.
Deliberate: ROUTEFALLTHROUGH-2026-07-30.
"Popups bound after setRouteMode(true) escape suppression." NO.

⛔⛔ THE ORPHAN BUG — 303,585 rows
The trails clear removed 86,969 trails and 303,585 trail_properties rows. Fred
called it: "the Utah identifiers are in the trails extension db which we did not
clear."
⚠ geom_hash is the IDENTITY; trail_id is the KEY. trail_properties
joins on trail_id, a UUID minted at insert. Delete the trails and those rows
join to nothing. And the damage was active: TrailImporter:461 inserts
with INSERT OR IGNORE on (source_id, source_unique_id), so a stale
row KEPT THE SLOT and the re-imported trail got no properties, with nothing reporting an
error. Ledger: inserted=30 before, inserted=86923 after.
⚠⚠ METHOD — seven guard failures, one root cause
Every failed patch guard today had the expected NUMBER written from what the edit was
MEANT to do rather than derived from what it does. TARGETED RIDE DURATION also
in a comment; "trailhead" already in WAYPOINT_TYPES;
ROUTEFALLTHROUGH in three handlers; weight(1f)) { three others
already present; braces asserted balanced on a file that was 952/951 before the patch.
⭐⭐ STANDING FIX, adopted from patch E onward: DERIVE the expected count. Count
the token in the OLD blocks and the NEW blocks, compute before − removed + added.
It caught a correct edit in patch I where a comment mentioned .width(248.dp)
while replacing it. Never write an expected count by hand.
And the bracket invariant is "UNCHANGED", not "balanced" — asserting a property the
file never had cost a cycle.
⭐ MEASURED — rider points, the base cost dominates
3 points → 93.5 mi. 5 → 97.3. 7 → 110.6. 10 → 139.0. Three points already blow an
80-mile ceiling, and seven more cost only 45 miles. Getting into the region costs ~60;
the points are nearly free once there. Two points two miles apart cost 32.9 network miles.
A rider cannot predict this from a map — hence live feedback while pins are dropped.
Dead-end spurs: 1,388 on the main component, only 38 carry a feature (2.7%). A
"short AND featureless" cut at 300 yd removes 606 and loses none worth riding. Length alone
is the wrong test.
⭐ OSM ACCESS TAGS DO NOT EXIST IN WHAT WE IMPORT
PRAGMA on both .gpkg extracts: ten columns on the roads layer, no access
field of any kind. Geofabrik's GeoPackage is shapefile-derived and flattens OSM's tag
model — ohv, motor_vehicle, access,
4wd_only all dropped at export. fclass answers by SHAPE, not by
permission.
⭐ THE PBF INSIGHT. Fred: "isn't the route id the same as the protobuf file?
Can't we just mine the attributes?" YES — source_unique_id already holds
osm_id, so the PBF is read for id and tags only and geometry keeps coming
from the GeoPackage. That removes node resolution entirely. Mapping is ONE PREPROCESS at
import, carried through C3 in the same insert — no update pass, no drift.
See GroupTrack_design_trail_classification_2026-08-24.html.

⭐⭐ THE SHAPE THAT MADE IT SMALL (Fred, 08-21)
"The bbox is the decider; where it comes from is the driver." State and area share one
pipeline — the state run's bbox is the state's corners, the area run's is the drawn box. Catalog
resolution, the manifest builder, the execution loop and the recap counters are all shared and
unmodified.
"The existing progress and completion IS the import process. Everything else is serving it.
Building the JSON, no work." Selection UI decides a bbox and writes a manifest; it does no
work. That is why the multi-state loop is not a new loop — the builder emits one
geofabrik_area row per state and the existing source loop simply sees N pending rows.
⭐ Consequence worth keeping: granular restart recovery is now latent. The whole plan —
every source, and the bbox that defines the work — is written down before any of it runs. A drawn
box is ephemeral; area.bbox survives the app dying. Nothing has to be reconstructed.

⚠ BBOX STATE SELECTION IS OVER-INCLUSIVE — decided, not built
The defect, measured: findByBbox tests the drawn box against each state's
RECTANGLE. California's reaches east to -114.13; the box's west edge was
-114.573, so California was selected, downloaded (600 MB+), extracted, imported
ZERO trails, and swept. A rectangle tested against a rectangle can only ever be a
rectangle.
⭐⭐ DECISION (Fred 08-21): the deselect checkbox is the fix, on the bbox confirmation
screen that the 08-18 mockup already specifies. Cheap, no network dependency, no tuning parameter,
no failure modes — and honest: the rider knows the ground, the app does not.
Panel must EXPLAIN the mechanism, not just offer the control (Fred). Draft wording:
"Some states may not have trails in your area. States are matched using a rectangle around each
state, and those rectangles overlap. A state can be listed here without reaching into the area you
drew. If you know a state isn't part of your ride, uncheck it — you'll skip its download."
⚠ Keep "bounding box" out of rider-facing text; audience is riders 65–75.
Default ALL CHECKED. Over-inclusion costs time; under-inclusion costs coverage the rider
does not discover until they are out there.
Show the download size per state if available — that is what makes the choice real.
💡 Considered and NOT chosen: perimeter geocoding. Sample the box edge every ~10 mi,
reverse-geocode each point, deselect any bbox-selected state whose name never appears. Fred's
insight: a state cannot be inside the box without crossing its edge, so perimeter sampling is
complete for a rectangle and interior points add nothing. Measured on the real box: 28 sample
points, 11 of them west of California's bbox edge. Written and parked as
resolveStatesByPerimeter_2026-08-21.kt. More correct in principle; costs a network
round trip, a tuning parameter and three failure modes to buy what a checkbox does for free.
⚠ Structure if ever revived: bbox proposes, perimeter DESELECTS — never let the geocoder add,
and deselect nothing when lookups fail.

Architecture Decisions (08-20)
Manifest check for fresh install — hasCompletedImport() scans Documents/GroupTrack/imports/ for completed JSON. Does NOT query the DB (may not exist on fresh install).
Geocoder for GPS detection — bbox matching fails at state borders. Geocoder returns actual state name. Bbox is fallback.
OsmImportLedger.create() MUST be called before setPendingImport() — the ledger silently returns null if no file exists.
Geofabrik -latest- URLs return 302 redirects to dated files — HttpURLConnection needs explicit redirect following.
Download progress requires MutableStateFlow not plain var for Compose visibility across threads.
collectAsState() must be hoisted above LazyColumn items block.
Gate uses manifest check (hasCompletedImport) not DB query — DB may not exist on fresh install. ⛔ SUPERSEDED 08-21 — see 00-GATE-FINAL → THE STARTUP JOB. The check is now spatial DB file exists → trail count &gt; 0; the file-existence step is what makes it safe on a fresh install, and it must not OPEN the DB.

Patch Script Lessons Banked
Always use dated filenames for deliverables to avoid download overwrite confusion.
Python \u2630 in triple-quoted strings is the glyph, not the escape — double the backslash
when anchoring on literal escape text in the file.
contentColor on a Surface ≠ the text colour.
Verify assets INSIDE the AAB before uploading: unzip -p &lt;aab&gt; base/assets/&lt;file&gt; | grep -c.
⛔⛔ 00-SAVEPATHS (08-17) — DISCARD WAS NEVER DIVERGED. SAVE WAS.
⭐⭐⭐ Fred: "the issue was standardizing the discard function. i have seen
no divergence in discard. our divergence is in save correct?" — and the code agrees.
The two genuine discard sites, onExit (~1646) and the in-progress dialog (~1775),
both do all five operations, identically. No drift. The entire "six variants of discard"
framing in 00-DISCARD-DESIGN was built on a survey table that counted SAVE sites and
LIST-MANAGEMENT sites as discard variants.
SiteWhat it actually is
~1646 onExitdiscard ✅ all five
~1775 dialogdiscard ✅ all five
~1834 resolverpresents the discard CHOICE when an in-progress file is found on entry — nothing loaded yet, so its omissions are correct
~1923 pickerthe In-Progress list — a reminder shown when more than one autosave exists. "Not part of the discard process." Pure list management; nothing to tear down
~1539 saveCompletednot a discard
~1717 save-as-WIP"not a discard process, it is what we do as an alternative" — and it RENAMES rather than deletes, so it correctly has no deleteDraft
⭐ And the sixth operation was never a discard concern at all. Fred: "it just
does not belong in the discard function." setRouteMode is ambient exit behaviour
that got copied into each site because it sat nearby. Ending a Route+ session closes the draw panel
and turns draw mode off; re-entering is an explicit act.
⚠ METHOD NOTE, worth more than the fix. Claude built an elaborate six-variant
consolidation plan from a grep table, and Fred dismantled it by asking what each site actually IS.
The tell was that the "variants" needed increasingly baroque justification to remain variants.
The real defect was in the code nobody had looked at, because the 08-13 survey filed it under a
different word and moved on.
What the save paths actually had wrong — all three fixed today
1. saveCompleted violated a DOCUMENTED invariant.
RouteDraftStore.kt:15 states a route lives as a draft JSON or a spatial-DB row,
never both; ConvoyRouteToolbar.kt:176 documents this path as "insertRoute (DB
row) + delete draft if any [graduation]". The code had insertRoute and
no deleteDraft, no draftListTick++ — so a graduated route stayed in
route_drafts/ and in the picker, and reopening that stale draft forked it into two
diverging versions. Fixed a17b10fda: deletes both routeName and
UNNAMED, because routeName can be blank while the autosave file exists
(insertRoute substitutes a generated name for the DB row only), and
deleteDraft returns true for an absent file so a miss is free.
2. Save-as-WIP never bumped draftListTick, and the list is built in
remember(draftListTick) — so a freshly saved draft did not appear until the user left
the map and returned, rebuilding the screen. Found on device by Fred. Fixed f71e2ddc9.
⚠ Correctly NO deleteDraft there — it is a rename.
⚠ 3. There is a SECOND, near-identical saveCompleted at
ConvoyScreen.kt:1771, carrying the same "one proven completed-save path"
comment. Route+ is PLANNER-ONLY, so it is unreachable dead code — deliberately not touched
(convoy frozen). ⭐ The two copies had ALREADY drifted: the planner one sets
addPointMode = false, the convoy one does not. A comment asserting singularity
stopped being true the moment the second copy was made. Remove the dead copy when the freeze
lifts.
⚠⚠ The radio-meter crash — and a guard that was never reached
The vertical interval slider in GroupHud (ConvoyScreen.kt ~2496, "5s"
above / "INT" below, rotated -90°) calls setGpsInterval →
channelViewModel.setConfig. With no radio the binder throws
RemoteException: Not connected to radio on the main thread and the app dies.
⛔ setGpsInterval ALREADY wrapped that call in try/catch, logging
"Failed to set GPS interval" — and the app still died. setConfig RETURNS before the
binder throws, so the exception fires outside the try block. This is why the fix is to not RENDER
the control rather than to test before calling it. Second instance in two days of a guard that
reads correct and is never reached (see 00-GATE-FINAL's latch correction). ⭐ When a guard exists
and the failure happens anyway, the guard is not being reached — check that before adding
another.
Fix: render the slider only when state.nodes.size > 1. state is
already a GroupHud parameter — no signature change, no call-site edit, no new
observation, one conditional in a frozen file. It also matches the usefulness rule: "you're not
adjusting broadcast times in a ride with one radio." ⚠ Node count INFERS radio presence rather
than testing it; the direct signal is ConvoyViewModel.myNodeInfo != null (line 62, what
ConvoyApplyRadioScreen uses). simulationMode exists, so if convoy state is
ever populated without a radio, add a check inside setGpsInterval too.
⚠ R8-MINIFIED STACKS ARE ACTIVELY MISLEADING. That trace attributed frames to
coil3.RealImageLoader, okhttp3.Cache, androidx.room.RoomRawQuery
and UsbKt — all nonsense. Trust only frames naming real behaviour
(MeshService.setConfig, SliderState.dispatchRawDelta); file attribution is
a hint, not a fact — it sent Claude to the wrong file twice. ⭐ Find a UI element by its LABEL:
greps for "meter", "broadcast" and "Slider" all missed it; grep -n '"INT"' found it in
one shot.
🗺 00-TRAILDATA (08-17) — WHAT THE TRAIL DATA ACTUALLY CONTAINS, AND WHAT THE SUGGESTER CAN CLAIM
⭐ Full detail — 11 sections, every number measured off utah.gpkg and the

⛔⛔ THE DAY'S HEADLINE: a plain uninstall/reinstall was deleting both databases,
and had been all along.
Three wipes in about twelve hours — 08-15 23:22, 08-16 07:10, 08-16 08:15 — all one defect.
The v3 delete-gate in SpatialDbManager.init() was gated on a marker held in
SharedPreferences (app-private), while the databases it deletes live in
Documents/GroupTrack/ (public). An uninstall wipes the marker and not the data, so
every reinstall read marker was 0, concluded "pre-v3", and deleted
grouptrack_spatial.db + grouptrack_data.db. Full detail, the fix and the
certification: 00-MARKER-LIFETIME.
⭐ AutoResyncHost's conviction is WITHDRAWN. Killing it on 08-15 was correct —
it was a vestigial startup migration opening the DB pre-authority — but it did not cause these
wipes, and 08-15's diagnosis credited it with the whole thing.
METHOD, banked today:
The reinstall test is the one that found it. A clear-cache test had already passed
byte-identical and would have been accepted as proof the install work was done. Fred pushed for the
uninstall/reinstall anyway. The cheaper test passing is not evidence the expensive one will.
The logcat capture is what made it a five-minute diagnosis instead of another evening —
353,608 lines, grabbed before the buffer rolled, and the answer was three I/ lines in it.
A guard and the thing it guards must share a lifetime. App-private state protecting
public-storage data is the defect, and it reads as correct in review because both halves are
individually sensible. Look for this shape wherever a flag, marker or receipt decides whether to touch
data that outlives the flag.
Instrumentation earned its keep, twice. The gate emitted nothing, so working out what it had
concluded meant inferring from platform quota noise around the canary file. One log line per evaluation
turned the next question from a theory into a reading — and immediately disproved the theory we had
just built a fix around (see 00-GATE-FINAL).
A multi-line anchor built from sed output missed a blank line and a patch aborted
cleanly at anchor 6 of 6, no write, tree clean. cat -A showed it in one command. The rule
holds: cat -A when an anchor spans lines.

⛔⛔⛔ 00-MARKER-LIFETIME (08-16) — A PLAIN REINSTALL WAS DELETING BOTH DATABASES. FOUND, FIXED, CERTIFIED.
The defect
SpatialDbManager.init() carries a one-time "regenerate-not-migrate" delete gate. Its own
comment stated the assumption that broke it: "DBs live in PUBLIC storage and survive uninstall/clear-data,
so this in-app delete is the SOLE clearing mechanism." True — but the marker gating it was
db_schema_marker in SharedPreferences, which is app-private and does not
survive an uninstall. The gate and the thing it gated had different lifetimes. "Fires exactly once
per upgrade" was really "fires once per install."
08:15:02.463  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: delete grouptrack_spatial.db = true
08:15:02.503  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: delete grouptrack_data.db = true
08:15:02.514  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: spatial-clean=true extension-clean=true (marker was 0)
08:15:02.515  SpatialDbMgr: DB v3 migration: marker set to 3; DBs will rebuild from v3 assets
08:15:02.978  SpatialDbMgr: Spatial DB: 0 trails, 0 tracks, 0 waypoints, 0 routes
⭐ marker was 0 is the whole story. Not a failed open, not an authority problem —
the app deliberately deleted the data because it could not tell "never migrated" from "migrated, then
reinstalled." The authority canary ran at 08:15:02.123, 340 ms BEFORE the deletion, and passed.
The gate worked. This was never an authority bug.
⚠ This is the inverted form of the guard specced after 08-01: marker absent + external DB
present = fresh install over existing data → STOP. The marker was designed as a stop condition and
implemented as a delete trigger.
The fix — two commits, two independent halves
233e61e50 — marker moves to a FILE, .db_schema_version, beside the
databases so its lifetime matches theirs. Read order is file → legacy prefs → 0; the prefs
fallback carries existing installs across the changeover, without which this fix would itself have wiped
every current install exactly once. Plus a row-count guard: populated databases mean the install has
already been through the migration whatever the marker says, so it stamps and skips. A count that cannot be
taken (the SELinux ioctl denial on the FUSE-mounted .db is routine) returns −1 and is treated
as populated — refuse to delete on uncertainty.
c503b3247 — stamp-if-missing. Caught on device, not in review: an install whose
marker came from the legacy prefs value reached neither of the two branches that write the file, so
the file was never laid down at all and the install stayed protected by app-private state — the exact
mismatch the whole fix exists to remove. Now: marker resolved and current but file absent → write it.
Certification (Droid 2, 08-16)
Install over live data → marker file appears containing 3; sizes unchanged.
Uninstall → marker file survives in Documents/; prefs gone with the package.
Reinstall → log shows no migration block at all, and
Spatial DB: 152200 trails, 88 tracks, 559 waypoints. Sizes byte-identical.
⭐ Note what that proves: not the row guard catching a miss, but the marker being read straight
from public storage so the gate never armed. Belt and braces both verified independently.
Consequences to carry
THE 08-12 CLEAR-CACHE PROHIBITION IS RETIRED. Clear-cache on live data left both DBs
byte-identical and mesh setup values intact; no state restore fired, no install questionnaire.
⚠ Scope of the proof: that run had no UID change and no named-track import in flight.
⭐ Consequence: "clear the WebView cache to fix a stale bundled asset" is an available remedy again.
REFUSE-TO-CREATE (00-REFUSE) is now load-bearing, not aspirational. Today's fix closes
this trigger. A DB open that refuses to CREATE where a file should already exist is what turns the NEXT
unknown trigger into a loud error instead of silent loss. There is no backup and the map DBs are 50–60 GB.
On today's evidence it is arguably promotable into 2.6f.
Signature worth reading instantly: maps survive + artifacts vanish = a create-if-missing DB
overwrite, NOT an authority failure. .mbtiles never go through this path, so their survival
proves nothing about correctness — and a UID that could not read the DBs could not read the tiles either.
Empty-schema fingerprint: grouptrack_data.db ≈ 208,896 B, grouptrack_spatial.db
≈ 118,784 B.
Recovery profile, measured: trails re-import from OSM, tracks resync from the track directory,
waypoints likewise — full rebuild ≈ 1 hour. Graduated routes are the only unrecoverable class
(see 00-DISCARD-DESIGN). Maps are never lost.
✅ 00-GATE-FINAL (08-16, UPDATED 08-21) — THE AUTHORITY GATE: SETTLED BEHAVIOUR, THE LATCH CORRECTION, AND THE STARTUP JOB (designed 08-21, NOT BUILT)
Behaviour as shipped — all three paths device-verified
SituationWhat happens
Authority already real on the FIRST evaluation of the sessionNo gate at all — straight to Convoy. Nothing was just granted, so there is nothing to settle.
State changed to Granted DURING the session (returned from settings)Continue barrier retained — the tap lets the grant land before the DB opens. This is the flash-past race and it is still real.
Went to settings, came back WITHOUT granting all-filesStorageDeclined. States the app will not open without it, and that exiting is safe. Buttons: Try again / Exit. No proceed door.
Background location not grantedAdvisory. Skip for now proceeds. Deliberately NOT remembered — the prompt recurs every launch.
Why no proceed door on storage (Fred, 08-16): "the app is unusable without that authority,
period" and "cancel is the option that should be taken — they can choose not to use the app."
Claude had proposed a proceed-at-your-own-risk path and then argued against it: without refuse-to-create,
proceeding means silently destroying data, described to the user as a risk they cannot evaluate, because
the failure looks like "no trails" rather than "your data was overwritten." Settled: no third door. The
screen also states that exiting changes nothing — which is accurate, because the gate halts before
any database is opened or created.
Why background location IS skippable and IS repeated (Fred): "background authority is not
destructive — it reduces functionality and can be quickly changed." And the repetition is deliberate:
"the reminder is fine, it warns of degradation when recording a track with an app that goes to
sleep." A rider who skipped three weeks ago will not remember before a ride that their track dies when
the screen sleeps.
⚠⚠ THE DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION — record this, not the first story
Symptom: grant all-files, return, and the screen stayed on StorageDeclined; a
force-close and relaunch then passed immediately.
Claude's theory: a settle race — the probe taken the instant the user returns reads "not granted"
because the grant has not landed yet. A five-attempt / 400 ms retry loop was built on that theory.
The logs disproved it the moment they existed. Every retry read
realStorage=false all the way through attempt 4, and the successful grant passed on
attempt 0. The retries never once rescued a grant.
The real defect: LifecycleResumeEffect(Unit) evaluated once on resume and
latched the result. With settingsVisited set, a negative read became
StorageDeclined and nothing re-evaluated — the user who had just granted access was
stranded on a screen saying the app would not open. Latched state, not a timing race. The fix that
mattered was re-evaluating on each resume; the retry loop is harmless insurance.
⭐ The general lesson: a fix built on an unverified theory can pass its test for a reason
unrelated to the theory. The instrumentation that made this visible was added in the same patch — without
it this would have gone into the release recorded as a race condition that never existed.
Also fixed: Exit was a dead button
onExit was bound to navController?.popBackStack() in
ConvoyNavigation.kt — but the gate is the nav START destination, so there is nothing
beneath it, the call returns false and no-ops. A dead button on the one screen that tells the user the app
will not open. Now finishes the hosting activity: exiting from the start destination means leaving the app,
which is the stated intent.
Gate logging (new): tag ConvoyGate, one line per evaluation —
realStorage=, background=, chosen state, attempt index.
adb -s &lt;serial&gt; logcat -s ConvoyGate. ⚠ StorageManager /
MediaProvider "Failed to update quota type for .authority_probe" is noise —
platform bookkeeping reacting to a file created and deleted within milliseconds. It appears on launches
that pass cleanly and open 152,200 trails.
⭐⭐ THE STARTUP JOB (settled with Fred 08-21 — DESIGNED, NOT BUILT). GATEJOB-2026-08-21
⛔ THIS SUPERSEDES grouptrack_design_unified_import_2026-08-20.html §8 (gate
integration) and the Recovery on App Restart half of §7A. The rest of that document — the
upsert rules, source model, two entry points, manifest shape — is unchanged and still governing. The
design lives HERE, in the checklist, not in a parallel design doc: design in flight expands in place,
and a reader who finds §8 first must not get the superseded reasoning without the correction.
ONE JOB, TWO THINGS, before the rider reaches any map:
Resolve every manifest in imports/ — completed swept to history, incomplete
stamped killed and swept to history. Fred: "completed is swept, incomplete is killed on
startup. Period."
Decide whether the rider needs trail data — and if so, hand off to the Home State picker.
Afterwards imports/ is empty and the rider is either on the Ride Map or in the
picker. There is no third state.
The sweep
ConditionAction
Every source section carries a countLeave process_state as written → move to history
Any source section carries no countStamp process_state = "killed" + killed_at → move to history
⭐ ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: stamp first, then move. Same reason
OsmImportLedger.archiveLedger() renames before discardState() sweeps. Stamp
fails → nothing moved, retried next launch. Move fails after a good stamp → a marked file sits in
imports/, visible and recoverable. The state to avoid is a file in history nobody
stamped, because then killed must be inferred rather than read.
⚠ "Has a count" must tolerate pre-08-21 manifests. The 08-20 NH manifest carries
imported per source but none of the five recap counters and no manifest_id.
Absent fields mean OLD, not broken. If the test requires the new fields, a device holding
43,348 records reads as never-imported and gets sent to the picker.
⚠ The sweep must never touch a live manifest. It would archive the controller's own file
out from under a running import. The ordering that prevents it is the slot: inside the authority
task, before anything can launch an import. Do not call the sweep from anywhere else.
⭐ The one-time cleanup is the same code — both droids hold several completed 08-20
manifests in imports/; first launch after this ships sweeps them. No migration.
The zero-data check — replaces §8's condition
Two tests, in order, both misses landing on Home State (Fred 08-21):
Spatial DB file exists? No → Home State setup.
Exists and holds zero trails? Yes → Home State setup.
Otherwise → straight through to the Ride Map.
⛔⛔ THE FILE CHECK MUST NOT OPEN THE DATABASE. Refuse-to-create is still unbuilt and the
gate halts before any DB opens by design — that ordering is what makes the declined path's "exiting
is safe, nothing on your device changes" promise true. A create-if-missing open in front of that
screen is the 08-01 mechanism: an empty schema written over real data. The count runs only once
the file is known to exist.
Query failure falls through to the map. Fred: "query has to be successful to request home
state add." Locked/mid-write/unreadable → proceed; the panel remains available at any time. The
consequence of being wrong here is a redundant import, not data loss.
⚠ This supersedes the 08-20 architecture note "Gate uses manifest check
(hasCompletedImport) not DB query" and §8's trails.count == 0 AND waypoints.count
== 0. Waypoints are not the signal — a rider can hold waypoints with no trails — and the
file-existence step is what keeps the check safe when no DB exists at all.
Where it lives
Inside the authority task. Not the nav handoff, not ConvoyScreen. The gate is
already a state machine: evaluateState() at
ConvoyAuthorityGateScreenV2.kt:143 resolves a state, :353 renders Granted.
The zero-data condition is a new state in that same structure, rendered with the picker as its
resolution. Slot confirmed by the 08-16 ordering finding: after the authority gate, before
Convoy — which the gate already owns as the nav start destination, so no navigation change.
⛔ CONVOY IS FROZEN — ConvoyScreen.kt IS NOT TOUCHED. Fred 08-21: "too many
competing threads." Nothing here needs that file.
⚠ Do not disturb the three certified paths above: clean pass renders no gate at all; the
Continue settle-barrier survives only for the state-changed-during-session path
(passedOnEntry at :169); StorageDeclined has no proceed
door. The new state is additive — a branch beside them, not a modification of them.

🗣 00-DISCARD-DESIGN (08-16) — THE FIVE-PLUS-ONE BOUNDARY. DESIGN SETTLED, NOT BUILT. (2.6g)
⛔ THE DIAGNOSIS (Fred): "that tangle is what caused unpredictable results — 6
versions of discard all mixing and matching the 6 functions."
Six sites, six independently-assembled combinations of the same operations. Each looked reasonable
alone, so every fix was site-local and the next path exhibited a different variant. The bug was the
ABSENCE of the module; site-local fixes kept producing new variants. The tell: each fix works and the
next report describes different behaviour. This is worse than literal copy-paste — literal copies at
least fail identically.
⛔⛔ And some sites are genuinely WRONG, not merely different (Fred): they did not
remove the in-memory data or the JSON, and "those items are all joined." The JSON on disk, the
in-memory route and the drawn canvas are three representations of one thing. A site that updates a
subset leaves them disagreeing, and the next operation reads whichever it happens to consult — state
divergence. That is why the "phantom draft" looked recreated: it never left memory.
⭐ VISIBLE SYMPTOM, now a signature: the route reappears when the next vertex is dropped. Memory
was never cleared, so the append redraws it with the new vertex attached. The divergence is created at
discard and revealed later — which is why it resisted attribution. It points straight at the site; no
bisecting needed.
The boundary, as Fred specified it — FIVE in the module, ONE owned by the caller
MODULE (unconditional, every path):
  1. clearRoute()
  2. deleteDraft(name)
  3. JS clearBuildLine()
  4. addPointMode = false
  5. draftListTick++
CALLER:
  6. setRouteMode(...)
Fred: "route mode is a function of the process discard is in — does it stay in the app, in which case
draw mode stays active, or does it end the route draw session." Only the caller knows the destination.
⭐ This makes the module take no flags and no exit-vs-stay parameter, and it makes the
audit mechanical: any site doing fewer than all five is a bug, full stop. A missing
setRouteMode is not automatically a bug — it depends on where the user is going.
Previously those two questions were tangled, which is why the 08-13 survey could only mark the resolver
site "missing clearRoute + JS + arm flags" without knowing which absences mattered.
⭐⭐ It is TWO operations, not one: discard and save
Both END a route session; they differ only in what happens to the draft first (delete vs persist).
Consequence: the two SAVE sites (~1539 SAVE-as-completed, ~1717 SAVE-as-WIP) were filed in the 08-13
survey as "not discards" and were therefore never audited for teardown completeness. Under this
factoring they are the same shape and must be checked with the rest. If any save path leaves arm flags set
or the build line drawn, that is the same class of bug — just filed under a different word.
The six sites to classify by destination (ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt, ⚠ re-grep line
numbers, they drift): ~1646 onExit (fixed 08-13, the archetype) · ~1775 "Delete in-progress"
dialog · ~1834 resolver Discard · ~1923 picker Delete · ~1539 SAVE-completed · ~1717 SAVE-WIP.
⚠ No STUB: markers were ever placed — Phase 1 of the 08-13 stub plan never ran
(08-15 went to the authority gate instead). The extraction source is f9652276c.
Route recovery — the only unrecoverable data class
Trails re-import, tracks resync, waypoints likewise. Graduated (permanent) routes have nothing behind
them, because graduation is exactly the step that stops maintaining a file on disk. WIP drafts survive
everything (Fred: "they have survived since day 1") because they are files outside the DB-open path.
That asymmetry is the defect, not the incident.
Fred's fix (08-16): archive the WIP into a completed/ subfolder we can recreate from.
⭐ Cheapest useful version: COPY at save time, DB row stays authoritative — a few lines, no new read path,
no format decision, and it closes the class on its own. ⚠ OPEN: copy-and-keep-DB-authoritative, or does the
archived file become the recovery format with its own re-import path? The second is real work and overlaps
the route-distribution feature already wanted.
🔎 00-STARTUP-SURVEY (08-16) — THE DECLARED STARTUP PHASE, AND THE HUNT FOR OTHER ONE-SHOTS. (2.6g)
⭐⭐⭐ THE ARGUMENT IS OBSERVABILITY, NOT SEQUENCING (Fred): "the issue was the
unobservability of a one-shot process that deleted and recreated DBs."
It announced itself as three I/ log lines inside a 353,608-line buffer. No UI, no
user-facing consequence, no record that survives the session. We caught it only because the ring buffer had
not rolled yet. A one-shot destructive operation should be the loudest thing the app does. Same
principle already banked for the queue: the record is the artifact — filtering hides reversibly, deletion
destroys evidence.
⚠ ORDERING CORRECTION. "Ahead of the authority grants" does not work mechanically: the
08-16 log shows the canary at 08:15:02.123 and the deletes at .463 — the migration
already ran AFTER authority. Running it earlier means operating without a verified grant, and a delete that
fails on scoped storage takes the retry branch (marker NOT advanced, will retry next launch) = a loop
where each attempt is another chance to half-delete. ⭐ Correct slot: AFTER the authority gate, BEFORE
Convoy — a slot the gate already owns as the nav start destination, so it needs no edit to
ConvoyScreen at all.
Fred on why this outranks the individual fix: "a big ball of yarn twisted into a circle — it
rolls, but you are still afraid to untangle the strings." Least-invasive is how a tangle keeps rolling.
The deliverable is the RULE about where work belongs, not the relocation. A rule tells a future
migration where to go without anyone having to remember today.
⚠ Recorded honestly: a pre-convoy job would have run the SAME logic against the SAME marker
and produced the SAME wipe, just from a tidier place. The structural work buys observability and ordering;
refuse-to-create buys protection. Keep the two credits separate.
The survey — not started, and it is the input the phase needs
Fred: "who knows how many other start-up tasks are embedded in convoy using the hunt-seek-find method
of locating it within the startup stack so it runs today and produces the right results but maybe not

No reason to assume they are the last two.

▶ TOMORROW — TWO TASKS, IN ORDER. Full detail so a fresh conversation can execute.
TASK 1 — Standardize all discard functions to the same 6-call teardown
Why: the discard/teardown logic is duplicated across sites, each doing a different
subset of the steps — classic copy-paste drift, and exactly what let the onExit bug hide.
Fred: "standardize all discard functions to the same 6 calls … there is no reason for the
differences." Consistency pass FIRST (safe — only adds missing steps), refactor to a shared
function SECOND (separate, later step). Rationale: refactoring identical code is safe;
consolidating divergent code forces picking a winner per difference and can propagate a bug to every
call site at once.
The canonical 6-step teardown (active-session discard):
1. RouteManager.clearRoute()
2. RouteDraftStore.deleteDraft(&lt;name&gt;)
3. webViewRef?.evaluateJavascript("setRouteMode(false); clearBuildLine();", null)
4. addPointMode = false
5. routeMode = false
6. draftListTick++
Sites in app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/ConvoyMapViewerScreen.kt
(⚠ RE-GREP line numbers first — they drift every edit):

TASK 2 — Run recommit_docs_v16.sh and verify no issues
What v16 fixes: the recommit bug where a bare git commit committed the ENTIRE

untracked in git (was at docs/recommit_docs_v16.sh).
Pre-run guards (Fred's standing rules — DO NOT skip):

regardless, but the glance is free.)
ONE tree-touching job at a time. No Gradle build running; not inside any patch's
generate→certify window. Recommit runs AFTER an AAB publish, never during a build.
Steps:

Commit the v16 script itself deliberately BY NAME first (don't let a recommit be what commits
it): git add docs/recommit_docs_v16.sh &amp;&amp; git commit -m "docs: recommit v16 (scope commit to docs pathspec)".
Run bash docs/recommit_docs_v16.sh.
Verify no sweep: git show --stat HEAD on the resulting docs commit — confirm

Confirm the xref / AllDocs regenerated (not stale). Freshness assertions / completion marker

🗣 00-2.7-DISCUSSION — planning substrate for 2.7 (accumulated design findings, 08-14). NOT a spec — a roadmap to plan from.
⭐⭐ FEATURE VISION (Fred 08-15) — THE "MOST INTERESTING ROUTE" PLANNER. Differentiated; future (2.7+ / own tier). NOT 2.6f.
The feature: user drops vertices/waypoints all over a map → app auto-designs 3-4 DISTINCT rideable routes, each 45-60 miles / 5-9 hours of riding (at OHV speeds), that collectively connect all the dropped points. Multi-day trip planning over the trail network.
⭐ THE DIFFERENTIATOR: existing routing (Google/onX/standard nav) optimizes SHORTEST/FASTEST. OURS optimizes the MOST INTERESTING route — the best RIDE, not the quickest path. For OHV riders "shortest" is the WRONG answer; nobody off-roads to get somewhere fast. We BORROW the routing machinery (graph traversal / pathfinding — solved, take from existing algos) but CHANGE THE OBJECTIVE FUNCTION from minimize-distance to MAXIMIZE-INTERESTINGNESS. Plumbing is standard; the optimization TARGET is ours = the innovation.
The real work isn't the algorithm (borrow it) — it's DEFINING "interesting" (a product problem = where we win). Scoring inputs: trail quality/difficulty (technical sections, the good stuff — Thunderforest Outdoors trail data + trail classifications), scenery (overlooks, vistas, terrain variety), loop-ness (good rides loop, not out-and-back), variety (mix trail types, avoid 40mi of the same fire road), hitting the user's dropped waypoints, all within the 45-60mi/5-9hr envelope as the FRAME. Leans on the spatial DB (89K trails, routing graph) + RideCalc (10-15 mph → the constraint that makes it multi-DAY trip planning, not point-to-point). Big nav apps CAN'T easily do this — built around shortest-path, no OHV-trail-quality data, no rider's-day framing. ⚠ constrained-optimization / vehicle-routing-family problem (distance + time + coverage constraints) — real algorithm needed (nearest-neighbor+constraints or a proper solver). Fits the 2.7 MapLibre/spatial-routing direction. NOT 2.6f (compliance only), likely 2.7+ or its own premium-tier feature.
Raw findings recovered from the design docs + past conversations on 08-14, parked here so 2.7 planning starts from what's already been analyzed rather than re-recovering it. Each item tagged DECIDED / OPEN. Sources: SCOPING_v2.7_vector_rendering_2026-07-26.html, memory grouptrack-vector-rendering / grouptrack-map-sources, and conversations "Track map downloading in 2.6c corridor" (07-26), "Release 2.6e route and convoy handling improvements" (08-02).
Rendering engine — the core decision
DECIDED 08-14 MapLibre, rendering satellite imagery, to leverage the spatial DB + improve functionality + tighter integration with existing JS functions. INTEGRATE not rip-and-replace: JS functions kept and integrated more tightly; MapLibre upgrades the rendering surface beneath them; spatial DB drives sat-image rendering.
DECIDED 08-02 ⭐⭐ THE (A)/(B) SPLIT — carry this into planning, every prior version bundled them:
(A) MapLibre as RENDERER, raster/satellite sources UNCHANGED — gets rotation, 3D tilt, Terrain-RGB slope shading, data-driven artifact styling, and the iPad/PC cross-platform multiplier, while satellite stays exactly as it is. (B) VECTOR BASEMAPS — the storage-savings argument. ⭐ (A) does NOT require (B). The 08-14 direction (sat imagery in MapLibre) is essentially (A).
DECIDED Fred 08-02: "If I could rotate sats we would not be having this discussion." → He CAN — MapLibre rotates RASTER tiles, the camera is source-agnostic. Rotation/tilt/pitch all work on plain satellite with no vector tiles. Leaflet cannot rotate at all (a Leaflet limitation, not a raster one).
What (A) buys — judge each on load-bearing vs. pleasant (Fred's framing)
WEIGH Rotation (heading-up) — arguably NAVIGATION, not decoration: a rider following a trail reads a rotated map faster than north-up (every handheld GPS offers it). Judge SEPARATELY from 3D — it was not previously on the list.
WEIGH Terrain-RGB slope shading — for OHV arguably more useful than the imagery itself.
WEIGH Cross-platform reuse — MapLibre GL is both native iOS/macOS SDK and JS lib; map layer is already HTML/JS in a WebView → one renderer all three surfaces (Android/iPad/PC) inherit. Ties to 2.8.
WEIGH 3D tilt / styling polish — closer to genuinely nice-to-have.
The real cost of (A) — known and large
Renderer swap on FROZEN code — the dominant cost is operating on the frozen convoy tangle. SUPERSEDED 09-30 — convoy tracking changes already made minimally invasively (Fred); see 08c item 3 ⭐ SEQUENCING ARGUMENT: a convoy rewrite opens that tangle anyway → rewrite the layer ONCE with MapLibre as target, or TWICE. (This is why 2.7 = convoy rewrite is the right home.)
spatial_artifacts.js rewritten from L.polyline to GeoJSON sources + layer specs (MapLibre gives no DOM per feature — queryRenderedFeatures instead).
MapStateStore + self-saving setView extended for BEARING and PITCH.
Tile interception moves from shouldInterceptRequest to MapLibre's addProtocol. ⭐ ties to the 2.6e shared-tile-module work — build that module with this migration in mind.
⚠ Snap is UNAFFECTED — it's Kotlin, renderer-independent, resolves by DB ID.
⚠⚠ 08-02 — "THE WHOLE APP CHANGES, MAP SOURCES ETC HAVE TO BE RE-THOUGHT." A MapLibre move re-opens the whole source model: the catalog is RASTER-SHAPED (url_template {z}/{x}/{y}, cache_dir, max_zoom per source); vector needs a style spec, glyph/sprite URLs, source-layers. And the SLOT concept assumes 4 mutually-exclusive raster basemaps while MapLibre composites raster+vector+terrain simultaneously — slots may not survive as a concept.
⭐ PROPOSED (Fred 09-30) — THE 3D ROUTE VIEW: 3D WITHOUT TOUCHING THE LEAFLET MAPS
➡ MOVED TO 2.7b (Fred 09-30) — section 08c, item 3 This card stays as the record of the proposal; the work is tracked there.
PROPOSED · post-2.7a A separate 3D view of one route or ride, opened from its detail panel: a small standalone page on MapLibre GL JS showing that route (and its trailhead / waypoints) draped over the terrain, with tilt and rotation — the 07-26 prototype (vector_label_prototype.html) turned into a viewer. The planning map and the ride map stay on Leaflet, untouched and still frozen; the renderer swap (A) remains a separate, later decision.
Size: days, not weeks — a new page and one button, no change to either map, to MapStateStore, to tile interception or to tap handling. The route's geometry goes in as GeoJSON exactly as it does today.
Elevation: the public terrarium DEM tiles (AWS, no key, capped z13). ⚠ Online-only unless an elevation download is added to the tile pipeline later (small: a whole state at z13).
Imagery: online Esri imagery first; using the rider's own downloaded SAT tiles offline would need MapLibre's addProtocol reading the MBTiles — a later step, same work item as (A)'s tile interception.
Why it is worth having before (A): it proves MapLibre in the WebView, on a real device, on GroupTrack data, with no risk to the frozen maps — a low-cost first step toward the (A) sequencing ("planning map first").
Related, also without leaving Leaflet (not decided): hillshade / relief under the satellite (a pre-rendered hillshade tile source, or computed on the tablet from the elevation tiles on a canvas layer); slope-angle shading from the same tiles; rotation via a Leaflet rotation plugin (must be tested against the frozen map code before relying on it). None of these is true 3D.
REJECTED — AND WHY (09-30) Fred checked whether a Leaflet plugin gives 3D. None gives 3D terrain while keeping Leaflet: OSM Buildings extrudes BUILDINGS on a flat map from an online service — no terrain, nothing on a trail; WebGL Earth 2 replaces L.map with its own WE.map (a renderer swap in disguise), is a world-scale GLOBE, and appears unmaintained for years; eegeo.js is a commercial 3D CITY engine behind the vendor's account and service — not our tiles, not offline. The same source concludes: for terrain, tilt and rotation, move to MapLibre. ⭐ Every GroupTrack record agrees: Leaflet is strictly 2D (07-26, 08-02, 08-14).
If (B) vector is ever pursued — the storage arithmetic + gotchas (parked, not decided)
≈80% tile reduction finding: two of SAT's three stores are LABELS not photography (place + transportation labels delivered as photographs of words). Bar 10: ~107,000 raster → ~21,700 with vector labels. Vector is small because it STOPS at ~z14 and renders deeper by scaling geometry — z15-18 is ~98% of downloads; vector removes those levels rather than shrinking them.
⛔ GLYPH BUNDLING for offline labels — the requirement most likely to be missed if (B) is done.
⚠ The storage argument is the part that FAILS in the woods (tagged-data coverage question) — which is why (A) may be all that's wanted.
Tooling if ever built: Protomaps/PMTiles (single-file, pmtiles extract --bbox), Planetiler / Tilemaker, OpenMapTiles schema. Local artifacts exist: vector_label_prototype.html.

🆕🆕🆕 AUTO-EXPLORE ROUTES BY AREA — PROVEN IN RESEARCH 2026-08-22. AUTOEXPLORE-2026-08-22
Fred, 08-22: "so with this function I start with any trailhead waypoint and explore an
area for recommendations." That is the feature. Drop a pin or tap an existing waypoint,
give it a mileage ceiling, and get four rides back — each with a mile-by-mile narrative of what
is on it.
Built and run against the LIVE spatial DB (216,616 trails) in three corridors. Nothing
was tuned between them. Scripts: nav_pass1..7, D:\nav_test\.
⭐⭐ THE THREE CORRIDORS — evidence the model generalises
Toroweap (fixed dest)Bar 10 (free)PanguitchBroken Ridge

⭐ Panguitch produced the best rides because its ground is NAMED — Indian Hollow Trail,
Trail Creek, Upper Bear Valley Road, Showalter Mountain, Buckskin Road, Sandy Caddy Creek OHV
Loop. The Strip's routes ran on "unnamed track" for most of their distance and could not be
described. Naming is what makes a suggestion communicable, which is the argument for the
rider-naming channel in 3.0.
⭐ Broken Ridge produced ONE unconfirmed junction across 79 miles, against 176 on the
Strip — same tolerance, same code. The caution count is a property of the DATA, not the
setting: sparse well-separated roads have no ambiguous junctions, dense parallel BLM tracks
have thousands. That kills the idea that the threshold needed tuning.
⛔⛔ FOUR WRONG TURNS, recorded so they are not taken again
1. DISTANCE MUST NOT BE IN THE SCORE. The first search scored
poi_value − miles×0.06, which is a CHEAPEST-PATH search wearing a POI bonus. It
returned 5 features on 69 miles and no springs at all though springs were 22 of the 39.
Fred: "point value should be the winner and if we are not getting all features &amp; POIs the
scoring is incorrect?" ⭐ Miles are a BUDGET, never a cost. Score the features; spend
miles until the budget runs out.
2. PENALISE, DO NOT FILTER. Generating 4,000 candidates, ranking them, then filtering
for distinctness returns one route — on a corridor with a fixed spine every candidate
shares it. Navigation apps do the opposite: find the best, penalise its edges (×2.2), re-solve.
The second route is then the best route that AVOIDS the first. That is the difference between
"one answer and 3,999 rejects" and four alternatives.
3. RANK, DO NOT PRE-CONSTRAIN. Fred: "if we used typical navigation on its head and
ranked the explored tracks by total distance and highest score we could then set the distance/time
cutoff to that list." Searching inside a 55–70 band strangled it before it found anything.
Explore widely, score, rank — the rider's time budget becomes a cutoff on a ranked list.
4. THE GREEDY RUNS TO THE CEILING. With one target distance every restart produced the
same length and the ranked table read "none" at every cutoff below the max. ⭐ Fix: each
restart draws its OWN target from the range, so the pool spans it.
⭐ AND A POSITIVE-SCORE FLOOR IS REQUIRED. The iterative penalty eventually makes every
scoring corridor too expensive and the search returns the best REMAINING route, which visits
nothing — Toroweap 3 and 4 both came back score 0.0. Two good routes beat four padded
ones.
⭐ THE COVERAGE CURVE — what mileage BUYS (measured, Arizona Strip)
budgetmilesfeatures
60 mi57.04
100 mi99.48
150 mi139.912
200 mi188.815
unlimited448.739 (all)
⭐ Roughly 12 miles per feature, near-LINEAR, no knee. There is no cheap cluster to
sweep — the features are genuinely spread. So a 60-mile ride reaching 4–5 features is not a
scoring failure, it is what the corridor costs. All 39 were reachable; nothing was stranded.
⭐ The ride is a coverage TRADE and the app should say so: "this 62-mile route reaches
5 of 39 features in the area" is honest, and it is what makes a longer option meaningful.
⭐⭐ JUNCTION CONFIDENCE — the tolerance sweep, and why cautions are carried not hidden
Trails are joined into a network by snapping nearby vertices. The tolerance decides what
counts as a junction, and it was MEASURED rather than picked:
tolerancejunctionscomponentsdead endsdegree-4sample gaps
0 ft5,54013219%30%exact shared vertices
10 ft7,6598514%48%0.0–6.0 ft — float noise, REAL
25 ft13,864628%70%11.8–14.8 ft — probably real
50 ft21,915494%81%25–45 ft
100 ft26,233373%85%53–92 ft
150 ft25,530383%85%junctions FALL
⛔ Degree-4 climbing to 85% is parallel tracks being WELDED TOGETHER, not crossings — a
real trail network is mostly degree 1, 2 and 3. And at 150 ft junctions fall, because the
snap grid starts merging genuinely separate junctions. Anything above 25 ft is invention.
⭐⭐ FRED'S CALL (08-22): do not hide it behind a threshold — carry it as a rating.
"add that factor to the trail rating. caution 25ft intersection boundaries" and
"highlight the 25' intersection on the suggested route map so they can use sat to zoom in."
Build at 25 ft; every junction wider than 10 ft is a CAUTION carrying its real gap. The wording a
rider can act on: "trails mapped 14 ft apart — junction not confirmed, check the satellite
view." They can see the ground; the data cannot.
⚠ Still to decide: cautions are currently emitted for every junction the route PASSES
THROUGH. A rider only needs the warning where the route TURNS onto a trail that may not
connect. That would cut 176 to a handful and is the honest version of the warning.
⭐ And it feeds the 3.0 channel: a rider who rides an unconfirmed junction knows whether
it exists. Same shape as naming an unnamed section — an observation from the ground, dated,
uploaded, distributed.
The output shape, as settled
WIP DRAFTS, not GPX tracks. Four route_drafts/&lt;Set&gt; N.json at
schema 1, so the planner opens them as WIPs over satellite with its own editing tools. Only one
gets renamed and saved as a real route. ⭐ The planner is already the inspection surface —
no HTML viewer needed, and review happens at the zoom that matters.
FULL FIDELITY vertices. Fred: "start out with the 4000 points and see if it is a
problem we even need to solve." It is not — 4,203 vertices loaded fine. lineId
carries the source trail and snapped: true, because these came from real geometry.
A .highlights.json SIDECAR beside each draft: summary, trail-by-trail legs
with cumulative mileage, cautions, features — plus a narrative block in plain English.
Fred: "nothing human readable here about feature and poi on this route."
⛔ NO POI WAYPOINTS. Fred, 08-22: "don't need waypoints of POI. they are already on
the map." reference_points came in with the OSM import and already renders.
Creating waypoints would duplicate map data and leave litter when a WIP is discarded.
⚠ GPX waypoint import does not currently work — found 08-22. Affects any rider
importing from onX or Gaia, so it earns a fix on its own merits.
🔴 PLANNER PREREQUISITES — found by using it, not polish
A WIP must open in ARTIFACT mode, not draw mode. Opening in draw means the first tap
adds a point. Measured: one stray vertex took Toroweap 1 from 78.8 to 109.0 miles with a
21.9-mile straight line out and back. Two undos restored it — the geometry was never
damaged — but a suggestion is for evaluating first and editing second.
A lock field in the draft JSON. Soft: opens read-only, rider unlocks deliberately.
Same principle as the naming rules — a suggestion is not a fact, and the rider's edit outranks it,
but only on purpose.
Fit-to-route on open, as track fit already does. A 78-mile route opening at the
previous viewport cannot be judged. The bbox+padding logic exists.
⚠ Sidecars currently sit in route_drafts/ beside the drafts. If the picker lists
them as routes they need a different folder or extension.
What it needs to become an app function
Inputs are already there — an anchor (any waypoint or dropped pin), a mileage ceiling,
and a corridor box derived from the anchor. Nothing else was supplied by hand in any of the three
runs.
⚠ The GRAPH BUILD is the heavy part, not the search. 27,000 edges rebuilt from scratch
every run — seconds on a laptop, longer on a phone, and it is the SAME work each time for the
same area. Cache it, or build it once per import rather than per request.
The search is cheap once the graph exists — 2,500 restarts in seconds.
RideCalc supplies the time estimate — 12–18 mph, already calibrated.
⬜ STILL TO DISCUSS — route build with points INCLUDED
This section covers auto-explore: an anchor and a budget, the app chooses the features.
The other half is a route built through points the rider supplies — the Toroweap run was a
crude version (start, must-visit, return) and it showed the cost: 53.7 of every 80 miles went
on the tether, leaving ~26 for features and forcing 50% retrace.
⭐ The general form Fred described: a SEQUENCE of fixed points, and the search fills the
gaps. One point = out and back. Two = a destination ride. Three+ = an overnighter, each leg
carrying its own mileage band — a rider doing 50–70 a day for three days is three separate
searches, not one 180-mile problem. Not yet designed.
💾 THE RESEARCH CODE — embedded so it is not recreated. AUTOEXPLORE-CODE-2026-08-22
Fred, 08-22: "please drop your code in there as a model so we do not recreate."
These ran against a copy of the live spatial DB at D:\nav_test\grouptrack_spatial.db
(407 MB, pulled from Droid 2 after the four-state area import). All are READ ONLY on the
database. They are research tools, not app code — but the model they encode is what the
suggester should be built from, and the wrong turns are as valuable as the working version.
Superseded passes are named in the prose above but NOT embedded — pass 2 (endpoint-only
junctions, produced 408 components), pass 3/3b/3d (distance in the score, filter instead of
penalty), pass 4/4b (pre-constrained band). Their lessons are recorded; their code would only
