nav_pass2c_tolerance_sweep_2026-08-22.py
THE TOLERANCE SWEEP. Builds the network at 0/10/25/50/100/150 ft and reports components, dead ends, degree distribution and sample junction gaps. This is what decided 25 ft and proved 150 ft was inventing junctions. Run it against any new corridor before trusting its network.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_pass2c_tolerance_sweep_2026-08-22.py
HOW MUCH OF THE NETWORK IS REAL?
Pass 2b snapped vertices within 150 ft into shared junctions and produced a
network that LOOKS healthy -- 3% dead ends, 38 components, 99% in one piece.
But 22,243 of 26,237 nodes came out at degree 4, and that is not what a trail
network looks like. Real networks are mostly degree 1, 2 and 3, with degree 4
as genuine crossroads.
Fred, 08-22: &quot;we really need to be sure trails have a junction before suggesting
a route.&quot; A route that turns where no turn exists is worse than no route -- the
rider is out past Mt Trumbull with no signal and the app told them to go that
way.
So: build the graph at several tolerances and MEASURE, rather than pick one.
WHAT TO READ IN THE OUTPUT
  1. Where the component count stops falling. Junctions gained between 0 and
     ~25 ft are float noise being repaired and are real. Junctions still being
     gained at 150 ft are parallel tracks being welded together.
  2. Where degree-4 starts to dominate. That is the tolerance at which trails
     that merely pass near each other become crossings.
  3. The SAMPLES at the bottom -- actual pairs of trail names being joined, with
     the real distance between the vertices. That is the eyeball test.
READ ONLY. Writes nothing.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import sqlite3, math, os, sys, re
from collections import defaultdict, Counter, deque
DB = r&quot;D:\nav_test\grouptrack_spatial.db&quot;
BAR10    = (36.43, -113.35)
TOROWEAP = (36.20, -113.07)
LAT_S, LAT_N = 35.95, 36.65
LON_W, LON_E = -113.80, -112.80
TOLERANCES_FT = [0, 10, 25, 50, 100, 150]
NONAMES = {&quot;&quot;, &quot;not named&quot;, &quot;unnamed&quot;, &quot;none&quot;, &quot;null&quot;, &quot;n/a&quot;, &quot;-&quot;}
def hav(a, b):
    R = 3958.8
    p1, p2 = math.radians(a[0]), math.radians(b[0])
    dp = p2 - p1
    dl = math.radians(b[1] - a[1])
    h = math.sin(dp/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dl/2)**2
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))
def wkt_points(wkt):
    if not wkt:
        return []
    nums = re.findall(r&#x27;(-?\d+\.?\d*)\s+(-?\d+\.?\d*)&#x27;, wkt)
    return [(float(la), float(lo)) for lo, la in nums]
def real_name(n):
    return bool(n) and str(n).strip().lower() not in NONAMES
def build(geoms, tol_ft):
    &quot;&quot;&quot;Returns (adj, nodes, edges, junction_keys, keyfn).&quot;&quot;&quot;
    if tol_ft &lt;= 0:
        # exact match on the stored coordinate, to ~1e-6 deg (about 4 inches)
        def keyfn(p):
            return (round(p[0], 6), round(p[1], 6))
    else:
        d = (tol_ft / 5280.0) / 69.0
        def keyfn(p):
            return (int(round(p[0] / d)), int(round(p[1] / d)))
    touch = defaultdict(set)
    for tid, nm, pts in geoms:
        for p in pts:
            touch[keyfn(p)].add(tid)
    shared = {k for k, s in touch.items() if len(s) &gt; 1}
    edges, nodes = [], {}
    for tid, nm, pts in geoms:
        cuts = [0, len(pts)-1]
        for i in range(1, len(pts)-1):
            if keyfn(pts[i]) in shared:
                cuts.append(i)
        cuts = sorted(set(cuts))
        for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:]):
            seg = pts[a:b+1]
            if len(seg) &lt; 2:
                continue
            L = sum(hav(seg[i], seg[i+1]) for i in range(len(seg)-1))
            if L &lt;= 0.0005:
                continue
            ka, kb = keyfn(seg[0]), keyfn(seg[-1])
            if ka == kb:
                continue
            nodes.setdefault(ka, seg[0]); nodes.setdefault(kb, seg[-1])
            edges.append((ka, kb, L, nm, tid))
    adj = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (a, b, L, nm, tid) in enumerate(edges):
        adj[a].append((b, i)); adj[b].append((a, i))
    return adj, nodes, edges, shared, keyfn, touch
def components(adj):
    seen, comps = set(), []
    for n in adj:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        q, c = deque([n]), []
        seen.add(n)
        while q:
            x = q.popleft(); c.append(x)
            for y, _ in adj[x]:
                if y not in seen:
                    seen.add(y); q.append(y)
        comps.append(c)
    comps.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
    return comps
def main():
    if not os.path.isfile(DB):
        print(&quot;NOT FOUND: %s&quot; % DB); return 1
    con = sqlite3.connect(&quot;file:%s?mode=ro&quot; % DB.replace(&quot;\\&quot;, &quot;/&quot;), uri=True)
    cur = con.cursor()
    rows = list(cur.execute(
        &quot;SELECT trail_id,name,geometry FROM trails &quot;
        &quot;WHERE min_lat&lt;=? AND max_lat&gt;=? AND min_lon&lt;=? AND max_lon&gt;=?&quot;,
        (LAT_N, LAT_S, LON_E, LON_W)))
    geoms = []
    for tid, nm, wkt in rows:
        pts = wkt_points(wkt)
        if len(pts) &gt;= 2:
            geoms.append((tid, nm, pts))
    print(&quot;trails in corridor: %d   (usable geometry: %d)&quot; % (len(rows), len(geoms)))
    name_of = {tid: (nm if real_name(nm) else &quot;(unnamed)&quot;) for tid, nm, _ in geoms}
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot; * 78)
    print(&quot;%-7s %8s %8s %7s %8s %8s %7s %9s&quot; %
          (&quot;tol ft&quot;, &quot;junct&quot;, &quot;edges&quot;, &quot;nodes&quot;, &quot;comps&quot;, &quot;deadend&quot;, &quot;deg4%&quot;, &quot;B10-&gt;TOR&quot;))
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 78)
    prev_shared, prev_touch, prev_keyfn = None, None, None
    results = {}
    for tol in TOLERANCES_FT:
        adj, nodes, edges, shared, keyfn, touch = build(geoms, tol)
        comps = components(adj)
        deg = Counter(len(v) for v in adj.values())
        n = max(len(adj), 1)
        dead = deg.get(1, 0)
        d4 = deg.get(4, 0)
        # anchors + shortest path in the biggest component
        cid = {}
        for i, c in enumerate(comps):
            for x in c:
                cid[x] = i
        def nearest(pt, comp=0):
            best, bd = None, 1e9
            for k, p in nodes.items():
                if cid.get(k) != comp:
                    continue
                d = hav(pt, p)
                if d &lt; bd:
                    bd, best = d, k
            return best, bd
        import heapq
        nb, db_ = nearest(BAR10)
        nt, dt_ = nearest(TOROWEAP)
        spd = None
        if nb and nt:
            dist = {nb: 0.0}; pq = [(0.0, nb)]
            while pq:
                d, x = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if x == nt:
                    spd = d; break
                if d &gt; dist.get(x, 1e18):
                    continue
                for y, ei in adj[x]:
                    nd = d + edges[ei][2]
                    if nd &lt; dist.get(y, 1e18):
                        dist[y] = nd; heapq.heappush(pq, (nd, y))
        print(&quot;%-7d %8d %8d %7d %8d %7.0f%% %6.0f%% %9s&quot; %
              (tol, len(shared), len(edges), len(adj), len(comps),
               100.0*dead/n, 100.0*d4/n,
               (&quot;%.1f mi&quot; % spd) if spd else &quot;none&quot;))
        results[tol] = dict(shared=shared, touch=touch, keyfn=keyfn,
                            comps=len(comps), anchors=(db_, dt_))
        prev_shared = shared
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 78)
    print(&quot;\nANCHOR DISTANCE TO THE MAIN NETWORK&quot;)
    for tol in TOLERANCES_FT:
        db_, dt_ = results[tol][&quot;anchors&quot;]
        print(&quot;  %3d ft   Bar 10 %5.2f mi   Toroweap %5.2f mi&quot; % (tol, db_, dt_))
    # ── the eyeball test ────────────────────────────────────────────
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot; * 78)
    print(&quot;JUNCTIONS GAINED BETWEEN TOLERANCES -- are these real?&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 78)
    for lo, hi in zip(TOLERANCES_FT, TOLERANCES_FT[1:]):
        s_lo, s_hi = results[lo][&quot;shared&quot;], results[hi][&quot;shared&quot;]
        t_hi, k_hi = results[hi][&quot;touch&quot;], results[hi][&quot;keyfn&quot;]
        # keys shared at hi. we cannot compare keys across tolerances directly
        # (different grids), so sample the hi-only junctions by re-testing the
        # actual vertex distance between the two trails meeting there.
        gained = len(s_hi) - len(s_lo)
        print(&quot;\n  %d ft -&gt; %d ft : %+d junctions&quot; % (lo, hi, gained))
        shown = 0
        for k in s_hi:
            tids = list(t_hi[k])
            if len(tids) &lt; 2:
                continue
            a, b = tids[0], tids[1]
            if a == b:
                continue
            pa = next((p for t, n, ps in geoms if t == a for p in ps if k_hi(p) == k), None)
            pb = next((p for t, n, ps in geoms if t == b for p in ps if k_hi(p) == k), None)
            if not pa or not pb:
                continue
            gap_ft = hav(pa, pb) * 5280
            if gap_ft &lt;= lo:      # would already have joined at the lower tol
                continue
            print(&quot;     %6.1f ft apart : %-30s  x  %s&quot;
                  % (gap_ft, name_of.get(a, &quot;?&quot;)[:30], name_of.get(b, &quot;?&quot;)[:30]))
            shown += 1
            if shown &gt;= 6:
                break
        if shown == 0:
            print(&quot;     (no sample found in this band)&quot;)
    con.close()
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot; * 78)
    print(&quot;READ: the tolerance where components stop dropping is where real&quot;)
    print(&quot;junctions end. Junctions still appearing above that are trails that&quot;)
    print(&quot;pass NEAR each other, not trails that MEET.&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 78)
    return 0
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    sys.exit(main())
nav_pass3c_coverage_2026-08-22.py
THE COVERAGE CURVE. Removes the mileage limit entirely and reports what each budget buys, plus the ceiling for full coverage. This is what established 12 miles per feature and killed the idea that a 60-mile ride reaching 4 features was a scoring bug.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_pass3c_coverage_2026-08-22.py
PASS 3c -- take the mileage limit OFF and find out what the data can actually do.
WHY. Pass 3b produced ONE route, 69.5 mi, collecting 5 POIs of 39 -- and no
springs at all, though 22 are on the network. Fred: &quot;not sure why closest trail
is taking priority. point value should be the winner and if we are not getting
all features &amp; POIs the scoring is incorrect?&quot;
He was right, and the bug was structural rather than a bad constant. Pass 3b
scored `poi_value - miles*0.06`, which makes it a CHEAPEST-PATH search with a
POI bonus. What was asked for is a MAXIMUM-POI search with a mileage budget.
Distance should never have been in the score -- it is a constraint, not a cost.
With a 53.7 mi direct round trip inside a 50-70 band there was ~16 mi of slack,
and every detouring branch lost the beam to a direct one before it could pay off.
SO: score POIs only. Miles are spent until the budget runs out. And this pass
removes the budget entirely first, to establish the CEILING -- what does full
coverage cost? Then it reports the curve: POIs collected at 60, 80, 100, 150,
200 mi and unlimited. That curve is what should inform the suggester, rather
than a band picked in advance.
ALSO FIXED FROM 3b:
  - cautions were emitted per NODE VISIT, so one junction the route passes three
    times appeared three times (310 cautions, 186 waypoints from 39 POIs).
    Now deduped by junction.
  - leg accounting dropped ~17 mi around the Toroweap turnaround.
READ ONLY.

import sqlite3, math, os, sys, re, heapq, json, datetime
from collections import defaultdict, Counter, deque
DB  = r&quot;D:\nav_test\grouptrack_spatial.db&quot;
OUT = r&quot;D:\nav_test\out&quot;
BAR10    = (36.43, -113.35)
TOROWEAP = (36.20, -113.07)
BUDGETS = [60, 80, 100, 150, 200, None]   # None = unlimited
SNAP_FT, CAUTION_FT, POI_BUF_MI = 25.0, 10.0, 0.5
SPEED_MPH = (12.0, 18.0)
LAT_S, LAT_N, LON_W, LON_E = 35.95, 36.65, -113.80, -112.80
NONAMES = {&quot;&quot;, &quot;not named&quot;, &quot;unnamed&quot;, &quot;none&quot;, &quot;null&quot;, &quot;n/a&quot;, &quot;-&quot;}
WATER = {&quot;spring&quot;}
VIEW  = {&quot;peak&quot;, &quot;cliff&quot;, &quot;volcano&quot;}
def hav(a, b):
    R = 3958.8
    p1, p2 = math.radians(a[0]), math.radians(b[0])
    dp = p2-p1; dl = math.radians(b[1]-a[1])
    h = math.sin(dp/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dl/2)**2
    return 2*R*math.asin(math.sqrt(h))
def wkt_points(w):
    if not w: return []
    return [(float(a), float(b)) for b, a in
            re.findall(r&#x27;(-?\d+\.?\d*)\s+(-?\d+\.?\d*)&#x27;, w)]
def real_name(n):
    return bool(n) and str(n).strip().lower() not in NONAMES
def esc(s):
    return (str(s).replace(&quot;&amp;&quot;,&quot;&amp;amp;&quot;).replace(&quot;&lt;&quot;,&quot;&amp;lt;&quot;)
            .replace(&quot;&gt;&quot;,&quot;&amp;gt;&quot;).replace(&#x27;&quot;&#x27;,&quot;&amp;quot;&quot;))
def main():
    if not os.path.isfile(DB):
        print(&quot;NOT FOUND: %s&quot; % DB); return 1
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(OUT, &quot;route_drafts&quot;), exist_ok=True)
    con = sqlite3.connect(&quot;file:%s?mode=ro&quot; % DB.replace(&quot;\\&quot;,&quot;/&quot;), uri=True)
    cur = con.cursor()
    print(&quot;=&quot;*76)
    print(&quot;PASS 3c -- WHAT CAN THE DATA ACTUALLY DO?  (no mileage limit first)&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*76)
    geoms = []
    for tid, nm, wkt in cur.execute(
            &quot;SELECT trail_id,name,geometry FROM trails WHERE min_lat&lt;=? AND max_lat&gt;=? &quot;
            &quot;AND min_lon&lt;=? AND max_lon&gt;=?&quot;, (LAT_N, LAT_S, LON_E, LON_W)):
        p = wkt_points(wkt)
        if len(p) &gt;= 2: geoms.append((tid, nm, p))
    d_ = (SNAP_FT/5280.0)/69.0
    def key(p): return (int(round(p[0]/d_)), int(round(p[1]/d_)))
    touch, spread = defaultdict(set), defaultdict(list)
    for tid, nm, pts in geoms:
        for p in pts:
            k = key(p); touch[k].add(tid); spread[k].append(p)
    shared = {k for k, s in touch.items() if len(s) &gt; 1}
    gap_ft = {}
    for k in shared:
        ps = spread[k]; g = 0.0
        for i in range(len(ps)):
            for j in range(i+1, min(len(ps), i+6)):
                g = max(g, hav(ps[i], ps[j])*5280)
        gap_ft[k] = g
    edges, nodes = [], {}
    for tid, nm, pts in geoms:
        cuts = sorted(set([0, len(pts)-1] +
                          [i for i in range(1, len(pts)-1) if key(pts[i]) in shared]))
        for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:]):
            seg = pts[a:b+1]
            if len(seg) &lt; 2: continue
            L = sum(hav(seg[i], seg[i+1]) for i in range(len(seg)-1))
            if L &lt;= 0.0005: continue
            ka, kb = key(seg[0]), key(seg[-1])
            if ka == kb: continue
            nodes.setdefault(ka, seg[0]); nodes.setdefault(kb, seg[-1])
            edges.append((ka, kb, L, (nm if real_name(nm) else None), tid, seg))
    adj = defaultdict(list)
    for i, e in enumerate(edges):
        adj[e[0]].append((e[1], i)); adj[e[1]].append((e[0], i))
    seen, comps = set(), []
    for n in adj:
        if n in seen: continue
        q, c = deque([n]), []; seen.add(n)
        while q:
            x = q.popleft(); c.append(x)
            for y, _ in adj[x]:
                if y not in seen: seen.add(y); q.append(y)
        comps.append(c)
    comps.sort(key=len, reverse=True); main_c = set(comps[0])
    print(&quot;network: %d edges, %d nodes, main component %d&quot;
          % (len(edges), len(adj), len(main_c)))
    def nearest(pt):
        best, bd = None, 1e9
        for k in main_c:
            v = hav(pt, nodes[k])
            if v &lt; bd: bd, best = v, k
        return best, bd
    n_bar, _ = nearest(BAR10); n_tor, _ = nearest(TOROWEAP)
    poi_at = {}
    for nm, fc, la, lo in cur.execute(
            &quot;SELECT name,fclass,lat,lon FROM reference_points WHERE lat BETWEEN ? AND ? &quot;
            &quot;AND lon BETWEEN ? AND ?&quot;, (LAT_S, LAT_N, LON_W, LON_E)):
        k, v = nearest((la, lo))
        if v &lt;= POI_BUF_MI:
            poi_at.setdefault(k, []).append({&quot;name&quot;: nm, &quot;fclass&quot;: fc,
                                             &quot;lat&quot;: la, &quot;lon&quot;: lo, &quot;off_mi&quot;: round(v,3)})
    allp = [p for v in poi_at.values() for p in v]
    print(&quot;POIs reachable: %d at %d nodes  (%s)&quot;
          % (len(allp), len(poi_at),
             &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s %d&quot; % (k,v) for k,v in
                       Counter(p[&quot;fclass&quot;] for p in allp).most_common())))
    terms = [n_bar, n_tor] + [k for k in poi_at if k not in (n_bar, n_tor)]
    def dij(s):
        dist = {s:0.0}; prev = {}; pq=[(0.0,s)]
        while pq:
            d0,x = heapq.heappop(pq)
            if d0 &gt; dist.get(x,1e18): continue
            for y,ei in adj[x]:
                nd = d0+edges[ei][2]
                if nd &lt; dist.get(y,1e18):
                    dist[y]=nd; prev[y]=(x,ei); heapq.heappush(pq,(nd,y))
        return dist, prev
    D, P = {}, {}
    for t in terms: D[t], P[t] = dij(t)
    def pe(s,t):
        out,x = [],t
        while x != s:
            if x not in P[s]: return None
            px,ei = P[s][x]; out.append(ei); x=px
        out.reverse(); return out
    base = D[n_bar].get(n_tor)
    print(&quot;direct: Bar10 -&gt; Toroweap %.1f mi, round trip %.1f mi&quot; % (base, 2*base))
    pn = [k for k in poi_at if D[n_bar].get(k) is not None and D[n_tor].get(k) is not None]
    print(&quot;POI nodes routable from BOTH anchors: %d of %d\n&quot; % (len(pn), len(poi_at)))
    # ── greedy nearest-unvisited coverage, no budget ────────────────
    # Deliberately simple: this establishes the CEILING and the curve, not the
    # optimal tour. Optimality can come later; what matters now is the shape.
    def cover(order_from, must_end, budget):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Greedy: from a start node, repeatedly hop to the nearest unvisited POI
        node that still leaves room to finish. Returns (nodes, miles, poinodes).&quot;&quot;&quot;
        cur_n, miles, seq, got = order_from, 0.0, [order_from], []
        left = set(pn)
        while True:
            best, bd = None, 1e18
            for k in left:
                s1 = D[cur_n].get(k)
                if s1 is None: continue
                back = D[k].get(must_end)
                if back is None: continue
                if budget is not None and miles + s1 + back &gt; budget: continue
                if s1 &lt; bd: bd, best = s1, k
            if best is None: break
            miles += bd; cur_n = best; seq.append(best); got.append(best)
            left.discard(best)
        fin = D[cur_n].get(must_end)
        if fin is None: return None
        miles += fin; seq.append(must_end)
        return seq, miles, got
    print(&quot;=&quot;*76)
    print(&quot;COVERAGE CURVE -- Bar10 -&gt; (POIs) -&gt; Toroweap -&gt; (POIs) -&gt; Bar10&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*76)
    print(&quot;%-10s %10s %8s %8s   %s&quot; % (&quot;budget&quot;, &quot;miles&quot;, &quot;POIs&quot;, &quot;of&quot;, &quot;mix&quot;))
    curve = {}
    for B in BUDGETS:
        half = None if B is None else B*0.55
        a = cover(n_bar, n_tor, half)
        if not a: continue
        seq_a, mi_a, got_a = a
        rem = None if B is None else B - mi_a
        cur_n, miles_b, seq_b, got_b = n_tor, 0.0, [n_tor], []
        left = set(pn) - set(got_a)
        while True:
            best, bd = None, 1e18
            for k in left:
                s1 = D[cur_n].get(k); back = D[k].get(n_bar)
                if s1 is None or back is None: continue
                if rem is not None and miles_b + s1 + back &gt; rem: continue
                if s1 &lt; bd: bd, best = s1, k
            if best is None: break
            miles_b += bd; cur_n = best; seq_b.append(best); got_b.append(best); left.discard(best)
        miles_b += D[cur_n].get(n_bar, 0.0); seq_b.append(n_bar)
        full = seq_a + seq_b[1:]
        total = mi_a + miles_b
        names = []
        for k in got_a + got_b:
            names.extend(p[&quot;name&quot;] for p in poi_at[k])
        mix = Counter(p[&quot;fclass&quot;] for k in got_a+got_b for p in poi_at[k])
        curve[B] = (full, total, names, mix)
        print(&quot;%-10s %9.1f %8d %8d   %s&quot;
              % ((&quot;unlimited&quot; if B is None else &quot;%d mi&quot; % B), total, len(names), len(allp),
                 &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s %d&quot; % (a_, b_) for a_, b_ in mix.most_common())))
    # ── what the ceiling misses ─────────────────────────────────────
    if None in curve:
        got = set(curve[None][2])
        missed = [p for p in allp if p[&quot;name&quot;] not in got]
        print(&quot;\nUNREACHED even unlimited: %d&quot; % len(missed))
        for p in missed[:20]:
            print(&quot;   %-10s %s&quot; % (p[&quot;fclass&quot;], p[&quot;name&quot;]))
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*76)
    print(&quot;READ: the curve is what mileage BUYS. If 100 mi collects most of the&quot;)
    print(&quot;39 and 60 mi collects a third, that is the trade -- and it should&quot;)
    print(&quot;drive the suggester&#x27;s design rather than a band picked in advance.&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*76)
    con.close()
    return 0
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    sys.exit(main())
nav_pass5_bar10_explore_2026-08-22.py
⭐ THE WORKING MODEL — free loop from any anchor. Explore-then-rank, iterative edge penalties for genuine alternatives, positive-score floor, per-restart target distance. Emits WIP drafts + sidecars. Panguitch and Broken Ridge are THIS FILE with SET_NAME, the anchor and the box changed — nothing else. That is the whole argument that it generalises.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_pass5_bar10_explore_2026-08-22.py
PASS 4 -- FIXED-POINT INCLUSIVE.  Bar 10 -&gt; Toroweap -&gt; Bar 10.
TWO CORRECTIONS FROM 3d, both structural.
1. RANK, DO NOT PRE-CONSTRAIN.  Fred: &quot;if we used typical navigation on its head
   and ranked the explored tracks by total distance and highest score we could
   then set the distance/time cutoff to that list.&quot;
   3d searched INSIDE a 55-70 band, and with a 53.7 mi fixed tether that band
   strangled the search before it could find anything. This explores across a
   wide distance range, scores everything, and RANKS. The rider&#x27;s time budget
   becomes a cutoff applied to the ranked list, not a constraint that shapes
   the search.
2. PENALISE, DO NOT FILTER.  3d generated 4,000 candidates, ranked them, then
   filtered for distinctness -- which on a corridor with a fixed spine leaves
   exactly one. Navigation apps do the opposite: find the best, PENALISE the
   edges it used, re-solve. The second route is then the best route that avoids
   the first. That is the difference between &quot;one answer and 3,999 rejects&quot; and
   &quot;four alternatives.&quot;
OBJECTIVE IS SCORE, NOT DISTANCE.  Miles are a budget, never a cost. Variety is
weighted: a second class of feature beats another of the same.
OUT: D:\\nav_test\\out\\route_drafts\\&lt;SET_NAME&gt; N.json  + .highlights.json
     D:\\nav_test\\out\\grouptrack_suggested_waypoints_2026-08-22.gpx

            # each restart gets its OWN target, so the pool spans the range.
            target = random.uniform(EXPLORE_MAX * 0.62, EXPLORE_MAX)
            chosen, cur_n, mi = [], n_bar, 0.0
            left = set(pn)
            while True:
                cands = []
                for k in left:
                    s1 = D[cur_n].get(k); back = D[k].get(n_bar)
                    if s1 is None or back is None: continue
                    # the only constraint is getting home inside the target
                    if mi + s1 + back &gt; target: continue
                    g = setscore(chosen + [k]) - setscore(chosen)
                    if g &lt;= 0: continue
                    cands.append((g / max(s1, 0.35), k, s1))
                if not cands: break
                cands.sort(reverse=True)
                _, k, s1 = cands[min(int(random.random()**2 * 5), len(cands)-1)]
                mi += s1; cur_n = k; chosen.append(k); left.discard(k)
            fin = D[cur_n].get(n_bar)
            if fin is None: continue
            seq = [n_bar] + chosen[:] + [n_bar]
            eids, ok = [], True
            for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
                q = pe(P, a, b)
                if q is None: ok = False; break
                eids.extend(q)
            if not ok: continue
            real_mi = sum(edges[e][2] for e in eids)
            if real_mi &gt; EXPLORE_MAX: continue
            found.append({&quot;seq&quot;: seq, &quot;eids&quot;: eids, &quot;eset&quot;: set(eids),
                          &quot;miles&quot;: real_mi, &quot;score&quot;: setscore(chosen),
                          &quot;chosen&quot;: chosen})
        return found
    print(&quot;\nexploring (no mileage band)...&quot;)
    pen = {}
    D, P = build_tables(pen)
    pool = explore(D, P, pen)
    print(&quot;routes explored: %d&quot; % len(pool))
    if not pool:
        print(&quot;nothing found&quot;); return 3
    # ── the ranked table: what distance BUYS ────────────────────────
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;RANKED -- best score available at each distance cutoff&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;%-10s %10s %8s %8s   %s&quot; % (&quot;cutoff&quot;, &quot;miles&quot;, &quot;score&quot;, &quot;feats&quot;, &quot;mix&quot;))
    for cutm in REPORT_CUTS:
        sub = [r for r in pool if r[&quot;miles&quot;] &lt;= cutm]
        if not sub: 
            print(&quot;%-10s %10s&quot; % (&quot;&lt;= %d mi&quot; % cutm, &quot;none&quot;)); continue
        b = max(sub, key=lambda r: r[&quot;score&quot;])
        names = {p[&quot;name&quot;]: p[&quot;fclass&quot;] for k in b[&quot;chosen&quot;] for p in poi_at[k]}
        mix = Counter(names.values())
        print(&quot;%-10s %9.1f %8.1f %8d   %s&quot;
              % (&quot;&lt;= %d mi&quot; % cutm, b[&quot;miles&quot;], b[&quot;score&quot;], len(names),
                 &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s %d&quot; % (a_,b_) for a_,b_ in mix.most_common())))
    # ── four alternatives by iterative penalty ──────────────────────
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;FOUR ALTERNATIVES (each penalised away from the ones before)&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    picks = []
    for i in range(N_ROUTES):
        if i &gt; 0:
            for e in picks[-1][&quot;eset&quot;]:
                pen[e] = pen.get(e, 1.0) * PENALTY
            D, P = build_tables(pen)
            pool = explore(D, P, pen)
            if not pool:
                print(&quot;  (no further alternative found)&quot;); break
        # POSITIVE SCORE FLOOR (Fred 08-22): a route with no features is not a
        # suggestion. The iterative penalty eventually makes every scoring
        # corridor too expensive and the search returns the best REMAINING route,
        # which visits nothing -- Toroweap 3 and 4 both came back score 0.0.
        # Better to return two good routes than pad to four.
        cand = [r for r in pool
                if r[&quot;score&quot;] &gt; 0.0
                and all(len(r[&quot;eset&quot;] &amp; q[&quot;eset&quot;])/max(len(r[&quot;eset&quot;] | q[&quot;eset&quot;]),1) &lt; 0.75
                        for q in picks)]
        if not cand:
            print(&quot;  (no further alternative with a positive score)&quot;); break
        b = max(cand, key=lambda r: r[&quot;score&quot;])
        b[&quot;repeat&quot;] = 1.0 - len(b[&quot;eset&quot;])/max(len(b[&quot;eids&quot;]),1)
        picks.append(b)
        print(&quot;  %s %d: %.1f mi, score %.1f&quot; % (SET_NAME, i+1, b[&quot;miles&quot;], b[&quot;score&quot;]))
    # ── emit ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(&quot;%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ&quot;)
    wpts = {}
    for idx, r in enumerate(picks, 1):
        verts, legs, caut = [], [], {}
        cum, prev_name, leg_start, leg_pois = 0.0, None, 0.0, []
        seenpoi, plist = set(), []
        for e in r[&quot;eids&quot;]:
            a, b, L, nm, tid, seg = edges[e]
            s = seg
            if verts and hav((verts[-1][&quot;lat&quot;], verts[-1][&quot;lon&quot;]), s[0]) &gt; \
                         hav((verts[-1][&quot;lat&quot;], verts[-1][&quot;lon&quot;]), s[-1]):
                s = s[::-1]
            for j, p in enumerate(s):
                if verts and j == 0: continue
                verts.append({&quot;lat&quot;: round(p[0],6), &quot;lon&quot;: round(p[1],6),
                              &quot;lineId&quot;: tid, &quot;lineType&quot;: &quot;trail&quot;,
                              &quot;segmentIndex&quot;: -1, &quot;t&quot;: 0.0, &quot;snapped&quot;: True})
            lbl = nm or &quot;unnamed track&quot;
            if lbl != prev_name:
                if prev_name is not None:
                    legs.append({&quot;trail&quot;: prev_name, &quot;from_mi&quot;: round(leg_start,2),
                                 &quot;to_mi&quot;: round(cum,2),
                                 &quot;miles&quot;: round(cum-leg_start,2), &quot;pois&quot;: leg_pois})
                prev_name, leg_start, leg_pois = lbl, cum, []
            cum += L
            for k in (a, b):
                for p in poi_at.get(k, []):
                    if p[&quot;name&quot;] in seenpoi: continue
                    seenpoi.add(p[&quot;name&quot;]); plist.append(p)
                    leg_pois.append({&quot;name&quot;: p[&quot;name&quot;], &quot;fclass&quot;: p[&quot;fclass&quot;],
                                     &quot;at_mi&quot;: round(cum,2), &quot;off_mi&quot;: p[&quot;off_mi&quot;]})
                g = gap_ft.get(k, 0.0)
                if g &gt; CAUTION_FT and k not in caut:
                    caut[k] = {&quot;at_mi&quot;: round(cum,2), &quot;gap_ft&quot;: round(g,1),
                               &quot;lat&quot;: round(nodes[k][0],6), &quot;lon&quot;: round(nodes[k][1],6)}
        if prev_name is not None:
            legs.append({&quot;trail&quot;: prev_name, &quot;from_mi&quot;: round(leg_start,2),
                         &quot;to_mi&quot;: round(cum,2), &quot;miles&quot;: round(cum-leg_start,2),
                         &quot;pois&quot;: leg_pois})
        cautions = sorted(caut.values(), key=lambda c: c[&quot;at_mi&quot;])
        lo_h, hi_h = r[&quot;miles&quot;]/SPEED_MPH[1], r[&quot;miles&quot;]/SPEED_MPH[0]
        name = &quot;%s %d&quot; % (SET_NAME, idx)
        mix = Counter(p[&quot;fclass&quot;] for p in plist)
        print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;-&quot;*78)
        print(&quot;%s      %.1f miles      %.1f-%.1f hours      score %.1f&quot;
              % (name, r[&quot;miles&quot;], lo_h, hi_h, r[&quot;score&quot;]))
        print(&quot;-&quot;*78)
        print(&quot;  %d of %d features (%s)   %d vertices   %d cautions   %.0f%% retrace&quot;
              % (len(plist), len(allp),
                 &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s %d&quot; % (a_,b_) for a_,b_ in mix.most_common()),
                 len(verts), len(cautions), 100*r[&quot;repeat&quot;]))
        for p in plist:
            print(&quot;      %-9s %-28s mile %.1f&quot; %
                  (p[&quot;fclass&quot;], p[&quot;name&quot;][:28],
                   next((q[&quot;at_mi&quot;] for lg in legs for q in lg[&quot;pois&quot;]
                         if q[&quot;name&quot;] == p[&quot;name&quot;]), 0)))
        print(&quot;  named trail legs over 1 mi:&quot;)
        for lg in legs:
            if lg[&quot;miles&quot;] &lt; 1.0 or lg[&quot;trail&quot;] == &quot;unnamed track&quot;: continue
            print(&quot;    %5.1f-%5.1f  %-32s %4.1f mi&quot;
                  % (lg[&quot;from_mi&quot;], lg[&quot;to_mi&quot;], lg[&quot;trail&quot;][:32], lg[&quot;miles&quot;]))
        print(&quot;  unconfirmed junctions: %d&quot; % len(cautions))
        json.dump({&quot;schemaVersion&quot;:1, &quot;name&quot;:name, &quot;createdAt&quot;:now, &quot;updatedAt&quot;:now,
                   &quot;method&quot;:&quot;point&quot;, &quot;vertices&quot;:verts},
                  open(os.path.join(OUT,&quot;route_drafts&quot;,&quot;%s.json&quot;%name),&quot;w&quot;))
        json.dump({&quot;name&quot;:name, &quot;generated&quot;:now,
                   &quot;summary&quot;:{&quot;total_miles&quot;:round(r[&quot;miles&quot;],2),
                              &quot;est_hours&quot;:[round(lo_h,2), round(hi_h,2)],
                              &quot;speed_mph&quot;:list(SPEED_MPH), &quot;score&quot;:round(r[&quot;score&quot;],2),
                              &quot;vertices&quot;:len(verts), &quot;features&quot;:len(plist),
                              &quot;of_available&quot;:len(allp), &quot;feature_mix&quot;:dict(mix),
                              &quot;unconfirmed_junctions&quot;:len(cautions),
                              &quot;retrace_pct&quot;:round(100*r[&quot;repeat&quot;],1)},
                   &quot;legs&quot;:legs, &quot;cautions&quot;:cautions, &quot;features&quot;:plist},
                  open(os.path.join(OUT,&quot;route_drafts&quot;,&quot;%s.highlights.json&quot;%name),&quot;w&quot;),
                  indent=1)
        for p in plist:
            wpts[p[&quot;name&quot;]] = (p[&quot;lat&quot;], p[&quot;lon&quot;],
                               &quot;water&quot; if p[&quot;fclass&quot;] in WATER else &quot;viewpoint&quot;,
                               &quot;Drinking Water&quot; if p[&quot;fclass&quot;] in WATER else &quot;Summit&quot;,
                               p[&quot;fclass&quot;])
        for c in cautions:
            wpts[&quot;CAUTION %.4f,%.4f&quot; % (c[&quot;lat&quot;], c[&quot;lon&quot;])] = (
                c[&quot;lat&quot;], c[&quot;lon&quot;], &quot;caution&quot;, &quot;Danger Area&quot;,
                &quot;Trails mapped %.0f ft apart - junction NOT confirmed. Zoom satellite.&quot;
                % c[&quot;gap_ft&quot;])
    g = [&#x27;&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;&#x27;,
         &#x27;&lt;gpx version=&quot;1.1&quot; creator=&quot;GroupTrack route research&quot; &#x27;
         &#x27;xmlns=&quot;http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1&quot;&gt;&#x27;,
         &#x27;&lt;metadata&gt;&lt;name&gt;%s waypoints&lt;/name&gt;&lt;/metadata&gt;&#x27; % SET_NAME]
    for nm,(la,lo,ty,sy,de) in sorted(wpts.items()):
        g.append(&#x27;&lt;wpt lat=&quot;%.6f&quot; lon=&quot;%.6f&quot;&gt;&lt;name&gt;%s&lt;/name&gt;&lt;type&gt;%s&lt;/type&gt;&#x27;
                 &#x27;&lt;sym&gt;%s&lt;/sym&gt;&lt;desc&gt;%s&lt;/desc&gt;&lt;/wpt&gt;&#x27;
                 % (la,lo,esc(nm),esc(ty),esc(sy),esc(de)))
    g.append(&#x27;&lt;/gpx&gt;&#x27;)
    gp = os.path.join(OUT, &quot;%s_waypoints_2026-08-22.gpx&quot; % SET_NAME.lower().replace(&quot; &quot;,&quot;_&quot;))
    open(gp,&quot;w&quot;,encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;).write(&quot;\n&quot;.join(g))
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;%d drafts + sidecars -&gt; %s\\route_drafts&quot; % (len(picks), OUT))
    print(&quot;%s  (%d waypoints)&quot; % (os.path.basename(gp), len(wpts)))
    print(&quot;\n1. WAYPOINTS FIRST:&quot;)
    print(&#x27;   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb -s 24039703201775 push &quot;%s&quot; /sdcard/Download/&#x27;
          % gp.replace(&quot;\\&quot;,&quot;/&quot;))
    print(&quot;2. THEN DRAFTS:&quot;)
    print(&#x27;   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb -s 24039703201775 push &quot;%s/route_drafts/.&quot; &#x27;
          &#x27;/sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/route_drafts/&#x27; % OUT.replace(&quot;\\&quot;,&quot;/&quot;))
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    con.close()
    return 0
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    main()
nav_pass4c_toroweap_2026-08-22.py
The FIXED-DESTINATION variant (start, must-visit, return). Kept because the points-included problem is still to be designed and this is the crude version of it — including the evidence of what the tether costs.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_pass4c_toroweap_2026-08-22.py
PASS 4 -- FIXED-POINT INCLUSIVE.  Bar 10 -&gt; Toroweap -&gt; Bar 10.
TWO CORRECTIONS FROM 3d, both structural.
1. RANK, DO NOT PRE-CONSTRAIN.  Fred: &quot;if we used typical navigation on its head
   and ranked the explored tracks by total distance and highest score we could
   then set the distance/time cutoff to that list.&quot;
   3d searched INSIDE a 55-70 band, and with a 53.7 mi fixed tether that band
   strangled the search before it could find anything. This explores across a
   wide distance range, scores everything, and RANKS. The rider&#x27;s time budget
   becomes a cutoff applied to the ranked list, not a constraint that shapes
   the search.
2. PENALISE, DO NOT FILTER.  3d generated 4,000 candidates, ranked them, then
   filtered for distinctness -- which on a corridor with a fixed spine leaves
   exactly one. Navigation apps do the opposite: find the best, PENALISE the
   edges it used, re-solve. The second route is then the best route that avoids
   the first. That is the difference between &quot;one answer and 3,999 rejects&quot; and
   &quot;four alternatives.&quot;
OBJECTIVE IS SCORE, NOT DISTANCE.  Miles are a budget, never a cost. Variety is
weighted: a second class of feature beats another of the same.
OUT: D:\\nav_test\\out\\route_drafts\\&lt;SET_NAME&gt; N.json  + .highlights.json
     D:\\nav_test\\out\\grouptrack_suggested_waypoints_2026-08-22.gpx
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import sqlite3, math, os, re, heapq, json, random, datetime
from collections import defaultdict, Counter, deque
DB  = r&quot;D:\nav_test\grouptrack_spatial.db&quot;
OUT = r&quot;D:\nav_test\out&quot;
SET_NAME = &quot;Toroweap&quot;          # -&gt; &quot;Toroweap 1&quot;..&quot;Toroweap 4&quot;
BAR10, TOROWEAP = (36.43, -113.35), (36.20, -113.07)
EXPLORE_MAX = 80.0             # ceiling (Fred 08-22: lowered from 200)
N_ROUTES    = 4
TRIES       = 2500
PENALTY     = 2.2              # multiplier on edges already used by a chosen route
REPORT_CUTS = [60, 65, 70, 75, 80]
SNAP_FT, CAUTION_FT, POI_BUF_MI = 25.0, 10.0, 0.5
SPEED_MPH = (12.0, 18.0)
LAT_S, LAT_N, LON_W, LON_E = 35.95, 36.65, -113.80, -112.80
NONAMES = {&quot;&quot;, &quot;not named&quot;, &quot;unnamed&quot;, &quot;none&quot;, &quot;null&quot;, &quot;n/a&quot;, &quot;-&quot;}
WATER, VIEW = {&quot;spring&quot;}, {&quot;peak&quot;, &quot;cliff&quot;, &quot;volcano&quot;}
random.seed(20260822)
def hav(a, b):
    R = 3958.8
    p1, p2 = math.radians(a[0]), math.radians(b[0])
    dp = p2-p1; dl = math.radians(b[1]-a[1])
    h = math.sin(dp/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dl/2)**2
    return 2*R*math.asin(math.sqrt(h))
def wkt_points(w):
    if not w: return []
    return [(float(a), float(b)) for b, a in
            re.findall(r&#x27;(-?\d+\.?\d*)\s+(-?\d+\.?\d*)&#x27;, w)]
def real_name(n):
    return bool(n) and str(n).strip().lower() not in NONAMES
def esc(s):
    return (str(s).replace(&quot;&amp;&quot;,&quot;&amp;amp;&quot;).replace(&quot;&lt;&quot;,&quot;&amp;lt;&quot;)
            .replace(&quot;&gt;&quot;,&quot;&amp;gt;&quot;).replace(&#x27;&quot;&#x27;,&quot;&amp;quot;&quot;))
def main():
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(OUT, &quot;route_drafts&quot;), exist_ok=True)
    con = sqlite3.connect(&quot;file:%s?mode=ro&quot; % DB.replace(&quot;\\&quot;,&quot;/&quot;), uri=True)
    cur = con.cursor()
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;PASS 4 -- EXPLORE THEN RANK   %s   explore to %.0f mi&quot;
          % (SET_NAME, EXPLORE_MAX))
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    geoms = []
    for tid, nm, wkt in cur.execute(
            &quot;SELECT trail_id,name,geometry FROM trails WHERE min_lat&lt;=? AND max_lat&gt;=? &quot;
            &quot;AND min_lon&lt;=? AND max_lon&gt;=?&quot;, (LAT_N, LAT_S, LON_E, LON_W)):
        p = wkt_points(wkt)
        if len(p) &gt;= 2: geoms.append((tid, nm, p))
    d_ = (SNAP_FT/5280.0)/69.0
    def key(p): return (int(round(p[0]/d_)), int(round(p[1]/d_)))
    touch, spread = defaultdict(set), defaultdict(list)
    for tid, nm, pts in geoms:
        for p in pts:
            k = key(p); touch[k].add(tid); spread[k].append(p)
    shared = {k for k, s in touch.items() if len(s) &gt; 1}
    gap_ft = {}
    for k in shared:
        ps = spread[k]; g = 0.0
        for i in range(len(ps)):
            for j in range(i+1, min(len(ps), i+6)):
                g = max(g, hav(ps[i], ps[j])*5280)
        gap_ft[k] = g
    edges, nodes = [], {}
    for tid, nm, pts in geoms:
        cuts = sorted(set([0, len(pts)-1] +
                          [i for i in range(1, len(pts)-1) if key(pts[i]) in shared]))
        for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:]):
            seg = pts[a:b+1]
            if len(seg) &lt; 2: continue
            L = sum(hav(seg[i], seg[i+1]) for i in range(len(seg)-1))
            if L &lt;= 0.0005: continue
            ka, kb = key(seg[0]), key(seg[-1])
            if ka == kb: continue
            nodes.setdefault(ka, seg[0]); nodes.setdefault(kb, seg[-1])
            edges.append((ka, kb, L, (nm if real_name(nm) else None), tid, seg))
    adj = defaultdict(list)
    for i, e in enumerate(edges):
        adj[e[0]].append((e[1], i)); adj[e[1]].append((e[0], i))
    seen, comps = set(), []
    for n in adj:
        if n in seen: continue
        q, c = deque([n]), []; seen.add(n)
        while q:
            x = q.popleft(); c.append(x)
            for y, _ in adj[x]:
                if y not in seen: seen.add(y); q.append(y)
        comps.append(c)
    comps.sort(key=len, reverse=True); main_c = set(comps[0])
    def nearest(pt):
        best, bd = None, 1e9
        for k in main_c:
            v = hav(pt, nodes[k])
            if v &lt; bd: bd, best = v, k
        return best, bd
    n_bar, _ = nearest(BAR10); n_tor, _ = nearest(TOROWEAP)
    poi_at = {}
    for nm, fc, la, lo in cur.execute(
            &quot;SELECT name,fclass,lat,lon FROM reference_points WHERE lat BETWEEN ? AND ? &quot;
            &quot;AND lon BETWEEN ? AND ?&quot;, (LAT_S, LAT_N, LON_W, LON_E)):
        k, v = nearest((la, lo))
        if v &lt;= POI_BUF_MI:
            poi_at.setdefault(k, []).append({&quot;name&quot;: nm, &quot;fclass&quot;: fc,
                                             &quot;lat&quot;: la, &quot;lon&quot;: lo, &quot;off_mi&quot;: round(v,3)})
    allp = [p for v in poi_at.values() for p in v]
    print(&quot;network %d edges / %d nodes;  %d POIs at %d nodes&quot;
          % (len(edges), len(adj), len(allp), len(poi_at)))
    terms = [n_bar, n_tor] + [k for k in poi_at if k not in (n_bar, n_tor)]
    def dij(s, pen):
        dist={s:0.0}; prev={}; pq=[(0.0,s)]
        while pq:
            d0,x = heapq.heappop(pq)
            if d0 &gt; dist.get(x,1e18): continue
            for y,ei in adj[x]:
                w = edges[ei][2] * pen.get(ei, 1.0)
                nd = d0 + w
                if nd &lt; dist.get(y,1e18):
                    dist[y]=nd; prev[y]=(x,ei); heapq.heappush(pq,(nd,y))
        return dist, prev
    def build_tables(pen):
        D, P = {}, {}
        for t in terms: D[t], P[t] = dij(t, pen)
        return D, P
    def pe(P, s, t):
        out, x = [], t
        while x != s:
            if x not in P[s]: return None
            px, ei = P[s][x]; out.append(ei); x = px
        out.reverse(); return out
    def setscore(ks):
        seenn, byc, v = set(), Counter(), 0.0
        for k in ks:
            for p in poi_at[k]:
                if p[&quot;name&quot;] in seenn: continue
                seenn.add(p[&quot;name&quot;]); byc[p[&quot;fclass&quot;]] += 1
                b = 3.0 if p[&quot;fclass&quot;] in VIEW else 2.0 if p[&quot;fclass&quot;] in WATER else 1.0
                v += b / (1.0 + 0.22*(byc[p[&quot;fclass&quot;]]-1))
        return v
    def explore(D, P, pen):
        &quot;&quot;&quot;Randomised greedy, NO mileage band -- explore to EXPLORE_MAX and let
        ranking sort it out afterwards.&quot;&quot;&quot;
        found = []
        pn = [k for k in poi_at if D[n_bar].get(k) is not None]
        for _ in range(TRIES):
            # each restart gets its OWN target, so the pool spans the range.
            # without this the greedy always runs to the ceiling and every route
            # comes out the same length -- which is why the ranked table read
            # &quot;none&quot; at every cutoff below the max.
            target = random.uniform(EXPLORE_MAX * 0.62, EXPLORE_MAX)
            chosen, cur_n, mi, phase, endn = [], n_bar, 0.0, 0, n_tor
            left = set(pn)
            while True:
                cands = []
                for k in left:
                    s1 = D[cur_n].get(k); back = D[k].get(endn)
                    if s1 is None or back is None: continue
                    if mi + s1 + back &gt; target * (0.55 if phase == 0 else 1.0):
                        continue
                    g = setscore(chosen + [k]) - setscore(chosen)
                    if g &lt;= 0: continue
                    cands.append((g / max(s1, 0.35), k, s1))
                if not cands:
                    if phase == 0:
                        st = D[cur_n].get(n_tor)
                        if st is None: break
                        mi += st; cur_n = n_tor; phase, endn = 1, n_bar; continue
                    break
                cands.sort(reverse=True)
                _, k, s1 = cands[min(int(random.random()**2 * 5), len(cands)-1)]
                mi += s1; cur_n = k; chosen.append(k); left.discard(k)
            if phase == 0:
                st = D[cur_n].get(n_tor)
                if st is None: continue
                mi += st; cur_n = n_tor
            fin = D[cur_n].get(n_bar)
            if fin is None: continue
            seq = [n_bar] + chosen[:]
            if n_tor not in seq: seq.append(n_tor)
            seq.append(n_bar)
            eids, ok = [], True
            for a, b in zip(seq, seq[1:]):
                q = pe(P, a, b)
                if q is None: ok = False; break
                eids.extend(q)
            if not ok: continue
            real_mi = sum(edges[e][2] for e in eids)
            if real_mi &gt; EXPLORE_MAX: continue
            found.append({&quot;seq&quot;: seq, &quot;eids&quot;: eids, &quot;eset&quot;: set(eids),
                          &quot;miles&quot;: real_mi, &quot;score&quot;: setscore(chosen),
                          &quot;chosen&quot;: chosen})
        return found
    print(&quot;\nexploring (no mileage band)...&quot;)
    pen = {}
    D, P = build_tables(pen)
    pool = explore(D, P, pen)
    print(&quot;routes explored: %d&quot; % len(pool))
    if not pool:
        print(&quot;nothing found&quot;); return 3
    # ── the ranked table: what distance BUYS ────────────────────────
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;RANKED -- best score available at each distance cutoff&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;%-10s %10s %8s %8s   %s&quot; % (&quot;cutoff&quot;, &quot;miles&quot;, &quot;score&quot;, &quot;feats&quot;, &quot;mix&quot;))
    for cutm in REPORT_CUTS:
        sub = [r for r in pool if r[&quot;miles&quot;] &lt;= cutm]
        if not sub: 
            print(&quot;%-10s %10s&quot; % (&quot;&lt;= %d mi&quot; % cutm, &quot;none&quot;)); continue
        b = max(sub, key=lambda r: r[&quot;score&quot;])
        names = {p[&quot;name&quot;]: p[&quot;fclass&quot;] for k in b[&quot;chosen&quot;] for p in poi_at[k]}
        mix = Counter(names.values())
        print(&quot;%-10s %9.1f %8.1f %8d   %s&quot;
              % (&quot;&lt;= %d mi&quot; % cutm, b[&quot;miles&quot;], b[&quot;score&quot;], len(names),
                 &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s %d&quot; % (a_,b_) for a_,b_ in mix.most_common())))
    # ── four alternatives by iterative penalty ──────────────────────
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;FOUR ALTERNATIVES (each penalised away from the ones before)&quot;)
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    picks = []
    for i in range(N_ROUTES):
        if i &gt; 0:
            for e in picks[-1][&quot;eset&quot;]:
                pen[e] = pen.get(e, 1.0) * PENALTY
            D, P = build_tables(pen)
            pool = explore(D, P, pen)
            if not pool:
                print(&quot;  (no further alternative found)&quot;); break
        # POSITIVE SCORE FLOOR (Fred 08-22): a route with no features is not a
        # suggestion. The iterative penalty eventually makes every scoring
        # corridor too expensive and the search returns the best REMAINING route,
        # which visits nothing -- Toroweap 3 and 4 both came back score 0.0.
        # Better to return two good routes than pad to four.
        cand = [r for r in pool
                if r[&quot;score&quot;] &gt; 0.0
                and all(len(r[&quot;eset&quot;] &amp; q[&quot;eset&quot;])/max(len(r[&quot;eset&quot;] | q[&quot;eset&quot;]),1) &lt; 0.75
                        for q in picks)]
        if not cand:
            print(&quot;  (no further alternative with a positive score)&quot;); break
        b = max(cand, key=lambda r: r[&quot;score&quot;])
        b[&quot;repeat&quot;] = 1.0 - len(b[&quot;eset&quot;])/max(len(b[&quot;eids&quot;]),1)
        picks.append(b)
        print(&quot;  %s %d: %.1f mi, score %.1f&quot; % (SET_NAME, i+1, b[&quot;miles&quot;], b[&quot;score&quot;]))
    # ── emit ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(&quot;%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ&quot;)
    wpts = {}
    for idx, r in enumerate(picks, 1):
        verts, legs, caut = [], [], {}
        cum, prev_name, leg_start, leg_pois = 0.0, None, 0.0, []
        seenpoi, plist = set(), []
        for e in r[&quot;eids&quot;]:
            a, b, L, nm, tid, seg = edges[e]
            s = seg
            if verts and hav((verts[-1][&quot;lat&quot;], verts[-1][&quot;lon&quot;]), s[0]) &gt; \
                         hav((verts[-1][&quot;lat&quot;], verts[-1][&quot;lon&quot;]), s[-1]):
                s = s[::-1]
            for j, p in enumerate(s):
                if verts and j == 0: continue
                verts.append({&quot;lat&quot;: round(p[0],6), &quot;lon&quot;: round(p[1],6),
                              &quot;lineId&quot;: tid, &quot;lineType&quot;: &quot;trail&quot;,
                              &quot;segmentIndex&quot;: -1, &quot;t&quot;: 0.0, &quot;snapped&quot;: True})
            lbl = nm or &quot;unnamed track&quot;
            if lbl != prev_name:
                if prev_name is not None:
                    legs.append({&quot;trail&quot;: prev_name, &quot;from_mi&quot;: round(leg_start,2),
                                 &quot;to_mi&quot;: round(cum,2),
                                 &quot;miles&quot;: round(cum-leg_start,2), &quot;pois&quot;: leg_pois})
                prev_name, leg_start, leg_pois = lbl, cum, []
            cum += L
            for k in (a, b):
                for p in poi_at.get(k, []):
                    if p[&quot;name&quot;] in seenpoi: continue
                    seenpoi.add(p[&quot;name&quot;]); plist.append(p)
                    leg_pois.append({&quot;name&quot;: p[&quot;name&quot;], &quot;fclass&quot;: p[&quot;fclass&quot;],
                                     &quot;at_mi&quot;: round(cum,2), &quot;off_mi&quot;: p[&quot;off_mi&quot;]})
                g = gap_ft.get(k, 0.0)
                if g &gt; CAUTION_FT and k not in caut:
                    caut[k] = {&quot;at_mi&quot;: round(cum,2), &quot;gap_ft&quot;: round(g,1),
                               &quot;lat&quot;: round(nodes[k][0],6), &quot;lon&quot;: round(nodes[k][1],6)}
        if prev_name is not None:
            legs.append({&quot;trail&quot;: prev_name, &quot;from_mi&quot;: round(leg_start,2),
                         &quot;to_mi&quot;: round(cum,2), &quot;miles&quot;: round(cum-leg_start,2),
                         &quot;pois&quot;: leg_pois})
        cautions = sorted(caut.values(), key=lambda c: c[&quot;at_mi&quot;])
        lo_h, hi_h = r[&quot;miles&quot;]/SPEED_MPH[1], r[&quot;miles&quot;]/SPEED_MPH[0]
        name = &quot;%s %d&quot; % (SET_NAME, idx)
        mix = Counter(p[&quot;fclass&quot;] for p in plist)
        print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;-&quot;*78)
        print(&quot;%s      %.1f miles      %.1f-%.1f hours      score %.1f&quot;
              % (name, r[&quot;miles&quot;], lo_h, hi_h, r[&quot;score&quot;]))
        print(&quot;-&quot;*78)
        print(&quot;  %d of %d features (%s)   %d vertices   %d cautions   %.0f%% retrace&quot;
              % (len(plist), len(allp),
                 &quot;, &quot;.join(&quot;%s %d&quot; % (a_,b_) for a_,b_ in mix.most_common()),
                 len(verts), len(cautions), 100*r[&quot;repeat&quot;]))
        for p in plist:
            print(&quot;      %-9s %-28s mile %.1f&quot; %
                  (p[&quot;fclass&quot;], p[&quot;name&quot;][:28],
                   next((q[&quot;at_mi&quot;] for lg in legs for q in lg[&quot;pois&quot;]
                         if q[&quot;name&quot;] == p[&quot;name&quot;]), 0)))
        print(&quot;  named trail legs over 1 mi:&quot;)
        for lg in legs:
            if lg[&quot;miles&quot;] &lt; 1.0 or lg[&quot;trail&quot;] == &quot;unnamed track&quot;: continue
            print(&quot;    %5.1f-%5.1f  %-32s %4.1f mi&quot;
                  % (lg[&quot;from_mi&quot;], lg[&quot;to_mi&quot;], lg[&quot;trail&quot;][:32], lg[&quot;miles&quot;]))
        print(&quot;  unconfirmed junctions: %d&quot; % len(cautions))
        json.dump({&quot;schemaVersion&quot;:1, &quot;name&quot;:name, &quot;createdAt&quot;:now, &quot;updatedAt&quot;:now,
                   &quot;method&quot;:&quot;point&quot;, &quot;vertices&quot;:verts},
                  open(os.path.join(OUT,&quot;route_drafts&quot;,&quot;%s.json&quot;%name),&quot;w&quot;))
        json.dump({&quot;name&quot;:name, &quot;generated&quot;:now,
                   &quot;summary&quot;:{&quot;total_miles&quot;:round(r[&quot;miles&quot;],2),
                              &quot;est_hours&quot;:[round(lo_h,2), round(hi_h,2)],
                              &quot;speed_mph&quot;:list(SPEED_MPH), &quot;score&quot;:round(r[&quot;score&quot;],2),
                              &quot;vertices&quot;:len(verts), &quot;features&quot;:len(plist),
                              &quot;of_available&quot;:len(allp), &quot;feature_mix&quot;:dict(mix),
                              &quot;unconfirmed_junctions&quot;:len(cautions),
                              &quot;retrace_pct&quot;:round(100*r[&quot;repeat&quot;],1)},
                   &quot;legs&quot;:legs, &quot;cautions&quot;:cautions, &quot;features&quot;:plist},
                  open(os.path.join(OUT,&quot;route_drafts&quot;,&quot;%s.highlights.json&quot;%name),&quot;w&quot;),
                  indent=1)
        for p in plist:
            wpts[p[&quot;name&quot;]] = (p[&quot;lat&quot;], p[&quot;lon&quot;],
                               &quot;water&quot; if p[&quot;fclass&quot;] in WATER else &quot;viewpoint&quot;,
                               &quot;Drinking Water&quot; if p[&quot;fclass&quot;] in WATER else &quot;Summit&quot;,
                               p[&quot;fclass&quot;])
        for c in cautions:
            wpts[&quot;CAUTION %.4f,%.4f&quot; % (c[&quot;lat&quot;], c[&quot;lon&quot;])] = (
                c[&quot;lat&quot;], c[&quot;lon&quot;], &quot;caution&quot;, &quot;Danger Area&quot;,
                &quot;Trails mapped %.0f ft apart - junction NOT confirmed. Zoom satellite.&quot;
                % c[&quot;gap_ft&quot;])
    g = [&#x27;&lt;?xml version=&quot;1.0&quot; encoding=&quot;UTF-8&quot;?&gt;&#x27;,
         &#x27;&lt;gpx version=&quot;1.1&quot; creator=&quot;GroupTrack route research&quot; &#x27;
         &#x27;xmlns=&quot;http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/1&quot;&gt;&#x27;,
         &#x27;&lt;metadata&gt;&lt;name&gt;%s waypoints&lt;/name&gt;&lt;/metadata&gt;&#x27; % SET_NAME]
    for nm,(la,lo,ty,sy,de) in sorted(wpts.items()):
        g.append(&#x27;&lt;wpt lat=&quot;%.6f&quot; lon=&quot;%.6f&quot;&gt;&lt;name&gt;%s&lt;/name&gt;&lt;type&gt;%s&lt;/type&gt;&#x27;
                 &#x27;&lt;sym&gt;%s&lt;/sym&gt;&lt;desc&gt;%s&lt;/desc&gt;&lt;/wpt&gt;&#x27;
                 % (la,lo,esc(nm),esc(ty),esc(sy),esc(de)))
    g.append(&#x27;&lt;/gpx&gt;&#x27;)
    gp = os.path.join(OUT, &quot;%s_waypoints_2026-08-22.gpx&quot; % SET_NAME.lower().replace(&quot; &quot;,&quot;_&quot;))
    open(gp,&quot;w&quot;,encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;).write(&quot;\n&quot;.join(g))
    print(&quot;\n&quot; + &quot;=&quot;*78)
    print(&quot;%d drafts + sidecars -&gt; %s\\route_drafts&quot; % (len(picks), OUT))
    print(&quot;%s  (%d waypoints)&quot; % (os.path.basename(gp), len(wpts)))
    print(&quot;\n1. WAYPOINTS FIRST:&quot;)
    print(&#x27;   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb -s 24039703201775 push &quot;%s&quot; /sdcard/Download/&#x27;
          % gp.replace(&quot;\\&quot;,&quot;/&quot;))
    print(&quot;2. THEN DRAFTS:&quot;)
    print(&#x27;   MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 adb -s 24039703201775 push &quot;%s/route_drafts/.&quot; &#x27;
          &#x27;/sdcard/Documents/GroupTrack/route_drafts/&#x27; % OUT.replace(&quot;\\&quot;,&quot;/&quot;))
    print(&quot;=&quot;*78)
    con.close()
    return 0
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    main()
nav_sidecar_narrative_v2_2026-08-22.py
Turns the sidecar into something a rider reads. Groups co-located features, scales the retrace warning to the actual figure.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_sidecar_narrative_v2_2026-08-22.py
Rewrite the existing sidecars with something a RIDER can read.
Fred, 08-22: &quot;nothing human readable here about feature and poi on this route.
needs to point to what&#x27;s in this ride.&quot;
He is right -- the sidecar was machine-shaped. Nested from_mi / off_mi / fclass
is data for a popup that does not exist yet, not something you read to decide
whether to ride it.
This adds a `narrative` block ALONGSIDE the structured fields. Nothing is
removed: the structured data is what the popup will eventually render and what
the waypoints get created from; the narrative is what you read today.
⚠ NOTE, worth keeping: storing generated prose in a file is a compromise. If the
route is edited, the narrative describes a route the rider no longer has. The
right long-term answer is to GENERATE this at display time from the structured
fields. It is written here because the sidecar is currently the only consumer.
⚠ WAYPOINTS: to be created when the WIP is written, once that code exists (Fred
08-22). GPX waypoint import is currently not working, so the sidecar carries
name / lat / lon / type / mile for each feature and the app creates them later.
Reads and rewrites, in place:
    D:\\nav_test\\out\\route_drafts\\Toroweap 1.highlights.json
    D:\\nav_test\\out\\route_drafts\\Toroweap 2.highlights.json
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import json, os, glob
from collections import Counter
DIR = r&quot;D:\nav_test\out\route_drafts&quot;
WATER = {&quot;spring&quot;}
VIEW  = {&quot;peak&quot;, &quot;cliff&quot;, &quot;volcano&quot;}
PLAIN = {&quot;peak&quot;: &quot;summit&quot;, &quot;cliff&quot;: &quot;cliff&quot;, &quot;volcano&quot;: &quot;volcanic cone&quot;,
         &quot;spring&quot;: &quot;spring&quot;, &quot;hamlet&quot;: &quot;settlement&quot;, &quot;locality&quot;: &quot;locality&quot;}
def ordinal_list(items):
    if not items:
        return &quot;&quot;
    if len(items) == 1:
        return items[0]
    return &quot;, &quot;.join(items[:-1]) + &quot; and &quot; + items[-1]
def narrate(d):
    s = d[&quot;summary&quot;]
    feats = d.get(&quot;features&quot;, [])
    legs = d.get(&quot;legs&quot;, [])
    cauts = d.get(&quot;cautions&quot;, [])
    miles = s[&quot;total_miles&quot;]
    lo, hi = s[&quot;est_hours&quot;]
    mix = Counter(f[&quot;fclass&quot;] for f in feats)
    # what is on this ride, in plain words
    bits = []
    for fc, n in mix.most_common():
        word = PLAIN.get(fc, fc)
        bits.append(&quot;%d %s%s&quot; % (n, word, &quot;s&quot; if n &gt; 1 and not word.endswith(&quot;s&quot;) else &quot;&quot;))
    headline = (&quot;%.0f miles, roughly %.0f to %.0f hours of riding. &quot;
                &quot;%s along the way.&quot;
                % (miles, lo, hi, ordinal_list(bits).capitalize() if bits else &quot;No named features&quot;))
    # where each feature sits, by mile
    at_mi = {}
    for lg in legs:
        for p in lg.get(&quot;pois&quot;, []):
            at_mi[p[&quot;name&quot;]] = p[&quot;at_mi&quot;]
    seq = sorted(feats, key=lambda f: at_mi.get(f[&quot;name&quot;], 0))
    # group features that sit at the same point -- &quot;Oak Spring and Aspen Spring,
    # both at mile 28.7&quot; reads better than two separate stops at one place.
    stops, i = [], 0
    while i &lt; len(seq):
        f = seq[i]
        m = at_mi.get(f[&quot;name&quot;], 0)
        same = [f]
        while i+1 &lt; len(seq) and abs(at_mi.get(seq[i+1][&quot;name&quot;], 0) - m) &lt; 0.15:
            i += 1; same.append(seq[i])
        off = f.get(&quot;off_mi&quot;, 0)
        near = &quot;&quot; if off &lt;= 0.05 else (&quot; (%.0f yards off the trail)&quot; % (off * 1760))
        if len(same) == 1:
            stops.append(&quot;mile %.0f  %s -- %s%s&quot;
                         % (m, f[&quot;name&quot;], PLAIN.get(f[&quot;fclass&quot;], f[&quot;fclass&quot;]), near))
        else:
            stops.append(&quot;mile %.0f  %s -- together at the same spot&quot;
                         % (m, ordinal_list([x[&quot;name&quot;] for x in same])))
        i += 1
    # the named ground it uses
    named = {}
    for lg in legs:
        t = lg[&quot;trail&quot;]
        if t and t != &quot;unnamed track&quot;:
            named[t] = named.get(t, 0) + lg[&quot;miles&quot;]
    named_txt = ordinal_list([&quot;%s (%.0f mi)&quot; % (k, v) for k, v in
                              sorted(named.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5]])
    unnamed_mi = sum(lg[&quot;miles&quot;] for lg in legs if lg[&quot;trail&quot;] == &quot;unnamed track&quot;)
    pct_unnamed = 100.0 * unnamed_mi / max(miles, 1)
    warn = []
    r = s.get(&quot;retrace_pct&quot;, 0)
    if r &gt; 40:
        warn.append(&quot;About %.0f%% of the ride retraces ground you have already &quot;
                    &quot;covered. Much of the way back is the way out -- the trail &quot;
                    &quot;network here does not close into a loop.&quot; % r)
    elif r &gt; 20:
        warn.append(&quot;About %.0f%% of the ride doubles back on itself, usually a &quot;
                    &quot;short out-and-back to reach something worth seeing.&quot; % r)
    if cauts:
        worst = max(c[&quot;gap_ft&quot;] for c in cauts)
        warn.append(&quot;%d junctions on this route are not confirmed in the map data. &quot;
                    &quot;The two trails are drawn between 10 and %.0f feet apart, which &quot;
                    &quot;usually means they meet -- but check the satellite view before &quot;
                    &quot;relying on the turn.&quot; % (len(cauts), worst))
    if pct_unnamed &gt; 50:
        warn.append(&quot;%.0f%% of the distance is on tracks with no name in the data. &quot;
                    &quot;They are real tracks; nobody has recorded what they are called.&quot;
                    % pct_unnamed)
    return {
        &quot;headline&quot;: headline,
        &quot;what_you_will_see&quot;: [
            &quot;%s%s&quot; % (f[&quot;name&quot;], &quot; -- %s&quot; % PLAIN.get(f[&quot;fclass&quot;], f[&quot;fclass&quot;]))
            for f in seq],
        &quot;stops_in_order&quot;: stops,
        &quot;ground_covered&quot;: (&quot;Named trail: %s. The rest -- %.0f of %.0f miles -- is &quot;
                           &quot;unnamed track.&quot; % (named_txt or &quot;none&quot;,
                                               unnamed_mi, miles))
                          if named else
                          (&quot;All %.0f miles are on tracks with no name in the data.&quot;
                           % miles),
        &quot;before_you_go&quot;: warn,
        &quot;waypoints_to_create&quot;: [
            {&quot;name&quot;: f[&quot;name&quot;],
             &quot;type&quot;: &quot;water&quot; if f[&quot;fclass&quot;] in WATER else &quot;viewpoint&quot;,
             &quot;lat&quot;: f[&quot;lat&quot;], &quot;lon&quot;: f[&quot;lon&quot;],
             &quot;at_mile&quot;: at_mi.get(f[&quot;name&quot;], 0)}
            for f in seq],
    }
def main():
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(DIR, &quot;*.highlights.json&quot;)))
    if not files:
        print(&quot;no sidecars found in %s&quot; % DIR); return 1
    for path in files:
        d = json.load(open(path, encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;))
        d[&quot;narrative&quot;] = narrate(d)
        json.dump(d, open(path, &quot;w&quot;, encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;), indent=1)
        n = d[&quot;narrative&quot;]
        print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
        print(os.path.basename(path))
        print(&quot;=&quot; * 74)
        print(&quot;\n  %s\n&quot; % n[&quot;headline&quot;])
        print(&quot;  WHAT YOU WILL SEE&quot;)
        for x in n[&quot;what_you_will_see&quot;]:
            print(&quot;    %s&quot; % x)
        print(&quot;\n  IN ORDER&quot;)
        for x in n[&quot;stops_in_order&quot;]:
            print(&quot;    %s&quot; % x)
        print(&quot;\n  GROUND COVERED&quot;)
        print(&quot;    %s&quot; % n[&quot;ground_covered&quot;])
        if n[&quot;before_you_go&quot;]:
            print(&quot;\n  BEFORE YOU GO&quot;)
            for x in n[&quot;before_you_go&quot;]:
                print(&quot;    - %s&quot; % x)
        print(&quot;\n  waypoints to create on promotion: %d&quot;
              % len(n[&quot;waypoints_to_create&quot;]))
        print()
    return 0
if __name__ == &quot;__main__&quot;:
    raise SystemExit(main())
nav_check_draft_2026-08-22.py
Diagnostic: reads an emitted draft and separates stitching errors (big steps AT trail switches) from sparse source geometry (big steps WITHIN one trail). This is what proved the straight lines were not my stitching.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_check_draft_2026-08-22.py
Read the emitted draft and find out whether the straight lines over empty
ground are a stitching error in my geometry or something on the planner side.
Fred saw: &quot;straight lines crossing wide areas with zero trails&quot; and
&quot;lots of criss-crossing&quot;.
MY SUSPICION, to be confirmed or killed by this: when consecutive edges in the
Dijkstra path are stitched, I flip each segment to match the previous endpoint.
If two consecutive edges do not actually share a vertex -- because the path was
found in the SNAPPED graph while the emitted geometry is RAW -- the vertex list
jumps, and the planner draws a straight line across the jump.
If the largest gaps are miles, it is my stitching. If they are all under a few
hundred feet, the cause is elsewhere and I look at the planner.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import json, math, os, sys
FILES = [r&quot;D:\nav_test\out\route_drafts\Toroweap 1.json&quot;,
         r&quot;D:\nav_test\out\route_drafts\Toroweap 2.json&quot;]
def ft(a, b):
    R = 20902231.0          # earth radius in feet
    p1, p2 = math.radians(a[0]), math.radians(b[0])
    dp = p2 - p1
    dl = math.radians(b[1] - a[1])
    x = math.sin(dp/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dl/2)**2
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(x))
for path in FILES:
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        print(&quot;missing: %s&quot; % path); continue
    d = json.load(open(path, encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;))
    v = d.get(&quot;vertices&quot;, [])
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(os.path.basename(path))
    print(&quot;=&quot; * 70)
    print(&quot;  name        : %s&quot; % d.get(&quot;name&quot;))
    print(&quot;  schema      : %s   method: %s&quot; % (d.get(&quot;schemaVersion&quot;), d.get(&quot;method&quot;)))
    print(&quot;  vertices    : %d&quot; % len(v))
    if len(v) &lt; 2:
        continue
    gaps = []
    for i in range(len(v) - 1):
        g = ft((v[i][&quot;lat&quot;], v[i][&quot;lon&quot;]), (v[i+1][&quot;lat&quot;], v[i+1][&quot;lon&quot;]))
        gaps.append((g, i))
    total = sum(g for g, _ in gaps)
    gaps.sort(reverse=True)
    print(&quot;  path length : %.1f mi   (%.0f ft)&quot; % (total/5280.0, total))
    print(&quot;  median step : %.1f ft&quot; % sorted(g for g, _ in gaps)[len(gaps)//2])
    over = lambda n: sum(1 for g, _ in gaps if g &gt; n)
    print(&quot;  steps over  200ft: %d   500ft: %d   0.25mi: %d   1mi: %d&quot;
          % (over(200), over(500), over(1320), over(5280)))
    jump_ft = sum(g for g, _ in gaps if g &gt; 500)
    print(&quot;  miles inside jumps over 500 ft: %.1f  (%.0f%% of the route)&quot;
          % (jump_ft/5280.0, 100.0*jump_ft/total))
    print(&quot;\n  largest steps:&quot;)
    for g, i in gaps[:15]:
        a, b = v[i], v[i+1]
        same = &quot;same trail&quot; if a.get(&quot;lineId&quot;) == b.get(&quot;lineId&quot;) else &quot;TRAIL CHANGE&quot;
        print(&quot;    %9.0f ft  idx %5d  %.5f,%.5f -&gt; %.5f,%.5f  %s&quot;
              % (g, i, a[&quot;lat&quot;], a[&quot;lon&quot;], b[&quot;lat&quot;], b[&quot;lon&quot;], same))
    # how many distinct trails, and how often it switches
    switches = sum(1 for i in range(len(v)-1)
                   if v[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;) != v[i+1].get(&quot;lineId&quot;))
    trails = len({x.get(&quot;lineId&quot;) for x in v})
    print(&quot;\n  distinct lineIds: %d   trail switches: %d&quot; % (trails, switches))
    # are the big steps AT trail switches? that is the stitching signature
    bigsw = sum(1 for g, i in gaps if g &gt; 500 and
                v[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;) != v[i+1].get(&quot;lineId&quot;))
    bigsame = sum(1 for g, i in gaps if g &gt; 500 and
                  v[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;) == v[i+1].get(&quot;lineId&quot;))
    print(&quot;  steps over 500ft AT a trail switch : %d&quot; % bigsw)
    print(&quot;  steps over 500ft WITHIN one trail  : %d&quot; % bigsame)
    print(&quot;\n  READ: big steps at trail switches = my stitching (edges that do&quot;)
    print(&quot;  not share a vertex). Big steps within one trail = the source&quot;)
    print(&quot;  geometry itself is sparse there, which is the data, not the code.&quot;)
    print()
nav_compare_after_2026-08-22.py
Diagnostic: compares a draft before and after the planner opened it. This is what found the single stray vertex that added 30 miles, and proved snap-2 does NOT rewrite our geometry.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
&quot;&quot;&quot;
nav_compare_after_2026-08-22.py
The planner rewrote the draft: 662,973 -&gt; 596,024 bytes. Find out what it did.
Three things worth knowing:
  1. Did it DROP vertices, or change their fields?
  2. Did it MOVE any -- and how far? That is snap-2 pulling points onto trails.
  3. Did lineId survive, or did it re-snap to a different trail?
The third matters most. If our vertices were re-snapped to a NEIGHBOURING track
rather than the one we chose, the route on screen is not the route we computed,
and that would explain lines wandering across ground with no trail on it.
&quot;&quot;&quot;
import json, math, os
from collections import Counter
BEFORE = r&quot;D:\nav_test\out\route_drafts\Toroweap 1.json&quot;
AFTER  = r&quot;D:\nav_test\after\Toroweap 1.json&quot;
def ft(a, b):
    R = 20902231.0
    p1, p2 = math.radians(a[0]), math.radians(b[0])
    dp = p2 - p1
    dl = math.radians(b[1] - a[1])
    x = math.sin(dp/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dl/2)**2
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(x))
for p in (BEFORE, AFTER):
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        print(&quot;missing: %s&quot; % p); raise SystemExit(1)
b = json.load(open(BEFORE, encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;))
a = json.load(open(AFTER, encoding=&quot;utf-8&quot;))
vb, va = b[&quot;vertices&quot;], a[&quot;vertices&quot;]
print(&quot;=&quot; * 72)
print(&quot;BEFORE (written by the research script) vs AFTER (rewritten by the app)&quot;)
print(&quot;=&quot; * 72)
print(&quot;  vertices      %6d  -&gt;  %6d   (%+d)&quot; % (len(vb), len(va), len(va)-len(vb)))
for k in (&quot;schemaVersion&quot;, &quot;name&quot;, &quot;method&quot;, &quot;createdAt&quot;, &quot;updatedAt&quot;):
    print(&quot;  %-13s %-24s -&gt; %s&quot; % (k, b.get(k), a.get(k)))
# field-level: what keys does each vertex carry now?
kb = Counter(tuple(sorted(x.keys())) for x in vb)
ka = Counter(tuple(sorted(x.keys())) for x in va)
print(&quot;\n  vertex keys BEFORE: %s&quot; % (list(kb)[0],))
print(&quot;  vertex keys AFTER : %s&quot; % (list(ka)[0],))
for fld in (&quot;snapped&quot;, &quot;lineType&quot;):
    print(&quot;  %-9s before: %s&quot; % (fld, Counter(x.get(fld) for x in vb).most_common()))
    print(&quot;  %-9s after : %s&quot; % (fld, Counter(x.get(fld) for x in va).most_common()))
nb = len({x.get(&quot;lineId&quot;) for x in vb})
na = len({x.get(&quot;lineId&quot;) for x in va})
print(&quot;\n  distinct lineIds  %d -&gt; %d&quot; % (nb, na))
print(&quot;  lineId null       %d -&gt; %d&quot;
      % (sum(1 for x in vb if not x.get(&quot;lineId&quot;)),
         sum(1 for x in va if not x.get(&quot;lineId&quot;))))
# geometry: length and the biggest steps, same measure as before
def stats(v, label):
    g = [ft((v[i][&quot;lat&quot;], v[i][&quot;lon&quot;]), (v[i+1][&quot;lat&quot;], v[i+1][&quot;lon&quot;]))
         for i in range(len(v)-1)]
    tot = sum(g)
    gs = sorted(g)
    print(&quot;\n  %s&quot; % label)
    print(&quot;    length      %.1f mi&quot; % (tot/5280.0))
    print(&quot;    median step %.1f ft   max %.0f ft&quot; % (gs[len(gs)//2], gs[-1]))
    print(&quot;    steps &gt;500ft %d   &gt;0.25mi %d   &gt;1mi %d&quot;
          % (sum(1 for x in g if x &gt; 500),
             sum(1 for x in g if x &gt; 1320),
             sum(1 for x in g if x &gt; 5280)))
    return tot
tb = stats(vb, &quot;BEFORE&quot;)
ta = stats(va, &quot;AFTER&quot;)
print(&quot;\n  length change: %+.1f mi (%+.0f%%)&quot;
      % ((ta-tb)/5280.0, 100.0*(ta-tb)/tb))
# if the counts match, measure how far each vertex moved
if len(vb) == len(va):
    moved = [ft((vb[i][&quot;lat&quot;], vb[i][&quot;lon&quot;]), (va[i][&quot;lat&quot;], va[i][&quot;lon&quot;]))
             for i in range(len(vb))]
    ms = sorted(moved)
    print(&quot;\n  VERTEX MOVEMENT (counts match, so index-for-index)&quot;)
    print(&quot;    unmoved (&lt;1ft) %d of %d&quot; % (sum(1 for x in moved if x &lt; 1), len(moved)))
    print(&quot;    median %.1f ft   90th %.1f ft   max %.0f ft&quot;
          % (ms[len(ms)//2], ms[int(len(ms)*0.9)], ms[-1]))
    print(&quot;    moved &gt;25ft %d   &gt;100ft %d   &gt;500ft %d&quot;
          % (sum(1 for x in moved if x &gt; 25),
             sum(1 for x in moved if x &gt; 100),
             sum(1 for x in moved if x &gt; 500)))
    ch = sum(1 for i in range(len(vb))
             if vb[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;) != va[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;))
    print(&quot;    lineId CHANGED on %d vertices (%.0f%%)&quot;
          % (ch, 100.0*ch/len(vb)))
    print(&quot;\n    farthest moves:&quot;)
    idx = sorted(range(len(moved)), key=lambda i: -moved[i])[:10]
    for i in idx:
        print(&quot;      %7.0f ft  idx %5d  %.5f,%.5f -&gt; %.5f,%.5f  %s&quot;
              % (moved[i], i, vb[i][&quot;lat&quot;], vb[i][&quot;lon&quot;],
                 va[i][&quot;lat&quot;], va[i][&quot;lon&quot;],
                 &quot;lineId changed&quot; if vb[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;) != va[i].get(&quot;lineId&quot;)
                 else &quot;same lineId&quot;))
else:
    print(&quot;\n  vertex counts differ -- the app dropped or added points, so an&quot;)
    print(&quot;  index-for-index comparison would be misleading. The length and step&quot;)
    print(&quot;  figures above are the honest comparison.&quot;)

The first device run died:
corridor: 53711 edges, 112 POI nodes
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError at java.lang.Long.valueOf
112 POI nodes meant 112 simultaneous Dijkstra tables with boxed Long keys on a 256 MB
heap. ⛔ The cause was the RADIUS FORMULA, not the algorithm. The research always used a
HAND-SET box (~38×45 mi) and never hit this; the port derived it as
milesHigh/2 × 0.75 + 5 — 35 miles, a 70×70 box.

IdeaWhat the measurement said
Distance clusteringcluster POIs, route to a cluster
    No natural link value. 2 mi → 234 clusters with 160 singletons. 3 mi → one blob of 150.
    5 mi → 307 in one. 8 mi → all 545 in one. The POIs are a continuum, not natural
    groups.
Grid pruningtile the box, drop empty cells
    10 mi grid: only 12% of cells empty, holding 3% of edges. 5 mi grid: 30% empty — but
    keeping only POI cells shattered the network to 36%. The connectors run through empty
    ground.
The funnelcommit to a direction early
    POIs by sector 77/67/52/46/43/38/28/24 — best is 14%, no dominant arc. And density
    RISES with distance (15 within 10 mi, 149 between 30 and 40) because ring area grows with the
    square of the radius.
Radius from mileage
    35 mi → 53,711 edges (OOM). 40 mi → 129,474.

⚠⚠ METHOD — the same mistake three times in one day
Three patches aborted on their own correct output because a guard grepped for a TOKEN
instead of testing the EXPRESSION:
STUB:AISEARCH — the replacement comment said "STUB:AISEARCH satisfied", so the
check found its own text
The radius formula — the comment quoted the formula it was describing
onRouteTap — counted the bare name, which appears twice by design (existence
test, then call), exactly as the track handler does
⭐⭐ STANDING RULE: GUARD THE EXPRESSION, NOT THE TOKEN. A check must test the thing
that changed — an assignment, an invocation — never a string that may legitimately appear in
prose or in a second position.
⭐ And a marker must be ABSENT once satisfied. Writing "STUB:X satisfied" in a comment
keeps grep -rn "STUB:" app/src reporting it as outstanding, which defeats the
completeness checklist the whole stub-first rule depends on.

⭐⭐⭐ THE IDEA, IN ONE LINE
A route's notes ARE its detail panel, they travel inside the same file as its geometry,
and one handler processes both formats.
