Server-side function that belongs under a hosting release (NOT a release title)
Same-ride track dedup — pruning duplicate recordings when tracks are served. ⚠ This is a HOSTING problem and only exists once tracks are served. Locally, ten riders each holding their own recording of one ride is CORRECT.
⛔ geom_hash cannot do this job. Perfect for trails (89,536 rows / 89,536 hashes; the 313 UT/AZ border trails collapsing automatically prove it). Useless for tracks from one ride: ten devices drop GPS points at different moments → ten point sets, ten hashes, all legitimately the same ride.
⭐ COLLAPSE FOR PRESENTATION, DO NOT DELETE. Canonical track per hash, hash + date → alias. Nobody loses their own ride and the collapse stays reversible. Server-side, not on the phone. Scope is bounded (same bbox + date window). Goal is "prune as best we can", not perfect matching.
Candidate metrics (none chosen): bbox overlap + Hausdorff/Fréchet · rounded/simplified-geometry hash · start/stop coordinates + time window (Fred 07-29, cheaper than either) ⚠ needs tolerance on both axes.
⭐ CROSS-REFERENCE, not scope: 2.7's snap-2 makes recorded tracks converge on shared trail geometry, so part of this becomes hash-matchable outright. That work belongs to 2.7.
⚠ Two riders on the same ground can store different lineIds. For DRAWING it does not matter; it matters only when two routes are COMPARED. Fix at compare time by geometry proximity, never by making snap pick differently.
🆕🆕 3.0 FEATURE — RIDER TRAIL NAMING, AND THE PENDING-CHANGE QUEUE (Fred 2026-08-22). TRAILNAMES-2026-08-22
Fred, 08-22: "unnamed is no name so first name replaces unnamed and becomes the
single source of truth. we would move to server and back down users in v3." And:
"when riding the user can name the section if it has a name that is not in our database
(route markers)."
The ground has names the data does not. Route markers exist on the trail, on posts,
and in no dataset we import. The only place that knowledge lives is with the rider who is
standing next to the marker — which makes this the one mechanism by which the trail data can
get better rather than merely bigger.
The measurement that motivates it
Bar 10 → Toroweap corridor, measured 08-22 against the live spatial DB (216,616 trails):
4,311 trails in the corridor · 2,894 miles
3,334 of them carry the literal string Not Named — 77%. Only 977
(23%) have a real name.
The named ones are good — Mt Dellenbaugh, Mt Trumbull, Whitmore Canyon, Temple Trail,
Sullivan Draw — but they are the minority.
⚠ Not Named IS A VALUE, NOT A BLANK, and it already caused a false
reading: the 08-22 inventory reported "100% named" because the column was populated. Anything
testing does this trail have a name with an emptiness check is fooled the same way.
Treat the placeholder set as data to be normalised, not as names.
⭐⭐ THE RULE — an absence loses to anything; a real name is never silently overwritten
A placeholder is an ABSENCE. Not Named, Unnamed, blank,
None — all mean the same thing. The first REAL name replaces it outright and
becomes the trail's name.
A real name is never overwritten by another source. Two genuine names for one
geometry is the ALIAS case, which insertTrail already returns a decision for and
which the alias machinery already handles.
A rider name outranks a placeholder, never a source name. A rider standing at a
marker beats OSM's silence; they do not silently overrule MassGIS or UGRC. Rider-vs-source on
the same geometry is a conflict for the server to arbitrate, not for the device to decide.
⭐ This sits on machinery that already exists. Identity is geom_hash
alone — the rule that made a UGRC trail and an OSM trail over the same ground ONE artifact with
two names. A rider-supplied name is a third name against the same hash. And
updateExistingFeature already refuses to touch geometry (NEVER
geometry/bbox/geom_hash), which is exactly the guarantee naming needs.
⭐⭐⭐ THE PENDING-CHANGE QUEUE — what Fred asked for, and why it is the load-bearing part
Fred: "db updates must be saved for application for AWS server."
⛔ The naming happens where there is no signal. That is not an edge case, it is the
normal case — the rider is at a route marker on the Arizona Strip. So a name cannot be an API
call. It is a local write plus a durable record of intent, uploaded whenever the device
next has a connection.
Two writes, not one:
Apply locally, immediately. The rider sees their name on their map before they have
left the marker. No round trip, no spinner, no failure mode in the field.
Queue the contribution in a pending table that survives app restarts, reinstalls and
months offline.
What the record must carry — enough to be applied by a server that has never seen this
device:
FieldWhy
geom_hashTHE identity. Not trail_id — that is a
per-device UUID and means nothing to the server or to another rider.
proposed nameWhat the rider read off the marker
previous valuePlaceholder or real name — the server needs to know which case
this was, because the rule differs
source of the nameroute marker · local knowledge · signage. A marker photo is
a later refinement, not v1
where and whenCoordinate and timestamp of the naming. Two riders naming the
same segment from the same marker is strong agreement; from 40 miles apart it is not
contributorThe Google Sign-In identity already used as the cross-platform
identifier
upload stateDerived where possible. ⚠ See the status-field warning below
⚠⚠ DO NOT GATE BEHAVIOUR ON A status FIELD IN THIS TABLE. That shape has
burned this project twice — isSourceFullyImported() reading
status=="processed" from a record written unconditionally marked three FAILED runs
as permanently imported (07-27), and the same class produced the 08-21 manifest work.
Prefer: a row exists = not yet uploaded; the row is deleted (or moved) on server
acknowledgement. Presence is the state, and presence cannot drift.
⭐ The queue is the artifact. Same principle as the import manifest and the OSM
ledger: a rider who names twenty sections on a three-day ride has twenty rows waiting when they
reach signal. Nothing depends on them being online at the moment of naming.
Server side — arbitration and distribution
Stack is already standing: Google Sign-In · AWS RDS MySQL · PHP REST on EC2, with
users, rides, enrollments, invites live
through Phase B.
A names table keyed on geom_hash, holding every contribution rather
than a single winner. The canonical name is DERIVED from the contributions, so it can be
recomputed when a new one arrives and an arbitration mistake is reversible.
Agreement is the signal. Three riders independently naming the same hash
Sullivan Draw is far stronger than one. Cheap first rule: most-agreed name wins;
ties break to earliest.
Distribution back down is a list of geom_hash → name. That is small —
names are bytes, not geometry — and it applies with the same "placeholder loses to a real name"
rule the device already uses. ⭐ No geometry ever moves in either direction.
A rider's own name is never taken away from them. If the server's canonical name
differs, theirs becomes an alias on their device rather than being replaced. Same principle as
the same-ride track dedup above: collapse for presentation, do not delete.
⚠ Open questions — not settled
Which geometry does the rider actually name? Segments are short — the corridor's
median is 0.31 mi — so a named road may be forty rows. Does naming apply to the tapped segment
only, or propagate along connected same-name-absent segments? Propagation is a much bigger
feature and probably not v1.
Moderation. Two riders, two different names, no agreement. Also: profanity, and
names that are someone's private joke. A hosting release that publishes rider content back to
other riders owns that problem.
Does a rider name reach OSM? Contributing upstream would help everyone and raises
licensing questions that have deliberately been kept off this project — GroupTrack has
never hosted or redistributed OSM data, which is what keeps ODbL share-alike clear of Fred
entirely. Do not open this without deciding it explicitly.
Numbering. This is filed under 3.0 as Fred stated. ⚠ The unresolved 3.0-vs-4.0 split
above applies — if names ride the same distribution path as tiles and rides, check which block
owns it before building.
Related, not the same
2.7's TRAIL GAP FILL FROM RIDDEN TRACKS (section 08 above) promotes a recorded track
to a trail where no trail exists. That creates geometry; this creates names on geometry that
already exists. They meet at one point: a promoted track is unnamed by definition, so it is
immediately a candidate for naming — and the rider who rode it is the one person who knows what
it is called.

📱 12 — iPAD — POST-V2.6 TARGET (restored 07-30; was absent from the checklist entirely)
⭐⭐ UPDATED 10-08 — 2.9 iOS PLAN NOTES (Fred, exploratory — for planning; nothing decided against the 10-02 plan below). XPLAT-2026-10-08
Release 2.9 = the Apple versions (10-05): iPad with functionality identical to Android; Mac = planning map only, no riding.
1 · The build route being tested — Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform. "One shell, build versions from it": GroupTrack's Compose panels run on iPad (Compose Multiplatform for iOS declared stable and production-ready in 1.8.0, May 2025); the maps (HTML/JS) run in WKWebView; GroupTrack's Kotlin logic in shared modules; only platform pieces written per platform; Android Studio builds Android, Xcode builds iPad, one project on the Mac. RAD / low-code builders (e.g. FlutterFlow) set aside — they rebuild everything in their own language and cannot import a Kotlin/Compose app. Relation to 10-02 (below): 10-02 put the shared web pages in an iOS shell; Compose Multiplatform would carry the native panels too — decision for planning (planner P8, design v18 §R8).
2 · What moves — measured 10-08 (convoy/, 161 files, ~65,000 lines): 54 files have no Android ties and port nearly as-is; the rest lean on platform services — Android extras Log/Toast/Build (81 files, trivial wrapper), Context glue (72), files/storage (56), the map WebView bridge (11 files, 274 uses — re-implemented on WKWebView), database (12), background downloads/imports (11 — iOS background rules are stricter), location (7), Hilt (8), Bluetooth (5 — going to comm). Comm was the first boundary; platform services (files, database, location, background work, the map bridge) is the second — same pattern: one contract, Android implementation = today's code moved behind it, iPad implementation.
3 · The spatial database — finding. Candidates named for iOS: SpatiaLite with SQLite, NGA's geopackage-ios. Measured: GroupTrack uses neither on Android — the trail/spatial database is plain SQLite with bounding-box columns and ordinary indexes (no SpatiaLite, no ST_ functions), and GeoPackage imports are read by our own decoder (OsmGpkgDecoder.kt). iOS ships SQLite; KMP SQLite drivers use it → shared code; the decoder becomes shared Kotlin after one contained change (it uses Java's ByteBuffer). SpatiaLite / geopackage-ios = fallbacks only if true spatial operations are ever needed. Remaining risk = performance with a full state's trails on an iPad (spike).
4 · Comm on iPad — Bluetooth-first, a proven model. A native implementation of the SAME Comm API (Fred: "the comm modules we are building now would have to be recreated as an iPad native too, but the core functionality is inherited from the Meshtastic iPad model"). iTAK runs on iPad with native Bluetooth through the mesh (Fred) and Meshtastic-Apple does the same — "we have a model, not unexplored ground"; their background-Bluetooth handling is the pattern to follow. The translator / CoT mapping / rules can be shared Kotlin. Considered and set aside: Wi-Fi/IP between radio and iPad — range (spread rides need LoRa; Fred: "range is our issue again"), only ESP32 radios have Wi-Fi (not the T1000-E), Wi-Fi turns Bluetooth off on ESP32 radios (as far as known), and the cart would need a network host. IP stays where it belongs: through the Nucleus when one is in the cart (its device access point is 5 GHz in Natak's setup). Wi-Fi on the purpose-built SxS radio = a "maybe later" question for vendors, not a requirement.
5 · The mountain (Fred): moving our code and data is the uphill side — ours alone, nobody has done it; comm is very large but the downhill side — integration of proven parts (Meshtastic-Apple / iTAK) behind a contract already proven on Android.
6 · The three early proofs (planner P8) — small, before any port: (1) one GroupTrack Compose screen on the iPad simulator; (2) the trail database + our decoder on the iPad simulator, timed against a real state import; (3) the iPad applying our managed fields to a radio from the SAME ride document (the 10-02 rule: prove config before code) — the one part iTAK does not prove for us.
7 · Guardrails in 2.7b so Android and iPad converge (applied at point of contact): no JVM-only types in the Comm API — found 10-08: the config document is org.json.JSONObject (does not exist on iOS) → a plain JSON String before CommConfig (P4) is wired; the API module can become a KMP module (the build already has meshtastic.kmp.library); new logic in plain Kotlin files; Toast / file calls through wrappers; the map bridge's function names treated as a contract; Hilt kept at the wiring point.
8 · Timeline — honest (Fred: "on a path to actually create an iOS version by the first of the year, or at least have identified what works and moves and what our issues are"): by 1 January, likely: knowing what works, moves and where the issues are (spikes are days; the platform-services contract is design). Possible: a phase-1 iPad GroupTrack WITHOUT radio comm (maps, planning, routes, rides) on TestFlight, if the spikes pass. Unlikely: full parity with radios — early spring is honest. Sketch: October — finish the small comm steps + run the spikes; November — platform-services contract + the main cycle-1 pieces; December — phase-1 iPad on TestFlight; Q1 — the iPad comm plugin. Competing for the same weeks: the rest of 2.7b, GA support, one developer, January field tests in Utah. A failed spike is learned in October, not March.

Native port via external dev — Roadmap V9, Mar 25 (iOS-01..08: fork Meshtastic-iOS, Apple Developer enrollment $99/yr, port the coordination layer, WKWebView + convoy_map.html, offline tiles in Swift, Apple IAP, TestFlight, com.grouptrack.ios).

⭐ THE COLLAPSE (07-04) — the whole PWA arc solved a non-problem
Convoy is a fork/extension of core Meshtastic's messaging. The native-vs-PWA-vs-WKWebView arc was all answering "how do we get BLE on iOS?" — a question that dissolves once convoy is understood as a fork of the mesh app. So iPad = a fork of Meshtastic-Apple (Swift/SwiftUI + Core Data + BLE + protobuf; already App-Store-approved; universal incl. iPad; ships an offline map + radio config). Mac + Xcode is the prerequisite. ⚠ FLAG: Meshtastic-Apple ships native TAK/CoT — reconcile against the roadmap's "TAK as design pattern only."
🔴 STILL OPEN — the A/B decision
(A) BRIDGE — convoy is its own native iOS app consuming mesh messages from the separate Meshtastic app over a local port. Less code; adds a runtime dependency + iOS-lifecycle fragility. (B) FORK — import Meshtastic's BLE/mesh and extend, as on Android. More work; no runtime dependency; same architecture as Android. Trade: effort favours A; field reliability + Android-sameness favour B. For an off-grid safety app, "bridge dies if iOS backgrounds the neighbour app" is a real mark against A — leans B, not decided.
Settled
Three surfaces split on connectivity: PC = planning-only web app (no mesh, no radio, online) · Android + iPad = off-grid native convoy execution. Convoy cannot be web.
SwiftUI REJECTED for presentation — does not port to a browser, zero reuse of the Android web layer. Swift's only job on iPad is the native shell (mesh source + WebView host + JS↔native bridge).
Config write is offloaded: the planning side creates a Meshtastic restore FILE; Meshtastic's own restore applies it. GroupTrack never does BLE for config.
KMP is the natural target — logic is already Kotlin; migration is incremental, expect/actual is literally "configured API resolves per platform." Does not let you fork Meshtastic-Apple (that is Swift); produces a shared logic module a Swift shell consumes.
Target end-state: a messaging/logic service layer behind an interface + logic-free presentation panels. Serving three platforms means logic written ONCE, not three copies.
🔴 NEXT ACTION (unchanged since 07-04, still not done)
Enumerate the bridge/IO surface from the current Android code — every JavascriptInterface method + every evaluateJavascript/postMessage crossing. That inventory is the true iPad build cost AND which functions can/cannot go to PC. It is the blast-radius question the xref docs answer.

📜 13 — ORIGINAL (07-30): TILE SOURCE HYB IS DEAD (Fred 07-30) — live tester-facing defect
NEW predicted risk, materialized

A dead source can still be chosen and queued — jobs segment and enqueue normally, then every tile fails. Burns queue time; may leave an empty/partial .mbtiles that later looks like a corrupt download.
⚠ Rule it in or out as a feeder for the open queue defects — markComplete refreshMode collision, refresh-never-completes, ETA starvation. A source where every fetch fails is exactly the input that would make completion accounting behave strangely.
The manual and any source-picker capture showing four working sources are now wrong.

Google Hybrid / Google tiles: rejected on download reliability, field-observed — free Google download resources proved slow and unreliable at bulk scale — and now on dead endpoint. NOT rejected on quality or storage, and NOT reversible by a storage argument.

⭐⭐ THE METHOD LESSON (Fred 07-30) — why this happened
That May 9 document is 19,514 chars and eight sections: every URL template, {y}/{x} ordering gotchas, rate limits, API-key tiers, a tile_sources table design, Leaflet integration code. It is a thorough catalogue with no risk analysis, no strengths/weaknesses column, and no storage arithmetic — and the consequence sat in its own text: Google Hybrid = satellite + labels in ONE stream (1×); Esri World Imagery = no labels, therefore two extra raster label stores (3×). SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT / SAT_LABELS_PLACES appear in the handoffs from May 10 — the very next day — and the multiplication was never performed. It surfaced on 07-26 from a delete log, and Fred spotted it: "it is 65,000 tiles because of the three layers."
The Esri choice was right on the axis that governs (bulk download reliability beats storage efficiency for an offline-first app). A risk table would not have changed the source — it would have moved the vector conversation to May, before Leaflet was wired in and before the tangle froze.
⚠ Also unweighed at the time and still live: Esri World Imagery is flagged in that same doc as legacy "mature support" — Esri pushing migration, max zoom 19 vs Google's 20. Both are risk-column entries about the dependency the whole map rests on.

🔴🔴 14 — CARRIED FROM 07-27: MAP REFRESH ON SOURCE CHANGE (do first, stop-the-bleeding)
DO FIRST not a root-cause fix
The REPLACE/refresh function on the map-source select screen spawned 3287 downloads, lat/long spanning the continental US; downloads then stopped entirely.
⚠ Cancel All does NOT persist. Cancel appeared to clear the queue; all 3287 jobs resurfaced on restart — the clear happens in memory and is never written to disk, so loadQueue re-reads the stale file every launch. This is the boot-loop mechanism, demonstrated — just without a crash.
⛔ No recovery path on a release build. adb run-as = denied; X-plore cannot reach Android/data/&lt;pkg&gt;/ — Android 13+ removed third-party file-manager access entirely, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE excludes it, the document-tree picker refuses it. Only root, adb-on-debuggable, or the app itself can read there. The only escape is Clear-App-Data.
Decision (Fred 07-23): turn off the JSON write / auto-refresh on source change. Refresh becomes manually requested as an Area download, riding the hardened submitDownload → enqueueArea → segmentCells path. DISABLE, don't delete — gate behind a marked constant; the bug is still undiagnosed and the path will be wanted.
⚠ This does NOT fix Cancel All — separate defect, still open.
⛔ DO NOT run replace-map-source again until this ships — recovery costs an hour and possibly all app-internal data.
Root cause still open: leading hypothesis is that the bbox handed to enqueueRefresh is not the viewport — a zero-initialised value, or swapped bounds arguments. Note 3287 ≈ ceil(enormous/50K), so segmentation worked correctly on garbage input → the bug is upstream of segmentCells. Compare ConvoyMapSourceScreen.kt:255-290 against ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:218-250 for argument order; also read ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:440-490 (:473 declares a quarantine file, and it is likely the same function where cancel's persistence fails).

🔴🔴 16 — CARRIED FROM 07-27: THREE DEVICE DEFECTS (07-24 PM) + completion-state family
gate the Play upload, not the build
⚠ ETA poisoning (likely feeder of defect 1): completedAt gets stamped early, so throughput maths is computed against work that has not happened.
⭐ Same family as the refresh bug — completion state and actual work drifting apart. Two symptoms, one root shape.
⛔ The benign explanation is dead. First read was "hasTile skipped tiles already on device"; that no longer accounts for it.
⚠ If SAT is broken, testers get corridor downloads with no satellite imagery — the primary layer. Highest-severity of the three.
🔴🔴 markComplete refreshMode COLLISION (found 07-26 — ONE LINE, high value)
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:641. ⚠ enqueueArea AND enqueueCorridor both set refreshMode = replaceExisting, so any area/corridor job collides. ⭐ Strong candidate for BOTH the refresh-never-completes report AND a large share of the ETA starvation. Displaced twice already — do it.
🔴 REFRESH DOES NOT LOG AS A COMPLETED JOB (new 07-24)
⚠ Bigger than a cosmetic status. ⚠⚠ Does it hold a concurrency slot? If the entry never leaves running/active, it consumes a slot forever. ⭐ Check ConvoyCorridorWorker in the SAME pass — the corridor worker deliberately duplicates completion calls per worker, so this class of miss can exist independently there. 🔵 17 — G5 ROUTE CORRIDORS (07-24 design, DESIGNED IN FULL 08-09 — NOT WRITTEN)
ready to write
⛔⛔ FIRST — A CONTRADICTION IN OUR OWN RECORD. RESOLVE BEFORE WRITING CODE.
This section (07-27) says the routes table ALREADY CARRIES geom_hash. The
08-06 notes say the opposite — that routes carry none and it must be added as a column plus a call
at insert plus a backfill. Both cannot be true.
⚠ The whole 08-09 design below was reasoned out against the 08-06 version without this
section being read first — the exact failure Fred named today: "another long lengthy
discussion without awareness of prior discovery." If 07-27 is right, a chunk of the work below
does not exist.
grep -n "geom_hash" app/src/main/java/com/geeksville/mesh/convoy/SpatialDbManager.kt | grep -i route
sqlite3 grouptrack_spatial.db ".schema routes"
THE GOAL (Fred 08-06, verbatim intent)
⭐⭐⭐ "I do not care about route. I am trying to create a method where a PRE-RIDE
ROUTE CAN BE DISTRIBUTED AND IMPORTED WITH MAPS, allowing a rider to download accurate maps with
efficient space utilisation BEFORE TRAILS ARE CAPTURED."
⭐ CORRIDOR, NOT AREA. Fred 08-09: "we know 90% of area are air." Confirmed by the
08-08 measurement — 30 tracks swept as areas cost 2M+ tiles on ONE source; 89 as corridors cost
1.5M across THREE. A route bbox is mostly air, so route downloads run as corridors from the WKT.
⚠ Half a mile either side is the padding (~1 mile band). Fred 08-09: "we should be fine
with maps downloaded and trail being on it." ⚠ Holds for a SNAPPED route, whose geometry IS
trail geometry via snap-2. A DRAWN route cuts across country — its corridor covers ground the rider
will not travel and misses the trail where it bends. Open: does a drawn route download at all,
or must it be snapped first?
⭐ WHAT FRED TESTED 08-09 — TWO THINGS DO NOT WORK TODAY
SAVE MAPS does not render for routes. ArtifactDetailPanel:111 gates on
artifactType == "Tracks" &amp;&amp; onDownloadCorridor != null.
⭐ The panel is otherwise ALREADY generic — line 27 documents "Routes" as valid, and
rename/delete work for them (only Trails is excluded). SAVE MAPS is the one place someone
narrowed it.
Import did not process maps for routes. Routes may have imported as artifacts —
unconfirmed which half failed. ConvoyMapViewerScreen:230 calls
ConvoyTrackOps.importGpxAllArtifacts.
⭐⭐ THE ARTIFACT-SPECIFIC SURFACE IS THREE LINES. EVERYTHING ELSE IS ALREADY GENERIC.
ComponentArtifact-specific?
enqueueCorridor:667 getTrackPoints(context, geomHash)
YES — geometry resolve
enqueueCorridor:~702 allTrackGeomHashes() label lookup
YES — a route would show a hex fragment as its queue label
ConvoyCorridorWorker:49 re-resolves from inputData
YES — the job may run in a fresh process
corridorTiles(segments)✅ takes points, no opinion
slot/layer multiplier · bbox loop · QueueEntry✅ all derive from segments
worker dispatch · download · progress · tile write · ORPHAN block · markFailed✅ untouched
⭐ So there is NO second worker, NO parallel enqueue, NO duplicated job-building. Fred
08-09: "two new callable functions, return geometry for tracks and return geometry for artifacts,
and all the work comes out of here and does not complicate this job."
⭐⭐ THE BUILD — TWO PASSES (Fred 08-09)
"Separate the existing working function into a new route/track solution but only
implement the existing track in the new method. We will test and certify and then introduce the
route bits."
⭐ WHY: this is the 08-08 lesson applied. Every component of the migration was already
working; the REASSEMBLY introduced the defects and cost a device rebuild. Proving the refactor
behaviour-neutral first means any failure in pass 2 is unambiguously the route code.
PASS 1 — structure only, ZERO behaviour change:
resolveGeometry(context, type, key)   -> wraps getTrackPoints; "Tracks" only
resolveLabel(context, type, key)      -> wraps allTrackGeomHashes; "Tracks" only
enqueueCorridor(..., artifactType)    -> explicit at EVERY call site
QueueEntry.artifactType               -> new field, persisted
inputData "artifact_type"             -> worker reads it, calls resolveGeometry
CERTIFY PASS 1: corridor downloads behave EXACTLY as before — same tile counts, same queue
rows, same labels, same completions. Nothing new in the UI, so any difference is a regression.
PASS 2 — routes: the route branch in both resolvers · the routes SAVE MAPS button ·
import offers downloads at the END of the batch (Fred: "current import process creates db tables
and submits imports at the end. I prefer that approach.") · route-create on final save.
⭐ Fred's entry-point order: prove it from Work-With-Artifacts FIRST — a stable bench where
any number of SAVE MAPS requests can be submitted — then attach to import and route-create by
artifact key.
⚠ DECISIONS AND TRAPS — carry these into the build
⛔ NO DEFAULT ON artifactType. ~7 call sites edited explicitly. A default
silently sends a route to the tracks table — CODE RULE 1.
⚠ replaceExisting: Boolean = false is an existing default at a function we are
touching — CODE RULE 2 says evaluate it at point of contact.
⛔ THE SILENT SKIP AT :670. No geometry returns 0 with a log warning, and
enqueueCorridorBatch counts it as SKIPPED, not failed. A route that cannot
resolve would report as skipped and download nothing — worse than an error, because it looks like
it worked. ⭐ Make it a real failure during PASS 1, before routes can hit it.
⚠ QueueEntry.geomHash becomes a KEY whose meaning depends on type (routes
would put a route id there). Name it honestly in pass 1 rather than leaving a field called
geomHash holding a route id in pass 2.
⚠ SERIALISATION MUST BE BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE — startedAt/tilesPerSec
were added 08-08 with optLong/optDouble so old queue files still load.
The new field needs the same, or Droid 2's persisted queue breaks on read.
⚠ The worker error text at :55 ("Corridor job missing track or source")
becomes wrong for routes.
⭐ ADD THE ENTRY ID TO THE COMPLETION LOG LINE. The start line carries
id= and hash=; Corridor complete carries NEITHER, so per-job
durations cannot be matched from logcat — proven on 08-09 when the analysis had to fall back to
completion sums. One field makes every future run exactly measurable.
⚠ A BATCH SUBMIT IS WHERE 08-08 BIT. The migration queued 172 jobs and became
unexitable. Route import producing several corridors must show the count BEFORE submitting and
leave a way out after.
⚠ Dedup: a route drawn along an existing track produces an IDENTICAL geom hash.
resolveByGeom(type, name, geomHash) is type-aware so probably fine — verify, or
planning a route over known trail could fail to save.
⚠ insertRoute returns a FABRICATED id on duplicates — newId(),
then INSERT OR IGNORE, then returns the fabricated id rather than the surviving row's.
Fix while in there (carried from 07-27).
⭐ A mixed route is the best test artifact (Fred 08-09): snap-2 segments and straight-line
draws within ONE route exercise the whole range at once. Snapped portions should hug the trail;
drawn portions produce a straight band across country. If they look identical, something is
re-deriving geometry instead of using what was stored.
⭐ The blocker dissolved on inspection: the routes table already carries geom_hash. ⚠ Defects to fix while in there: insertRoute returns a fabricated id on duplicates — newId(), then INSERT OR IGNORE, then returns the fabricated id rather than the surviving row's.

🟠 19 — FIX 6 — PLANNER PADDING DRIFT (Fred priority)
FRED PRIORITY
"Annoying continually entering a shrinking panel." Trail shrinks / map grows on every reopen: the FIT function is reused for persistence, so restore re-pads an already-padded saved bbox → cumulative zoom-out.
Chosen fix: explicit padding argument — fitToBounds(bbox, padding:Int); restore passes 0, content-fit passes ~60. If the function is SHARED with convoy, default the argument to the content-fit value so convoy's call site is untouched (respects the freeze).
Scope first: grep -rn "fitBounds\|fitToBounds" --include='*.kt' app/src/main/java/ and grep -n "fitBounds" app/src/main/assets/*.html — the planner fit may go through the HTML.
THE PERSIST CHAIN (confirmed 07-29, three hops): the fit call → (…, 400) (MVS:284-285) → savePlanningState() (MVS:259) writes planning_panel.json. ⚠ savePlanningState() reads lastViewport* and ONLY onViewportChanged sets them, so a redraw racing a map move can persist a stale viewport.
⛔ CORRECTION: "convoy has cumulative zoom-out" is misleading as written — the convoy map is frozen and its call site is untouched; the drift is the planner's restore path.
THE PLANNER HAS TWO FIT IDIOMS AND THEY DISAGREE — site idiom vs content idiom. Reconcile before patching.

1. The decision: freeze 2.7b, and One Map becomes 2.7c
2.7b is frozen in scope (Fred 13:23). It ships once three things are done:
the estimate / gap-fill rule (desk test, then patch);the cleanup patch: remove the POLYTEST test button, fix the duplicate VM listener, fix the COMMHEALTH foreground-service start while the app is in the background;2.7b release notes, manual and Quick Start.
Moved to 2.7c: polyline statistics, reconnect panel v4, and the polyline-dots question. The two-person field test waits for Utah in January (Fred decides whether 2.7b goes to internal testers before it).
Why separate releases:
2.7b changed how positions flow (the tick removed, lead track, gap polyline, trim, estimate); 2.7c changes how riders move around the app. Each needs its own testing and release notes, or a trail problem cannot be traced to one change.2.7c rewrites every lettered control in manual sections 4 and 5.

2. Principles (Fred, 10-18 to 10-21)
One map. The planning map is folded in; the Ride Planning / Back to Ride switches are retired.
A launch layer over the existing features. Each process gets ONE first screen that takes every value it needs (defaults from the ride and settings), then runs to the end with no further screen prompts. The only stop kept is the confirm before something that cannot be undone.
Two layouts. Group adds a lot of complexity and is used by some. Android only is the default; Group adds the Group button, CHECK IN, the GROUP readout, other carts and the lead track. One switch decides which.
Riders ride in landscape and pan in portrait. In landscape, panels open as a side panel so the map stays in view.
Every control shows an icon and its text on an opaque background, readable on any map. No hover, no long-press meanings.
North up only. Leaflet cannot rotate, and Hybrid labels are baked into the imagery (heading-up needs a rotating map engine: not 2.7c).
Show/hide is FILTER, how lines look is KEY: as onX and Gaia do, the filter is on every view.

0. PICK UP HERE — 10-21 morning
10-21 morning (11:58). Code is unchanged since 10-20 (2.7b = c176d4026, docs 894c7b0bb, pushed, in sync). This card records two sets of decisions. The Nucleus work is paused until Nathan replies.
A. THE ESTIMATE AND GAP-FILL RULE (Fred 10-20 17:15&ndash;17:18). It supersedes the earlier route &rarr; saved route &rarr; trails &rarr; straight line chain.
What was seen (Fred 10-20 last test): the lead was not heard. The radio marker did not move after the last-heard marker was dropped, even though the lead was on a track that ran on to a trail.
Fred's words: "there is a track and a trail. should we not move at least until&hellip; intersection junction?" and "our rule was use the route only if it is the only route on the current map. in lieu of the route it should be tracks and or trails." He confirmed the same rule applies to the gap fill.
CaseThe silent-lead ESTIMATE followsThe GAP FILL (between two heard points) follows
Exactly ONE route on the current mapThat route, in its direction (as built)That route
No route, or more than one routeThe track or trail the lead was on. It moves along it and stops at the next junction, never guessing a branchThe track or trail the lead was on, joined through a junction only when the next heard point is past it
Not on any track or trailHolds at the last-heard point (as now)A straight line (a polyline replaces it when one arrives)
Saved routes (not displayed)REMOVED from both. A saved route the lead's points happen to lie on is no longer used.
Status: agreed and not built. Method: desk test first, as with the trim. Replay the 10-20 Long Fast logs through the rule, then patch. The work is in TrackRules / LeadEstimate (the estimate route source, estRouteNow()) and in the gap-fill chain in TrackWriter. Callers are untouched.
Still Fred's call: whether polyline points show as dots when no route is displayed.
B. 10-21: WHAT WAS DONE ON THE NUCLEUS (node 46, V3-OS 0.11.0), through Droid 1 on its Wi-Fi, using only Nathan's tools
Factory config saved first, in ~/Downloads/natak46/ (factory_*.json, openapi_0.11.0.json, bridge logs). The keyed originals are private and never go on Drive or git. Scrubbed copies are on Drive GroupTrack/natak46/.
Radio put on GroupTrack through HIS API with nucleus_radio_grouptrack_2026-10-21.py. It does a preview, then --apply or --restore, via adb push and nc on Droid 1. It changed MEDIUM_FAST, channel GroupTrack, slot 0 and the key, through POST /api/v1/meshtastic/config/apply. The read-back matched, and the key fingerprint (psk_fingerprint = first 8 hex of SHA-256 of the key) was verified. --restore puts back his factory Natak link and SHORT_FAST.
Proven:
  LoRa works both ways between node 46 and a T1000-E: 46 heard ours at SNR 11, and a text from 46 reached our rider.
  Wi-Fi &rarr; LoRa works: a CoT from Droid 1 went out as a 52-byte ATAK packet ("TX &rarr; LoRa | GT-wifi-test-1").
  Port 72 is NOT bridged to Wi-Fi. cot_bridge keeps only 257, text, voice and heartbeat.
His API:
  Base address http://10.20.46.1/api/v1/&hellip;, no authentication.
  0.11.0 has no heartbeat endpoint.
  The tx_min_interval_secs rate limit was added by Nathan on 09-24.
  The full spec is at /openapi.json.

C. 10-21: WHAT WAS DECIDED AFTERWARDS. It supersedes the proposal v9 and email 1 where they differ.
TopicDecision (Fred 10-21)Why
Message standardStay on the Meshtastic V1 standard: positions and role reports as TAKPacket on port 72, as the T1000-Es and GroupTrack already send. GroupTrack does NOT move to 257. Email 1 said it would, and that is corrected in email v3.Stock ATAK/iTAK users on any Meshtastic radio, with the plugin, read V1 on 72 directly. Port 78 (V2) exists only in 2.8, which is alpha. 257 carrying TAKPacketV2 is Nathan's own choice, and only his bridge reads it. Format and port go together: 72 = V1, 78 = V2. V1 on 78 would be discarded.
Gap polylineStays V2 on port 78, uncompressed (0xFF), GroupTrack to GroupTrack only. No polyline in ATAK/iTAK ("we do not need polylines in ATAK"). The ask to Nathan for polyline &rarr; CoT is dropped.Both ends are GroupTrack, and the radios relay any port without reading it. That is why it works today on 2.6.11. Nathan's bridge ignores 78, so ATAK never sees it.
Port 257Nathan's only. It is how his Wi-Fi riders reach LoRa (CoT &rarr; 257, as built). GroupTrack only READS 257. Nothing of ours goes on 257.Fred's "256" in an earlier message meant 257. Port 256 is Nathan's voice port.
Radio firmwareNo firmware update. The fleet stays on 2.6.11 (TAK_TRACKER &rarr; port 72).2.8.x is Alpha/Revoked only; 2.7.26 is the latest Beta. The first 2.8.0 build was revoked for T1000-E LR1110 start-up failures. #11607: TAK_TRACKER position reports stop after 10&ndash;15 min on 2.8.0, fix unconfirmed. Discussion #8724: T1000-E send/receive breaks after 2.7.15. 2.8 also defaults to LongTurbo, takes node IDs from the public key (our uid basis), turns position and telemetry off by default, and changes nRF52 storage (full erase). A bench test on Billy beans waits for a 2.8 Beta.
The NucleusPaused. Starlink and the internet link are removed (off grid). Ten bare radios do everything ten Nucleus units do for GroupTrack, and for ATAK/iTAK users with a radio. The Pi adds only Wi-Fi for radio-less ATAK users near its cart, the internet link, and voice. S00104 at $430 is not justified per cart; the bare radio at ~$100 (+$50 optional power) is the ask.All cart-to-cart work is LoRa. Nucleus Wi-Fi range does not cover a spread-out group. His default SHORT_FAST is shorter range than our MEDIUM_FAST. Range comes from the radio (the 1 W module plus external antenna), not the Pi.
Wi-Fi (IP) instead of BluetoothBluetooth stays. Wi-Fi is not shown to be more reliable. ESP32-class bare radio requested only as an option.Meshtastic documentation:
"Enabling Wi-Fi will disable Bluetooth" (one or the other);
"SoftAP mode is not supported" (the radio cannot be the hotspot);
reports of ESP32 Wi-Fi drops after 1&ndash;2 h, about 20% loss (old 1.3 firmware);
TCP is the secondary transport on Android.
An Android hotspot without a SIM or internet varies by device (missing on Wi-Fi-only tablets). A local-only hotspot gets a random name and password each start, which a radio cannot store. Check: Droid 1 and Droid 2 in airplane mode with Wi-Fi on &rarr; does Hotspot switch on? If a fixed network is ever needed, a USB travel router costs far less than a Pi.
Starlink later?If an off-ride view is ever wanted, the lead's GroupTrack tablet is the gateway: the mesh by radio plus the internet by Starlink Wi-Fi, forwarding to a TAK server or AWS. No Pi.Every cart's position reaches the lead over LoRa.

E. 2.7b APPLICATION SIMPLIFICATION: remove screens, let the processes take their parts as input (Fred 10-18 direction; tasks set out 10-21 12:01)
Fred 10-21: remove screens, "letting functions take parts as input so screens are not called back to back", "moving data to the launch screen", and "running processes without further screen prompts".
Fred 10-18: the app is overwhelmingly complex, and navigation must be simplified. Take the screens out of processes and move their value forward to the processes that call them, so we are not nesting six layers deep. Each flow executes one task. Separate the prompt screen from a parameter-driven process. Simplification follows the tick removal ("we will have tamed the app"), and the tick is now gone.
The rule each flow must meet:
ONE launch screen collects everything the task needs, with defaults pre-filled from the ride or settings.
It hands those values to a process function as parameters.
The process runs to the end with no further screen prompts.
A process never opens another screen to get a value; that value is a parameter or a default.
The only allowed stop is a confirmation before something destructive or irreversible.
No screen-to-screen chains.
TaskWhatHow / output
S1 InventoryEvery function that shows a screen, panel or dialog, and who calls it. Find every chain where a screen or process opens another screen, with its depth (the "six layers").The function references (function universe / where-used, the navxref tool) &rarr; a table: flow, launch screen, chain of screens, depth, the values each intermediate screen collects. Desk work only, no code change. Comes first.
S2 Split prompt from processFor each chain, pull the work out of the screens into a process function that takes its parts (parameters) as input.Process functions callable with no UI: testable, and reusable from a check-in, a ride package or another process.
S3 Move the data forwardThe values the intermediate screens collected move to the launch screen, or to defaults from the ride or settings. The intermediate screens are removed.One launch screen per task. Fewer screens in total.
S4 Order of workThe deepest and most-used chains first. One flow per patch, bench-tested before the next (as with the tick removal).The S1 table ranked by depth &times; use.
S5 ReadabilityThe text navigation line (Search, Map Features, Map Keys, Group Help, GRP Awareness, Work with Rides) is hard to read over some maps. The colour choices on the artifact detail panels.Contrast that holds on every basemap (satellite, red rock, topo).
S6 Side menuOne button slides a panel out with the navigation options, and the panel closes once an option is chosen. It replaces the text line.Fred's idea (10-18 19:37).
S7 Compare onX and GaiaHow they keep navigation flat.A short comparison to guide S3 and S6.
Also still open at the back of 2.7b: the radio-setup timeout on a delayed reboot (Wio Tracker). It reads like the phantom connection that spoils the reconnect.
F. 2.7b NAVIGATION, VISIBILITY, LOOK AND FEEL (Fred 10-21 12:04). Ideas taken from onX and Gaia. Plain labelled controls: no complex icons, no hover-for-text. Expands E's S5&ndash;S7.
Fred 10-21: "navigation and visibility improvements in app improving navigation and look and feel. reference onX and Gaia for conceptual ideas. staying away from complex or hover over icons for text".
Why no hover: a touch screen has no hover. In a moving cart, with gloves, vibration and sun glare, an icon whose meaning needs a long press or a tooltip will not be read.
What onX and Gaia do (concepts only, nothing copied):
The map is the home screen. onX: "Most of the tools you'll use live in the bottom toolbar". There are only a few controls along the top and the right side.
One location button with two states. onX: the first tap centres the map north-up, the second tap switches to heading-up.
Layers and basemap behind one button that opens a sheet. Both apps do this. Offline maps are reached from the same place in Gaia.
One big primary-action button. Gaia uses a large green "+" at the bottom right for its most common task.
A unified icon set, refined colours, fonts and layouts. This was the core of Gaia's redesign, made to make backcountry navigation simpler.
Account, settings and help sit in a main menu, off the map.
TaskWhatRule / output
V1 Navigation barReplace the hard-to-read text navigation line (Search, Map Features, Map Keys, Group Help, GRP Awareness, Work with Rides) with a short bar of 4&ndash;5 items. Each item is an icon with its text label always shown. Everything else goes in one menu: Fred's slide-out side menu (S6), which closes once an option is chosen.No more than one level of menu. Fred decides what goes in the bar and what goes in the menu.
V2 Readable on any mapEvery control and its label sits on an opaque background (a chip or panel with an edge), never as bare text over the map.Readable on satellite, red rock and topo. This fixes S5.
V3 Big touch targetsButtons sized for a moving cart and gloves, well above the phone minimum, with space between them.Size set once and used everywhere.
V4 One lookOne colour palette (built around the bright blue #1E88FF already used for the tracks), one type scale readable in sun, one simple icon set. The colours on the artifact detail panels are brought into line.Written down once as the GroupTrack style and used on every screen.
V5 Location buttonOne button: tap = centre north-up, tap again = heading-up. Shown as an icon with a label of its state.From onX.
V6 One primary actionOne large button for the task a rider does most (for example REC / start the ride). Fred names it.From Gaia.
V7 One layers buttonMap Features, Map Keys and the basemap choice behind one button that opens one sheet.Fewer items in the bar.
V8 Mock-ups firstA picture of the main map screen (the bar, menu, buttons, colours) for Fred to review before any code. Then one screen per patch, bench-tested.Done together with E: the S1 inventory shows which screens survive.
The rules for every control:
no icon without a visible label;
no meaning that only appears on long press or hover;
no bare text over the map;
no second-level menus;
the same control looks and behaves the same on every screen.
Sources (10-21): onX support, "Interactive Tutorial and Controls"; UTV Driver, "Gaia GPS Gets a Key Redesign"; Bikepacking.com, "New Gaia GPS".

The gap polyline (POLYLINE-2026-10-20) -- the design as built
Lead side (GroupTrack): dead air = the time the LEAD hears NO other cart (one cart heard = the hops relay to the rest). After &ge; 60 s of it (Fred 14:45: "a good even number" = six broadcasts), the first report heard from another cart sends ONE polyline: 20 points at equal time steps across [last heard .. heard again] from the lead's own radio fixes (option 1), plus one repeat at the next report heard &ge; 10 s later. Fewer than 2 own fixes in the window = nothing sent (logged). The lead = checked in as Leader, or the cart locked as lead at REC. Pop-up "Gap polyline sent: m:ss of dead air".
Receive, three layers (Fred 14:27 -- keep GroupTrack's message out of the mesh layer): core/data TakShapeInbox (NEW, generic: ANY TAK drawn shape, no GroupTrack knowledge; POLYTEST's GtPolylineInbox retired -- renamed *.removed_POLYLINE-2026-10-20, uncommitted, delete at clean-up) &rarr; comm layer MeshCommMessaging recognises u-d-f + uid GT-gap- &rarr; CommEvent.PolylineReceived (NEW, additive) &rarr; GroupTrack onGapPolylineReceived: pop-up; the LEAD's polyline with REC on &rarr; TrackEntry.Poly &rarr; LeadCartProcess.onGapPolyline &rarr; TrackWriter.pin. The repeat is recognised (sender + start) and not applied twice.
Pin (Fred 14:02-14:04, 14:47): the polyline REPLACES -- never a second line. Kept: the lead track up to the LAST REAL point heard before the window; removed: everything inferred after it; the 20 points joined in order by the fill rules (displayed route &rarr; known tracks &rarr; saved routes &rarr; trails &rarr; straight); the reconnect point joined to the first real point after the window; everything after stays. A point more than 50 m off the displayed route (or off every known line near it) is a DOT, never joined ("one point off turns the path into angles").
Radio setup: rebroadcast mode = ALL is now managed at check-in (written + verified: 25 checks); NONE / CORE_PORTNUMS_ONLY would stop relaying or drop TAK.
Desk test: LF loop 10,845 m pinned vs 10,768 m real (4 dots); afternoon 10,954 vs 11,115 (2 dots).
Road test 15:30-15:47 (Droid 1 leading the loop, Droid 2 parked): Droid 2 last heard the lead 15:29:01; the lead's own dead air 15:30:19 &rarr; 15:36:18 = 359 s; sent 15:36:18 (20 points, 202 bytes), received 2.1 s later (the clock difference within that), pinned with 10 of 20 as dots; repeat 15:36:38 recognised. All 20 points lie on the road Droid 1 drove (19 within 0-2 m, 1 at 22 m between fixes). The 10 dots = where this afternoon's loop left this morning's saved tracks (7 points 66-168 m from them; no route displayed) -- the rule worked as written; proposal (Fred to decide): with NO route displayed, a polyline point joins straight (it is the lead's real position).
The trim (TRIM-2026-10-20) -- my cart replaces the lead track behind me
Fred 14:49-14:56: "rather than overlay it replaces"; "any lead cart point behind my cart ... trimmed at the next my-track write"; BY TIME, not geometry ("we had problems with these rules in twists"); all times UTC epoch ms (Arizona &rarr; Utah is a time-zone change -- local time would wreak havoc).
Each MY-CART position (the feed that moves my icon -- tablet GPS, or my radio without a chip): the first lead-track SEGMENT within 50 m of my cart, searching FORWARD ONLY from the last cut; on to the next segment only while my cart is level with the joint (twists); DRIVING ORDER -- the cut moves no further along the lead's line than my cart has driven since the last cut (+150 m; steps &ge; 5 m, jitter is not driving). The DISPLAY is cut at that segment's start, by time; the written lead track stays whole (fills, pins, other carts' off-track). Polyline pins are trimmed the same way.
Desk test (TrimSim, Droid 1's real fixes lf / est / range, follower 30 s .. 20 min behind, my-cart updates every 3 / 6 / 10 s -- 45 runs): never skipped ground; the cut at most ~60 m ahead of my cart (where the lead was parked); at most one lead segment behind (&le; 435 m on these fixes; shorter with route fill). Two failures found and fixed on the way: point matching jumped 10 km to an out-and-back's return leg (fixes ~160 m apart at speed) &rarr; segments; a parked follower was cut to the lead's return home after a 10 km loop &rarr; driving order. A chipless tablet (6 s radio fixes) trims the same (Fred's concern, 16:04).

What the logs and the code proved today (evidence, not theory)
The tablet GPS chip needs about 5 minutes of open sky for its first lock (Unisoc chip; no SIM, no Wi-Fi assist). Log: fixStatus=A/V, num_svs. Recording works once it has locked (13:20 run). Not a defective chip (my wrong claim this morning, withdrawn).
The second stream of my cart on other tablets was our own role report (every 30 s, it carried my cart's position = the tablet's since ONEFEED). Fred: "check the logs" -- they showed it. Fixed by ROLEPOS.
Sleep 84 s after REC (Droid 2): REC at 11:11:50 in the same app process as the 10:48 recording &rarr; the sleep clock still held the earlier time &rarr; "no movement for 25 min" at the first points (11:13:14). A recording that ended asleep also left every new point dropped. Fixed by RECSLEEP.
The z0 / white screen: every restart that restored the saved frame was followed ~2.5 s later by a zero-size view at 43.06888777, -71.71875 -- exactly my cart rounded to one pixel at ZOOM 0 -- then the whole world. Leaflet's fitBounds works the zoom out from the map's size; called before the map has a size it picks zoom 0. setView (given its zoom) never did this. Offline there are no z0 tiles = white. The saved frames themselves were good (my first theory, a 0,0,0,0 saved frame, was wrong). Only ONE place restores the ride map from the saved file (start-up, ConvoyScreen ~964 + drawPersistedState); FIT uses the database's own bounds. Fixed by FITSIZE + MAPSTARTUP.
The lead track did not follow home6 on the 13:20 drive because Fred drove it against its arrows and the forward-only rule refused the route (simulation lead_sim_track13_2026-10-19_v2.png). Fixed by ROUTEBOTH.
This morning's Droid 1 Bluetooth stack was stuck: registerApp got no onClientRegistered, scans failed with ApplicationRegistrationFailed; only Bluetooth off/on cleared it. FORGET does remove the radio from Android when it is really connected (Fred).
Droid 1's radio GPS mode was found DISABLED (Fred 17:14) -- its position had been frozen at 42.80064,-71.27742 since 09:55. GroupTrack's default writes gpsMode: ENABLED and the setup checks it, so it was not our setup. Likely (not certain): the Meshtastic firmware toggles GPS on a triple press of the user button -- the T1000-E's only button, pressed all day for power cycles. After both radios were powered down and reconnected both tablets saw each other (17:28); that radio still had a weak GPS signal. "1 radio, 0 active" in GRP Awareness = radio linked but sending nothing.
The reconnect panel v3 never opened (Droid 1, ~17:00): it was gated on "riding with a group" = this tablet sees at least one other cart -- false, because Droid 1 heard no other cart. The log was lost to a reboot; the cause is from the code and what Fred saw. v4 gates on group awareness ON.
A reboot wipes the log buffer AND resets logcat -G 16M (twice today). Pull logs before any reboot; set -G again after one.
Android 13+ will not let an app switch Bluetooth (we target 36): the panel uses Android's own dialogs. The turn-OFF dialog (android.bluetooth.adapter.action.REQUEST_DISABLE) is not a published Android call -- whether these tablets show it is a tablet test (fallback: Android's Bluetooth screen after 8 s).
Recovery timing is inherited, not measured: tries 45 s apart and "stuck connecting" 45 s came from LINKHB (10-05). A normal reconnect took ~20-25 s in the setup logs; once 98 s after an install.
Range this morning: Droid 2 lost between about 100 and 175 m out. Droid 2's clock is Utah time (2 h behind).

ModuleWhat it doesBuild 1Later
TrackPath (plain Kotlin, no Android — testable alone)previous point + new point + map context (loaded route, nearby trails) → the points to draw between them, the snapped location of the new point, and the rule used: ROUTE · TRAIL · STRAIGHT · WAIT.
Order: ROUTE (both points within 50 m of the loaded route → path along the route) → TRAIL (nearest trail within the snap distance → path along it; at a junction WAIT until the next point BEYOND the junction is received — never guess a branch) → STRAIGHT.
STRAIGHT works; ROUTE and TRAIL are placeholders that answer "not applicable" and log itbuild 3 ROUTE filled · build 4 TRAIL + junction wait — inside the module only, callers untouched
CartMotiona received message → the path from TrackPath split into N one-second steps; the cart icon (and the drawn track) advance each second so carts move steadily. Goal (Fred 07:58): the mapping progress COMPLETES BEFORE THE NEXT UPDATE arrives; after a long silence (e.g. 2 min) there will be a jump — accepted.
placeholder = the full gap in ONE step (Fred 08:06: today's behaviour)build 5 stepping
CartMotion rules (proposed 07:56, taken as agreed 07:58): the steps are display-only — not stored as track points, never sent, no last-heard or status change, not used for off-track or the 50 m passed rule (only real reports count);
catch-up from the last real point to the new one, never projected ahead (consistent with "wait for real fixes"); N = the cart's NORMAL report interval so the steps finish before the next expected report (observed radios ~20 s, configured 6 s / 30 s);
a report that arrives early continues from wherever the icon is. The stepping is a short job per received message, not a standing timer. Separate NON-software task: maximise cart broadcast distance to shrink the dead spots (preset MEDIUM_FAST vs LONG_FAST, antenna placement).

ONE lead track whoever leads: old points stay as assigned, new points come only from the current leader, a lead change CONTINUES the track (replaces "a lead change starts a new line"). Underneath, every message carries its UTC epoch time; elapsed = message epoch − ride-start epoch. TrackPath / CartMotion / the board never use a tablet's local clock time (Droid 2 runs on Utah time, so its logs read 2 h behind; its epoch time is the same). Ride start = each tablet's own REC press (Fred 08:11). RECEIVED-ACTIVITY RECORD (Fred 08:14 → 08:16): each tablet writes a detail file of the activity it RECEIVES — for every received report of every cart: the cart, the time received, the elapsed time since this tablet's REC, the message's own time, the location (and speed / course when sent). It is the source for the metrics later and for CartMotion's steady segments (each cart's normal report interval). Right now it only RECORDS the data — no broadcast change, no calculations (distance, metrics) yet. Format (Fred 08:17–08:20): a separate ride detail JSON beside the track file (&lt;track&gt;_ride_detail.json), held in memory by cart, written at END and when the app goes to the background (event, not timer). Lead (Fred 08:22): the lead is identified in the JSON — each report carries lead: true when that cart was the lead at that moment, and a leadChanges list records every change (elapsed, from, to) — so a replay can draw the lead track, then my cart's track. Ride detail JSON — the target definition (v1, Fred 10-18 08:14–08:26)
What it is: each tablet's record of the messaging payload it RECEIVED during one recording (REC → END) — the full received-message data captured for later analytics
(ride metrics, replay at selectable speeds, CartMotion's per-cart report interval, weak-device and range analysis). Built AFTER the tick, as part of ride metric reporting; this definition is the target.
File: &lt;track name&gt;_ride_detail.json beside the recording's track file (separate — the track file keeps my tablet's own GPS points; they are not doubled here).
Writes: held in memory, grouped by cart; written at END and when the app goes to the background (an event, not a timer).
Time: every time is UTC epoch ms; e = elapsed seconds since THIS tablet's REC (ride start = each tablet's own REC press).

Pipeline (Fred 08:30–08:31): 1) receive — the comm side makes the CoT message; the board updates the cart's TRUTH at once (last heard, status, lead) and the ride detail JSON records the report (when built — on RECEIVE, never on process); lead-track points and off-track come from the real report here. 2) CartMotion black box → 3) map position function → one or more queue entries (cart, position, due time, real / in-between) → 4) map queue: every radio receipt goes through it; an entry is processed when due — cart icon moves, the drawn track extends through TrackPath, the 50 m trim applies. In-between steps are display-only and never recorded. One queue, one process (Fred 08:33–08:34): every received message goes into the RECEIVING QUEUE (stamped with its received time); one consumer takes them in order, updates the board truth, writes the ride JSON (placeholder until the metric reporting), and CartMotion puts N entries back on the SAME queue — N = 1 now, N = the cart's steps later; same queue, same process, only N changes. Each entry is flagged real or in-between: only the REAL one updates the truth and the JSON; in-between entries only move the display. First pass (build 1): the FULL message only — ONE entry per received message, due now; no per-second entries driven by the report frequency (later, build 5).
Lead change (Fred 08:39–08:41): the new lead is picked up from where he is; NO line is drawn for him until he passes the last known lead position — he comes within 50 m of it, and the track continues from his NEXT report (ahead) — no backwards lines. Lead silent = no lead movement until heard again; heard again = the track is laid from his last point to the new one (over route/trail) on every map, shown back to each tablet's own cart. My track trails my cart.
Queue placement (08:37): the receiving queue + its consumer run in the BACKGROUND, ONCE for the app (an app-wide owner — not one per view-model copy, item J, or every message would be processed and written twice); the map drawing runs in the FOREGROUND, only while the map shows (hidden: keep each cart's latest position, catch up on return).
Model run (tracksim_2026-10-18.py, 10-18 08:36–08:45): 15 min, reports every 20 s, lead silent 140 s, a lead change at 10:00 to a cart 200 m behind — at N = 1 and at N = steps: no lead points during the silence (status Drop) · JSON = real messages only · lead changes logged · only points ahead of my cart shown · NO backward lines. Rules the model forced (now part of the design): (1) a new real report CANCELS that cart's pending steps; (2) N = the NORMAL interval (median of the last 5 gaps), never the last gap — a 160 s gap had produced 160 overlapping steps; (3) the lead LINE grows from its own end toward the real point, not from the cart icon; (4) the JSON leaves out my tablet's own GPS points; (5) the 50 m trim uses the real lead points.
THE PROCESS — seven boxes, one queue (Fred 08:45; model process_model_2026-10-18.py): 1 Receiver (every report → the receiving queue, stamped; background, once for the app) → 2 Truth (last heard, position, lead + the CLOCK, ageing only) → 3 Recorder (ride JSON on receive; not my tablet's GPS) → 4 LeadTrack (real lead points, one track, lead-change hold, waits through silence, off-track per report) → 5 TrackPath (ROUTE / TRAIL placeholders, STRAIGHT) → 6 Segmenter (CartMotion: N entries on the same queue; N = 1 now; a new report cancels pending entries) → 7 Map (foreground: icon moves, lead line grows from its end, 50 m trim, my track behind my cart).Tests 10-18 08:50 — one message: processed, queue empty, line started, 1 JSON report. Three carts with connects/disconnects for each (L silent 140 s, B gone 350 s, my radio off 60 s) and a lead change at 10:00, at N = 1 and at N = steps: my cart from the tablet during my radio drop, Active, my track without gaps · L Drop while silent, NO lead points added · B Lost while gone, Active on its first report back · 0 backward lines · JSON 92 real reports, none of my tablet's GPS · lead changes logged · shown line only ahead of my cart · queue drains. 9. Lead track · my cart and my track · lead polyline · removing the tick — the design in fullCarried here in full (Fred 10-15 EOD: the living docs must hold it, not point to the plan). Source: Tick Replacement Plan v6, sections 0, 4c, 5, 6, 11, 12, 14, 17.
A. The lead track — what the code does today (in the tick, ConvoyViewModel ~1172–1293):
While REC is on, each NEW lead position (the lead's own report, never a substitute) adds one straight segment from the previous lead position to the new one (_routeTrailSegments).
A lead change starts a new line. _leadTrackSegments = the lead only, drawn black (or per-cart colours).
Off-track = a cart farther than OFF_TRACK_MILES (Settings → Off Track) from any segment, swept every tick.
Proxy snap (a cart within ~250 ft of the quiet lead's last position stands in for the lead) — KILLED (Fred 15:15).
Found 10-15 on the ride: the lead's OWN tablet drew no lead track — its lead position came from its own radio's record, which never moved on its own tablet (the same cause as the my-cart freeze; MYCARTMSG fixes the source).
B. The lead-track rules (Fred 10-15 13:25–13:29):
Source order: 1) the route if loaded — a lead position within 50 m is snapped onto the route and the track runs along the route (ROUTETRACK); 2) no route → the trails — snap to the nearest trail and follow it; 3) neither nearby → the raw reported positions, two points joined.
At a trail junction: place only the lead's cart pointer and WAIT for the next position before connecting the track — the next point shows the branch taken; never guess a branch.
Difficulty / build order: route = easy · two points = easy · trails = touchy (junctions, parallel trails). Build: two-point first, then route, trails last once the junction rule is proven.
Off-track (Fred 14:12): the track is a PATH each cart is measured against when that cart's own position arrives — not a sweep of every cart on a timer.
Fred 10-15 EOD — a trail behind EVERY cart; the lead's trail is one of them. Same builder for every cart, fed by that cart's new fixes on the board.
Open: snap distance to a trail; what happens when the lead leaves the trail; (a) a lead change mid-ride — new line (today) or join to the new lead's position; (b) does the trail follow the projected cart during Signal Drop or wait for real fixes; (c) keep OFF_TRACK_MILES as is.
Builds: LEADTRACK-1 / TRAILS-1 = the two-point trail rebuilt on the board on each cart's new fix (no tick) + off-track per cart message → T5.5 can then remove the tick · ROUTETRACK (route snap ≤ 50 m) · trails with the junction wait. Each its own build.
C. My cart and my track:
My cart = a CoT message from the tablet's GPS (MYCARTMSG 3583eda96, Fred 17:16–17:46): uid MESHTASTIC-!&lt;my radio&gt;, point + altitude, speed/course from the fix; sent on every CHANGED fix (~1 s moving), a keep-alive once per reporting interval parked; through onBoardMessage like every other cart. My radio's own record no longer drives my cart while the tablet has had a fix in the last 15 s. No radio known / group off → the tablet-cart path.
My recorded track (GPX) is written from the tablet's own GPS (~1/s). RADIOTRACK (751a0a230) feeds my radio's new fixes to the recorder, in METRES, only for a tablet WITHOUT GPS hardware (the tick passed display feet → 3.3× high altitudes). Not yet tried on a no-GPS tablet.
REC active: my cart icon = the head of my track (every fix) (Fred 09:49–09:55) — T5c.
No-GPS tablet: my cart's message is built at the radio's frequency from the radio's fix — open (DIAGPOS, written, not applied).
Other carts between broadcasts (4c, Fred 07:55–09:39): on the route (≤ 50 m, snapped) a cart keeps moving along the route at its last reported speed until heard again (no cut-off), then ONE correction move to the reported position; off the route it holds at the last report and moves to exactly the reported position (how the group sees someone getting lost). Move only on a NEW fix. Display only — never changes the board. Status still Signal Drop 2 min / Lost 10 min.
D. The lead polyline (T7, Phase 1) and segment display (Phase 2):
Phase 1 / T7: the lead transmits his polyline — the last 2 minutes of his track, every broadcast (6 s); receivers mine ONLY its last point as the lead's position. No sender checkbox (v2 change). First check whether the polyline message exists yet; if not, sending it is part of T7.
Phase 2 (after certification): polyline SEGMENT display with an on/off toggle on the receiver — the sender always sends the same message. 4. Findings (connection)
Two owners reconnect the same radio: Meshtastic's own connect (Android background connect, auto:true) and GroupTrack's recovery (MeshCommLink keep-alive: 20 s not talking / 45 s stuck / 120 s no traffic for a Rider → forced drop + reconnect; 3 tries → banner). Droid 1 13:31–13:35: 7 connects in 4 minutes, then a stuck link.
Meshtastic's connect timeout (15 s) does not cancel its pending request (NordicBleInterface.connect() catch: no bleConnection.disconnect()) — requests can stack on the same device. One-line fix found, NOT applied.
Meshtastic starts a connect by itself in three places (AndroidRadioInterfaceService): MeshService start, every Bluetooth-state change (including each pairing change — our pairing listener refreshes it), network available.
After an install the background connect took 98 s (Droid 2 14:01); a direct connect came up within a second.
Recovery only acts after a first connection this session (hConnectedThisSession) — it did not run before the first connect; after a drop it can act while Meshtastic is attaching.
Hide Mesh stacks copies of the convoy logic: mesh rail screens remove the ride map from the stack (popUpTo(start){saveState=true}) and Hide Mesh re-runs the gate → a new ride map + view model + tick each time. HIDEMESHBACK v1 failed for that reason; MESHOVERLAY (mesh opens on top of the ride map) written, not applied.
Processes 1183 / 1679 seen connecting alongside ours = Android's own Bluetooth service, not another app.
Android's last-known position is read in 5 places (my cart fallback in the tick, ride-map entry centring, planning-entry check, planning map, home-state detection). Fred 22:30: it can be a week old, but the first radio / tablet fix moves the map — no change.

9. Lessons
Compare a good startup log with a bad one FIRST (Fred 20:43): we had a recording of every install and still chased radios and configs. Tonight's 20:3x install is the recorded known-good startup.
A collector started in init runs at once on the main thread — everything it touches must be declared above init (the 12:14 crash).
A crash loop during Meshtastic's connect leaves half-open Bluetooth links — a plausible cause of the afternoon's Bluetooth trouble.
Never reason past evidence: every theory today that was not checked against the log was wrong at least in part (second app = Android's own service; "recovery ran before the first connect" — it did not).
Our own red message caused damage: it told the rider to Forget while the radio had just started talking.
Read the right tablet: with two plugged in every adb command uses -s &lt;serial&gt;.

7. Lessons
Change ONE thing at a time. Rolling back the code AND rebooting together hid which one cured it; it took a bisect to separate them.
Contaminated devices prove nothing. Once Bluetooth was stuck, every later install failed whatever its code — re-establish a clean baseline (reboot) before testing a suspect. Claude wrongly "cleared" DISCPANEL at 12:09 from a contaminated test; Fred caught it.
Android refuses a lower version code silently in deploy.sh. To test older code without uninstalling (which wipes maps, rides and settings): a test branch with git revert (version code goes UP), then git merge -s ours back so the main branch stays above it.
Git Bash rewrites /sdcard/… into a Windows path — use //sdcard/… with adb shell. git log opens a pager — use git --no-pager log (or press q).
Kotlin extension functions need an import (animateFloat) — a fully-qualified call does not reach them.
Patch anchors with escapes: the file writer turned \u00b7 into a literal ·; the patch aborted cleanly. Check written patches for escaped characters.
Self-tripping post-checks, third time (REPORTNOW's comment named the very token it forbade) — word marker comments to avoid forbidden tokens.

⚠ FALLBACK RULE (Fred 10-12 19:53) — do not confuse the two: Android device only is a MODE the rider chooses (no radio asked, group functions hidden). The fallback is different: in Meshtastic group-awareness mode, when the radio disconnects, Android data is substituted for radio data on the local node — my cart takes the tablet's GPS so its information stays current (today's LINKFIX / LINKFIX2: other carts held at their last tick position, nothing invented). When the radio returns, my cart goes back to the radio's data. The data must roll back and forth with the link, as many times as it drops, with the group functions staying visible. GRPMODE must not switch the mode when the link drops, and P5.1 must keep this substitution when the tick's source moves to members() (with the radio down, members() is stale or empty — my cart comes from the tablet). Tablet check for both: in Meshtastic mode, radio off → my cart keeps moving on the tablet's GPS, others held, GRP Awareness red; radio on → my cart back on the radio's position, same cart id; repeat twice.
⚠ MY-CART SOURCE RULE (Fred 10-12 19:55) — refines the fallback rule: with GRP Awareness on, my cart is ONE cart, keyed by my callsign. Its data comes from the radio when the radio's own report has been refreshed within the last 2 broadcast intervals; if the radio's data is more than 2 broadcast intervals old, from the tablet. A fresh radio report switches it back. Same cart, same callsign, either way. Today the switch follows link health (radio "not talking" = no own report for 45 s, LINKHB). To settle 10-13 (G5): which interval — proposed: 2 × the moving interval while the tablet's GPS shows motion (e.g. 6 s → 12 s), 2 × the stationary 30 s when stopped (60 s), so a parked cart does not flip between its 30-s reports. The intervals come from the comm side (currentReporting(), P5.2) — so P5.2 moves before P5.1b.
✅ G5 DECIDED (Fred 10-12 19:57) — "really simple": the limit is 2 broadcast intervals (moving every 6 s → 12 s). When my radio's last report is older than that, my cart takes the tablet's GPS only if the tablet has moved since the last update; if it has not moved, my cart stays where the last update put it. No motion test on the radio side, no separate stationary limit — a parked cart simply does not change. Fresh radio report → back to the radio. Same cart, same callsign.
✅ TWO POSITIONS IN MY CART'S RECORD (Fred 10-12 19:58): my node records both the radio's GPS (position + fix time, from the comm side) and the tablet's GPS (position + fix time). The display applies the G5 rule to choose which to show: radio fix ≤ 2 broadcast intervals old (12 s at 6 s) → radio; older AND the tablet has moved since the last update → tablet; otherwise the last shown position. Why: it ends the GPS jitter between cart and radio — today one position field is overwritten by whichever source wrote last, so two receivers a few feet apart make the cart hop. Both values stay in the record for logging and tests. Only my own cart has two sources; other carts are radio-only and unchanged. Lands in P5.1b (ConvoyNode gains the radio and tablet fixes for my cart; the choice is one function, logged when it switches).

Reference numbers (10-12): one Meshtastic packet ≈ 230 bytes of data ≈ 40–50 points (first point ~8 bytes, then ~4 bytes each). Simplified (Douglas–Peucker, ~5 m) riding needs ~3–10 points per minute → 1 min ≈ 20–50 bytes, 2 min ≈ 35–90 bytes, 5 min ≈ 70–210 bytes (twisty may need coarser older detail). 20 min does not fit one packet and is not needed — each tablet stitches the full lead track from the pieces.
Why the ride must reach every rider (Fred): a point on a map without a route is useless. Group tracking needs (1) faithful distribution of ride invites to all GroupTrack users before the ride and (2) compliance — even Android-only riders stay on course far better with the ride imported. 5. Lessons
A patch's own comment can trip its own post-check — twice now (P2b "scanModel", P4.4 "radioOps()"). Word marker comments so they never contain a forbidden token; the scratch test caught it before Fred saw it.
gt_build's "N UNCOMMITTED change(s)" counts tracked files only — new untracked files are in the build but not in the count; a move needs an explicit git add of the folders (git then records renames).
Long commit messages: plain ASCII only (Fred's paste picked up bad characters); give add / commit / push as three separate commands and always paste git log --oneline -1.
"Never applied" ≠ "never set up": GRP Awareness judged the radio by this tablet's records; the radio's own network is the truth (RADIONET).
A stale report: the comm side's applyReport outlives the screen — cleared at the start of every apply (found in scratch review before sending P4.2).
6. Other threads today
Sean Connell's meshtastic_flutter (github.com/seancmt/meshtastic_flutter, BSD-3): a fork of Madhav Gupta's package (0.0.3) + 12 commits by Sean (9–10 Apr 2026): write-with-response, non-zero want_config_id, iOS MTU / Android-12 permission guards, sendData, sendAdminConfig. ~650 hand-written lines + generated protobufs. No reconnect, sleep or timeout handling, no pairing, no multi-step config write. Nothing to take for Android; a possible starting point for the 2.9 Apple Bluetooth layer behind the same comm contract. Fred's reply to Sean: reconnects, sleeps and Bluetooth timeouts were his biggest T1000-E problems and where he wrote his own recovery code.
AI cost question: GroupTrack makes no AI calls; the trail narrative (RouteExplorer.narrative()) is template text built on the tablet from OSM features — free per rider, works offline. If richer AI text is ever wanted: generate once per trail on the AWS server and store it.

📚 10-11 (evening) — USER DOCS NOW IN THE DAILY EOD SET · manual v53 · release notes v33 · Quick Start v80
The rule (Fred 10-11): the current manual, release notes and Quick Start are carried in the EOD set every day, beside the handoff, living master, WHERE WE ARE and ledger. Each day's user-visible changes go into them that day — text updated, and every screen that changed labelled in the manual as it changes. That is the only way to stay on top of the changes; a catch-up later becomes a large task that misses them.
Labels in the manual (visible, with a grep-able RECAPTURE-2026-10-11 comment): 📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED (red — the picture is out of date) · 📷 IMAGE TO CHECK (amber — may have changed) · 📷 NEW SCREEN — CAPTURE TO ADD (blue — a screen not yet pictured). A label is removed only when its picture is recaptured. Labels are visible to readers until then — remove or hide them before a public refresh only if Fred decides so.
Each EOD: for every rider-visible change of the day (a release, or a build headed to one): release notes entry · manual text · Quick Start step if a step changed · a label on every affected picture. New version numbers each day something changed; never reuse a file name.
Online copy (grouptrack.org) is refreshed at release time from the current versions (standing step, WEBDOCS-2026-10-03).
