10-10 — ROOT CAUSE 1: the tester's missing trails
Symptom: after Remove all trail data + Utah re-import, the tester (and then Droid 2, deliberately) had no trails at all — e.g. Four Mile Wash, way 1003674700. The PC trace (gt_osmtrace_2026-10-10_v2.py) said the trail is KEPT and SHOWN, hash identical, land PUBLIC — so the import was right; the device's step 9 was not.
Mechanism: step 9 (OwnershipReclass.run) applied category, use AND land in one pass, and was skipped when the ownership file was missing or refused. Skipped → carto_code NULL → the map's filter carto_code NOT IN (off list) is NULL for NULL → every unclassified trail hidden, whatever Map Keys says.
Why the file was refused: OOMGUARD (09-15) checked heap headroom against the file size before reading. The streaming reader (09-17) made it obsolete, but it stayed. Fred's own 72 MB file (09-12) was loaded before the guard existed; a fresh download is 78.7 MB and was refused every time. The step reported "0", nothing in the log said why.
Fred's rule (10-10): "our categories are meaningless unless they are applied" — "the process has to run". Missing input → a default (land PUBLIC), never a skipped step.
Proof: failure replicated on Droid 2 first (clear → Utah import → no trails), the refusal found in Droid 1's log, release k on both tablets → all trails back; the launch pass repairs a tablet without a re-import.
10-10 — ROOT CAUSE 2: "Cannot use this target: String arg == null" on check-in
Symptom: "Cannot use this target: String arg == null" right after group 1b on every CHECK IN apply that restarts the radio, any ride; the radio nevertheless ended exactly on target (Fred's compare). Applying from "Apply ride to radio" never showed it; re-applying a ride already on the radio (nothing to write, no restart) never showed it.
Values were never the issue: the configurator reads only the ride's network.mesh (region, preset, slot, hop limit, TX power, role, channel name, key), the default asset's standalone reporting group and the callsign — all required; the two rides differed only in channel name, hop limit and key.
Mechanism: group 1b restarts the radio → node id goes null and back → LaunchedEffect(nodeId) rebuilds targets → the CHECK IN auto-apply LaunchedEffect(targets) fires again while autoRideId is still set → choose() runs mid-apply against a half-reconnected radio and paints the error over a successful apply.
Fix: APPLYGUARD (above). Tablet-tested 10-10: no errors on check-in.
Network choices — what Fred asked for (10-10, verbatim intent): "the Organization network replaced by GroupTrack Default, the Creator's network shown as Creator's name – Network id, and then private network." A ride on the GroupTrack default is heard by every GroupTrack radio — accepted by Fred. "No scheduled ride" check-in also uses the default unless the rider asks to keep the radio as it is.
Release l tablet tests (all passed 10-10, Fred): (1) Create Ride shows the three choices; (2) check in to a default ride sets the radio to GroupTrack, re-check-in shows "Radio ready"; (3) no-ride check-in applies the default, "Keep" leaves it; (4) no error on any check-in apply.
Method lessons 10-10 (keep):
A step that depends on an input must run with a default when the input is missing — never skip silently (Fred: "the process has to run").
Remove a guard when its reason goes: OOMGUARD outlived the reader it protected and broke every fresh import for three weeks.
Replicate the failure before fixing it (Fred cleared Droid 2 and reproduced the tester's empty map first).
Compose: an automatic action inside a LaunchedEffect keyed on state that changes during a long operation will re-fire — gate it on the phase.
Compare the paths that work with the path that fails (check-in vs manual apply; restart vs nothing-to-write) — that, not the values, found the apply error.

DECIDED 10-08 (Fred) — the boundary rules (full text: service-layer design v17 §R7): GroupTrack owns the panels (moving GRP Awareness to the comm side rejected — "not an option"); the comm module has service-level access only, headless, returning results · requests GroupTrack → comm, events comm → GroupTrack, a sender and a matching function on each side · a request never waits for its outcome · recovery is a request, the action is performed in the comm module, reconnection is an event · errors are events with reason codes; GroupTrack owns the words ("your radio is not recovering — forget it and pair again") · native Meshtastic menus and screens stay UNCHANGED, opened by request OVER GroupTrack (how they END is open) · no new direct Meshtastic calls · one service at a time, both directions — slow and steady, using the existing where-used inventory (gen_xrefs_v2.sh) before and after each step · finish line = GroupTrack in its own module, the compiler finds zero.
Separate-app model and licensing (§R7.3; not legal advice): like ATAK + Meshtastic — a mesh app that owns the radio and gives service-level access; we can ship our own open-source (GPL) mesh app ("GroupTrack Comm") so riders need no stock Meshtastic; GroupTrack talks to it at arm's length. Today and through 2.7b everything is one APK = one GPL work (source public keeps it compliant). Confirmed: the boundary is in the right place and the handoffs are compatible with the licence terms. 1. Where we are — in one card
TESTERS Release v2.7a-internal-2026-10-07e — commit 3db12ebd9, version code 29321295 (2.7.14). Built, bundle-checked, archived, tested on Fred's tablet, uploaded to Play. The remote tester has picked it up.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND The tester's "compare never launches / back to the start" was not compare, the batch files or his tablet. He had switched all trail types off in the map key and dropped his trailhead on one of his tracks. GroupTrack converts tracks into trails where no trail exists, so it looked like a trail — but those trails were hidden by the key. By design (Fred 09-01, "we route what you put on the map") the AI search uses only the trails the map key shows → empty network → 0 routes → no compare header → nothing to compare. The search's "no connected network" exit was silent (log only) and the AI panel, given no results, reopens on its first page — so the rider just saw "back to the start".
IN FLIGHT Release …-07f (not built yet): removes the "Clear AI routes" buttons (wasted effort once the cause was found) and adds the real fix — TRAILHEADNEAR: the AI trailhead step refuses a trailhead with no shown trail within ½ mile, with a message, and the search's own reach becomes ½ mile. 7. Radio — findings and open items
Reconnect loop (status: fixed): every ~76 s on old builds; gone with 30 s stationary (Droid 1 clean 20:53–21:34 on 10-06; Droid 2 clean all night with one self-healed drop).
Droid 1's radio …C4:6A dropped at the Bluetooth level (status 8) on 10-06 night despite 100 % battery → factory reset. After the reset it carried position.gps_en_gpio: 43 (the other radio …DE:DA has none; same firmware) → cleared to 0. Both radios then matched and their LED patterns synced. Cause of the drops still unproven.
"Every 4 s" TAK traffic was a counting artifact: each report received over the air is logged twice (uncompressed + compressed, 30 ms apart — two transmissions would need ~210 ms each). Own radio's reports appear once. Real rate ~8–12 s. to prove sender's numPacketsTx over 60 s (the CLI 2.7.11 --info did not print it).
Hop experiment: channel utilization ~6.6–7.0 % at hop 3 → ~5.0 % at hop 0 (relays ≈ 2 points with two radios); ~4–5 % is outside traffic on the frequency. Both radios now hop 2, 30 s / 100 m / 6 s, set by CLI (existing rides still carry hop 3 — a check-in to an old ride writes 3 back; use a fresh ride).
CLI over USB knocks the tablet's Bluetooth session off (one app connection at a time) — no CLI readings during a soak.
Soak: the hop-2 overnight run's logs (~/soak/droid1_night_2026-10-07_full.txt, droid2_… on the PC) — status not confirmed; compress and upload. GA decision depends on it. Fallback if not clean: ship GA with the 10-05 proven values (15 s, old smart, hop 3).
Debug Panel export writes a 0-byte file — defect, not urgent.

Release procedure (standing, Mac): commit + tag → gt_release.sh &lt;name&gt; (refuses uncommitted code / untagged HEAD / missing keystore; checks the release certificate; bundle to the Desktop; nothing to Drive) → check_build_v2.sh ~/Desktop/&lt;file&gt;.aab (+ that release's markers) → build_publish_v2.sh --release &lt;name&gt; (one Drive copy, releases/ only; LATEST points at it) → PC: deploy by name + tablet test — the gate → Play upload from the Mac Desktop.
gt_release.sh (new), build_publish_v2.sh (new; a release publishes ONCE, was twice ≈ 210 MB), check_build_v2.sh (new; 15 markers incl. STATIONARY30 at 30 s; accepts an AAB path) — v1 retired. check_build_v1.sh had been written in another session 10-06 13:58.

9. Lessons (for the Living Master)
Ask what the rider actually did before building fixes. Ten rounds of compare/batch/leftover fixes were built before the cause (map key off + trailhead on a track) came from looking at his map. The first question for a single-device failure: version installed, and a screenshot of the screen.
Load and test locally before Play (Fred: "this is what happens when we do not load and test locally — a mess"). Now a gate in the procedure.
Fixes go where the rider is: a tool that needs leaving the screen destroys the state it should capture; a button in a dialog the flow never reaches does not exist.
Silent exits are bugs: two of the AI search's five zero-route exits only logged; and 0 routes reopens the AI panel at its first page. TRAILHEADNEAR stops the main cause up front; the silent restart itself remains (patch_aiempty was dropped by choice).
Tracks become trails where no trail exists — so a trailhead "on a track" is on a trail, and the map key can hide it.

The Android app is known to show "connected but sleeping" while actually disconnected, and not to reconnect by itself. The fork ALREADY sends a ToRadio heartbeat every 30 s (AndroidRadioInterfaceService.kt:154–169, 299–311) — so keep-alive alone did not prevent the drops. TAK_TRACKER stays the default (chosen 09-25: radios broadcast their own TAK position with callsign) — not changed without the bench test. Fred: "cannot reboot what you are not connected to" — a remote restart cannot rescue a dead link.THE RULE (Fred 10-03):No radio talking → Android mode: position from the tablet's GPS, map and route as normal; the group is not shown as if live.GRP Awareness turns RED while no radio is connected.GroupTrack cycles disconnect → reconnect automatically (the fallback to tablet GPS IS the detection), repeating until the radio answers; after a minute or two without success: "Turn your radio off and on."On reconnect, my cart is matched by CALLSIGN (not the radio's device id); GRP Awareness back to connected; other carts reappear. The group survives: no carts dropped, no roles reset (the 09-29 group rule).Uses the ONE reconnect (inventory found three copies — 2.8 service A6); answers passed/failed with a reason (R3).No-GPS tablets: hold the last known position with "Radio not answering — position from hh:mm".BENCH TEST first (two T1000-Es on 2.7a, still for 20 min): Radio A TAK_TRACKER (as shipped) vs Radio B TAK — does the Bluetooth link survive; does the other tablet still receive positions? ⭐⭐⭐ 2.8 — AGREEMENTS ON HOW TO PROCEED (Fred 10-03). Renumbered: the comm-layer separation is release 2.8 (a major revision), not 2.7b. Two models: 2.7.x stays on the Windows PC (current branch, fixes only); 2.8 starts on the Mac Air from a pull. Git: tag the released 2.7a commit v2.7a (once Saturday's AAB is chosen) → branch 2.8 from the tag → the Mac checks out 2.8; 2.7 fixes are carried forward into 2.8, never back; same app id and Play listing.The rules: open payloads, private processes; the three separation tests on every service (R1 only door · R2 plain data, no shared state · R3 expect failure); ⛔ no convergence fixes; Android stays on its proven Meshtastic code.The Group riding switch: Settings On/Off. On = GRP Awareness available, radio connection required, comm layer started; Off = solo. The install question sets the first value and runs or skips the initial radio default config as now. The value lives in the default config API as a device setting — "groupRiding": { "enabled", "method", "setBy", "setAtMs" } — read at every session start; never in a ride package.No tick: the comm layer hands off deduped, normalised messages; GroupTrack processes each on arrival; time-based status is derived; one next-deadline timer for silence. Ends the 3-second cycle that could show 6-second-old values.CoT is the data standard: Layer 1 and the panels use a CoT-shaped model (uid, type, time/start/stale, point with accuracy, contact, group + role, track, status); status follows each sender's stale time; mesh = Meshtastic's compact TAK packet, IP = TAK protocol, converted in the comm layer; GroupTrack's ride / check-in / END in a CoT detail extension; roles LEADER→Team Lead, MIDDLE→RTO, TAIL_GUNNER→Forward Observer, RIDER→HQ.The API, first pass: GroupTrack Comm API v0.2 (GroupTrackComm_API_DRAFT_2026-10-03_v2.kt, module :grouptrack-comm): CommLink (A1–A6), CommIdentity (B7), CommConfig (C8–C11), CommMessaging (D12–D14, the event stream), CommSession (E15–E16), GroupCommPlugin (F17 + start/stop from the setup value), CommSetupStore, GroupState (apply / status / nextDeadline). Each API definition = model name · module name · contract data in · service performed · data returned · the Android functions moved into the plugin · the Meshtastic open-source code they use.The inventory (31 functions, 11 files): reconnect ×3 → one; reporting frequency ×2 → one; the TAK send reads check-in state → passed in; installProfile fire-and-forget → returns a result; configurator + compare are pure → shareable with the iPad; five per-setting editors + the older profile builders → reachability check; TakRoleStore (18 lines, Meshtastic core) → service-owned.The order: any critical 2.7a fixes first → the 2.8 design phase (finish the API definitions; the Apple column to functional calls, cited; the contract tests; the CoT research) → the Mac environment → build 2.8 Android → start Apple on the iPad (spikes; the config go/no-go before plugin code).Full design: grouptrack_service_layer_design_2026-10-03_v8.html (32 sections); its content is carried here and in the service-layer card below.

FOUND AND FIXED — THE STRANDED IMPORTWhy imports "never finished and could not be restarted — we had to clear data": extract and import ran as WorkManager jobs enqueued with ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP; the coordinator waited on them with no time limit. A job stuck queued held it forever → isImporting stayed true → the picker silently ignored Load ("import already running — ignoring request"). Closing the app killed the coordinator but not the job (Android keeps its own job database); KEEP re-attached the next import to the dead job; only clearing data removed it. Also: the gate shows the picker only on an empty trail database, so a part-finished import opened the map with half a state. Fixed by INPROCESS + KILLEDIMPORT (ec749561c), verified on Droid 2.
REJECTED — AND WHYKILLEDIMPORT v2 — cancel leftover jobs at startup + a 3-minute queued-job limit: managed the background jobs instead of removing them; Fred's in-process call replaced it before it ran.The queue-only legibility patch (white + 11sp on two lines, dimText to grey): Fred — "just the dark slate", then white app-wide; the search found 162 uses on 47 screens.Release-notes entries for the import and slate fixes: never seen in the field.Landscape promo panels; two separate promo sets: Fred — portrait, one cohesive weekly series.The obfuscation change in the 10-02 upload: renaming breaks by-name code only in release builds; it needs its own tested build (2.7b).
RULES LEARNEDA long job with two owners strands people. One owner, visible start to finish, that dies with the app, is the safe shape for anything a rider waits on.Read the colour, not the hex: a "dim" token can be a whole app's secondary text — search every use before changing one.Context-based classification needs a human pass: the slate patch called a field label "disabled" because disabledTextColor sat two lines above — the report caught it.Play links: keep &amp;hl=en_US; the bare link can 404 depending on region.

🔴 PROBLEM 1 — MY RADIO'S OWN REPORTS NEVER REACH MY TABLET (first)
Symptom: GPS panel → APPLY → Written · Disconnecting in 3 s · Reconnecting in 20 s · Done. GRP Awareness goes RED (a real disconnect) then GREEN and flashing (reconnected, hearing the group). SELECT CART lists BOTH carts, but my cart's pointer is not on the map; a manual DISCONNECT then CONNECT in GRP Awareness restores it. Also: "no activity for 24 minutes" in the app while the Mesh Nodes screen shows the radio every 15 s; the radio broadcasts every 10 s and the other tablet sees it.
Analysis: a radio's broadcasts are never received back by its own tablet (TAK reports included), so my radio's record on my tablet (position, last heard) is refreshed only by the radio's own local updates. The GPS panel's reconnect is a shortcut — ConvoyViewModel.radioOps(ui): disconnect() = ui.setDeviceAddress("n"), reconnect() = ui.setDeviceAddress(saved) — which appears to reset that record; the position comes back empty, the list shows the cart, the map cannot draw it. GRP Awareness's buttons use Meshtastic's connection manager (scanModel.disconnect() / connect) and keep it. The stale last-heard may also make my cart count as silent/Lost.
Fix, two parts: (a) the GPS panel AND the check-in's radio setup (RadioConfigWriter uses the same ops) disconnect/reconnect exactly as GRP Awareness does (Main.kt: onDisconnect = { scanModel.disconnect() }; find the CONNECT path) — the check-in's 09-28 first-run blindness looked the same; (b) my cart's position and presence from the tablet (GPS; the check-in) — the identity rule. ⚠ (b) changes how MY CART is built: design with Fred before any code. Test: APPLY → my pointer stays, not counted Lost; the check-in's setup the same.
🔴 PROBLEM 2 — THE SURVEY OWNED BY THE ROUTE
Decision (Fred): "the survey belongs to the route" — "route is the key"; ten riders on one ride = one route's rating; even if tied to a ride, it resolves to the route; no track reference (one track per ride kept — the first replicated). Today: END → EndOfRideForm → pendingSurvey → finalizeTrack() → ConvoyRideStore.saveSurvey(trackId, sv) (keyed to the TRACK; asked only on a public scheduled ride). At END the ride is known (endingCheckIn) and rideForEdit(rideId).routeId gives the route. Needed: the route's GLOBAL identity (same on every tablet, carried in the ride file); the survey table keyed by route (ride as context) + a migration; saveSurvey by route. Read first: ConvoyRideStore.kt (RideSurveyInput, saveSurvey, the table), the route table, the ride file format. 3.0: the device is the target; routes → rides → surveys are the first data mined for AWS.

⭐⭐ THE ROLE ANSWER — proven 09-28 evening. Ride roles travel in a standard TAK position report that the TABLET fills in; every tablet lifts the role from the report received (Fred's idea). No radio settings, no firmware, no reboot, no custom messaging. Leader → TeamLead · Middle → RTO · Tail gunner → ForwardObserver · (HQ = Rider, for a reassignment). The radios' own TeamMember reports are ignored, so they cannot erase a role. Only the three special roles broadcast. The node array is the single source (my own role goes into the same store); the tick assigns lead and tail from the roles; the HUD, markers and labels follow within a couple of seconds. REC's lead question appears only while no lead is locked.
What failed first (do not re-try): the role in the radio's own reports via Meshtastic's TAK Identity (ModuleConfig.tak) — the T1000-Es ignore it on their firmware, even after a power cycle (2.8-era feature; Fred will not flash 2.8); a custom PRIVATE_APP frame and request/reply schemes — rejected as custom messaging; roles through the configurator's apply — a settings write per change. Full record: living checklist v98+, THE RADIO → TICK HANDOFF … UPDATED 09-28.

Every cart has a role — Leader, Middle, Tail gunner or Rider — chosen at check-in and carried in its reports with its callsign (the check-in writes the role to the radio: TAK module config). One Leader, one Middle, one Tail gunner per ride; everyone else is a Rider.

SELECT CART (the button beside MY CART) — available to every cart: the list of all carts on the ride (callsign + role); tap one to open its display.
From that list, the Leader, Middle or Tail gunner (only they) can SWITCH ROLES with the selected cart: pick which special role it takes → the selected cart gets that role, that role's previous holder takes the selected cart's old role (a swap — never two holders). Any special-role holder can move ANY of the three — so a broken-down Leader never leaves the ride stuck. Every switch announced on every tablet; the tick follows the latest switch, not a silent radio's old role. (REMOVE FROM RIDE: restricted the same way.)
The check-in preloads the ride map ("Show this ride's route and trailhead on the ride map", ticked by default, rides only): CHECK IN clears the ride map to the ride's route and trailhead, fitted (through the ride map's own saved state); at REC the leader's track and the group's positions appear on top.

3 · 🔴 Blocking riders — fix before anything else
IMPORTLOCK — the importer can be bricked, and a rider cannot clear it.
⭐ Root cause ISOLATED 09-20: it is beginImport()'s IN-MEMORY LATCH at HomeStatePickerScreen:133, NOT the stranded manifest.
A dead run leaves the latch set and nothing launches — no message, no log. Force-stop alone frees it.
Fix is 2.6g, two parts: release the latch, then SRCLIST — list the state's sources, tick what is already held (bypassed), untick to pull one back in.
⭐ SRCLIST subsumes the resume prompt entirely: a failed source simply arrives unticked, so "resume" is pressing import again.
⚠ Make the tick an ACTION, not a status — the maps checkbox had exactly that ambiguity and it cost a day.
Why it pays: the Utah rerun fetched 49,125 records to insert 52, for 27–31 minutes. A rerun pays the full cost for almost none of the benefit — and area downloads over a held state have the same problem.

7 · Rules a new conversation must not break
Added 09-25:
(09-29) No fundamental change to a working function without a conversation with Fred first.
(09-29) Never fall back on the last-known position map; the previous tick is the last known position.
(09-29) Every cart speaks only for itself — no reports about other carts; the Leader is the last assignment.
(09-29) The method: a collection of related fixes → Kotlin compile → commit → release build → install. Present every file for download.
(09-28) Ride roles travel ONLY in the tablet-filled TAK position report; no radio settings writes for roles, no custom messaging (Fred). The radios' own reports are never used to set a role.
(09-28) A radio joins the ride network only at its check-in — everybody checks in first thing at the trailhead.
(09-28) Before any calculation change: a restore-point tag, pushed. One build and one test per change.
Radios are configured with the configurator — Android's settings screens cannot express seconds (hour presets only); hand-set values caused the 3 s rhythm.
One staleness rule: the Settings slider, applied AT THE READ. Never re-add a second time filter downstream.
No whole-image restore, anywhere. Apply = managed fields only.
Until the callsign override exists, configure only your own radio (the configurator writes the runner's callsign).
TAKDUMP is a diagnostic — remove before the 2.7 release.
⭐ 09-23: every apply starts from the ride JSON — on every device, whatever the target. The JSON is a stored file written on every Save; Send attaches it; import stores a received one unchanged.
⭐ 09-23: a ride is in progress until distributed, then ONLY the date changes. State is derived from distributed_at. Complete = route + trailhead + network.
⭐ 09-23: every route has a trailhead in its RECIPE (anchor). Route+ first point needs one within ½ mile; ride creation needs one; track conversion WILL need one (task in the master).
⭐ 09-23: nothing filters nodes by channel NAME — the channel KEY does, at the radio. Prefix is Group+6; GroupTrack is the reserved default channel.
⛔ The convoy map is FROZEN — ConvoyScreen.kt is not edited. The MENU (ConvoySubMenu from ui/Main.kt) and the planner are not frozen.
Leader = organizer = a role on the profile. Several orgs per rider. In 2.7 the leader of a ride you create is ALWAYS you.
Networks generated in exactly three places — org added · leader chooses "my own" · a unique ride network. GT id + 32-byte key + base values, TX at or below the licence-free limit. Immutable; rotation makes a new one. ALWAYS write both mesh and nucleus blocks.
ONE WRITE PATH — profile maintenance creates every rider, org, leader setting and network.
Other people exist only as ride data. Callsigns may repeat; riders matched by DEVICE (tak_uid, or node_num).
Four role rules — single holder · release then claim · only a person changes a role (a quiet radio means nothing) · leaving releases it.
Only ROUTES travel, distilled to a polyline. Identity is (type, geom_hash), never the hash alone.
Nothing written until Save. No ghosts.
Nothing is sent to GroupTrack unless the rider shares — and sharing sends only their ride and their email.
⛔ No OSM-derived data on GroupTrack infrastructure, ever. ⚠ This may exclude the route RECIPE from ride files — check what readRouteNotes actually holds before building the writer.

What comes next, in plain terms: every cart leaves a trail behind it on the map, built from that cart's own reports — the lead's trail is the one the group follows. The trail follows the route when the lead is on it, then the trails, and only joins raw points when neither is near; at a junction it waits for the next report rather than guess. Each cart is checked against the lead's trail when its own report arrives. Your own cart and your own track always come from your tablet's GPS. Later the lead also sends the last two minutes of his track, so riders behind see his line even through gaps. Once the trails run on reports, the 5-second tick that rebuilt the cart list is deleted in one step, with two safety tags to roll back to.

10-14 — the comm separation's P5 complete; the tick replacement begun; a hard day ended stable
The separation: everything GroupTrack reads about the radios now comes through the comm side, sleep and wake included, and the old radio code is gone. Only Meshtastic's own screens (step 6) remain, after the tick replacement.
The tick replacement: turning group awareness off now starts with only your cart. Your cart follows every tablet GPS fix. A new cart board runs alongside the old tick, fed only by messages actually received, so it can take over the map step by step.
The hard part: from midday the radios became unreliable. After hours spent on radios and pairing, Fred rolled the code back to the morning's milestone and re-applied each change on its own with the same connect test. Everything passed except one connection change, which stays out, and the board was rewritten once so its rules only run on messages received. By 22:14 both tablets connected, reconnected and showed both carts.
Learned: compare a good start-up log with a bad one first; one change per build; connection work waits for one end-to-end design with one owner of the connection.
Next: the overnight soak, the Hide Mesh fix, then the screen switches to the board (T5.2 → T5.5) — about a working day — then the route track, the lead polyline and one certification pass.
10-13 — group awareness becomes a choice; the tick's data proven through the comm side; a Bluetooth scare traced to the tablets
For riders: GroupTrack now asks at first start whether you will use a Meshtastic radio to see your group, or this tablet only — and you can switch any time in Settings. With group awareness off, the group controls grey out and nothing talks to a radio. Settings shows the group options only when they apply; four settings nobody needed are gone; the alert settings are now remembered after a restart; and the radio list shows your call signs straight away.
The separation: the comm side now reports everything the radio has heard, and for a full test it matched the old read field for field on both tablets. The GPS panel's interval also comes through the comm side. Next, the tick switches over to it (written and ready).
The scare: at midday both tablets lost their radios after an install. A careful step-by-step test cleared every one of today's changes; the cause was the tablets' Bluetooth after a week without a restart, and a reboot fixed it. Fred's rule from it: only simple additive changes until the whole recovery process is designed end to end.
What is left of the separation: the tick switch, sleep and wake (on its own), clean-up, and Meshtastic's own screens — about 2 working days — then the tick replacement.
10-12 — setting up the radio moves to the comm side: GroupTrack says WHAT, the comm side does HOW
What happened: seven more steps, each installed on both tablets and checked by Fred before it was kept. Everything that writes to the radio now lives on the comm side: the radio's own settings screen, applying a ride (and check-in's setup), the saved configs and their comparisons, and the GPS panel's "sent every N seconds". GroupTrack hands over what the radio should be — the ride file and the callsign, or the interval — and shows the progress and the result in its own words. GroupTrack's main view model no longer talks to the radio at all.
Fred's design call: one request, two kinds of radio — the same ride setup can configure a mesh radio or a Nucleus, with nothing in GroupTrack changing. "We simplify reading and navigating GroupTrack — a major plus before dealing with the tick."
Better for riders along the way: GRP Awareness now asks the radio which network it is on — a GroupTrack network shows green, anything else amber — so a guest's radio set up on another tablet no longer reads "never set up". Saved configs keeps its buttons at the top while the list scrolls.
What is left of the separation: what the tablet hears (the tick) and moving Meshtastic's own shell out — about 2½–3 working days.
10-11 — the radio link moves out of GroupTrack: GroupTrack now asks and reports, the comm side does the work
What happened: the separation of GroupTrack from Meshtastic finally moved in earnest — eight steps in one day, each installed on both tablets and checked by Fred before it was kept. Everything about the radio connection now lives on the comm side behind the GroupTrack Comm API: which radio this is, whether it is connected, connecting and disconnecting, forgetting and pairing, keeping the link alive (the reconnect rules, unchanged), the radio names, and the list of radios to choose from. GroupTrack's GRP Awareness panel only asks for things and shows what it is told — in GroupTrack's own words.
Fred's rule that shaped the day: "maintaining the connection is not a GroupTrack activity, it is a comm activity; reporting the state is a GroupTrack activity."
Better for riders along the way: GRP Awareness now draws its own radio list — paired radios first, then new radios nearby; one PAIR button pairs and connects; FORGET turns a radio back to PAIR at once (two out-of-date copies of "is it paired" were the reason it sometimes didn't); and with Bluetooth off the panel says just that — no false reconnects, and no "forget your radio" warning for a radio that is fine.
Why it matters: when the radio part is behind one contract, GroupTrack can later talk over a different radio (Natak's Nucleus, IP mesh) or run on iPad without touching the panels. And GroupTrack gets simpler before the next big step — removing the tick.
Also today: release l went to testers in the morning; the document set was recommitted from the Mac (now the home for docs as well as code); Fred set the power plan for Natak's demo carts — a cart USB port, a 20,000 mAh jump-starter that charges from the cart and powers the radio, given to every rider, with the radio unplugged before any jump-start.

10-10 — the missing trails found, and three releases that make GroupTrack easier to trust
The missing trails, solved: the last step of a trail import — the one that gives every trail its category — was being skipped on new imports, because an old safety check (written for a reader we replaced in September) refused the land-ownership file, which has grown. A trail with no category is hidden by the map whatever the rider chooses. Fred's rule now stands in the code: the step always runs; with no ownership data, land is public. Tablets that already imported are repaired the first time the new version opens. Fred reproduced the failure on our own tablet before we fixed it — and the trails came back.
New for riders and support: Settings → Remove all trail data (a clean start for trails, nothing else touched); Settings → Check a trail (what the tablet holds for one trail and why the map shows it or not — emailed to support); a notice before every file picker, so nobody gets lost in Android's files.
Rides and radios: new rides use the GroupTrack network by default — any GroupTrack radio can join; the organizer's own network and a private network for one ride remain choices. Checking in with no ride puts the radio back on GroupTrack unless the rider keeps it. And a false error that appeared on every check-in setup — after the radio restarted — is gone: the setup now starts once.
Where it stands (10-11 morning): release l (all of the above) is with internal and external testers; public by the end of 10-11. Next: the manual, its screens and the Quick Start reviewed against these changes; then the 2.7b separation resumes.
10-09 — rides become trails properly, and the map shows what is there
2.7a, three releases in a day (g, h, i — all on Play internal): emailed GPX files now open the import screen instead of vanishing; "trails from tracks" now follows the agreed rule — lay the ride over the known trails and add every stretch that connects two of them, with one GPS tolerance and nothing else; the trails it makes keep their identity from run to run, so routes and selections built on them stay valid and "added" means really new; and one trail with a quote in its name can no longer blank a whole screen of trails.
What "missing trails" turned out to be: mostly the rider's own map key — Land set to Public hides any road classified private, and the classifier labels a WHOLE road private when part of it is. Codes from some sources (UGRC numbers, New England TERRA/SNOW) are not in the key at all and can never be switched off. Both are on the planning list, with "remove all trail data" in Settings as the clean recovery for a device whose trails will not show.
How we work, learned the hard way: read the rider's map settings first; test against the real database pulled from the tablet; and the map now logs what it actually draws, so the next "missing trails" is minutes, not hours.
Still open — one tester's trails: a public OSM trail at Four Mile Wash draws on our tablet but not on his, even on the latest release. It is in his database: re-importing found it already there, and no rider trail was built over that ground. So the map is choosing not to show it, because of a map setting (the trail is "shape only") or because his copy of the trail or its details is damaged.Next, first (Fred, 10-09 evening): release j adds Settings → Remove all trail data. It clears the trails and their details together, then leads straight back to Import Trails by State. The tester starts clean with it, and we look further only if his re-import fails.2.7b: carries all three releases; the comm separation resumes with P1 (this radio's identity) after release j.
10-08 — the GA candidate is out, and the separation has begun the right way
2.7a: release f — the last planned 2.7a build, the GA candidate — is with internal testers (AI route design now refuses a trailhead with no trail shown nearby and can be cancelled at any step; the radio's GPS power pin is set; the compare table can be hidden; forgetting a radio updates at once).
2.7b: GroupTrack and the mesh now talk through one API for the first time: the ride-role reports go out and come back through it, and the Meshtastic menu opens through it. Nothing the rider sees changed. Five small steps, each built, checked on both tablets and saved.
The shape, decided by Fred: GroupTrack owns every screen the rider uses. The mesh side owns the radio: it does what GroupTrack asks (connect, pair, forget, reconnect, apply a ride) and reports what happened — including errors, which GroupTrack puts into words. Meshtastic's own menus stay as they are and open over GroupTrack when asked. This is the same arrangement as ATAK and Meshtastic, which also leaves the door open to shipping the mesh side as its own open-source app, so riders never need a separate Meshtastic install.

The direction, in one paragraph
2.7 = separate GroupTrack from the mesh: level 1 (standalone GroupTrack) stands alone; the mesh is a plugin (level 2).
Inside it, 2.7 delivers TAK packets and the first IP-configured mesh radios (the Nucleus); configuration over Bluetooth, USB and IP by one update process.
GroupTrack is separating from its Meshtastic origins. Release 2.7 makes the mesh one transport among two — LoRa radios and the
Nucleus (Natak's IP-mesh box) — and moves rider identity and position into TAK-format messages sent by the app. A ride is
one JSON file made on the leader's tablet and applied to every device from that file. The standalone T1000-E path is kept
working on the new channel but is being sunset; the aim is every rider on an app-attached radio.
09-25, sharpened: GroupTrack receives one common payload — a TAK position report — from any source. Radios configured by GroupTrack
(TAK_TRACKER, now the default) speak TAK by themselves, with the rider's callsign in every report; the only Meshtastic-specific piece left is
converting raw GPS broadcasts, behind a legacy switch in the plugin. "Me" is resolved first on every tick. ⚖ Direction for the licence boundary:
option A — the mesh side as a separate plugin app talking TAK. ⚠ This changes the T1000-E premise: a naked T1000 now speaks TAK — the sunset may
apply only to the old tool.

The system at 30,000 ft
Two worlds, one bridge: the LoRa mesh on the ride's channel, and the Nucleus Wi-Fi (SSID = the network id), joined by the Nucleus bridge.
Every device transmits once, in one message type: app-attached radios send TAK only; T1000-Es send GPS position only CORRECTED 09-25: every radio GroupTrack configures sends TAK itself (TAK_TRACKER, callsign included) — app-attached or not; the app sending TAK is optional. Raw GPS (radios GroupTrack did not configure) is converted to TAK by the plugin, behind a legacy switch.
Two networks with two jobs: GroupTrack — the default, for setup and control, a unit's home; Group+6 — one per ride, its own 256-bit key.
Apply writes only what we manage, records everything, and reports other differences as a document. Every apply starts from the ride JSON.
One map entry per device, keyed by the radio's node number (or a TAK-uid key for Wi-Fi-only riders); labelled by callsign. 09-25: a device not heard within the Settings slider's hours never becomes an entry — ONE staleness rule, decided at the read. Names only from reports (designed: the rider table, in the plugin).
The preset decides group size: LONG_FAST ≈ 1–2 riders at 3 s; MEDIUM_FAST ≈ 5–6; SHORT_FAST ≈ 13+ — at the cost of range. One preset per ride. 09-25 measured: two radios at 3 s on LONG_FAST ≈ 20% channel utilisation; the default reports every 15 s standing / 3 s moving (20 m) — 8–10 s standing measured indoors.
The rider profile is foundational — the first screen; the callsign is the map label, the radio's name and the TAK identity.

10-06 — GroupTrack is complete without a radio; group riding is the add-onThe principle: most riders (about 9 in 10) will never use a mesh radio, and they get the whole of GroupTrack: plan routes, create and share rides, download maps, navigate and record. Group riding — radios, check-in, seeing everyone on the map — is an add-on you switch on when you have a radio: "Do you have a mesh radio?" at install, and a Settings box "Activate GRP Awareness plugin". Learn the app first; the group is one more thing it can do, not a tangle of screens you don't need yet.The road, corrected:2.7a (finishing now): rides, ride sharing, and the radio fixes from this week — plus one more for radio stability: the app tunes how often each radio reports to the size of the group, so up to 10 radios share the air without crowding it.2.7b — the separation: everything that talks to radios moves into its own part of the app, behind that on/off switch. Riders without a radio never meet it.2.8: the radio side gets its new engine (the standard TAK message format, no constant polling, a clean boundary) and the groundwork for Apple.2.9: GroupTrack on iPad (the full app) and Mac (the planning station).Following the leader, honestly: other riders appear as dots exactly where their radios report them; the line you follow is the leader's real track, sent from his tablet — never a guess. Tested against 90 of our own recorded rides (4,241 miles).

10-04 — 2.7a gets sturdy: the radio can fail, the ride carries onWhat happened: on 10-03 our testers had a bad day on the older software. Their radios went quiet while they sat still, the app kept believing the radio was connected, and riders ended up with no position on the screen. That is the panic we never want a rider to feel.What we built in a day and a half, and what riders now get:The ride carries on without the radio. If the radio stops answering, GroupTrack quietly switches to the tablet's own GPS. Your cart keeps moving under your name, the maps stay, and the rest of the group stays on screen where they were last seen.A red light tells the truth. GRP Awareness turns red whenever the radio isn't really talking. GroupTrack tries to reconnect on its own, and only if that fails asks the rider for one simple step.The ride map never opens blank. It always finds something to show: your cart, your last area, or your first GPS fix.Radios that wouldn't connect now do. A hidden fault left from renaming the app in July stopped radios from ever finishing a connection. Only closing the app helped. It's fixed.Every radio keeps its real name. GroupTrack now remembers each radio's current name, so riders see "fred&amp;June" or "Billy beans", not "Meshtastic_deda", even after a disconnect.Simpler pairing. Radios now pair with no PIN, so a radio and a tablet can't quietly fall out of step. Each radio needs one re-pair the first time.Where it stands: built, proven on our two test tablets, and in our internal testers' hands. Next: the planning map can still open white for someone who goes straight to it offline before the GPS wakes up. That's first tomorrow, then tester feedback, then the public launch.What we learned: these radios can look healthy while being quietly out of step, and a rider can't tell. So GroupTrack has to notice for them, say so plainly, and keep the ride going. That's now the rule.
10-03 — how we proceed: 2.8The next big step is GroupTrack 2.8 — a major revision built on the Mac, while the released 2.7 stays on the PC for fixes. 2.8 separates GroupTrack from the radio behind a small, open set of services, so the same GroupTrack can run with a mesh radio, over the internet, or on an iPad.Riders will notice three things: a Group riding switch in Settings (set by the install question, changeable any time); a group map that updates the moment a report arrives instead of every few seconds; and GroupTrack speaking CoT, the language of the TAK world — so other TAK apps can see a GroupTrack rider, and GroupTrack can see them.First comes design: every service defined with what goes in and what comes out, mapped to the Android code it replaces and to the Apple components that will provide it on the iPad — proven before any of it is built.

How the doc set works
Living documents are EDITED IN PLACE and re-versioned — the new version contains everything the old one had, plus the day's work.
So the highest version number is always the complete one, and older copies can be ignored.
The handoff is the exception: it is rewritten each time, which is why it must carry every open item forward. v1 today did not; v2 does.
Filenames are never reused — a correction gets a new version number, because Windows appends "(1)" to a duplicate download and the wrong file gets run.
Today's design and every decision reaches the LIVING MASTER, not just a side document — a living doc that only references an external file is no use if that file is lost.

10-23 &mdash; One Map holds everything: every map tool, and both ways of building a route
One Map now remembers where you were (online it opens on your last view, offline on your cart), shows the map type as a button on the map, and carries every map tool the old maps had, in one Map menu: what is downloading, the map source, download maps by area or along your tracks, remove maps, map recovery, and every way of importing trails and tracks. The tools were copied, not rewritten, so the old maps kept working beside them while they were tested.Building a route moved too. Add Route checks first for anything unfinished — an AI comparison waiting for a decision, a route left open by a crash, routes you were building — and then offers Build it myself or AI route design. Both work on One Map, including the AI's guided steps, a search to find your area, and the side-by-side comparison. Along the way the long-standing public / private land problem was found and fixed: the step that classifies land ran out of memory and quietly wrote nothing, and a launch job then marked everything public.Next: move the last three things only the planning map can do (rebuild rides from a saved route's answers, and the route notes), then remove the planning map and the classic ride map, clear out the dead code, make One Map the screen the app starts on, and give every remaining screen one look. A new radio idea arrived from Nathan for later: the GMRS radios many UTV groups already carry can send a position over Bluetooth-connected packet radio — a candidate transport for 2.8.
10-22 &mdash; One Map built: every launch point on the screen, almost all of them working
The new navigation exists. Switch Settings › Layout to One Map and the ride map carries one clean set of buttons: RECORD at the top; MENU and zoom on the left; GRP Awareness, Mode, Status, Map Key, Filter and Centre on Me on the right; the readout bottom left; Map, Add Route, Rides, Search and Radio Setup along the bottom. Behind them sit today's functions, re-pointed rather than rewritten — except four that were rebuilt because the old ones confused riders: Map Key (now only what you are looking at), Filter (everything you show or hide, with each trail type explained), Centre on Me (new: follows you, and comes back on its own while you ride), and Search (one box that searches everything, then lets you narrow by type and state). Every screen touched now closes the same way — HELP and ✕ in the top right corner.
Two things are not there yet. Building a route still lives on the planning map — moving it is the most tangled piece, so it goes last. And One Map does not yet remember its own place between sessions; that is tomorrow's first job, followed by bringing the planning map's download and import tools over, then making One Map the screen the app starts on.

10-15 — the map now runs on messages received; your own cart fixed on the road
The tick replacement: the ride map now draws from the cart board, fed only by the messages actually received, in the team-awareness (CoT) format. Every job the 5-second tick did has a new home except one — the lead's track — so the tick itself can go next. Two safety tags mark the code before its removal.
For riders: the Meshtastic side menu is gone (NODES in GRP Awareness instead, with BACK TO MAP); roles show only while checked in; the Leader is the lead on every tablet, and two riders claiming one role both go back to Rider with a red conflict message; a radio lost for good leaves your tablet riding alone, cleanly; a tapped cart shows GAP between its reports.
On the road: the afternoon ride found your own cart standing still on your own tablet with the radio on. Fred's rule — your cart's updates travel as a message through the same path as everyone else's, always from the tablet's GPS — fixed it, confirmed in the car. The ride also showed the MEDIUM_FAST channel reaching only about 0.1 mile, and that a cart whose radio goes quiet can stay "Active" when nothing arrives.
What comes next, in plain terms: every cart leaves a trail behind it on the map, built from that cart's own reports — the lead's trail is the one the group follows. The trail follows the route when the lead is on it, then the trails, and only joins raw points when neither is near; at a junction it waits for the next report rather than guess. Each cart is checked against the lead's trail when its own report arrives. Your own cart and your own track always come from your tablet's GPS. Later the lead also sends the last two minutes of his track, so riders behind see his line even through gaps. Once the trails run on reports, the 5-second tick that rebuilt the cart list is deleted in one step, with two safety tags to roll back to.
Next: the idle sleep back to 25 minutes, the status decision, a trail behind every cart (the lead's is one of them), then the tick's removal (T5.5).
10-14 — the comm separation's P5 complete; the tick replacement begun; a hard day ended stable
The separation: everything GroupTrack reads about the radios now comes through the comm side, sleep and wake included, and the old radio code is gone. Only Meshtastic's own screens (step 6) remain, after the tick replacement.
The tick replacement: turning group awareness off now starts with only your cart. Your cart follows every tablet GPS fix. A new cart board runs alongside the old tick, fed only by messages actually received, so it can take over the map step by step.
The hard part: from midday the radios became unreliable. After hours spent on radios and pairing, Fred rolled the code back to the morning's milestone and re-applied each change on its own with the same connect test. Everything passed except one connection change, which stays out, and the board was rewritten once so its rules only run on messages received. By 22:14 both tablets connected, reconnected and showed both carts.
Learned: compare a good start-up log with a bad one first; one change per build; connection work waits for one end-to-end design with one owner of the connection.

10-13 — group awareness becomes a choice; the tick's data proven through the comm side; a Bluetooth scare traced to the tablets
For riders: GroupTrack now asks at first start whether you will use a Meshtastic radio to see your group, or this tablet only — and you can switch any time in Settings. With group awareness off, the group controls grey out and nothing talks to a radio. Settings shows the group options only when they apply; four settings nobody needed are gone; the alert settings are now remembered after a restart; and the radio list shows your call signs straight away.
The separation: the comm side now reports everything the radio has heard, and for a full test it matched the old read field for field on both tablets. The GPS panel's interval also comes through the comm side. Next, the tick switches over to it (written and ready).
The scare: at midday both tablets lost their radios after an install. A careful step-by-step test cleared every one of today's changes; the cause was the tablets' Bluetooth after a week without a restart, and a reboot fixed it. Fred's rule from it: only simple additive changes until the whole recovery process is designed end to end.
What is left of the separation: the tick switch, sleep and wake (on its own), clean-up, and Meshtastic's own screens — about 2 working days — then the tick replacement.
10-12 — setting up the radio moves to the comm side: GroupTrack says WHAT, the comm side does HOW
What happened: seven more steps, each installed on both tablets and checked by Fred before it was kept. Everything that writes to the radio now lives on the comm side: the radio's own settings screen, applying a ride (and check-in's setup), the saved configs and their comparisons, and the GPS panel's "sent every N seconds". GroupTrack hands over what the radio should be — the ride file and the callsign, or the interval — and shows the progress and the result in its own words. GroupTrack's main view model no longer talks to the radio at all.
Fred's design call: one request, two kinds of radio — the same ride setup can configure a mesh radio or a Nucleus, with nothing in GroupTrack changing. "We simplify reading and navigating GroupTrack — a major plus before dealing with the tick."
Better for riders along the way: GRP Awareness now asks the radio which network it is on — a GroupTrack network shows green, anything else amber — so a guest's radio set up on another tablet no longer reads "never set up". Saved configs keeps its buttons at the top while the list scrolls.
What is left of the separation: what the tablet hears (the tick) and moving Meshtastic's own shell out — about 2½–3 working days.
10-11 — the radio link moves out of GroupTrack: GroupTrack now asks and reports, the comm side does the work
What happened: the separation of GroupTrack from Meshtastic finally moved in earnest — eight steps in one day, each installed on both tablets and checked by Fred before it was kept. Everything about the radio connection now lives on the comm side behind the GroupTrack Comm API: which radio this is, whether it is connected, connecting and disconnecting, forgetting and pairing, keeping the link alive (the reconnect rules, unchanged), the radio names, and the list of radios to choose from. GroupTrack's GRP Awareness panel only asks for things and shows what it is told — in GroupTrack's own words.
Fred's rule that shaped the day: "maintaining the connection is not a GroupTrack activity, it is a comm activity; reporting the state is a GroupTrack activity."
Better for riders along the way: GRP Awareness now draws its own radio list — paired radios first, then new radios nearby; one PAIR button pairs and connects; FORGET turns a radio back to PAIR at once (two out-of-date copies of "is it paired" were the reason it sometimes didn't); and with Bluetooth off the panel says just that — no false reconnects, and no "forget your radio" warning for a radio that is fine.
Why it matters: when the radio part is behind one contract, GroupTrack can later talk over a different radio (Natak's Nucleus, IP mesh) or run on iPad without touching the panels. And GroupTrack gets simpler before the next big step — removing the tick.
Also today: release l went to testers in the morning; the document set was recommitted from the Mac (now the home for docs as well as code); Fred set the power plan for Natak's demo carts — a cart USB port, a 20,000 mAh jump-starter that charges from the cart and powers the radio, given to every rider, with the radio unplugged before any jump-start.
Next: P3 — the RADIO SETTINGS button asks the comm side to open Meshtastic's settings (one decision for Fred first); then P4, the radio configurator; then P5, what is heard and the tick.
10-10 — the missing trails found, and three releases that make GroupTrack easier to trust
The missing trails, solved: the last step of a trail import — the one that gives every trail its category — was being skipped on new imports, because an old safety check (written for a reader we replaced in September) refused the land-ownership file, which has grown. A trail with no category is hidden by the map whatever the rider chooses. Fred's rule now stands in the code: the step always runs; with no ownership data, land is public. Tablets that already imported are repaired the first time the new version opens. Fred reproduced the failure on our own tablet before we fixed it — and the trails came back.
New for riders and support: Settings → Remove all trail data (a clean start for trails, nothing else touched); Settings → Check a trail (what the tablet holds for one trail and why the map shows it or not — emailed to support); a notice before every file picker, so nobody gets lost in Android's files.
Rides and radios: new rides use the GroupTrack network by default — any GroupTrack radio can join; the organizer's own network and a private network for one ride remain choices. Checking in with no ride puts the radio back on GroupTrack unless the rider keeps it. And a false error that appeared on every check-in setup — after the radio restarted — is gone: the setup now starts once.
Where it stands (10-11 morning): release l (all of the above) is with internal and external testers; public by the end of 10-11. Next: the manual, its screens and the Quick Start reviewed against these changes; then the 2.7b separation resumes.
10-09 — rides become trails properly, and the map shows what is there
2.7a, three releases in a day (g, h, i — all on Play internal): emailed GPX files now open the import screen instead of vanishing; "trails from tracks" now follows the agreed rule — lay the ride over the known trails and add every stretch that connects two of them, with one GPS tolerance and nothing else; the trails it makes keep their identity from run to run, so routes and selections built on them stay valid and "added" means really new; and one trail with a quote in its name can no longer blank a whole screen of trails.
What "missing trails" turned out to be: mostly the rider's own map key — Land set to Public hides any road classified private, and the classifier labels a WHOLE road private when part of it is. Codes from some sources (UGRC numbers, New England TERRA/SNOW) are not in the key at all and can never be switched off. Both are on the planning list, with "remove all trail data" in Settings as the clean recovery for a device whose trails will not show.
How we work, learned the hard way: read the rider's map settings first; test against the real database pulled from the tablet; and the map now logs what it actually draws, so the next "missing trails" is minutes, not hours.
Still open — one tester's trails: a public OSM trail at Four Mile Wash draws on our tablet but not on his, even on the latest release. It is in his database: re-importing found it already there, and no rider trail was built over that ground. So the map is choosing not to show it, because of a map setting (the trail is "shape only") or because his copy of the trail or its details is damaged.Next, first (Fred, 10-09 evening): release j adds Settings → Remove all trail data. It clears the trails and their details together, then leads straight back to Import Trails by State. The tester starts clean with it, and we look further only if his re-import fails.2.7b: carries all three releases; the comm separation resumes with P1 (this radio's identity) after release j.
10-08 — the GA candidate is out, and the separation has begun the right way
2.7a: release f — the last planned 2.7a build, the GA candidate — is with internal testers (AI route design now refuses a trailhead with no trail shown nearby and can be cancelled at any step; the radio's GPS power pin is set; the compare table can be hidden; forgetting a radio updates at once).
2.7b: GroupTrack and the mesh now talk through one API for the first time: the ride-role reports go out and come back through it, and the Meshtastic menu opens through it. Nothing the rider sees changed. Five small steps, each built, checked on both tablets and saved.
The shape, decided by Fred: GroupTrack owns every screen the rider uses. The mesh side owns the radio: it does what GroupTrack asks (connect, pair, forget, reconnect, apply a ride) and reports what happened — including errors, which GroupTrack puts into words. Meshtastic's own menus stay as they are and open over GroupTrack when asked. This is the same arrangement as ATAK and Meshtastic, which also leaves the door open to shipping the mesh side as its own open-source app, so riders never need a separate Meshtastic install.
Pace: one service at a time, both directions — "slow and steady". About 50 direct calls remain; each service is planned first, then moved in one checked step.
The direction, in one paragraph
2.7 = separate GroupTrack from the mesh: level 1 (standalone GroupTrack) stands alone; the mesh is a plugin (level 2).
Inside it, 2.7 delivers TAK packets and the first IP-configured mesh radios (the Nucleus); configuration over Bluetooth, USB and IP by one update process.
GroupTrack is separating from its Meshtastic origins. Release 2.7 makes the mesh one transport among two — LoRa radios and the
Nucleus (Natak's IP-mesh box) — and moves rider identity and position into TAK-format messages sent by the app. A ride is
one JSON file made on the leader's tablet and applied to every device from that file. The standalone T1000-E path is kept
working on the new channel but is being sunset; the aim is every rider on an app-attached radio.
09-25, sharpened: GroupTrack receives one common payload — a TAK position report — from any source. Radios configured by GroupTrack
(TAK_TRACKER, now the default) speak TAK by themselves, with the rider's callsign in every report; the only Meshtastic-specific piece left is
converting raw GPS broadcasts, behind a legacy switch in the plugin. "Me" is resolved first on every tick. ⚖ Direction for the licence boundary:
option A — the mesh side as a separate plugin app talking TAK. ⚠ This changes the T1000-E premise: a naked T1000 now speaks TAK — the sunset may
apply only to the old tool.

The system at 30,000 ft
Two worlds, one bridge: the LoRa mesh on the ride's channel, and the Nucleus Wi-Fi (SSID = the network id), joined by the Nucleus bridge.
Every device transmits once, in one message type: app-attached radios send TAK only; T1000-Es send GPS position only CORRECTED 09-25: every radio GroupTrack configures sends TAK itself (TAK_TRACKER, callsign included) — app-attached or not; the app sending TAK is optional. Raw GPS (radios GroupTrack did not configure) is converted to TAK by the plugin, behind a legacy switch.
Two networks with two jobs: GroupTrack — the default, for setup and control, a unit's home; Group+6 — one per ride, its own 256-bit key.
Apply writes only what we manage, records everything, and reports other differences as a document. Every apply starts from the ride JSON.
One map entry per device, keyed by the radio's node number (or a TAK-uid key for Wi-Fi-only riders); labelled by callsign. 09-25: a device not heard within the Settings slider's hours never becomes an entry — ONE staleness rule, decided at the read. Names only from reports (designed: the rider table, in the plugin).
The preset decides group size: LONG_FAST ≈ 1–2 riders at 3 s; MEDIUM_FAST ≈ 5–6; SHORT_FAST ≈ 13+ — at the cost of range. One preset per ride. 09-25 measured: two radios at 3 s on LONG_FAST ≈ 20% channel utilisation; the default reports every 15 s standing / 3 s moving (20 m) — 8–10 s standing measured indoors.
The rider profile is foundational — the first screen; the callsign is the map label, the radio's name and the TAK identity.

10-06 — GroupTrack is complete without a radio; group riding is the add-onThe principle: most riders (about 9 in 10) will never use a mesh radio, and they get the whole of GroupTrack: plan routes, create and share rides, download maps, navigate and record. Group riding — radios, check-in, seeing everyone on the map — is an add-on you switch on when you have a radio: "Do you have a mesh radio?" at install, and a Settings box "Activate GRP Awareness plugin". Learn the app first; the group is one more thing it can do, not a tangle of screens you don't need yet.The road, corrected:2.7a (finishing now): rides, ride sharing, and the radio fixes from this week — plus one more for radio stability: the app tunes how often each radio reports to the size of the group, so up to 10 radios share the air without crowding it.2.7b — the separation: everything that talks to radios moves into its own part of the app, behind that on/off switch. Riders without a radio never meet it.2.8: the radio side gets its new engine (the standard TAK message format, no constant polling, a clean boundary) and the groundwork for Apple.2.9: GroupTrack on iPad (the full app) and Mac (the planning station).Following the leader, honestly: other riders appear as dots exactly where their radios report them; the line you follow is the leader's real track, sent from his tablet — never a guess. Tested against 90 of our own recorded rides (4,241 miles).

The radio side of GroupTrack is separated from the rest, so radio problems are handled in one place and the app no longer has to babysit the link. It uses an open, standard message format (Cursor on Target, used by TAK) and lays the groundwork for a second platform. 10-04 — 2.7a gets sturdy: the radio can fail, the ride carries onWhat happened: on 10-03 our testers had a bad day on the older software. Their radios went quiet while they sat still, the app kept believing the radio was connected, and riders ended up with no position on the screen. That is the panic we never want a rider to feel.What we built in a day and a half, and what riders now get:The ride carries on without the radio. If the radio stops answering, GroupTrack quietly switches to the tablet's own GPS. Your cart keeps moving under your name, the maps stay, and the rest of the group stays on screen where they were last seen.A red light tells the truth. GRP Awareness turns red whenever the radio isn't really talking. GroupTrack tries to reconnect on its own, and only if that fails asks the rider for one simple step.The ride map never opens blank. It always finds something to show: your cart, your last area, or your first GPS fix.Radios that wouldn't connect now do. A hidden fault left from renaming the app in July stopped radios from ever finishing a connection. Only closing the app helped. It's fixed.Every radio keeps its real name. GroupTrack now remembers each radio's current name, so riders see "fred&amp;June" or "Billy beans", not "Meshtastic_deda", even after a disconnect.Simpler pairing. Radios now pair with no PIN, so a radio and a tablet can't quietly fall out of step. Each radio needs one re-pair the first time.Where it stands: built, proven on our two test tablets, and in our internal testers' hands. Next: the planning map can still open white for someone who goes straight to it offline before the GPS wakes up. That's first tomorrow, then tester feedback, then the public launch.What we learned: these radios can look healthy while being quietly out of step, and a rider can't tell. So GroupTrack has to notice for them, say so plainly, and keep the ride going. That's now the rule.
10-03 — how we proceed: 2.8The next big step is GroupTrack 2.8 — a major revision built on the Mac, while the released 2.7 stays on the PC for fixes. 2.8 separates GroupTrack from the radio behind a small, open set of services, so the same GroupTrack can run with a mesh radio, over the internet, or on an iPad.Riders will notice three things: a Group riding switch in Settings (set by the install question, changeable any time); a group map that updates the moment a report arrives instead of every few seconds; and GroupTrack speaking CoT, the language of the TAK world — so other TAK apps can see a GroupTrack rider, and GroupTrack can see them.First comes design: every service defined with what goes in and what comes out, mapped to the Android code it replaces and to the Apple components that will provide it on the iPad — proven before any of it is built.

How the doc set works
Living documents are EDITED IN PLACE and re-versioned — the new version contains everything the old one had, plus the day's work.
So the highest version number is always the complete one, and older copies can be ignored.
The handoff is the exception: it is rewritten each time, which is why it must carry every open item forward. v1 today did not; v2 does.
Filenames are never reused — a correction gets a new version number, because Windows appends "(1)" to a duplicate download and the wrong file gets run.
Today's design and every decision reaches the LIVING MASTER, not just a side document — a living doc that only references an external file is no use if that file is lost.

📻 BTECH Relay — a transport candidate for 2.8+ (Nathan via Fred, 10-23 16:04)
github.com/darksteal/BTECH-Relay — an ATAK plugin that links BTECH UV-PRO / GMRS-PRO / UV-50X radios to ATAK over Bluetooth SPP + the radio's KISS TNC; AX.25 frames, a compact binary format with fragmentation, optional AES-256; position, chat, CoT markers / routes, contact age-out and Bluetooth auto-reconnect working, voice PTT a scaffold; 2 commits. Nathan: he has run a different networking stack over the UV-Pro, "the solution is pretty sound".
Fit: UTV riders already carry GMRS radios. 47 CFR 95.1787 lets a GMRS handheld send location (or a request for it) and brief text — each burst ≤ 1 s, no more than once per 30 s, integral antenna, not on the 467 MHz main channels — a GroupTrack position beacon fits; tracks / routes / markers do not. Packet modems typically 1200 baud. A transport behind the 2.8 separation beside Meshtastic and the Nucleus IP mesh.
Cautions: licence MIT + Commons Clause (commercial sale reserved) — do not copy their code into the paid app without the author's permission; KISS / AX.25 / SPP are open standards, write our own. Encryption is not addressed in 95.1787; amateur rules prohibit messages encoded to obscure meaning — check before any encrypted traffic on these bands. Needs real radios and distance (January).
Next: ask Nathan which stack he used over the UV-Pro and the throughput he saw.

📐 Rules set on 10-22 (Fred) — they govern every patch from here
One standard for leaving: HELP ✕ top right on every screen, panel and dialog. ✕ = leave (close / cancel; nothing else happens). The COMPLETE is the screen's own action button (CHECK IN, SAVE, APPLY, SEND). Panels that stay on screen add ☰ MOVE and HIDE / SHOW. One help viewer (GtHelpView) opens on top of every screen. (Fred 12:18–12:21: "no preference as long as it is consistent.")
The touch rule (12:06, 12:50): every screen we have touched is brought to the new standard — scroll, HELP, ✕ — even if the feature is a placeholder; when a function is touched, every screen it opens is brought to the standard in the same patch.
Nothing is removed without a home (11:47): a control is never hidden or replaced unless the same patch puts it somewhere. The hidden-controls ledger below records every one.
The one-option rule (11:09): a button whose module has one attached process runs it directly — no in-between list. Key functions are never hidden between navigation layers (11:07).
Bring over exactly as it exists, then restructure (14:35): moving a function never redesigns it; realignment comes after everything is moved.
Automated is not a menu item (15:10): a function that only runs inside another process (corridor downloads after an import, a source refresh) moves with its process and never gets a button.
Trace before attaching (Claude, after the Add Route detour 14:33): a function that crosses into another screen is traced start → work → complete → cancel → back before it is handed over, and the dead ends are reported first.
Route+ is not taken apart (13:48–13:58): it is moved whole; its start-up checks (in-progress routes, compare sets, leftover AI routes, the unnamed draft) always run.
Search filters after, not before (13:04): search everything; the result types are the filter.
Map selection and map sources belong together (15:10).
Persistence purpose (13:30–13:33): the state file is for returning BETWEEN SESSIONS to where you left off. Start-up ALWAYS restores the saved view — no exceptions; Centre on Me is one tap to where you are. ("If startup centres me where I am it is a lot of work to return to where I was. If I return to where I was it is one button to bring me to where I am.")
Attaching order (11:01): top row, down the right column, then the bottom bar left to right.
🗺 Roadmap (decided 10-22 in the open-items review)
ReleaseScope
2.7cONE MAP: navigation, simplification, the presentation layer including 3D / terrain and rotation, the manual rebuilt by a repeatable process. Portrait fully workable; landscape is riding mode.
2.8Ends with a deployed native iPad app; the Apple work folded together.
2.9Data-model sync and upload from Android to AWS — one direction only, services layer only, no paygate.
3.0AWS services: the paygate (Play promo codes — e.g. the first 200 users free for a year), Mac / PC planning against the AWS model, the map-licensing review (stay within Esri / Google / OpenTopoMap terms; corridors over HTTP).
4.0Tile brokering / staging DROPPED — "no benefit to the server deciding, as the app does this task already" on download and import.
2.7c method (Fred 10-22): a blank launch panel with every final launch point as a placeholder, then functions attached to the scaffolding; one module per launch point; the last step retires ConvoyScreen.kt and GroupTrack.kt becomes the start screen. 2.7c standards: every panel scrolls · one colour scheme (buttons and panels follow the map type: SAT / HYB white with blue letters, otherwise blue with white) · detail panels separate facts from actions and hide technical data (done one panel at a time in the reviews) · stay-panels have drag, collapse, complete, help · every launch point and function links to its manual pages through a data table the documentation process regenerates (grouptrack_help_links.json).

2. Principles (Fred, 10-18 to 10-21)
One map. The planning map is folded in; the Ride Planning / Back to Ride switches are retired.
A launch layer over the existing features. Each process gets ONE first screen that takes every value it needs (defaults from the ride and settings), then runs to the end with no further screen prompts. The only stop kept is the confirm before something that cannot be undone.
Two layouts. Group adds a lot of complexity and is used by some. Android only is the default; Group adds the Group button, CHECK IN, the GROUP readout, other carts and the lead track. One switch decides which.
Riders ride in landscape and pan in portrait. In landscape, panels open as a side panel so the map stays in view.
Every control shows an icon and its text on an opaque background, readable on any map. No hover, no long-press meanings.
North up only. Leaflet cannot rotate, and Hybrid labels are baked into the imagery (heading-up needs a rotating map engine: not 2.7c).
Show/hide is FILTER, how lines look is KEY: as onX and Gaia do, the filter is on every view.

5. Found by the cross-reference: functions the prototype did not show, and their homes
MENU › Settings › Storage &amp; data: Remove all trail data · Resync tracks · Add trails from tracks (from Settings, the track import screen and the RiderTrails dialog).
MENU › Settings › Diagnostics: Check a trail · Ride statistics · Conversion record (from Settings and the old ride-config menu).
Map › Map sources: change a source (clear or keep tiles: the migrate gate) and rebuild a source (MAP RECOVERY / recreate slot).
Map › Download for offline: show what you hold / what is coming, and remove tiles from an area.
Rides › Create a route: drafts in progress (resume, rename, roll back, delete, the unnamed-draft resolver), ROUTE DETAILS notes, CREATE TRAILHEAD at save, the planner's Review / Compare and saving the compare set.
Tap a feature: rename, change type, delete, fit, aliases, Create a ride; tracks add SHARE (the track export sheet).
Record button: the automatic-pause banner (CONTINUE), the ROLE CONFLICT banner, the lead question when no Leader is known (decide in phase 2).
Unchanged in 2.7c: Android permission prompts, the startup online/offline chooser, sign-in, terms and privacy gates, the V3 account and organizer screens, the developer menu.

📻 BTECH Relay — a transport candidate for 2.8+ (Nathan via Fred, 10-23 16:04)
github.com/darksteal/BTECH-Relay — an ATAK plugin that links BTECH UV-PRO / GMRS-PRO / UV-50X radios to ATAK over Bluetooth SPP + the radio's KISS TNC; AX.25 frames, a compact binary format with fragmentation, optional AES-256; position, chat, CoT markers / routes, contact age-out and Bluetooth auto-reconnect working, voice PTT a scaffold; 2 commits. Nathan: he has run a different networking stack over the UV-Pro, "the solution is pretty sound".
Fit: UTV riders already carry GMRS radios. 47 CFR 95.1787 lets a GMRS handheld send location (or a request for it) and brief text — each burst ≤ 1 s, no more than once per 30 s, integral antenna, not on the 467 MHz main channels — a GroupTrack position beacon fits; tracks / routes / markers do not. Packet modems typically 1200 baud. A transport behind the 2.8 separation beside Meshtastic and the Nucleus IP mesh.
Cautions: licence MIT + Commons Clause (commercial sale reserved) — do not copy their code into the paid app without the author's permission; KISS / AX.25 / SPP are open standards, write our own. Encryption is not addressed in 95.1787; amateur rules prohibit messages encoded to obscure meaning — check before any encrypted traffic on these bands. Needs real radios and distance (January).
Next: ask Nathan which stack he used over the UV-Pro and the throughput he saw.
