📐 Rules set on 10-22 (Fred) — they govern every patch from here
One standard for leaving: HELP ✕ top right on every screen, panel and dialog. ✕ = leave (close / cancel; nothing else happens). The COMPLETE is the screen's own action button (CHECK IN, SAVE, APPLY, SEND). Panels that stay on screen add ☰ MOVE and HIDE / SHOW. One help viewer (GtHelpView) opens on top of every screen. (Fred 12:18–12:21: "no preference as long as it is consistent.")
The touch rule (12:06, 12:50): every screen we have touched is brought to the new standard — scroll, HELP, ✕ — even if the feature is a placeholder; when a function is touched, every screen it opens is brought to the standard in the same patch.
Nothing is removed without a home (11:47): a control is never hidden or replaced unless the same patch puts it somewhere. The hidden-controls ledger below records every one.
The one-option rule (11:09): a button whose module has one attached process runs it directly — no in-between list. Key functions are never hidden between navigation layers (11:07).
Bring over exactly as it exists, then restructure (14:35): moving a function never redesigns it; realignment comes after everything is moved.
Automated is not a menu item (15:10): a function that only runs inside another process (corridor downloads after an import, a source refresh) moves with its process and never gets a button.
Trace before attaching (Claude, after the Add Route detour 14:33): a function that crosses into another screen is traced start → work → complete → cancel → back before it is handed over, and the dead ends are reported first.
Route+ is not taken apart (13:48–13:58): it is moved whole; its start-up checks (in-progress routes, compare sets, leftover AI routes, the unnamed draft) always run.
Search filters after, not before (13:04): search everything; the result types are the filter.
Map selection and map sources belong together (15:10).
Persistence purpose (13:30–13:33): the state file is for returning BETWEEN SESSIONS to where you left off. Start-up ALWAYS restores the saved view — no exceptions; Centre on Me is one tap to where you are. ("If startup centres me where I am it is a lot of work to return to where I was. If I return to where I was it is one button to bring me to where I am.")
Attaching order (11:01): top row, down the right column, then the bottom bar left to right.

2. Principles (Fred, 10-18 to 10-21)
One map. The planning map is folded in; the Ride Planning / Back to Ride switches are retired.
A launch layer over the existing features. Each process gets ONE first screen that takes every value it needs (defaults from the ride and settings), then runs to the end with no further screen prompts. The only stop kept is the confirm before something that cannot be undone.
Two layouts. Group adds a lot of complexity and is used by some. Android only is the default; Group adds the Group button, CHECK IN, the GROUP readout, other carts and the lead track. One switch decides which.
Riders ride in landscape and pan in portrait. In landscape, panels open as a side panel so the map stays in view.
Every control shows an icon and its text on an opaque background, readable on any map. No hover, no long-press meanings.
North up only. Leaflet cannot rotate, and Hybrid labels are baked into the imagery (heading-up needs a rotating map engine: not 2.7c).
Show/hide is FILTER, how lines look is KEY: as onX and Gaia do, the filter is on every view.

MENU › Settings › Diagnostics: Check a trail · Ride statistics · Conversion record (from Settings and the old ride-config menu).
Map › Map sources: change a source (clear or keep tiles: the migrate gate) and rebuild a source (MAP RECOVERY / recreate slot).
Map › Download for offline: show what you hold / what is coming, and remove tiles from an area.
Rides › Create a route: drafts in progress (resume, rename, roll back, delete, the unnamed-draft resolver), ROUTE DETAILS notes, CREATE TRAILHEAD at save, the planner's Review / Compare and saving the compare set.
Tap a feature: rename, change type, delete, fit, aliases, Create a ride; tracks add SHARE (the track export sheet).
Record button: the automatic-pause banner (CONTINUE), the ROLE CONFLICT banner, the lead question when no Leader is known (decide in phase 2).
Unchanged in 2.7c: Android permission prompts, the startup online/offline chooser, sign-in, terms and privacy gates, the V3 account and organizer screens, the developer menu.

New in 2.7bMost of 2.7b is under the hood: GroupTrack and the radio now talk through one connection, and the ride map is drawn only from the messages your tablet receives. What you do on the trail is the same. What you will notice:
Group awareness, or this tablet only &mdash; ride without a radio and GroupTrack hides everything that needs one. Group awareness
The lead's track &mdash; solid bright blue ahead, your own track dashed blue; behind you the lead's track gives way to yours. The lead cart
When the lead goes quiet &mdash; his cart keeps moving at an estimate, along the route or the trail he was on as far as the next junction, and his real path is filled in when he is heard again. The lead cart
The radio link &mdash; "Your radio isn't answering" tells you what to do; losing satellites no longer disconnects the radio.
Roles &mdash; no Leader, no lead; two riders on one role both go back to Rider. Roles on the trail
Smaller things &mdash; recording pauses after 25 idle minutes instead of 10, a GPS light above REC, arrows on your route, Medium Fast or Long Fast in the GPS panel, Ride statistics in Settings, NODES instead of the Meshtastic side menu.

1 About GroupTrackstart here
1.1 What GroupTrack is
GroupTrack is a trail app for off-road riders — side-by-side, UTV, ATV, dirt bike and Jeep — and it is complete as installed. It is two products in one: a complete personal navigation product that lets you share rides and maps with other GroupTrack users, and a true situational awareness product for your group on the trail.
On your own, it does the whole job. The trails and the maps live on your device, so it keeps working where there is no signal — which is most of where you ride. Plan a route by dropping pins that snap to the trails, or let the planner build several for you to compare; mark waypoints; download the maps along the route; record where you went. (The Ride Planning Map · Letting the planner build it · The Ride Map)
New: ★ Create a Ride. One ride holds the route, the trailhead, the date and time, the maps to download and the mesh radio configuration. Send it in one click; your friends open it in one click — and ride anywhere off grid in total confidence. Friends, organizers and clubs plan for each other and all ride from the same page. (The Ride · Sending a ride, and getting one)
Your identity. Your rider profile — your callsign and your email — is who you are in GroupTrack: your callsign on the map and in every ride you send, your email where rides reach you. It is private: it stays on your tablet and goes only to the riders you ride with. (Your rider profile)
Add a radio to experience full group awareness while riding
Add a Meshtastic radio — any Meshtastic radio — and you see your group on the map with no cell service: every cart where it is, with its callsign and role. GroupTrack sets the radio up for you. (Group Awareness)
Rides on the GroupTrack network — or your own. New rides use the GroupTrack default network, so any rider with a GroupTrack radio can join with nothing to change. When a ride should be heard only by its riders, choose your own network or a private network for that ride. (The ride form)
One standard language. Radios report in TAK, the format team-awareness apps use — your position with your callsign, even with the tablet in your pocket. (Setting up your radio)
Roles and presence. Riders check in at the trailhead to claim a role — Leader, Middle, Tail gunner or Rider — and announce that they are there; checking in also sets the radio up for the ride. (Checking in and recording your track · Roles on the trail)
So a ride goes like this: tap the Ride invite — the route, trailhead and ride description are created and the maps imported; with a radio, check in at the trailhead; then REC. For the organizer, one step: build the ride and send it.
What is new in this release: the release notes.
1.2 Which kind of rider are you?
There are two ways to ride with GroupTrack, and knowing which is yours tells you what to read and what to skip.
On your own. A tablet and nothing else: trails, maps, the planner, routes, waypoints, a record of where you went — and rides you can create, send and receive. Everything except seeing your group on the map. The record button reads ⏺ REC.
With a group. You also carry a Meshtastic radio, so you and the riders with you see each other on the map with no cell service. You join rides, check in, and take a role; the record button reads ✔ CHK IN › REC.
You can move between them. Nothing has to be decided now — connect a radio in GRP Awareness and the group side appears by itself.
Riding on your own? The parts about radios, check-in, roles and the group do not apply to you — GRP Awareness, VIEW CART ROLES, and the radio entries in Work with Rides. Skip them with a clear conscience.
1.3 How this goes
You do not have to take it all on at once. Most riders never go past the
second step, and that is a complete and useful app.
Ride and record. Trails on your device, maps that work with no
signal, and a record of where you went. Nothing else required.
Plan before you go. Download the maps you will need, and bring in what
you already have from Gaia or onX. And build the ride itself, two ways:
  Draw it yourself. Drop pins along the way and GroupTrack snaps the
  line to the trails underneath, drawing straight only where there are none. Use
  this when you know where you want to go.
  Let the planner build it. Give it a trailhead, how far you want to
  ride and any places you want to pass through, and it searches the trail network
  for you — then puts several routes side by side so you can compare distance,
  riding time and the trails each one uses. Use this when you know the area
  loosely, or not at all.
Ride as a group. See where everyone is, with no cell service. An organizer builds a ride and sends it; each rider opens it with one tap, checks in at the trailhead and takes a role. That can be you and a few friends on your own network, or a riding club that owns ten radios, hands them out at the trailhead and collects them afterwards.
You do not need a tablet to carry a radio. The radio reports its location
by itself, so a rider only has to put one round their neck to appear on
everyone else's map.
1.4 Structure and navigation
GroupTrack is built around two maps, with your radio one tap away on both. The important thing to take away is use the right map for the task.
The Ride Map — the map you use in the field, on the trail. Simple and focused: check in, record, and see your group.
The Ride Planning Map — built to be used online, at home. Design a route or have the planner build one, download maps for offline use, and create and share rides.
Your radio and your rides are on both. GRP Awareness connects your radio and shows your group's activity; Work with Rides holds your rides. There is no separate radio screen to open or hide.
All navigation is text. Words you tap, down the right-hand side of either map. No icons to decode. And the two maps carry the same controls in the same places — learn one and you know the other. Every control is lettered on each map's picture in its chapter.
1.5 Map Features — the four things on your map
Everything GroupTrack draws is one of four things. Together they are what we
call the Map Features, and they are what the Map Features panel
controls.
TrailDocumented ground you can ride, motorized or not. Many have no
name — that does not mean they are not real, or not documented.
TrackA recording of where you went.
RouteA line you plan to ride.
WaypointA place you marked.
1.6 Getting started
New to GroupTrack? Install, then follow the Quick Start: it asks for your rider profile (your name, callsign and email), then loads the trails for your home state. A radio is not needed — maps, routes and rides all work without one. Riding with a radio? Connect it whenever you like, then set it up: GRP Awareness → Select a ride and apply settings to the radio → GroupTrack default (see Setting up your radio). GroupTrack asks once, at first start: Do you have a mesh radio to use with GroupTrack? — see The radio question at first start.
Your first start, step by stepLocation permission — choose Allow all the time, so the map keeps your position while the screen is off.Your rider profile — your name, callsign and email, how you usually ride, your vehicle and your colour; Save.The radio question — Do you have a mesh radio to use with GroupTrack? YES connects it in GRP Awareness; NO leaves it for later.Your home state's trails — GroupTrack offers the state you are in; load it, or choose another.The import runs — it takes a while; keep GroupTrack open until it finishes. Updating from 2.6? The one-time steps — your rider profile, updating your radio once, and opening ride files with GroupTrack — and what has moved are in the release notes.
2 Your rider profilenew — set up once
2.1 What it is, and why GroupTrack asks
The first time you open this version, GroupTrack asks for your name, a callsign and an email address. It takes a
minute, and you only do it once.
GroupTrack uses standard TAK messaging to put your group on each other's maps. That needs a name to show beside your
cart, and an email so you can send ride details to the riders coming with you.
Your callsign is what everyone sees — on the map, and in every message your radio sends. Short and
recognisable works best. Two riders can share a callsign; the radios still tell you apart.
It stays on your tablet. Nothing is sent to GroupTrack. Your details go only to the riders you ride with, over
the radio, or in ride files you choose to send.
2.2 Changing it later
Settings → Your Profile → Edit rider profile. Everything is editable, though the callsign and email stay
required — they are what your group and your ride files depend on.
The rest are defaults for each ride you join: how you usually ride (leader, rider, middle, tail gunner), your
vehicle, and your colour on the map. You can change them on any individual ride.
Your default role — Leader, Rider, Middle or Tail gunner — is the role GroupTrack offers when you check in to a ride; most riders leave it as Rider. At check-in you can change it, and your callsign, for that ride only; your profile stays as it is. On a ride you created, Leader is offered instead. There is one leader per ride. (See Checking in and recording your track and Roles on the trail.)
2.3 Riding under an organizationdrafting
[PLACEHOLDER — belonging to a club, leading rides under it, and what that means for your group's network.]
3 The Ridewhat are its components, and what does it mean to me?
A ride is everything a group needs to ride together, in one package. The organizer builds it once and sends it; each rider opens it with one tap, checks in at the trailhead, and rides.
Create a Ride — new in 2.7aA ride is created from a route. Tap any route on the planning map: a route the planner built opens its description with CREATE RIDE; a route you drew opens its details with ADD A RIDE. The ride form opens with the route, its trailhead and its picture. Map Features → ★ Create a Ride · Creating a ride from a route · from a track you recorded: Creating a ride from a trackA route the planner built — tap it, then CREATE RIDE.A route you drew — tap it, then ADD A RIDE.
How a ride is built
Start from a route. A ride is always built on a route. Draw one yourself on the planning map — drop pins and it snaps to the trails (Drawing a route yourself) — or let the planner build several for you to choose from (Letting the planner build it). Every route is saved with its trailhead (Creating a route). Then tap the route on the map and CREATE RIDE — or ADD A RIDE on a route you drew yourself (Creating a ride from a route).
…or from a track you recorded. A track you recorded becomes a route — every turn kept, the track itself never changed — and the ride form opens (Creating a ride from a track).
Mark the places that matter with waypoints. A waypoint is a place you marked — the trailhead, fuel, water, a hazard, a viewpoint (A waypoint). Long press on the map to create one; it starts as a Trailhead (Long press — add a waypoint).
Fill in the ride form and save. Name, date and rollout time, public or private, the radio network, and the Leader's Notes (The ride form).
Share it. Send it as a Ride invite: the rider taps it, and GroupTrack creates the route, trailhead and description and imports the maps (Sending a ride, and getting one).
The radio network — group awareness
Seeing each other on the map with no cell service needs a Meshtastic radio for each rider. Every ride carries its radio network — the GroupTrack default network, unless the organizer chose their own network or a private one for the ride. At the trailhead, checking in sets each rider's radio up for that network by itself, and from then on every radio reports its rider's position, callsign and role to the group (Setting up your radio · GRP Awareness · Checking in and recording your track).
The components, and what they mean to you
The ride detailsIts name, date and rollout time, the organizer, public or private, and the Leader's Notes.What it means to you: you know when and where to show up, and what to expect — straight from the organizer. The ride form
The routeThe line the group will follow, with its description of what you will see and ride.What it means to you: you can study the ride before you go, and it is on your map the moment you open the email. Creating a route
The trailheadWhere the route starts — where riders meet and unload.What it means to you: no "where are we meeting?" — it is a marked point on your map. Creating a route
WaypointsFuel, water, hazards, viewpoints and other places marked along the way.What it means to you: you know what is ahead before you get there. Tapping a feature on the map
The mapsThe satellite and topo imagery along the route — the download starts when you open the ride.What it means to you: the whole ride is on your tablet, so the map works with no signal. Sending a ride, and getting one
The radio networkCarried in the ride: the GroupTrack default network, the organizer's own network, or a private network for this ride.What it means to you: when you check in, your radio is set up for it by itself — you hear your group. On the organizer's own or a private network, nobody else hears the ride. Setting up your radio
RolesLeader, Middle, Tail gunner and Rider — claimed when you check in, and broadcast to everyone.What it means to you: everyone knows who is leading and who is sweeping, and the map shows it. Roles on the trail
The check-inAt the trailhead you pick the ride and your role, and your radio is set up. Only with a radio — riding solo, there is no check-in.What it means to you: one step puts you on the ride and tells the group you are there. Checking in and recording your track
The end of the rideEND saves your track under the ride's name; on a public ride, rate it and choose whether to share your track.What it means to you: your ride is filed, and your rating helps the next group decide. Checking in and recording your track
In short: the organizer builds one ride; the rider taps it once and checks in — and has the route, the maps, the radio setup and a place in the group. The sections below take each step in order: create the route and the ride, send it, set up radios, then check in and ride.
3.1 Creating a route
Every route has a trailhead — its first point. Every route is saved with its trailhead, as part of the save: the route's first point — where you pressed REC on a track, or your first pin in Route+. If a Trailhead waypoint is already within 0.1 mile of it, that one is used; otherwise GroupTrack creates one there and asks only for its name. Every ride built on the route uses that trailhead. You can rename it later; to use a different spot, add a waypoint there first (long-press the map) and set its type to Trailhead.
Saving a Route+ route with no trailhead at its first pin: SAVE asks "The route's first point is being created as a trailhead. Please name it" — name it, CREATE TRAILHEAD, then SAVE again.
With the planner. Build a route with Route+ on the planning map — draw it yourself or let the planner build it (see Route+ under The Ride Planning Map). A route built by the planner comes with its own story: what you will see, mile by mile.
From a track you recorded. A track becomes a route as part of creating a ride from it — see Creating a ride from a track. The track itself is never changed.
The route's description is part of the route: tap the route and it opens with the first line, the distance, and your text under ABOUT THIS ROUTE. Riders you send a ride to see the same.
The planner's plan for the day — CONTINUE TO COMPARE, or START OVER.
3.2 Creating a ride from a routenew in 2.7a — CREATE RIDE / ADD A RIDE
Where it starts: the planning map. Find the route (the search box finds it by name) and tap it.
The route's panel opens. A route the planner built opens its description, with ROUTE DETAILS · CREATE RIDE · DOWNLOAD MAPS — tap CREATE RIDE. A route you drew yourself has no description, so it opens the detail panel — tap ADD A RIDE. (On a planner route, ROUTE DETAILS then ADD A RIDE does the same.) What each touch opens: The Ride Planning Map → Map gestures.
The map fits to the route and its trailhead. Every other layer is switched off, so the view shows only the route and where it starts; the ride's picture is taken from it. The map stays that way — turn layers back on in Map Features.
The ride form opens with the route, its trailhead and its picture — continue with The ride form.
Step 1, a planner route — its description: ROUTE DETAILS · CREATE RIDE · DOWNLOAD MAPS. Tap CREATE RIDE.
Step 1, a route you drew — its detail panel: tap ADD A RIDE.
FIT — the route fills the screen.
FIT on a route's details shows the same view at any time.
📷 IMAGE TO CHECK — the ride form's radio network is now three choices — recapture if the network row is in the picture (release l, 10-10)Step 3 — the ride form opens with the route and its picture.
3.3 Creating a ride from a tracknew
Where it starts: the planning map. Tap one of your tracks — a recording of where you went — to open its details.
Tap CREATE RIDE on the track's details.
The trailhead is settled first. A Trailhead within 0.1 mile of the track's first point (where you pressed REC) is used without asking. Otherwise a box explains: "The trail's first point is being created as a trailhead. Please name it" — name it and tap CONTINUE; the trailhead is on the map before the route is made.
Name and describe the route. A box asks for:
Route name — the track's name to start with; change it if you like. A name another route already uses is refused.
Route description — in your own words: skill level, terrain, highlights, cautions. GroupTrack writes the first line itself: "Created from track &lt;track&gt; — N miles", measured along the track you recorded.
The box shows "Trailhead: &lt;name&gt;".
Tap CREATE ROUTE &amp; RIDE. The track's line becomes the route — straights are thinned out, but every turn is kept, switchbacks included (within about a metre of what you rode). The route is saved with its trailhead. The track itself is never changed, and the route stays even if you cancel the ride.
The map fits to the new route and its trailhead, and the ride's picture is taken.
The ride form opens — continue with The ride form.
A track's detail panel.
This route needs a trailhead — name the start of the track.
Create a ride from this track — the route's name and description.
3.4 The ride form
Both ways of creating a ride — from a route and from a track — end here.
The ride's picture is the fitted view of the route and its trailhead, taken as the form opens.
The form, top to bottom:
Ride name — the only thing needed to save. You can save a ride with just a name and finish it later.
Private ride — off: a public ride (the default); on: private. The line under the switch says what each means (see Public or private below).
Radio network — choose one of three: GroupTrack default network (chosen for you), your own network (shown as your name and its network id), or Create a private network for this ride (see Your radio network).
Date and Rollout time — on one line. The date comes from a calendar; a ride can only be sent while its date is today or later. The time is optional.
Leader's Notes — the ride's own notes: meeting point, what to bring, timing. A new ride starts from the route's description. The box appears when the route has no description (then it is required) and whenever you edit a ride.
Trailhead — the route's own trailhead, shown for you. For a route saved before every route had one: if no trailhead is near its start, describe where to meet in the Trailhead box — it goes at the top of the Leader's Notes, and the ride can be sent.
The route — its name over its picture: the route and its trailhead. The route cannot be changed.
Your name and email, and the zip code (worked out from the trailhead), are recorded with the ride automatically — they are not on the form.
Tap SAVE RIDE — or CANCEL to leave the form with nothing saved.
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — three radio networks: GroupTrack default network (chosen) · your own network (name · id) · private network for this ride (release l, 10-10)The ride form — name, private or public, and the radio network.
The ride form, continued — date, notes, the trailhead and the route.
A ride's state tells you how far along it is: in progress while something is missing; completed once it has a route, a
trailhead, a date today or later and a description — only a completed ride can be sent; sent previously once it has gone out at least once.
After a ride has been sent, only its date can change — to reschedule it (weather, for example); then send it again so your riders get the new date.
The route stays with the ride. Tap the route on the ride screen and GroupTrack explains why — your riders plan around the route you sent.
To use another route, delete the ride (before sending) and add a new ride from that route. Deleting a ride never deletes the route.
What the ride carries: the route with its trailhead and its story, the date and description, who created it (name and email), and — for groups with radios —
the ride's radio network.
Public or private. A ride is public unless you switch on Private ride at the top of the form. The invitation email says which: "This is an open ride. Feel free to forward this email…" or "This is a private ride for the riders invited. Please don't forward this email."
Public — the invitation says riders may forward it to friends. At the end of the ride, each rider rates it and chooses — yes or no, every time — whether to share their track with the community. From 3.0, public rides are shown to the community through their organizer, and shared tracks help map the trails.
Private — for the riders you choose; the invitation asks them not to forward it. At the end of the ride there is no survey and no sharing: every rider's track stays on their own tablet, and no public trails are added from it.
Your radio network. The form offers three. GroupTrack default network — chosen for you: every GroupTrack radio shares it, so any rider can join your ride with nothing to change. Your own network, shown as your name and its network id (Fred K · GroupAB12CD) — GroupTrack creates it the first time you open the ride form, and every ride you put on it uses the same one, so riders who have joined one of those rides are already on it for the next. Create a private network for this ride — for a one-off event: it is created the moment you choose it, used only when the ride is added, and removed again if you cancel. Choose your own or a private network when the ride should be heard only by the riders on it; each rider's radio is set up for it when they check in. Saving a ride makes you an organizer. Another organizer's network is never offered: theirs reaches your radio only when you join their ride. Once a ride has been sent, its network cannot change: to use another, delete the ride and add a new one.
The end of the ride. See Checking in and recording your track: every recording starts with a check-in, and ends with one form — the survey and the share choice on a public ride, only the name on a private one.
3.5 Adding a rider to your ride
Send them the ride (see Sending a ride, and getting one). When they open it, the route, trailhead and maps arrive on their tablet.
Their radio. On their tablet — or on yours, with their radio connected — Work with Rides → Apply ride to radio / Nucleus, pick the ride, and type their callsign in Callsign for this radio. The radio joins the ride's network — the same one as yours, so you hear each other — and carries their name. Your own profile is not changed. (See Setting up your radio.)
What they need first: GroupTrack installed, and their rider profile filled in (GroupTrack asks for it the first time it opens).

3.8 Checking in and recording your tracknew
Check-in is for group awareness only. It needs a connected radio. Riding solo with a tablet alone, you never see these screens: the button reads ⏺ REC and records straight away.
Everybody checks in first thing at the trailhead. Radio on, GroupTrack started, check in. Checking in is what puts your radio on the ride's network — until then it cannot hear the group. The Leader, Middle and Tail gunner check in among the first, so the whole group learns their roles; the ride starts once everyone has checked in.

With No scheduled ride, CHECK IN first puts your radio back on the GroupTrack default network — after a ride on a private network, your radio returns to the network every GroupTrack rider shares. 3.9 Radio range and group sizenew
A quieter channel. GroupTrack's radios use the MEDIUM_FAST setting, and report every 30 seconds standing and, moving, every 100 metres — at most every 6 seconds. Measured with two radios at the earlier, busier values (15 s / 4 s), the share of airtime they use fell from about 22% to 4–5% — so many more riders fit on one ride before the channel gets crowded.
The trade-off is range. On a T1000-E, plan on about ¾ mile between riders in open country; terrain and trees shorten it, a clear line of sight lengthens it. Radios with a bigger antenna or more power reach further. These are estimates, to be measured on real trails.
Radios relay for each other. A rider out of direct reach is still heard through the riders between you, so a strung-out group stays connected as long as no gap between riders is longer than a radio's reach.
Strong radios make a backbone. A radio with a good antenna — 1 watt, mounted high on the vehicle — reaches much further, and hears weak radios better too. Put strong radios at the lead, at the tail, and in the middle of a long group. The leader's radio matters most: it carries the leader's track to everyone behind.
Every radio on a ride must use the same setting. GroupTrack sets this for you when you apply the ride; radios set differently cannot hear each other at all.
3.10 Roles on the trail
Your role is chosen when you check in — Leader, Rider, Middle or Tail gunner — for that ride only (see Checking in). There is one leader per ride.
Everyone is a Rider unless they check in as the Leader, Middle or Tail gunner. When those three check in, their tablets tell the group — over the radio, for a few minutes into the ride — so every cart learns who holds each role. Nothing is set on the radios themselves.
What you see: every cart's callsign and role beside it on the map and in VIEW CART ROLES; the lead and tail markers follow the riders who hold those roles. When the Leader is known, REC does not ask you to choose the lead cart.
Roles stay put for the ride — a cart that drops out of range keeps its role. They end with the ride.
One of each. A ride has one Leader, one Middle and one Tail gunner at most; any number of Riders. The Leader is the key role — the Leader's cart is the lead cart. With no Tail gunner, the last cart is the tail.
Each rider sets only their own role. Nobody can give a role to someone else, and a role someone already holds can't be taken until it is released.
Changing roles at a stop: open VIEW CART ROLES and tap your own cart in the list (Change my role). Choosing Rider releases your role. One rider at a time, and the Leader changes last — for example, to hand over the lead: the Leader changes to Rider, then the new Leader takes Leader. Every tablet follows within seconds.
The lead cart: when REC is pressed with no Leader known, GroupTrack asks you which cart leads — on your tablet only. As soon as a Leader is heard, the lead moves to them. This works on every ride, scheduled or not.
New in 2.7b: The rules for roles and the lead, in one place:
Roles show only while you are checked in. Before check-in, and after END, the carts show without roles.
The Leader is the lead — on every tablet. When a rider checks in as Leader, every tablet makes that cart the lead.
No Leader, no lead. When the Leader changes to Rider, the lead is cleared on every tablet. A rider claims Leader in VIEW CART ROLES, or REC asks which cart leads.
Two claims of one role — both go back to Rider. If two riders claim Leader, Middle or Tail gunner at the same moment, both are set back to Rider. Each tablet shows a flashing red ROLE CONFLICT message — "You and … both claimed Leader. Only one rider can hold Leader, so BOTH of you have been set back to Rider. Agree who takes Leader, then that rider claims it again in View Cart Roles (open behind this message). A role can be claimed once nobody else holds it." — with VIEW CART ROLES open behind it. Tap OK, agree, and one of you claims the role again.
Why both? The two tablets cannot tell whose claim came first, so neither keeps it — the riders decide.

By area.
The area selected — press Proceed.
Smaller and faster when you only need one part of a state.
4.5.8 Importing from Gaia or onXGPX from other apps
Tracks, routes and waypoints you have collected in other apps come across as
GPX files.
What GroupTrack found in Downloads.
Export from Gaia or onX. If you do it on this device the file lands in
Downloads and GroupTrack finds it.
Exported somewhere else? Get the file into the Android Downloads
directory however suits — email, a website, cloud storage.
Choose what to import.
There is no direct connection between the apps. It is export, then import, and
the file passes through Downloads on the way.
Sharing a route with another rider
Export a route and the file carries more than its shape. The narrative
travels with it — the summary, what you will see, the cautions — and so does the
recipe, the settings it was built from.
That means the rider you send it to can open BUILD FROM RECIPE and
search again on their own device. They may get different routes than you did,
and that is the point: the recipe is a set of instructions, not a copy of your
answer. Their trail data is not yours.
Opened in Gaia or onX, the route still reads normally — those apps see the name,
the description and the points, and ignore the rest.
Why you should import all of them
Importing your old tracks is worth more than keeping a record of where you have
been. Where one of your tracks crosses ground that no published map covers,
GroupTrack adds that stretch to your trails as an unnamed trail.
Published trail data misses a great deal. Roads and tracks that riders use
every weekend are simply not in it. Your own rides are proof that ground is
rideable — you rode it — and that is better evidence than any survey offers.
So every track you bring in makes the map more complete, and the route
planner is only as good as the network underneath it. A planner working from
published trails alone will route you the long way around ground you know
perfectly well.
Load your states first. A ride that crosses into a state you have not
imported has no trails underneath it, so the whole stretch is treated as new
ground — even where trails already exist there. Import the states you ride in,
then import your tracks.
After that the order does not matter. Each track is checked as it arrives, so
you can import them whenever you like and there is nothing to run afterwards.
How to import them. Put the GPX files in Downloads on your
Android — save them from an email attachment, or download them straight from
your navigation app. Then tap Import Trails on the Map Features
screen from the planning map, read the short notice (how to get back: system BACK, or CANCEL), and pick the files.
To select several files at once, press and hold the first file, then tap
the others.
Removing one
Tap a rider trail and you get a DELETE button. Surveyed trails do not
have one — deleting those achieves nothing, because the next trail reload brings
them straight back from the catalogue.
A rider trail comes back too, if the track that made it is still on the device
and trails are cleared and reloaded. To be rid of one for good, delete the track
as well.
The commonest reason to remove one: a recorder left running on the drive to
the trailhead. Highways are not in the trail data, so the whole drive reads as
new ground and gets added.
What each category means
Open Map Keys and press CATEGORIES EXPLAINED at the foot of
the panel. Every line on the map is one of these:
OHV — posted trails for ATV/OHV use only.
Track — two wheel tracks, farm, forest or open country.
Forestry / access — access unless posted otherwise. Look for a
sign.
Shape only — shape and route of reported trails that are otherwise unclassified. Somebody drew the
line; nobody said what it is — check the satellite imagery before you plan on it.
Rider trails — ridden on a recorded track, so UTV accessible. This
is ground you have been on, which is the strongest thing the map knows.
Unofficial / uncertain — not available for riding.
Hiking &amp; biking, Hiking, Biking,
Equestrian, Steps / bridge — non-motorized. Off by default;
switch them on in Map Features if you want to see them.
My tracks and My routes — your own recordings and plans.
Tap any name in the key panel to change its colour, line pattern or
thickness. Those choices are yours and stay on your device.
What these trails look like
They are unnamed, and they carry their own colour so you can tell them
from surveyed trails at a glance. They are filtered and displayed like any other
trail.
They are honest rather than perfect: a rider trail says you rode that ground,
not that it is a maintained road or that anyone else may use it. Check ownership
and access the same way you would anywhere else.
Routes you built before will come back different. Once there is more
network to work with, the planner finds rides it could not find before. That is
the improvement working, not a fault.

4.5.9.2 Letting the planner build itsix questions, up to six routes
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — CANCEL AI BUILD added to every step before the build (release f, 10-08)What the planner is about to do.
Six questions, then it searches the area's trails — up to 10,000 of them in
some places — and brings back as many as six routes that fit what you asked
for.
What you answer is saved with the routes you keep, so you can build six
more from the same brief at any time.
Get to where you want to ride first. Search for a town, region or feature, or
open one of your own tracks or waypoints, and centre the map on your starting
point.
Planning stays in portrait — the comparison needs the height.
CANCEL AI BUILD is on every step before the build: it leaves the planner completely, removes this run's unfinished route, and takes you back to the map.
1 · How long a day?
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — CANCEL AI BUILD added to every step before the build (release f, 10-08)Distance and speed give you a duration.
Set the shortest and furthest you want to ride, and an average speed. Together
they give a ride duration. Move the mileage until the hours match the time
you have.
Leave the average speed alone until you have a few rides behind you. It is
set from measured riding on this kind of ground, and changing it changes every
estimate the planner makes.
2 · Where you will park
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — CANCEL AI BUILD on the step banner; Map Features no longer opens by itself at the trailhead step; a trailhead with no shown trail within ½ mile is refused with a message (release f, 10-08)Tap a waypoint, or press and hold to make one.📷 NEW SCREEN — CAPTURE TO ADD — the message when the trailhead has no trail shown on the map within the half-mile circle (release f, 10-08)
Tap the waypoint where you will park. If there is none there, press and
hold for a second to create one — creating it selects it, so you do not need
to tap again.
Pick a spot that visibly reaches the trail network: several trails leaving in
different directions, not a single dead-end spur.
The trailhead must have a trail shown on the map within the half-mile circle around it. If not, the planner says so and you choose again — check Map Keys: a trail type switched off there is not used for planning. Map Features no longer opens by itself at this step.
3 · Points to cover
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — CANCEL AI BUILD on the step banner (release f, 10-08)Places the ride should reach.
Optional. If there are places you want the ride to reach, tap the closest
trail to each. Tap a pin again to remove it.
The planner includes as many as it can, as long as it can find a route over
existing trails to reach them. One it cannot reach, or one that would push
the ride past your distance, is refused with a reason rather than quietly
ignored.
4 · Where you finish
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — CANCEL AI BUILD on the step banner (release f, 10-08)A loop, or somewhere else.
A loop back to where you started is what most day rides use. The other option
is a different endpoint — a second trailhead, or somewhere you are staying.
5 · Review
📷 NEW IMAGE NEEDED — CANCEL AI BUILD on the plan summary (release f, 10-08)What it is about to build.

Continue to compare.

With a radio connected, the button first reads ✔ CHK IN › REC — check in to your ride, then tap ⏺ REC. See Checking in and recording your track.
Press the red button to start. Do it before you set off — the first
part of a ride is usually the part you most want on the map afterwards.
Recording has started.
Riding with a group
If you are riding with a mesh group you are asked to pick the lead
cart. That cart lays down a track which is visible on every device in the
group — so everyone behind can follow the line the leader actually took.
Once riders have checked in, the Leader role decides the lead — roles change at a stop, from VIEW CART ROLES.
What you will see
Keep the screen where you can see it. Riding alone, your cart sits in the
centre with your track behind you and the ground ahead.
In a group you also see the lead cart's track laid out ahead of you,
and a pin for every other cart.
If you stop for a while
Paused.
GroupTrack notices when you have not moved for a time and pauses recording
itself, closing the connection to your radio as it does.
That is deliberate. A T1000-E that times out on its own has a hard time
reconnecting; ending the session from this end is clean, and it reconnects
without trouble when you resume.
You come back to a flashing red banner. Tap it to carry on — the radio
reconnects and the recording continues into the same track.
New in 2.7b: the pause comes after 25 minutes without moving (it was 10), and the banner reads Sleeping &mdash; Recording paused, radio disconnected. Tap to wake.📷 IMAGE TO CHECK — the sleep banner now reads "Sleeping / Recording paused, radio disconnected. Tap to wake." (2.7b ZZZ25, 10-16)
While it is paused, your radio is disconnected — not just the recording. The group stops hearing you, and your map stops showing them, until you tap the banner.
The idle timer starts again at REC (2.7b, 19 October): pressing REC, or carrying on after a pause, starts the 25 minutes from zero &mdash; a new recording started where the last one ended no longer goes to sleep straight away.
Ending the ride
Press END.
Name it, or delete it.
Give the ride a name you will recognise later. The date is kept for you.
Save keeps it — it appears on the map and in your tracks.
Delete throws it away. There is no undo.
Recording uses GPS the whole time. On a long day, bring a charger.

5.5 G · QUEUESdownloads in the background
Map downloads run in the background so they do not tie up the screen.
Running.
Nothing queued.
Leave the screen and carry on — the download continues. If the device is
turned off it picks up where it stopped rather than starting again.
Managing the queue
A job can be held, cancelled, or purged once complete.
Anything waiting can be promoted to run next.
What runs first
The queue sorts itself so the work you need soonest happens soonest.
Tile deletions — freeing space before filling it.
Anything you promoted.
Corridor downloads — a route's tiles.
Area downloads — a bounding box.
Map source refreshes — last, and they wait.
A large refresh never blocks you. Ask for an area or a corridor while one
is running and yours goes ahead of it; the big job carries on afterwards.
There is a limit on how many downloads run at once. It is already tuned —
worth leaving alone.

5.7.2 SELECT on trailsnarrowing by category
Trails work differently, and they have to. There are 60,000 unnamed trails
in Utah — searching by name helps nobody.
Narrow by category, not by name.
So you limit trails by category instead:
Private land — include it or leave it out. Near a town, leaving it out
removes the residential street grid.
Motorized and non-motorized — take a whole group in or out.
Individual categories — choose exactly which kinds you want.
GroupTrack installs showing motorized trails on public land only. If a
trail you know exists is not on the map, that is usually why.
5.8 J · Map Keyswhat the lines mean
The legend.
GroupTrack installs with solid lines for motorized trails and
dashed lines for non-motorized, with colours defined for each type. The
legend tells you which is which.
Every trail gets its category. The last step of a state import, Classify trails, gives each trail its type, its use and its land — public or private — from the land-ownership record. It always runs: where there is no ownership data, the land counts as public, so trails show by default. A trail you expect but cannot see? Check Map Keys first — with Land = Public, roads classified as private are hidden by design — then Settings → Check a trail.

5.10 L · GRP Awarenessyour radio in one place
GRP Awareness sits where Mesh was, on both maps: white text on a green box when your radio is connected, a red box when it is not, and the box pulses as the group is heard. Tap it:

The radio list shows your radios' call signs at once, before any scan or connection (it showed the radio's own Meshtastic_xxxx name until then).
New in 2.7b: under the radio's name, GroupTrack shows the network the radio itself is on: GroupTrack network … (green) when it is set up for GroupTrack, or Not set up for GroupTrack (amber) when it is on another network. New in 2.7b: the lead's track &mdash; while you are recording, the lead cart's track is a solid bright blue line edged in black, with arrows; your own track is dashed blue. GROUP keeps the lead's track in view.
When the lead goes quiet (two reports missed), his cart blinks at where he probably is, with est. m:ss beside it and a grey last heard dot. It moves at the ride's average speed along the route you are displaying. With no route displayed, it moves along the track or trail he was on and stops at the next junction &mdash; it never guesses which way he turned. With nothing to follow, it stays where he was last heard. When he is heard again he jumps to his real position. Ride statistics keeps how far the estimate was out.
His track through the gap is drawn along the route you are displaying &mdash; or, with none displayed, a track you rode before or the trails &mdash; never faster than a cart could drive.
When he is back in range after at least a minute without hearing anyone, his tablet sends the path he really drove (20 points). Your tablet corrects his track to it and says so in a short pop-up ("Gap polyline from …"). A point more than 50 m from the displayed route shows as a dot, not joined.
Behind you, the lead's track is removed as you ride over it, and your own track shows there. It goes in the order you ride, so on a loop or an out-and-back the way back is never removed early. If you leave the lead's path, nothing is removed until you rejoin it.

5.17 T · GPShow often your location is sent
New in 2.7b: with group awareness off, the GPS row is dimmed and the GPS button explains how to switch group awareness on — the interval is your radio's, so it only applies with a radio.📷 NEW SCREEN — CAPTURE TO ADD — the GPS row dimmed with group awareness off (2.7b GRPMODE, 10-13)
On the ride map, above the HUD at the left edge: the GPS button (a satellite), and beside it two numbers:
How often your radio sends your location while moving — for example 6 s. Standing still, it sends every 30 seconds.
How busy the radio channel is, in green (plenty of room), yellow (getting busy) or red (congested).
Tap GPS to change it: the window shows the current value, the channel use and the number of carts. Key in 3 to 10 seconds and tap APPLY. Your radio is set once, then disconnects and reconnects by itself (about half a minute) — the window shows each step. CANCEL changes nothing.
Beside them, the HUD text switch — a circle, half white and half black — switches the readouts' text between white and dark: one setting for GROUP, MY CART and the selected cart, remembered for each map type during the session. White suits SAT; dark suits TOPO.
When to change it: green — leave it. Yellow — send less often (a higher number) to free the channel. Red — the channel is congested; lengthen the interval and let the group know. Checking in sets your radio back to the ride's standard value.
New in 2.7b: the window also lets you choose the radio's preset &mdash; Medium Fast (the standard) or Long Fast &mdash; beside the interval. APPLY sets your radio once (it restarts by itself) and reads every value back. Long Fast reaches only a little further (measured 10-30% in dense housing) and is slower; the choice lasts until your next check-in, which sets the ride's standard again.

6 Group Awarenesswhat a radio does for you in a group
Group awareness is seeing your group on the map, with no cell service. Every rider's cart is drawn where they are, labelled with their callsign and their role, and you know who has checked in to the ride. It works because each rider carries a radio, and the radios talk to each other directly — cart to cart, out where there is no signal.
What you need: a Meshtastic radio
Group awareness needs a Meshtastic radio for each rider. GroupTrack works with any Meshtastic radio — handheld trackers such as the SenseCAP T1000-E, radios with a screen, base stations. Connect yours to your tablet in GRP Awareness (connect, pair, forget). A radio also works on its own: set up by GroupTrack, it reports its rider's position by itself, so a rider with a radio and no tablet still appears on everyone's map.
Without a radio, everything else in GroupTrack still works — trails, maps, routes, rides and your own recording. You just do not see the group.
The default setup
The first time you use a radio with GroupTrack, give it the GroupTrack default: Work with Rides → Apply ride to radio / Nucleus → GroupTrack default. This makes it report in the standard team-awareness format (TAK) with your callsign, every 30 seconds standing, and while moving every 100 metres — at most every 6 seconds, on a channel setting that leaves room for many riders. GroupTrack writes each setting, reads it back and ticks it. (Setting up your radio)
Set your radio up with GroupTrack, not by hand — a radio set by hand can report far more often than it needs to and crowd the channel for everyone.
Applying a ride
Every ride carries its radio network — the GroupTrack default network, the organizer's own network, or a private network for that ride. Checking in to the ride applies it: if your radio is not on that network yet, CHECK IN sets it up first (about a minute), then checks you in. Checking in with No scheduled ride puts the radio back on the GroupTrack default, unless you tick Keep my radio as it is. (Checking in and recording your track)
You can also apply a ride to a radio yourself — to prepare before the day, or to set up a guest's radio at the trailhead under their callsign: Work with Rides → Apply ride to radio / Nucleus. (Apply ride to radio / Nucleus)
What a radio changes for you
The record button becomes ✔ CHK IN › REC — you check in to a ride, then record. (CHK IN › REC)
GRP Awareness shows your radio: green while your radio is talking, red when it is not — GroupTrack carries on with your tablet's GPS, so your cart stays on the map. It reconnects by itself; if three tries fail while you ride with a group, a red banner asks you to FORGET the radio in GRP Awareness and PAIR it again. Pulsing as the group is heard. (GRP Awareness)
New in 2.7b: after those three failed tries GroupTrack rides on this tablet only: the other carts, the lead and the lead's track are cleared and your cart follows the tablet's GPS. Group awareness stays on and keeps trying; when the radio talks again, the carts come back as they are heard.
Your role — Leader, Middle, Tail gunner or Rider — is claimed at check-in and broadcast to everyone; the lead and tail follow the riders who hold those roles. (Roles on the trail)
VIEW CART ROLES lists the carts on your ride, special roles first, with who has checked in; remove a cart from your map, or activate it again. (VIEW CART ROLES)
The group readout shows the whole group at a glance — span, carts, lead and tail. (GROUP, and the readout)
The GPS button sets how often your radio sends your location, and shows how busy the channel is. (GPS)
How far, and how many
Radios relay for each other, so a spread-out group stays connected as long as no gap between riders is too wide. How far a radio reaches, and how many riders fit on one ride, depend on the radio and the channel. (Radio range and group size)
// ⭐ ACCORDION. Opening a section closes its siblings, so you are only ever
// looking at one thing at a time at each level. Without it the document sprawls
// as you explore and you lose your place.
document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){
  d.addEventListener('toggle', function(){
    if (!d.open) return;
    // close only SIBLINGS -- never an ancestor, or the branch you are
    // standing in collapses under you.
    var p = d.parentElement;
    p.querySelectorAll(':scope > details').forEach(function(o){
      if (o !== d) o.open = false;
    });
    d.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest', behavior:'smooth'});
  });
  // ⭐ mark ancestors so their own material folds away, and unmark on close
  d.addEventListener('toggle', mark);
});
function mark(){
  document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){
    var kid = d.querySelector(':scope > .d > details[open]');
    d.classList.toggle('haschild', !!kid);
  });
}
mark();
function op(v){ document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){ d.open = !!v; }); }
/* MANUALLINK-2026-09-26: a link to a section (e.g. from the release notes) opens it and every section around it. */
function openHash(){ var t = location.hash && document.getElementById(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1))); if(!t) return;
  for(var e = t; e; e = e.parentElement){ if(e.tagName === 'DETAILS') e.open = true; }
  if (typeof mark === 'function') mark(); t.scrollIntoView(); }
window.addEventListener('load', openHash); window.addEventListener('hashchange', openHash);
document.addEventListener('click', function(ev){ var a = ev.target.closest && ev.target.closest('a[href^="#"]'); if(a){ setTimeout(openHash, 0); } });

GroupTrack 2.7c — in development
Not yet released · One Map: one map, every tool, a cleaner screen
2.7c replaces the ride map and the planning map with one map. While it is being finished it is switched on in Settings › Layout (One Map). Everything you could do on either map is on it, reached from a few buttons around the edge.
In development · Rel 2.7c
NEW One Map — one set of buttons around one mapRECORD at the top; MENU and zoom on the left; GRP Awareness, Mode, Status, Map Key, Filter and Centre on Me on the right; your readout bottom left; Map, Add Route, Rides, Search and Radio Setup along the bottom. Every screen closes the same way — HELP and ✕ in the top right corner. 22–23 OctWhat it means for you: one map to learn instead of two, and nothing hidden behind a second map.
NEW The Map menu — every map tool in one placeWhat is downloading (tap DETAILS for the queue) · the map source · download maps for offline use by area (draw a box) or along your tracks (all, or pick them, with a search by name) · remove maps · map recovery (your saved map recipes, refresh by source) · import trails by state or by area, import GPX, create trails from your tracks, resync tracks with their files. Choosing a tool closes the menu. 23 OctWhat it means for you: the download and import tools that lived on the planning map are on the map you ride with.
NEW The map type is a button on the mapMap: SAT ▾ shows the map you are looking at; tap it to pick another. 23 OctWhat it means for you: switching satellite and topo is one tap, and the button always says which you are on.
CHANGED The map opens where you left itWith internet, One Map opens on the view you last had; offline it opens on your cart; while recording it follows your cart. 23 OctWhat it means for you: planning picks up where you stopped, and on the trail you start on yourself.
FIXED Private land shows as private againImporting a large state could run out of memory at the step that decides public and private land, and the import still said it had completed — every trail then counted as public. The step now works through the trails in small pieces and says if it fails. If your trails all show as public, use Settings › Classify trails again. 23 OctWhat it means for you: the "Include private land" filter works again, and you can repair an earlier import without importing again.
NEW Filter: off-grid maps on the mapFILTER › OFF-GRID MAPS ☐ Available ☐ Downloading draws the areas you have downloaded, and the ones still downloading, on the map. 23 OctWhat it means for you: you can see where your offline maps reach before you lose signal.
NEW Area Search Radius worksChoose how far in a place search zooms (Z12 to Z18); One Map's search uses it. It was saved before but never used. 23 OctWhat it means for you: a place search lands at the zoom you want.
NEW Add Route on One Map — Build it myselfAdd Route checks first for anything unfinished: a route left open when the app closed is loaded straight back in, and routes you were building are offered to continue. Then Build it myself: tap along the trails, each point snaps and saves as you go; Save, Discard, or ✕ to leave. 23 OctWhat it means for you: you can plan a route on the map you ride with, and a crash never costs you the points you dropped.
NEW Add Route on One Map — AI route designThe guided steps: how far and how fast, your trailhead (with a search to find your area), a loop or a finish point, places you want to pass through, then FIND MY RIDES — and the comparison of the rides it builds, side by side in their own colours, fitted on the map. AI turns Trails and Waypoints on and keeps them on while it works; the comparison hides everything else and puts it all back when you leave. Nothing you left unfinished is deleted when you start. 23 OctWhat it means for you: the AI planner works on One Map, and an earlier comparison waits for your decision instead of being cleared.
NEW One Search, Filter and Map KeySearch: one box searches trails, routes, tracks, waypoints and (online) places, scoped to a state you choose, with the result types as a filter. Filter: everything you show or hide, each trail type explained. Map Key: only what you are looking at, and the colour styles. 22 OctWhat it means for you: one place to find something, one place to choose what shows, one place to read the map.
GroupTrack 2.7b — internal testing
22 October 2026 · one week with internal testers before release
Most of 2.7b is under the hood. GroupTrack and the radio side now talk through one connection, and the ride map is drawn only from the messages your tablet actually receives, instead of a 5-second polling loop. You should see a steadier map and a quicker response; what you do on the trail is the same. The changes you will notice:
Group awareness, or this tablet only &mdash; ride without a radio and GroupTrack hides everything that needs one. 13 Oct
The lead's track &mdash; solid bright blue ahead of you, your own track dashed blue; behind you the lead's track gives way to yours. 20 Oct
When the lead goes quiet &mdash; his cart keeps moving at an estimate, and his real path is filled in when he is heard again. 20 Oct and below
The radio link &mdash; "Your radio isn't answering" tells you what to do; losing satellites no longer disconnects the radio. 18 Oct
Roles &mdash; strict: no Leader, no lead; two riders on one role both go back to Rider. 15 Oct
Smaller things &mdash; recording pauses after 25 idle minutes instead of 10, a GPS light above REC, arrows on your route, Medium Fast or Long Fast in the GPS panel, Ride statistics in Settings, NODES instead of the Meshtastic side menu, and fixes to a white map at start and to a recording that paused itself.
Rel 2.7b · 21 October 2026
CHANGED With no route displayed, the quiet lead follows the trail he was on &mdash; to the next junctionWhen the lead goes quiet and you are not displaying a route, his estimated position now moves along the track or trail he was on, at the ride's average speed, and stops at the next junction, where another track or trail branches off. GroupTrack never guesses which way he turned. If he was not steadily on any track or trail, the estimate stays where he was last heard. With a route displayed, nothing changes: the estimate follows the route.What it means for you: on a ride without a route loaded, the blinking lead still shows a sensible place &mdash; and at a junction it waits there, which is where you need to decide.Manual: The lead cart
CHANGED Saved routes no longer guide the lead's track through a gapThrough a lost signal, the lead's track is drawn along the route you are displaying, or a track you rode before, or the trails. A saved route that is not on the map is no longer used: it was often a different ride over the same ground.What it means for you: the lead's track only follows lines you can see or have ridden.
Known in this test (please report what you see)
Not yet tried with two riders in the field: the estimate, the lead's path after a lost signal and the trim behind you have been tested on our tablets and on recorded rides, not yet on a group ride. Tell us where they look wrong.
Radio reconnect while GroupTrack is in the background: if your radio drops while another app is in front, GroupTrack may not reconnect until you bring it back on screen.
A quiet cart can stay "Active" (seen 15 October) &mdash; being checked this week.
Rel 2.7b · 20 October 2026
<!-- RELNOTES-2026-10-20 (2.7b, commits 1e2bba8c0..8bedb5b9c + ESTREC/BLUETRACKS -- NOT RELEASED; tablet-tested only). Not listed: fixes of unreleased 2.7b code

NEW Medium Fast or Long Fast, chosen beside the intervalThe GPS panel on the Ride Map now lets you choose the radio's preset &mdash; Medium Fast (the standard) or Long Fast &mdash; beside how often it sends. APPLY sets your radio once and checks every value. The choice lasts until your next check-in, which sets the ride's standard again.What it means for you: on a ride where carts spread out you can trade a little speed for a little more range. Measured: Long Fast reaches only 10-30% further, so Medium Fast stays the default.Manual: GPS
NEW Ride statisticsSettings &rsaquo; Group awareness &rsaquo; Ride statistics shows, for every cart heard on this ride: how far away it was, how often it was lost and for how long, and how busy the channel was. REFRESH updates it, RESET starts again.What it means for you: after a ride you can see how far your radios really reached on that ground.Manual: Settings
NEW When the lead goes quiet, his cart keeps moving along the routeIf the lead's reports stop arriving, his cart blinks at where he probably is &mdash; moving along the displayed route at the ride's average speed &mdash; with est. m:ss beside it and a grey dot where he was last heard. (21 October: with no route displayed it follows the track or trail he was on, as far as the next junction &mdash; see above.) GROUP keeps him in view. When he is heard again he jumps to his real position. Only while you are recording.What it means for you: out of range of the lead you still have a good idea where he is.Manual: The lead cart
NEW The lead's path is filled in after a lost signalWhile the lead is out of range his track is drawn along the route you are displaying (or a track you rode before, or the trails), never faster than a cart could drive. When he comes back into range his tablet sends the path he really drove while nobody could hear him, and your tablet corrects his track to it &mdash; a short pop-up says so. Points far from the route show as dots.What it means for you: after a dead spot the lead's track shows where he actually went, so you can follow it.Manual: The lead cart
NEW Behind you, the lead's track gives way to yoursAs you ride over the lead's track, the part behind you is removed and your own track shows there. Loops and out-and-backs are handled in the order you ride them, so the way back is never removed early.What it means for you: the lead track on your map is the way ahead &mdash; one line to follow.Manual: The lead cart
CHANGED Blue tracks you can see on red rockThe lead's track is a solid bright blue line and your own track a dashed bright blue line, both edged in black with arrows showing the direction of travel.What it means for you: both tracks stand out on satellite and on red rock; solid is the way ahead, dashed is ground you have covered.Manual: The lead cart
FIXED Saving a track no longer hangs on the hourglassSaving a recorded track could sit on the hourglass for a long time while it checked for a duplicate. The check now looks the track up directly.What it means for you: SAVE comes back quickly.Manual: CHK IN › REC
CHANGED Check-in also makes sure your radio passes every message onChecking in now also sets your radio to pass on every message it hears (its relay setting), and checks it with the rest: 25 checks instead of 24.What it means for you: carts out of each other's reach still hear each other through the carts in between.Manual: Roles on the trail

NEW A GPS light above RECA small light above the record button shows whether this tablet has a GPS lock: green &mdash; GPS LOCK with the number of satellites in use, red while it is still looking. On a tablet without GPS it shows whether your radio is supplying the position (RADIO GPS). The first lock after the tablet has been off can take about five minutes under open sky.What it means for you: wait for green before you press REC, and your track starts where you start.Manual: CHK IN › REC
NEW Arrows on your routeA route shown on the Ride Map now carries arrows along it in the direction it was built to be ridden.What it means for you: at a fork or on a loop you can see at a glance which way the ride goes.Manual: Map Features
FIXED The Ride Map no longer opens white or showing the whole worldSome riders opened the Ride Map to a blank white screen, or a view of the whole world, until they pressed MY CART. The map was being fitted to its last view before it had a size on the screen. It now waits until it is ready. With no internet it opens on your cart, on your downloaded maps.What it means for you: the map opens where you are, ready to ride &mdash; no more tapping MY CART to bring the maps back.Manual: The Ride Map
CHANGED Losing the internet on the trail switches you to your downloaded mapsIf the tablet loses its network while the Ride Map is open, the map switches to the maps you downloaded, by itself. Coming back into coverage does not switch back; use the map source button when you want online maps again.What it means for you: the map keeps showing the ground under you when the signal drops.Manual: SAT, TOPO and TOPO+
FIXED Recording no longer pauses itself straight after RECStarting a new recording near where an earlier one ended could put it to sleep within a couple of minutes, as if you had been parked for 25 minutes. REC and RESUME now start the idle timer from zero.What it means for you: the recording only pauses after a real 25 minutes without moving.Manual: CHK IN › REC
CHANGED You see yourself from this tablet; the group sees your radioYour own cart and your track follow this tablet's GPS. Every other rider sees your cart where your radio reports it.What it means for you: your own cart moves smoothly on your screen, and the group sees one position for you, not two.Manual: GRP Awareness
Rel 2.7b · 18 October 2026
<!-- RELNOTES-2026-10-18 (2.7b, commits 8aed6e286..94524303f -- NOT RELEASED; tablet-tested only). Internal fixes found while testing unreleased 2.7b code are NOT listed
     (Fred 10-15): the health-check reconnect loop, the phantom link, the GPS chip start (CHIPALWAYS), the loop trim. OPEN: MYCARTCHIP may restate the 10-15 "Your cart moves" note. -->
NEW "Your radio isn't answering. Check it is powered on."If your radio goes completely quiet while you ride with a group &mdash; nothing from it and nothing through it for 30 seconds &mdash; this message shows at once. 15 seconds later GroupTrack reconnects to the radio by itself, and keeps trying. If three tries fail, the message changes to the FORGET and PAIR advice. When the radio is heard again the message clears.What it means for you: a radio that was switched off or ran flat is spotted in about half a minute, and you are told what to check first.Manual: GRP Awareness
CHANGED Losing satellites no longer disconnects your radioUnder trees or in a canyon your radio can lose its GPS fix and stop sending its position. GroupTrack no longer treats that as a dead radio: the connection stays up, your cart carries on from this tablet's GPS, and your radio's position comes back by itself when it sees the sky again.What it means for you: no more reconnect loops on the trail when the radio loses its fix.Manual: GRP Awareness
NEW Your track and the lead's track on the ride mapWhile recording, a blue dotted line with arrows follows behind your cart, and a black dotted line with arrows shows the path the lead cart has driven ahead of you. The lead's line is drawn from the positions his radio sends; the part you have already driven is removed as you go.What it means for you: you can see where you have been and where the lead has gone.Manual: MY CART
Rel 2.7b · 16 October 2026
CHANGED Recording pauses after 25 minutes parked, not 10When you have not moved for 25 minutes (it was 10), GroupTrack pauses the recording and disconnects the radio, as before. The banner now says what happened: Sleeping &mdash; Recording paused, radio disconnected. Tap to wake.What it means for you: a lunch stop or a long wait at a junction no longer puts your tablet to sleep, and when it does sleep you know the group can't hear you until you tap.Manual: CHK IN › REC

FIXED Your cart moves with your radio connectedOn a ride with the radio connected, your own cart could stay where it was on your own tablet while everyone else's moved. Your cart on your map now always follows this tablet's GPS, every time it moves, radio connected or not. The other riders still see you from your radio.What it means for you: MY CART keeps up with you on every ride.Manual: MY CART
CHANGED The Meshtastic side menu is gone — NODES insteadThe Meshtastic menu down the left-hand side no longer appears. The one thing riders used it for — the list of radios heard — is now NODES in GRP Awareness. It opens on top of the map, and BACK TO MAP takes you straight back, the same way Radio settings does.What it means for you: no more leaving the ride map by mistake, and no menu of radio screens you don't need.Manual: GRP Awareness
NEW Two riders, one role — both go back to RiderIf two riders claim the same role — Leader, Middle or Tail gunner — at the same moment, both are set back to Rider. Each tablet shows a flashing red ROLE CONFLICT message naming the other rider, with VIEW CART ROLES open behind it. Agree who takes the role, and that rider claims it again.What it means for you: a ride never has two Leaders. If you see the red message, talk to the rider it names, then one of you claims the role.Manual: Roles on the trail
CHANGED The lead follows the Leader — on every tabletWhen a rider checks in as Leader, every tablet makes that cart the lead. When the Leader changes to Rider, the lead is cleared everywhere — nobody is left following a cart that no longer leads. The new Leader claims the role in VIEW CART ROLES, or REC asks which cart leads.What it means for you: the lead on your map is the rider who holds Leader — nobody else.Manual: Roles on the trail
FIXED Roles show only while you are checked inAfter END, a rider's old role could stay beside a cart. Roles now show only while your tablet is checked in to a ride; the carts themselves always show.What it means for you: no leftover roles from the last ride.Manual: Roles on the trail
CHANGED Radio gone for good? Your tablet carries on aloneWhen three reconnect attempts fail while you ride with a group (the red banner), GroupTrack switches to this tablet only: the other carts, the lead and the lead's track are cleared, and your cart follows the tablet's GPS. Group awareness stays on and keeps trying — when your radio comes back, the carts return as they are heard.What it means for you: you never ride on carts frozen where they were minutes ago.Manual: Group Awareness
CHANGED Tapping a cart: GAP, and live updatesThe details of a cart you tap now update with each report from that cart. SEEN is replaced by GAP: the time between that cart's last two reports — a quick check of how well you are hearing it. ALT shows its unit (ft).What it means for you: a GAP that grows means that rider's radio is getting hard to hear.Manual: GROUP, and the readout
CHANGED No "No location available" message at startThe message no longer interrupts the start while the first GPS fix arrives; the map moves to you as soon as it does.What it means for you: one less thing to dismiss.
Known in this test build (15 October)A cart whose radio goes quiet can stay "Active". Signal Drop and Signal Lost are worked out as reports arrive; when nothing arrives at all, a quiet cart's status may not change. Still to be confirmed in the 2.7b test week &mdash; see the list above.

GroupTrack 2.7a — the Community release
Group communication and ride sharing · 30 September 2026
GroupTrack is complete as installed, and 2.7a adds your community. It is two products in one: a complete personal navigation product that lets you share rides and maps with other GroupTrack users, and a true situational awareness product for your group on the trail.
On your own — the whole job
Trails and maps on your device, working with no signal; a planner that builds routes for you to compare; waypoints, map downloads and your own track recordings. Manual: The Ride Planning Map
New: ★ Create a RideOne ride holds the route, the trailhead, the date and time, the maps to download and the mesh radio configuration. Send it in one click; your friends open it in one click — and ride anywhere off grid in total confidence. Manual: ★ Create a Ride
Your identity
Your rider profile — callsign and email — is who you are in GroupTrack. It is private: it stays on your tablet, nothing is sent to GroupTrack, and it goes only to the riders you ride with. Manual: Your rider profile
Add a radio to experience full group awareness while riding
Add a Meshtastic radio — any Meshtastic radio, not only the T1000-E — and you see your group on the map with no cell service. GroupTrack sets the radio up for you. Manual: Group Awareness
A private network for organizers and clubs — your rides use your own radio network; riders who have ridden with you are already on it next time, and nobody outside the ride hears it.
One standard language — radios report in TAK, the team-awareness format: your position with your callsign, even with the tablet in your pocket.
Roles and presence — Leader, Middle and Tail gunner are broadcast to every member; riders check in to claim a role and announce that they are there.
The ride carries the radio settings — checking in at the trailhead sets your radio up for the ride's network by itself.
So a ride goes like this
Tap the Ride invite. GroupTrack creates the route, its trailhead and the ride's description, stores the ride's radio settings, and imports the maps along the route.
With a radio, check in at the trailhead. Your radio is set up for the ride, and your role is announced.
REC. You are riding — with your group on the map if you carry a radio.
For the organizer it is one step: build the ride and send it.
2.7a update · 17 October 2026 (release m)Offline maps now open with no signal. Before this update, downloaded maps only showed if GroupTrack was started with an internet connection; started with no signal, the map stayed blank. The map library is now inside the app, so the map opens anywhere.
Updating from 2.6 — what to do first
NEW Three one-time steps. (1) Your rider profile — GroupTrack asks for it the first time it opens. (2) Update your radio, if you ride with one: 2.7a moves GroupTrack to TAK messaging, so each radio needs the GroupTrack default once. GroupTrack asks at first start — Do you have a mesh radio to use with GroupTrack? — and YES takes you to GRP Awareness to connect it and apply the default. Said NO? Do it before your first ride: GRP Awareness → connect → Select a ride and apply settings to the radio → GroupTrack default. (3) Ride files — the first time you tap one, choose GroupTrack, then Always. New to GroupTrack? The Quick Start walks you through it. Manual: First start
IMPORTANT Before every ride: send the ride invite to every riderEveryone on the ride needs the same ride. Send the ride invite to every GroupTrack rider joining you — and make sure each one opens it and imports it before the ride. The ride brings the route, the trailhead and the maps. Without it, a rider sees carts as dots on an empty map and has nothing to follow. It matters even with no radio: a rider who has imported the ride can follow the route on their own tablet, and stays on course far more easily.What it means for you: when you create a ride, send it to everyone who is coming — and ask them to open it before you meet. At the trailhead, check that every rider has it.Manual: Sending a ride
