2026-08-28 — the route planner walks you through it
Planning a route is now a set of screens that ask one thing at a time. Instead of a
checklist you read all at once, each step tells you what it needs, you do it on the map, and the
next step appears.
What you will see
An overview first, explaining what you will get and what happens to the routes you do
not keep. Tick the box and you will not see it again.
Distance and pace on their own screen, with the ride duration updating as you move the
sliders. Set the mileage until the hours match the day you have.
One prompt per step after that, sitting at the bottom of the screen so the map and the
search box stay clear.
A pin the planner cannot reach is removed, and it tells you why rather than quietly
building a route that misses it.
Save Selected / Delete Unselected spells out both halves, and the comparison now says
that tapping a route name hides its line.
Planning stays in portrait throughout, and the map layers are cleared before the comparison so
the routes are readable.
— carried forward from 2026-08-27 —
DOCUMENT ID: RELNOTES-2026-08-27
2026-08-27 — comparing the routes the app suggests
When the planner finds you rides, you can now see them side by side. Ask for routes and
the app draws every one it found, each in its own colour, with a table underneath that lines them
up against each other.
What you will see
Every route on the map at once, in its own colour.
A table where the rows are places and trails and each column is one route. A green
check means that route reaches that feature; a number means how many miles of that trail it
uses.
The most-used trails at the top. The trails near the top are what these rides are made
of; the ones lower down are what makes them different. Two routes with big numbers on the same few
trails are variations on the same ride.
Tap a route's name to take its line off the map so you can see the others. Tap again to
bring it back.
Tick the ones you want to keep, type a name for the area, and they are saved —
Panguitch Mi. 79 Pts. 7. The ones you did not tick are discarded.
While you are comparing
Trails, tracks and waypoints are hidden so the routes are readable, and put back exactly as
you had them when you leave. The map does not switch to route-drawing mode, so tapping a route
to look at it will not add points to it.
Leaving without saving keeps everything — the routes are still there next time you tap Route+.
Only Save Selected finishes the job. If you tick nothing, the app asks first: all the routes
go, and you would have to start the search over.
Also fixed
The In-Progress list no longer opens empty — with nothing to continue, Route+ simply starts a
new route.
Renaming an in-progress route has been removed. The name you give a route when you save it is
the one that matters.
Saved routes follow the trail correctly even when part of the route is off the edge of the
screen.

DOCUMENT ID RELNOTES-2026-08-26-r2 &middot; issued 26 August 2026
GroupTrack Release Notes
V2.6h &middot; in development &middot; RELNOTES-2026-08-26
These notes ship inside the app, so they always describe the build you
are running.
Document revision RELNOTES-2.6h-r2 &middot; 26 August 2026
What changed in this release
Which document you want
QuickStart is for a new rider on a first install &mdash; getting the app on
the phone, permissions, radio pairing, and getting trails onto the map. It is a summary of how
things work right now, not a history. It opens by itself the first time you install.
These release notes are for riders who already have GroupTrack. They cover
what is new in this release and how to use it, and they open after an update. Earlier releases
are kept below under Release history.
The user manual is the walkthrough. Where something new needs more than a paragraph,
these notes point at the manual page for it.
Route planning is being rebuilt &mdash; not ready to use yet
What this means to you. Nothing in this build, and that is deliberate.
The part of GroupTrack that suggests rides was taken apart and rebuilt this week. It now works
properly on the bench &mdash; it will offer you several genuinely different rides from where
you park, rather than one &mdash; but the screens you would use it through are still being
finished.
How to use it. You cannot yet. It is listed here so you know it is
coming and that the quiet in this area is work, not neglect.
Manual: Planning a route &mdash; link pending anchors
Files other riders send you now import completely
What this means to you. When someone emails you a GPX file and you tap
it, everything in it comes across &mdash; the tracks, the waypoints and the routes. Before, only
the tracks arrived and the rest were dropped without saying so, which is why a file could look
like it imported nothing. If you learned to save files to Downloads first as a workaround, you
no longer need to.
How to use it. Tap the attachment in your email and choose GroupTrack.
Importing from Map Features &rarr; IMPORT TRACKS, WAYPOINTS &amp; ROUTES still works and
gives the same result.
Manual: Importing files &mdash; link pending anchors
Your trails stay put
What this means to you. If you loaded your state and found the trails
gone again a day or two later, that is fixed. It was a one-time cleanup that kept running every
time the app opened instead of once. You should not have to load a state twice.
How to use it. Nothing to do. If your trails are missing right now, import
your state one more time and it will stay.
Manual: Loading trails for your state &mdash; link pending anchors
Route planning &mdash; not ready yet
What this means to you. Nothing yet. Work is going on behind the scenes
to let GroupTrack suggest rides from your trail data, and to let you mark places a ride has to
reach. It is not finished and is not something to rely on in this build. It is listed here so
you know it is coming, not so you can try it.
Known issues as of 26 August 2026
KNOWN A state import can stop partway. Some sources
finish and the rest never start. Your trail count still looks reasonable, so nothing appears
wrong &mdash; but the largest source, Open Source Maps, is usually the one that did not
run, and it carries most of the trail network.
What it looks like: route building offers one route where you would
expect several, or comes back well short of the distance you asked for. The map still shows
plenty of trails, which is what makes it confusing.
What to do: run the state import again. Trails already on your device are skipped, so
only what is missing is fetched and nothing is duplicated.
KNOWN Route planning near a town suggests roads.
The trail data GroupTrack imports contains roads as well as trails, and it cannot yet tell them
apart. Planning from a staging point inside a town will offer you rides that follow streets.
What to do: plan from where the trails actually start &mdash; a
trailhead or a parking area out of town. Work to separate roads from trails in the imported
data is underway.
KNOWN An import record can be opened by the wrong import
routine. The record left behind by a run is picked up by an older code path than the one
that wrote it, so a run can be misread afterwards &mdash; and a stopped import may be reported
inaccurately. Being fixed by pointing the existing routine at the current one rather than
leaving two.
KNOWN Some trail sources report errors on every record in
some areas. Affected in some areas and not others; under investigation. The per-source
counts on the completion screen are what make it visible.
KNOWN A state may be listed for your area without having
trails in it. States are matched using a rectangle around each state and those rectangles
overlap. It costs download time; it does not affect your data.
KNOWN Re-importing the same state on the same day
replaces that day's earlier import record.
Release history
Earlier releases, newest first. Each one shows what changed at the time.
V2.6g &mdash; 23 August 2026 &mdash; Home State Import Pipeline
Release date: In development · Branch: feature/convoy-event-ride
Importing routes and waypoints from a GPX file
FIXED GPX files containing routes or waypoints now import.
Previously only the tracks in a file were read — routes and waypoints were skipped without any
message, so a file that contained them appeared to import nothing.
This affects files shared between riders, and exports from other apps.
HOW TO IMPORT
Save the file to your Downloads folder first, then open Map Features on the Ride
Planning Map and choose IMPORT TRACKS, WAYPOINTS &amp; ROUTES.
Tapping a GPX attachment directly in your email will not import routes yet — it still
reads tracks only. Save it to Downloads and import it from Map Features instead. This is being
worked on.
Note: the file is removed from Downloads once it has been imported.
Trail sources
FIXED US Geological Survey National Trails now imports. Every
record from this source was failing, in every state, and the source appeared simply to have no
data for your area. It was reading the wrong field names from the service. In New Hampshire it
now brings in 390 trails where it previously brought none.
Import Trails — by State or by Area (New)
NEW Import Trails now asks how you want to choose your ground.
One button on the Map Features panel, two ways in:
By State — pick any state from the list. Every available source for that state is
processed. Use this when you're planning a trip somewhere new.
By Area — draw a box on the map. GroupTrack works out which states your box reaches and
processes every source that covers it. Your box can cross state lines — a ride that runs from
Utah into Arizona brings in both.
Either way there is no source checklist. Every source that covers your ground runs, because that
is what lets one source fill in what another is missing.
Import Progress Detail
NEW Every import now records what happened to each record, not just
how many were added. Per source: how many were read, how many fell inside your state or area, how
many you already had, how many were added, and how many could not be processed.
The summary still shows one number — records added. The detail sits behind the source name if you
want it, and it is written into the import record on your device either way, so it can be looked up
later.
CHANGED Each import run now carries an identifier, so a run can be
identified exactly when something needs looking into.
Known Issues
Some sources report errors on every record in some areas. US Geological Survey
National Trails is fixed (see above). Other sources are still affected in some areas and not
others — under investigation. These sources previously reported zero records with no indication
anything had gone wrong; the new counts are what made it visible.
A state may be listed for your area without having trails in it. States are matched using
a rectangle around each state and those rectangles overlap, so a neighbouring state can be included
and then contribute nothing. It costs download time; it does not affect your data. A way to skip
those states is coming.
Re-importing the same state on the same day replaces that day's earlier import record.
Home State Setup (New)
NEW One-tap trail data setup on first launch. When GroupTrack detects no trail data, it offers to load your home state's trails automatically:
GPS auto-detection suggests your state (uses Android Geocoder for accuracy at state borders)
Searchable state picker with all 50 US states + DC + PR + USVI
California split into North (San Luis Obispo area and north) and South (Santa Barbara/Bakersfield area and south)
All available data sources processed automatically — US Forest Service, US Geological Survey, National Park Service, state agencies, and Open Source Maps (Geofabrik OSM)
Progress display: per-source step indicators (✅/►/○), download progress in MB, running elapsed clock
Blinking "Do not close GroupTrack" banner during processing
Completion summary with per-source record counts and grand total
New Hampshire verified: 42,338 OSM trails + 1,010 catalog trails imported in ~4 minutes
Geofabrik State Asset
NEW Shipped geofabrik_states.json — 54 entries with download URLs for every US state and territory. Supports the automatic Geofabrik GPKG download (302 redirect handling included). Refreshable via update_geofabrik_states.py.
Release-Assets Folder
NEW release-assets/ folder in the repo. Holds dated docs (manual, release notes, quickstart) and two Python scripts. One command (python release-assets/prepare_release_assets.py) refreshes Geofabrik URLs, copies newest dated docs to app assets, and verifies markers.
Source Name Improvements
CHANGED Plain-language source names throughout — no unexplained acronyms:
UGRC Utah Trails → Utah Trails and Pathways
BLM Ground Transportation → Bureau of Land Management Trails
USFS National Forest System Trails → US Forest Service Trails
USGS National Trails → US Geological Survey National Trails
NPS Public Trails → National Park Service Trails
USFS Motor Vehicle Use Maps → US Forest Service Motor Vehicle Use Maps
OSM Trails → Open Source Maps
Bug Fixes
FIXED Geofabrik -latest- URL 302 redirect now followed automatically.
FIXED GPS state detection at border areas (NH/MA) now uses Android Geocoder instead of bbox matching.
FIXED OSM import ledger creation before pending bbox set (prevented silent import failure).
Resolved since the 20 August notes
Home State setup now runs on first launch — it no longer has to be found on the Map
Features panel.
Import Trails by Area is built — draw a box, and every source covering it is processed,
across state lines.
The completion screen shows the full picture — records read, records in your area,
duplicates, added, and anything that could not be processed.
